translations.text: Glory in the highest, peace on earth.
The earth has yielded its fruit: the ends of the earth: Isaiah said long beforehand, "Behold, the virgin."
The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing; in a place [...]
You who shepherd Israel, look down. Joseph:
And there were shepherds in that same region, staying out in the field and keeping the night watches over their flock.
And an angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone upon them, and they were afraid with great fear.
And the angel of the Lord said to them: "Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people.
For a Saviour has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.
And this will be a sign to you: you will find the child wrapped in swaddling cloths, lying in a manger."
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the hosts of heaven, praising God and saying:
"Glory to God in the highest, peace on earth, and goodwill among people."
And when the angels had gone up into heaven, the shepherds said to one another:
"Let us go over to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened to us, which the Lord has made known to us."
And they came in haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.
And when they saw it, they understood the word that had been spoken to them about the child.
And all who heard were amazed at what the shepherds said to them. But Mary kept these words and laid them up in her heart.
And the shepherds turned and went away, glorifying and blessing God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
Creator of all created things:
The Lord said to me, "You are my son": "Ask of me, and I will give you":
Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel concerning the shepherds of my people: You have scattered my sheep and driven them away, and you have neglected them.
Behold, I will take vengeance on you according to the wickedness of your ways, says the Lord.
And I will have mercy on the remnant of my people from all the earth where I scattered them; I will settle them in their pasture, and they will flourish and multiply.
And I will raise up shepherds for them who will shepherd them; and they will no longer be afraid, nor will they be dismayed, says the Lord.

Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will raise up for David a righteous Rising (Dawn), and a righteous king will reign; he will understand, and he will execute judgment and righteousness on the earth.
In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell in hope.
In many parts and in many ways God formerly spoke to the fathers, the prophets,
but in these last days he has spoken to us through his own Son, whom he also appointed heir of all things, through whom he made the ages,
who was the radiance of glory and the image of power; [?] the words of power, he made purification of our sins;
and he sat down at the right hand of the majesty [?] on high. He became as much better than the angels as the name he inherited is more excellent than theirs.
For to which of the angels did he ever say: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you"?
And again he says: "I will be his Father, and he shall be my Son." And when he again brings the firstborn into the world, he says: "Let all the angels of God worship him."
Of the angels he says: "He who made his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire."
But of the Son he says: "Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the scepter of governance is the scepter of your kingdom."
"You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions."
"You, Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the heavens are the works of your hands;
they will all grow old like garments, and like a cloak you will change them, and they will be changed.
But you yourself are the same, and your years will not fail."
The Lord said to my Lord: Sit...
Now the birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way:
His mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, and before they came together she was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.
Joseph her husband was a righteous man and did not want to expose her, so he resolved to send her away secretly.
And as he was considering this, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a vision and said to him:
"Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife, for the one who is to be born of her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will bear a son, and they will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins."
All this took place so that the word of the Lord spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled:
"Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel," which means, translated, "God is with us."
Joseph awoke from his sleep and did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him;
he took his wife to himself, but did not know her until she had borne a son, and he called his name Jesus.
The Lord was born in Bethlehem of Judea:
What shall we offer:
On the Nativity of the Lord, in Bethlehem:
My heart has uttered [a good word]: In the beginning God made the heaven:
Rejoice, you righteous; heavens [?]. All you nations, lift up [your hands]:
And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz and said:
Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height.
And Ahaz said: I will not ask, and I will not put the Lord to the test. And Isaiah said: Hear, O house of David!
Is it a small thing for you to cause trouble for men? And how then will you cause trouble for the Lord?
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel.
Butter and honey he shall eat, until he knows and chooses; [rather than] evil he shall choose the good.
For before the child knows good or evil, he shall reject evil and choose the good.
The land shall be left desolate, the land you fear because of the two kings.
But the Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days
such as have not yet come, since the day when Ephraim took away from Judah the king of the Assyrians.
For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared:
Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised: And it was at the censer [?]:
The saying of the prophets was fulfilled: O God, have mercy on us and bless us:
And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, you are by no means the least.
And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are you by no means the least, that you should be among the thousands of Judah?
For from you shall come forth for me a ruler who shall rule over Israel, and his goings forth are from the days of eternity.
Therefore he will give them up until the time of her who gives birth; for she shall give birth, and the remnant of his brothers shall return to the sons of Israel.

And he shall stand and be glorified, and the Lord shall shepherd the flock with strength; and they shall be in the glory of the name of the Lord God, for now they shall be magnified to the ends of the earth.
And this shall be peace: when the Assyrian comes into your land, and when he comes upon your country,
then seven shepherds and eight wounds shall rise up against him, and they shall shepherd the Assyrian with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in its [?],
and he shall deliver you from the Assyrian, when he comes into your land and when he comes upon your territories.
And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like dew falling from the Lord and like lambs on the grass,
So that no one may gather them, nor withstand the sons of men. Nor anyone: [?] withstand among men.
We have seen in the cave, in the manger: O God, [give] your judgment to the king.
The proverbs of Solomon, son of David, who reigned over Israel:
to know wisdom and instruction, to understand words of understanding, and to receive the turnings of words, to understand truth and righteousness, and to direct judgments;
so that knowledge may be given to the innocent, and understanding and knowledge to young children.
Hearing these, the wise man will become wiser, and the man of understanding will gain skill in striving.
He will understand proverbs and hidden words, the sayings of the wise, and riddles. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; good understanding belongs to all who practise it;
and reverence toward God is good. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; the ungodly despise wisdom and instruction.
Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and do not depart from the law of your mother.
For you will set a crown of grace on your head and a chain of gold around your neck.
Today the heavens rejoice and are glad: Lord, you have been pleased with your land.
And they will wish that they had been burned with fire.
For a child has been born for us, a son has been given to us, whose government is upon his shoulders, and his name is called Angel of Great Counsel,
Mighty God and Sovereign, Prince of Peace, Father of the ages to come; for I will bring peace upon the rulers, peace and life.
And of his peace there is no number. He will sit upon his [?] (the text reads “curse”), and it will prosper in righteousness and truth from now and to the ages of eternity.
The zeal of the Lord of Hosts has done this.
Whence have you come, O Magi? Or: His foundations are on the mountains.
And a rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will spring up from his root.
And the Spirit of God will rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding,
the spirit of counsel and of knowledge and of godliness, the spirit of might and of the fear of God;
and it will fill him. He will not judge by appearance, nor reprove by hearsay, but he will judge with righteous judgment and reprove the great ones of the earth.
He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will destroy the ungodly.
And his loins will be girded with righteousness, and his sides made firm with truth.
Then the wolf will graze with the lambs, and the leopard will lie down with the young goats, and the calf and the bull and the lion will graze together, and a little child will lead them.
And the ox and the lion will graze together, and their young will be together.
And the little child will put his hand into the asp's hole, and nothing will harm him, nor will it be able to destroy on my holy mountain,
for the whole earth has been filled with the knowledge of God, as much water covers the sea.
To the One born of the Virgin: By your mercy, O Lord:
Be strong, you weary hands and loosened knees.
Comfort the faint of heart: be strong and do not fear. Behold, our Lord renders judgment, and he will render it.
He himself will come and save us. Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear.
Then the lame will leap like deer, and the tongue of the stammerer will be made straight, for water has burst forth in the wilderness, and streams in the thirsty land.
And the wilderness will become marshes, and in the thirsty land there will be a spring of waters.
There will be the joy of birds and the dwelling of serpents, reeds and marshes. There will be a straight way, and it will be called the holy way.
The unclean will not pass along it, nor will there be a way of the unclean there; but those crooked of heart will walk on it and will not go astray.
There will be no lion there, nor any of the evil beasts; none will go up, nor be found there, but those who have been redeemed and gathered by the Lord will walk on it.
They will return and come to Zion with joy and gladness, for upon their heads will be praise and gladness.
And pain and care, grief and groaning will depart.
At the Manifestation (Epiphany) of Christ, [?]: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand:
Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion;
lift up your voice mightily, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem; lift it up, do not fear; say to the cities of Judah:
Behold, God, our God! Behold, the Lord comes with might, and his arm with authority; behold, his reward is with him, and his works before him.
Like a shepherd he will tend his flock, and with his arm he will gather the lambs, and he will comfort those that are with young.
Who has measured the waters in his handful, and measured out the heavens with a span, and all the earth with his fist?
Who has weighed the mountains in a balance and the hills with a yoke? Who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counselor, to set him on the track?
Or who showed him justice, or who made known to him the way of understanding?
If all the nations are reckoned as drops from a bucket and as the tipping of a balance, and as spittle of the mouth;
and Lebanon is not sufficient for burning, and all the four-footed beasts are not sufficient for a burnt offering;
and all the nations are as nothing; they are as nothing and are reckoned as nothing.
King of the Jews and Savior: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good:
Jacob, my servant, I will help him;
and Israel, my chosen one, my soul will receive him. I will put my spirit upon him, and he will bring forth justice to the nations.
He will not cry out, nor will he let up, nor will his voice be heard outside.
A broken reed he will not crush, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, but he will bring forth justice in truth.
And all will tremble until he establishes justice on the earth; and the nations will hope in his name.
Thus says the Lord God, who created the heavens and made them firm;
who made firm the earth and everything that is in it, and gave breath to his people, and spirit to those who walk upon it:
I am the Lord God, who called you in righteousness, and held your hand, and strengthened you, and gave you as a covenant to the peoples and as a light to the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, and to bring out of prison those who are bound, who sit in darkness.
I am the Lord, and this is my name.
The city which you loved: Remember, O Lord, David:
In the eighteenth year:
Arise, O Lord, into your resting place: Remember, O Lord, David and:
And it came to pass in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered.
This was the first registration of the world, in the years when Quirinius was governor of Syria. Everyone went, and each person was registered in his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem,
because he was of the house and lineage of David, to go and be enrolled in the book of the registration of the world with Mary, who was betrothed to him.
And it came to pass, while they were still there, that the days of her giving birth were fulfilled.
And she bore her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
of all created beings: The Lord said to me, You are my Son: Ask of me:
The Lord established me as the beginning of his ways, for his works.
Before the ages he established me, in the very beginning, before the making of the earth,
and before the making of the abysses, and before the springs of the waters came forth.
And before the mountains, and before the hills were established, he begot me. The Lord made the inhabited lands and the wilderness, the farthest parts of what is under heaven.
And when he was ordering the heavens, I was with him; and when he set up his thrones upon the winds; and when he made the clouds above strong; and when he carefully laid down the waters under heaven.

For he set his fear upon the sea, so that none of the waters should pass beyond his commands, at the time when he was making firm the foundations of the earth, I was with him as one who ordered all things.
And I was the one in whom the Lord always delighted, and I rejoiced before him at every time,
when he was glad at the completion of the world and rejoiced over the children of men.
I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and like a mist I covered the earth.
I dwelt in the heights, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud. Alone I went around the circuit of heaven, and I walked in the depth of the abysses.
Over the waves of the sea, over all the earth, and over every people and nation I gained possession. After all this I sought a resting place: with whom should I take my rest?
Then the Creator of all things commanded me, and he who established my tent said to me: Dwell in Jacob, and make your home in Israel.
Before the ages he established me, and until the ages I shall not fail. And as a dwelling you/I served [?], and so I was established in Zion.
In the holy city likewise he gave me a home, and in Jerusalem was my authority. And I took root [?]
was cut out from the king [?] without the work of human hands,
struck the image on its feet of iron and clay and earthenware, and crushed them completely.
Then they were crushed together, the iron and the earthenware and the bronze and the gold, and they became like the dust of a threshing floor in summer.
And the force of the wind carried it away, and no place at all was found for them. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain
and filled the earth.
From among many [passages]: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit:
Now at the birth of Jesus Christ in Bethlehem of Judea,
in the days of King Herod, behold, magi came from the east to Jerusalem and said: Where is the newborn king of the Jews?
For we have seen his star in the east and have come to worship him.
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
And he gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them: Where is the Christ to be born?
And they said to him: In Bethlehem of Judea. For thus it is written by the prophet:
And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah, for from you shall come forth a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.
Then Herod secretly called the magi and learned from them the time of the star's appearing.
And he sent them to Bethlehem and said to them: Go and search carefully for the child, and when you find him, tell me, so that I too may come and worship him.
When they had heard this from the king, they set out, and behold, the star that they had seen in the east went before them,
until it came and stood over the cave where the child was. And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with very great joy.
And they came to the house and saw the child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshipped him. And they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense and myrrh.
And they received a command from angels in a vision not to return to Herod, but to go to their own country by another way.
And when they had gone, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a vision and said to him:
"Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod intends to kill the child and destroy him."
And he got up and took the child and his mother by night. They went to Egypt, and he stayed there until the death of Herod,
so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: "Out of Egypt I called my son."
When Herod saw that he had been mocked by the Magi, he became very angry. He sent men and killed all the children of Bethlehem and of all its region, from two years old and under,
according to the time that he had found out from the Magi. Then what had been spoken by the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled, where he says:
"A voice was heard in Ramah, of weeping and lamentation; Rachel was weeping for her children and would not be comforted, because they are no more."
But when Herod had died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a vision and said to him:
"Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for all those who were seeking the child's life have died."
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and came to his own land, to Jerusalem.
And when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod,
he was afraid to go there. He received a command from an angel in a vision and went away to the land of Galilee.
And there he settled in a city called Nazareth, so that what had been spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, that he would be called a Nazarene.
Remember David, O Lord: how the Lord swore:
He made salvation great for me. My God, your ways are blameless:
And all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said to him: "Behold, we are your bones [?] and your flesh.
In the past, while Saul was still king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought Israel in. And the Lord said to you:
'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be leader and ruler of Israel.'"
And the elders of Israel came to David at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the Lord, and there they anointed David as king over all Israel.
David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years over Judah.
He reigned seven years and six months in Jerusalem, and thirty-three years over all Jerusalem and Judah.
King David and all the people with him went against the Jebusite, who was settled [?] throughout all that land.
And David was told that the Jebusites were saying that David would not come in here, because the blind and the lame had risen up to attack him, and they were saying: "David shall not come in here."
And David arrived and took the stronghold of Zion, and said: "This is the city of David." And on that day David gave a command and said:
"Whoever strikes the Jebusite with the sword, let him go up against the blind and the lame and destroy them, those who hated David's soul."
For this reason they say as a proverb: "The blind and the lame shall not enter the house of the Lord."
And David settled in the stronghold and called it the city of David. And he built up the city around the hill, and within it he made his house.
And David went on advancing and growing great, and the Lord Almighty was with him.
After they had fallen silent, James answered and said to them: "Men, brothers, listen!
Simeon has related how God first looked favorably on the Gentiles, to take out from among them a people for his name.
And the words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written: 'After this I will return and rebuild the tent of David;
what has fallen of it I will raise up and rebuild, so that the rest of humankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles over whom my name has been called, says the Lord,
who has made all these things known from eternity.' Therefore I say that you should not put pressure on those from among the Gentiles who have turned to God,
but should instruct them to keep away from the pollution of idol sacrifices, from fornication, from adultery, and from blood.
For from the earliest generations Moses has had preachers in every city, who read him in the synagogues every Sabbath."
Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, together with the whole assembly, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas:
Judas, who was called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers. They wrote by their hand as follows:
"The apostles, the elders, and the brothers, to the brothers from among the Gentiles who are in Antioch and Cilicia: greetings.
For we have heard that some people from among us went out and troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying:
'Be circumcised and keep the Law,' which we did not command.
It seemed good to us, gathered together as one, rather to choose men to send to you with our beloved Paul and Barnabas, men
who have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. We have sent Judas and Silas, and they too will tell you everything by word of mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay no greater burden on you than this, which is necessary:
keep away from idol sacrifices, from blood, and from what is strangled. Keep yourselves from these things, do good, and farewell."
James [?] of our God:
I make known to you, brothers, the gospel that was preached to you by me,
that it is not human. I did not receive it or learn it from a human being, but through a revelation of Christ.
For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how I persecuted the churches of God beyond measure and plundered them.
And I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my own age, being far more zealous for the ancestral law of my fathers.
But when it pleased God, who set me apart from my mother's womb, that I should preach him among the Gentiles, I did not at once consult with flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went to Arabia and returned again to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
I saw none of the other apostles except James, the brother of the Lord.
And what I am saying, I say before the Lord: I am not lying.
The Lord swore to David — as far as "your":
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them, saying: "What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?"
They said to him: "David's." Jesus said to them: "How then does David call him Lord, saying: 'The Lord said to my Lord:
Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet'? If David calls him Lord, how is he his son?"
And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to ask him anything more.
Consecrated priests
The body of the Lord: the blood:
O glorious first martyr, soldier of the heavenly King.
Let them glory in you — as far as "[?] us": let them rejoice in you:
And Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit and of grace, and he worked great signs among the people in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Then some men arose from the synagogue called that of the Libertines and of the Alexandrians, and they disputed with Stephen.
And they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Holy Spirit with which he spoke.
Then they secretly induced some men, who said: "We have heard him speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God."
They stirred up the people and the elders and the rulers, and they came upon Stephen and brought him into their council.
And they set up false witnesses, who said: "This man does not cease speaking evil words against this holy and chosen place.
For we have heard him say that Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the law that Moses gave us."
Those who were standing there in the council gazed at him, and they saw his face as the face of an angel.
The high priest said to him: "Is this so?" And he said to him: "Men, brothers and fathers, listen to me!"
The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia of Assyria, before he settled in Haran.
And he said to him: "Go out from your land and come to the land that I will show you."
He went out from the land of the Chaldeans and dwelt in Haran.
After his father's death he settled in this land in which you are now settled.
And he gave him no inheritance in it, not even room to set his foot. But he promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his offspring after him, though he had no child.
God told him: "Your offspring will be strangers in a foreign land, and they will enslave them and mistreat them for four hundred years;
and I will judge the nation they serve," said the Lord, "and after that they will come out and serve me in this place."
And he gave him the law of circumcision. And he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day; and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered the twelve patriarchs.
But the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt; and God was with him.
And he rescued him from all his troubles and gave him wisdom and favour before the king of the Egyptians, and he made him ruler over Egypt and over all his house.
And there was a famine and great distress in Egypt and in the land of Canaan, and our fathers could find no food.
Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent our fathers there the first time.
And on the second journey Joseph made himself known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh's household.
Joseph sent and summoned his father Jacob and all his family, seventy-five souls.
And Israel went down to Egypt, and he died there, and so did our fathers;
and they were carried back and buried at Shechem, in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
And as the time of the promise that God had made to Abraham drew near, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
He oppressed our people and mistreated our fathers, and made them throw out their children so that they would not live.
And when Moses lay [? probably "was born"], he was [?] before the Lord, and he was raised for three months in his father's house.
And when they cast him out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and raised him as her own son.
And Moses was trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds.
And when he was reaching forty years of age, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
And he saw someone being wronged. He fought with the man who was harming him and took vengeance for the wronged man: he killed the Egyptian and covered him over with sand.
He supposed that his brothers would understand that God was giving them deliverance by his hand, but they did not understand.
Then again he saw some men who were fighting with each other. He tried to calm them and make peace, and said to them: "Men, you are brothers. Why are you harming each other?"
But the one who was harming his neighbour pushed him away and said: "Who made you ruler and judge over us?
Or do you want to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?"
At that word Moses fled. He lived as a stranger in the land of Midian, where two sons were born to him.
When forty years had passed, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire within a bush.
When Moses saw it, he marvelled at the sight. As he went closer to look, the voice of the Lord came to him and said:
"I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." And Moses trembled and did not dare to look.
The Lord said to him: "Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have indeed seen the affliction of my people, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come, and I will send you to Egypt."
This is the Moses whom they rejected, saying: "Who made you ruler and judge over us?"
This is the man God sent as ruler and deliverer, by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He led them out, and he performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel: "The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet from among your [?] own, like me. Listen to him."
This is the one who was with the people in the wilderness, together with the angel
who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. He received the words of life to give to you.
Your fathers refused to obey him. Instead they pushed him away, and in their hearts they turned back to the land of Egypt.
They said to Aaron: "Make us gods who will go before us. As for Moses, who brought us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
In that day they set up the calf and offered sacrifice to the idol, and they rejoiced in what their hands had made.
God turned them away and gave them over to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets:
"Was it to me that you offered slain beasts and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

And the chains fell from his hands. The angel said to Peter: "Put on your sandals."
And he did so, and the angel said to him: "Put on your garment and follow me." And Peter went out and followed him.
And Peter did not know that what the angel was doing was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.
And when they had passed the first guard and the second as well, they came to the iron gate that led into the city, which opened for them by itself.
And they went on and passed along one street, and at once the angel left him. And Peter came to himself and said:
"Now I know that God has truly sent his angel to me and rescued me from the hands of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting."

Therefore thus says the Lord:

So now, since we too have so great a multitude of holy martyrs standing around us,
let us put away every burden and the sin that comes on us so quickly, and let us run with endurance the contest set before us,
looking to Jesus, the leader and perfecter of our faith,
who, for the joy set before him, endured the cross, scorned its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the thrones of God.
Think about him who endured such things for the sake of us sinners, the opposition raised against him, so that you do not grow weary in your souls and lose heart.
You have not yet stood bravely against sin to the point of blood, and you have lost heart and turned away from the encouragement that speaks to you as to sons:
"My son, do not lose heart at the Lord's discipline, and do not give up when he rebukes you;
for the Lord disciplines those he loves, and he punishes every son whom he accepts."
Endure discipline, for God accepts you as sons. What son is there whom his father does not discipline?
If you are cut off from the discipline that everyone has shared in, then you are strangers and not sons.
Now, if we had earthly fathers to discipline us and we respected them, should we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
They disciplined us for a few days as they thought best, but he does it for our good, so that we may share in his holiness.
No discipline brings joy at the time it is given, only sorrow. Later, though, it produces the peaceful fruit of righteousness in those who have been trained by it.

For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Whoever serves Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people. Pursue peace and the building up of one another.
Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. Everything is clean, but it is wrong for a person who eats with doubt.
It is better not to eat meat or drink wine, or do anything by which your brother stumbles or is made to fall. Do you have faith?
Keep it to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself in what he approves.
But whoever doubts is condemned if he eats, because he does not eat from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

which has now been made manifest through the writings of the prophets and apostles, by the command of the eternal God, for the obedience of faith,

Or how can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when there is a beam lying in your own eye?
Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.

If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
So whatever you want people to do for you, do the same for them, for this is how the Law and the prophecy are fulfilled.
Enter through the narrow gate. For the gate is wide and the road is broad that leads to destruction, and many are those who go along it.
The other gate is narrow and the road hard that leads to life, and few are those who find it.

So every good tree brings forth good fruit, and a bad tree brings forth bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bring forth bitter fruit, nor can a bad tree bring forth good fruit.
Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore, by their fruits you will know them.

And it happened in the reign of Amraphel, king of Shinar; Arioch, king of Ellasar; Chedorlaomer, king of the Elamites; and Tidal, king of the nations.
They had come to make war against Bera, king of Sodom, and Birsha, king of Gomorrah, Shinab,
king of Admah, and Shemeber, king of Zeboiim, and King Barak [? = the king of Bela], that is, Zoar.
All these kings conspired together and gathered the people in the Salt Valley, and on the mountain, and at the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they had been subject to King Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled against him.
Now in the twelfth year King Chedorlaomer came, and the kings who were with him,
and they slaughtered the giants in Ashteroth and in Karnaim, and they wiped out the strong people together with them, and the Emim, who were of the city of Shaveh,
and the Horites, who were in Mount Seir, as far as the border of Bilekom [?], which lies in the desert of Paran.

And there they slew the rulers of the Amalekites and of the Amorites who dwelt in Hazazon-tamar.
Now the king of the Sodomites went out, and the king of the Admahites, and the king of the Zeboiimites, and Barak king of the Zoarites.
They drew up in battle order and made ready to fight those kings in the valley of Adaots:
Chedorlaomer king of the Elamites, and Thargal king of the nations, and Arioch king of the Serahites, these four kings, these potentates, against the five potentates.
And the valley of Adaots had pit after pit and pool after pool; that is, it was full of bitumen and pitch.
The kings of the Sodomites and of the Gomorrites fled and were scattered, and they fell into the pools, and those who were left fled toward the mountain.
The kings advanced, carried off and plundered the mountain region and the whole race of the Sodomites, and they carried off as booty all their wealth and livestock and all their possessions.
They also took captive Lot, Abraham's nephew, and all his goods and possessions, and departed.
And one crying out the alarm came to Abraham at the oak beyond Mamre. He was one of the brothers of Eshcol and of Aner, who were Abraham's sworn allies.
As soon as Abraham heard that Lot his nephew had been taken captive, he rose up at once,
and gave orders to the trained sons, his own servants, and pursued the track of those kings with three hundred and eighteen [?].
And the chief himself, with his servants, fell upon those potentates by night, struck them down and slew them.
And he named that plain the Plain of the Potentates, and he put those who were left of them to flight as far as Hobah, which is to the left of Damascus.
And he brought back all the captured herds and all the possessions of the Sodomites and the Gomorrites, and Lot,
his nephew, he brought back with all the plunder, and the wealth and possessions, and their wives and all their people.
When he came and reached the valley of Shaveh, the king of the Gomorrites came out to meet him, as he was returning and coming back after the slaughter of the kings.
He met him at the Plain of the Potentates, and Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine to meet him. He was a priest of God Most High.
And Melchizedek blessed Abraham and said: "Blessed be Abraham by God Most High, who made the heavens and the earth."
"Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies under your feet."
And Abraham took a tenth of all the plunder and gave it to Melchizedek. And the king of the Sodomites said to Abraham:
"Give me only the people from that plunder; and all those herds of [?], and the wealth and goods that you have gathered, let all of it be yours."
And Abraham said to the king of the Sodomites: "I lift up my hands to the Lord God Most High, who made the heavens and the earth,
that from a cut thread to a sandal-strap I will take nothing of all this that you have offered me, so that you may not say tomorrow:
'I made Abraham rich.' Except only what these [?] (young men?) have eaten, and the share of these my companions: Aner and Eshcol and Mamre."
Only let these take their share from you, and let them go.

who is the offspring of a foreigner, who is not of your offspring."
"The house-born servant of your house and everyone acquired with silver shall be circumcised. And my covenant shall be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant."
"And every male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people, for he has broken my covenant."
And the Lord God said to Abraham: "As for Sarai your wife, her name shall no longer be called Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name."
"I will bless her and give you a son by her. And she shall become a great nation, and kings shall come forth from her offspring."
And Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and spoke in his heart and said: "Will a man a hundred years old have a son? And will Sarah, at eighty years old, give birth?"
And the Lord God said to Abraham: "Behold, Sarah will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac."
"And I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his offspring after him."
The word of the Lord came in the third year:
To you belongs praise in song. But you, O Lord, do not take your mercy away from me.
Receive me. Blessed is the one who considers the poor:
Abraham set out and went toward the west,
and he came and settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he lived there as a stranger in the land of the people of Gerar.
And Abraham said of his wife, "She is my sister." Abimelech, king of the people of Gerar, sent and took Sarah to be his own wife.
God appeared to Abimelech in a vision of the night and said to him:
"Know that you will die because of the woman you have taken as your wife, for she has a husband of her own over her.
Turn away from this intention, Abimelech." And Abimelech said to God, "Lord God, will you destroy a nation that acted in ignorance and in righteousness?
Did Abraham himself not say, 'She is my sister'? And did the woman herself not say, 'He is my brother'?
And I took her as my wife with a pure heart and righteous hands."
God said to him, "I also know that you did this with a pure heart, and I had mercy on you, so that you would not sin before me by touching that woman.
Now give the woman back to her own husband, for that man is a prophet.
If you keep her, know that you will perish, along with everything in your house."
King Abimelech rose early in the morning, called his servants and told them all these words;
they were all very much afraid and humbled themselves before the Lord God. Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, "What is this thing you have done to us?
Did we sin against you in any way, that you brought a great sin upon me and upon my kingdom?
You have done to us a thing that no one has ever done." And Abimelech said to Abraham, "Tell me, why did you do this?"
Abraham answered and said, "I suspected in my heart that this land belonged to heathens, and that they would kill me and take my wife.
But in truth [?] she is also my sister, by my father and not by my mother, and now she is my wife.
And when God brought me out of my father's house, I said to this woman:
'Keep this righteousness for my sake: in every place we enter, say there,
"He is my brother," so that they will not look upon your beauty and kill me.'"
When Abimelech heard this, he took a thousand staters, double silver [?], sheep and oxen, and a great many male and female servants. He gave back [?] the woman and gave them to Abraham, her husband.
And King Abimelech said to Abraham, "Behold, this land of mine lies before you; settle wherever you wish."
And to Sarah he said: "Look, I have given your husband a thousand double satirs of silver. Let it be an honour to you, for that face of yours,
for my eyes desire you [?]. And whatever else may be yours, I have given to those who are with you. From now on be a speaker of the truth, Abraham."
And Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, Abimelech's wife, and his male and female servants. And then they began to bear children.
For every man had been held back from his natural function, and every womb of their women, in the whole house of Abimelech, had been closed because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
And the Lord God visited Sarah as he had said; the Lord God did for Sarah as he had promised.
And Sarah conceived and bore a child for Abraham in the days of his old age, at the time the Lord God had spoken of. And Abraham named his son Isaac.
And Abraham took his son Isaac on the eighth day and circumcised him, as the Lord God had commanded him. And Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac was born to him.
And Sarah said: "Truly God has made me a laughingstock, for whoever hears of it will rejoice and laugh at me. And they will say to me:
'Who would have told Abraham that I would give birth in my old age and that a child would be at my breast?'"
The child grew, and Abraham held a great feast on the day his son Isaac was weaned.
Can it be that the hand of the Lord is not able?
By the grace of the Saviour:
But I, in the abundance of mercy: … your house. Hear my words:
And after those days, Abraham began to speak to his chief servant,
who was in charge of his whole house, and said to him: "Bring your hand to me and place it on my thighs,
and swear to me by the Lord God of heaven and earth that you will bring [?] a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living.
Rather, you shall go to the land of my inheritance, from which I came out. Go to the kin of my tribe and bring a wife for Isaac my son."
And the steward said to him: "Lord, I understand completely whatever you command me,
but this is what I am considering: if I go at your command, and the woman does not want to come with me to this land,
shall I take your son back to the land from which you came out?" Abraham said to him: "Take care that you do not take my son back there.
And may it not be pleasing to the Lord God of the heavens and the earth, who brought me out of my father's house, out of the land of my inheritance;
and he swore to me and said to me: 'To you I will give this land, and to your descendants.'
But the Lord himself will send his angel before you and make your ways straight, and you shall bring a wife for my son Isaac.
And if the woman is not willing to come after you to this land, you will be free of this oath; only do not take this child of mine there."
And the steward placed his hand on his lord's thighs and swore to him concerning this matter.
And he loaded ten camels from his master's camels, and took with him some of all his master's goods. And he arose and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor of the Assyrians.
And he arrived at a certain place and made his camels lie down outside that city, before a well of water, in the evening, at the very hour when the women who draw water come out of the city.
He began to speak and make a vow in his heart. He prayed to God and said:
"O Lord, God of my master Abraham, prosper this journey of mine today, and show mercy to my master."
"And now I have arrived, and I am standing by this water. The daughters of the households of this city will come out, and they will come with the water-drawers of this city.
"And let it be this way: I will say to one of them, to a maiden, 'Lower your pitcher and give me a drink,' and she will say to me at once:

'Drink, and I will water your camels too until they have had enough.' Then let me know that you have prepared her for your servant Isaac, and by this I will understand that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham."
These words were still in his mouth when at once Rebecca came, the daughter of Bethuel, the granddaughter of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother.
And she was very beautiful of face. She was a virgin; she had not known a man. She came and reached the spring and filled her pitcher.
Abraham's steward went to meet her and said to her, "Give me a little of that water to drink."
And the girl said, "Drink, lord, and I will also give your camels a drink." And she hurried at once and lowered her pitcher and gave him a drink.
And she emptied the jug into the trough and began to draw water, and she gave all the camels a drink.
And the man watched, and he marveled first at the girl's appearance and then at the words she had spoken.
And he pondered in his heart and said to himself, "Has God prospered his way or not?"
And when the camels had had enough, the steward came at once and untied his goods and took out golden earrings, each weighing a double stater.
And he took bracelets weighing ten litrai and put them on her arms. Then he began to question her and said, "Whose child are you?
Is there a place to lodge in your house?" And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
And there is plenty of fodder for the [?] beasts in our house, and the place is also roomy for lodging."
And the man was pleased in his heart, and he bowed down and worshipped the Lord God and said:
"Blessed is the Lord God of my master Abraham, who has not let his righteousness and truth come to nothing, and has guided me to the house of my master's brother."
And the girl ran and told the people in her mother's house what the man had said. And Rebecca had a brother whose name was Laban.
She still had the earrings and the bracelets on, and he heard the words his sister Rebecca was saying, for she said:
"This is what he said to me." Then the man [Laban] himself ran out to the spring to meet him and speak with him, [to learn] who the man was or what he was saying.
And when Laban came to the spring, he saw the man, for he had dismounted and was standing by the camels at the water troughs.
And he said to him, "Come inside with us. I came for you, blessed of God! Why do you stand outside?"
I have prepared a house for you and a place for the camels. And when Abraham's steward went into Laban's dwellings,
he unloaded the camels, and they spread out straw and fodder for them. They brought water to wash his feet and the feet of the young men who were with him. And they set a table for them.
And the steward stood up and said to them: "It is not right for me to put my hand to bread before I have spoken the words that are set in my heart."
And they said: "Speak calmly." He began to speak and said: "I am Abraham's servant.
And the Lord God has blessed my master greatly and given him a great deal of livestock: sheep and cattle, gold and silver, male and female servants, and camels.
And Sarah his wife bore my master a son in his old age, and he has given that boy everything that he has.
And he made me swear and said to me: 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live as a sojourner in their land.
Instead, you shall arise and go to my father's house and take a wife for my son Isaac.'
Now if you are willing to deal truly with my master, tell me. If it is otherwise, let me know that too, so that I may turn either to the right or to the left."
Laban and Bethuel answered and said to him: "This command has come from the Lord, and we cannot give you a harsh answer, or anything but a good one.
Here is Rebekah before you. Go, and take her with you. Let her be a wife to your master's son."
And when Abraham's steward heard these words, he opened his treasures and brought out gold and precious silver and gave them to Rebekah. He also brought gifts to her brother and her mother.
They ate and drank, together with all who were with them, and they rested that night.
And when they rose in the morning, he said to them: "Let me go to my master, and do not detain me."
So they sent off their sister Rebekah with her property, along with the steward and his male and female servants.
And they blessed their sister Rebekah and said to her: "Our sister, may you become nations and tens of thousands, and may your offspring possess the cities of your enemies."
Rebekah and her [?] (perhaps attendants) arose. They were seated on the camels and went with the man. And the steward took Rebekah, and they departed.
And Isaac had gone out in the evening to take his ease near the [?] of water (literally "body of water"), for he was living in the east.
He lifted up his eyes and saw camels coming. Rebekah looked, saw Isaac, and quickly got down from the camel.
And she said to the steward: "Who is that man walking in the field?" And he said: "That is my master."
And she immediately took a [?] (probably a veil) and covered herself. And the steward told him all the things that had happened.
Isaac came and went into the house of his mother Sarah, and he took Rebekah as his wife. She became his wife, and he loved her.
The Lord has sworn by his holiness and said:
"Behold, days are coming upon you when they will carry you off with their weapons, and those who are with you they will throw into red-hot cauldrons.
And they will lead you out naked, fathers and mothers, each meeting the other face to face [?], and they will cast you out onto the mountains of Remman," said the Lord.
You went into Bethel and transgressed at Gilgal, and you multiplied ungodliness, and you brought and offered your offerings [?] in the morning and your tithes every three days.
And they read the law outside and called out with confession. Proclaim it, for this is how the sons of Israel loved it, says the Lord.
I will give you aching teeth in all your cities and a shortage of bread in all your places, and even so you did not turn back, says the Lord.
And I held back the rain from you for three months before the grape harvest. On one city I will not send rain; one part will be rained on, and one part will not be rained on.
And the part that is not rained on will dry up, says the Lord.
And two and three gathered into one city to drink water, and they were not satisfied, and even so you did not turn back to me, says the Lord.
And I struck you with scorching heat, and even so you did not turn back to me, says the Lord.
And you multiplied your lawlessness, and the caterpillar ate your vineyards, your fig orchards and your olive groves, and even so you did not turn back, says the Lord.
And I sent death on your land. I killed your young men with the sword and led you away captive before the feet of horses, and I judged your camp with fire and with my wrath.
And even so you did not turn back to me, says the Lord. And I overthrew you as Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown, and you became like a single firebrand snatched out of the fire.
Even so you did not turn back to me, says the Lord. Therefore this is what the Lord says to you: Israel, prepare yourself to call on the name of your God.
For see, here he is, the one who made the thunder firm and created the winds, who announces his anointed one among people,
who makes the dawn shine out, sets the mist in place and strides over the depths of the earth. The Lord God Almighty is his name.
Hear the word of the Lord, which I take up against you. The house of Israel will take up a lament.
The cities of the house of Israel have fallen and been shattered, and there will be no one to raise it up.
This is what the Lord says: of the city from which a thousand went out, a hundred will remain; and of the city from which a hundred went out, ten will remain there, for the house of Israel.
For the Lord has heard the sound of weeping from me. Lord, not in anger.
And it happened in those days that the camps of the Philistines gathered to fight against Israel.
And Achish said to David, "Know for certain that you will go out to battle with me, and your men with you."
And David said to Achish, "Now you will learn what your servant will do for you."
And Achish said to David, "Then I will make you my bodyguard and chief for all time."
Samuel died, and all Israel mourned for him, and they buried him in Armathaim [Ramah], his own city.
And Saul had removed all the mediums and wizards. And the Philistines gathered and camped at Shunem.
And Saul and all the men of Israel gathered and camped at Gilboa. And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was very afraid, and his heart trembled.
And Saul asked the Lord for guidance, and the Lord gave him no answer, whether through dreams, through revelations or through prophets.
And Saul said to his servants, "Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and inquire of her."
And his servants said to him, "Behold, there is a woman who is a medium in Endor." And Saul changed his clothing and put on other clothing.
And Saul went, and two of his servants with him, and they came to the woman by night.
And Saul said to her, "Divine for me by your mediumship, and bring up for me the one whom I tell you." And the woman said to him, "Do you know what Saul did?
How he destroyed the mediums and those who have knowledge from the earth? So why are you setting a snare for my life?"
And Saul swore to her and said, "As the Lord lives, no harm shall befall you over this matter." And the woman said, "Whom shall I bring up for you?"
And Saul said, "Bring up Samuel for me." And the woman saw Samuel, and she cried out with a loud voice and said, "Why have you deceived me?
You are Saul." And Saul said, "Do not be afraid; tell me what you saw." And the woman said to Saul, "I saw gods coming up out of the earth."
And Saul said to the woman, "What did you perceive?" She said to Saul, "A tall, upright man is coming up out of the earth, and he is wrapped in a double cloak."
And Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and did obeisance to him.
And Samuel said, "Why have you troubled me by making me come up?" And Saul said, "I am in great distress, and the Philistines are fighting against me,
and God has departed from me and no longer listens to me, neither by the hand of the prophets, nor in dreams, nor by revelation; and now I have called you, so that you may tell me what I should do."
And Samuel said to him, "Why do you ask me? For the Lord has departed from you and is with your neighbor.
And he has done just as he spoke by my hand: the Lord has torn your kingdom out of your hand and has given it to your neighbor David.
For you did not listen to the voice of the Lord and did not carry out the fury of his wrath upon Amalek; because of this matter the Lord God has done this to you.

And on this day the Lord will give Israel with you into the hands of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your son Jonathan [will be with me?], and the Lord will give the camp of Israel into the hands of the Philistines." [The verb governing "you and your son Jonathan" is unclear in the text: literally "and tomorrow you and your son Jonathan and the camp of Israel the Lord will give into the hands of the Philistines."]

And Saul, from where he stood, [fell] upon the ground [?], and was greatly afraid because of the words that Samuel had spoken to him, and there was no more strength in him, for he had eaten no bread that day, all day long.
And the woman came in and saw that Saul was faint, and she said to him,
"Behold, your maidservant has listened to your voice; I took my life in my hands and listened to your words,
which you spoke to me. Now listen to the voice of your maidservant: let me set bread before you, and eat, so that you may have strength, for you are going on a journey."
And he did not want to eat, and his servants urged him. Then he listened to their words, and he rose up from the ground and sat on the seat.
Now the woman had a calf in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it, and took flour and kneaded it and made it into unleavened bread.
And she brought it before Saul and his servants; and they ate, and rose up, and went away that night.
And the Philistines gathered all their camp at Aphek; and Israel encamped at Nain of Jezreel.
And the lords of the Philistines marched on by hundreds and by thousands. And David and his men marched in the rear with Achish.
And the rulers and commanders of the Philistines said, "Who are these men who are passing by?"
And Achish said to the rulers of the Philistines, "This is David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who came over to me."
"This is now the second year, and I have found no fault in him, not even one, from the day he came over to me until now."
And the rulers of the Philistines were angry with him and said to Achish, "Send those men back, and let them go to their own place, where you have stationed them there,
"and let them not come with us to battle, so that he may not become a plotter of evil against our camp and make his peace with his lord with the heads of these men.
"Is this not David, of whom the dancers sang praises, saying, 'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
And Achish called David and said to him, "As the Lord lives, you are upright and good in my eyes, your going out and your coming in with me in this camp,
"and I have found no blemish in you from the time you came to me until this very day; but in the eyes of the Philistines you do not appear good.
"So now turn back and go in peace, and do nothing evil before these rulers of the Philistines." And David said to Achish,
"What have I done to you, or what evil have you found in your servant from the time I have been before you until now, that I should not come and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
Achish answered and said to David, "I know that you are pleasing in my eyes, like an angel of God, but these commanders of the Philistines say, 'He must not come with us.'
"So now rise early in the morning, you and your young men who are with you, and go away from this place, and do not take the evil word to heart.
"Rise early for your journey, and when it has dawned for you [go]." And David and his men rose early in the morning to guard that land, and the Philistines were fighting against Israel.
And the people of Israel fled before the Philistines, and many wounded fell on Mount Gilboa.
And the Philistines pressed hard upon Saul and his sons, and they struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Melchishua, the sons of Saul.
And the battle grew heavy against Saul. And the archers found him, and they wounded him below the ribs.
And Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, lest the Philistines come and kill me and mock me."
But the armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. And Saul took his own sword and fell upon it.
And when the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell upon his own sword and died with him.
So Saul died, and his three sons and his armor-bearer, on that day, and all the men together.
And when the men of Israel who were on the other side of the valley and beyond the Jordan saw
that the people of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled.
And the Philistines came and settled [?] in them. And it happened on the next day that the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
And they cut off their heads and stripped them, and carried away their armor, and took it to the land of the Philistines, and they proclaimed the good news to their idols and to their people.
And they brought Saul's armor into the temple of Astarte, and they fastened his body to the walls of Beth-shan.
The inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the foreigners had done to Saul and his sons.
All the strong men rose up by night, went, and took the bodies of Saul and of his son Jonathan from the wall of Beth-shan. They brought them to Jabesh [?] and burned them with fire.
They took their bones and buried them in the land of Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days.
After Saul's death, David had returned from slaughtering the Amalekites, and David stayed in Ziklag for two days.
On the third day a man came from the camp, from the army that had been with Saul. His clothes were torn and he had earth thrown on his head.
He came before David, fell on his face on the ground, and bowed down to him. David said to him, "Where have you come from?"
He said, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel." David said to him, "What has happened? Tell me." And he said:
"The army fled from the battle, from the camp. The commanders of the army have fallen, and Saul and his son Jonathan have perished."
David said to the man who was bringing him the news, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"
The man said, "I happened by chance onto Mount Gilboa, and Saul was leaning on his sword, and the chariots and the commanders were closing in on him.
He turned around, saw me, and called me. He said to me, 'Who are you?'
I said, 'I am an Amalekite.' He said to me, 'Stand over me and kill me, for a terrible darkness has seized me, and my life is still in me.'
So I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he could not live after his fall.
I took the crown from his head and the bracelets that were on his arms, and I have brought them to my lord."
When David heard this, he took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
They wept, mourned, and fasted until evening for Saul, for his son Jonathan, for the people of Israel, and for the house of Judah, because they had fallen by the sword.
David said to the man who had brought him the news, "Where are you from?" He said to him, "I am the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite."
David said to him, "How were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the Lord's anointed?"
David called one of his servants and said, "Bring him here and fall upon him." They struck him and threw him down dead on the ground.
David said to him, "Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth said, 'I killed the Lord's anointed.'"
David sang this lament over Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the house of Israel.
Blow the trumpet in Zion, appoint a fast, proclaim a healing.
Gather the people, sanctify the assemblies, bring in the elders, gather the nursing infants, [?]. Let the bridegroom come out of his chamber and the bride out of her courtyard.
Between the steps of the altar, weep, you priests and ministers of the Lord, and say:
"Spare your people, O Lord, and do not hand your inheritance over to shame and reproach, so that the nations do not rule over them and do not say, 'Where is their God?'"
And God was jealous for his land and had mercy on his people.
From tomorrow it is necessary [?]
Christ the King, by his own authority:
Have mercy on me, O Lord, for to you [?]: for great is [your] mercy.
O Lord, your mercy is forever: stretch out your hand to me:
And a hand was upon me [?]
At that time Michael, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people, will arise;
and there will be a time of distress, such distress as has not been since there was a nation until that time;
and at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book of the living.
And many who had been sleeping in the earth, in the dust, will arise, these to eternal life and some to reproach and eternal shame.
But those who understand will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and many of the righteous like the stars of heaven, forever and ever.
If Christ is preached
as raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised either.
If Christ has not been raised, this preaching of ours is in vain, and that faith of yours is in vain.
We are found, then, to be false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise.
If the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either. If Christ has not been raised, that faith of yours is futile; you are still in your sins.
Then have those who fell asleep in Christ perished? If in this life we have hope in Christ, we are more to be pitied than all people.
But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the first of those who have fallen asleep. For death came through a man, and through a man the resurrection of the dead.
Just as all die because of Adam, so also all will be made alive through Christ.
But each in his own order: Christ first, then those who belong to Christ at his coming.
Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he has abolished every rule and every authority and power.
For he must reign until he has put his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be abolished is death. For he has put all things in subjection under his feet;
when it says that all things have been put in subjection, it is clear that this excludes the one who put all things in subjection to him.
Then the Son himself will also be subject to the one who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all.
Or why are we in hardship every hour? We die day by day. I swear by my boasting in you, which I have through Christ Jesus our Lord.
If I fought with wild beasts at Ephesus in a merely human way, what profit is it to me, if the dead are not raised?
Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die! Do not be deceived: evil talk corrupts good minds.
Wake up and live righteously, and do not sin. Some do not know God. I say this to your shame. I say this to your shame:
If someone says, "How are the dead raised?" If someone says, "How are the dead raised?"
Or with what kind of body will they come? Fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
And what you sow is not the body that is to be. What you sow is a bare grain, perhaps of wheat or of some other seed.
But God gives it a body as he wills, and to each seed its own body.
Not all flesh is the same flesh. Human flesh is one kind, the flesh of birds is another, and the flesh of fish is another.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. The glory of the heavenly is one kind, and the glory of the earthly is another.
The glory of the sun is one kind, the glory of the moon is another, and the glory of the stars is another.
For as one star surpasses another star in glory, so it is with the resurrection of the dead:
It is sown in corruption and is raised in incorruption. It is sown in dishonour and is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness and is raised in power.
A natural body is sown, and a spiritual body is raised. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
So also Scripture says: "The first man, Adam, became a living soul," but the second Adam became a life-giving spirit.
The spiritual does not come first. The natural comes first, and only then the spiritual. The first man was from the earth, made of dust. The second man is from heaven, spiritual.
Those who are of the dust are like the one made of dust, and those who are of heaven are like the one from heaven.
And as we have put on the image of the one made of dust, we shall also put on the image of the one from heaven.
I say this, brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, and corruption does not inherit incorruption.
Look, I tell you a mystery: we shall all fall asleep, but we shall not all be changed.
In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet, the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
For this corruptible body must put on incorruption, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
When this mortal body has put on immortality, then the saying that is written will be fulfilled: "Death is swallowed up in victory."
"O death, where is your sting? O hell, where is your victory?" For the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who has given us the law by the hand of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable, always increasing in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
I make known to you, brothers
I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, about those who have fallen asleep, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.
If we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so too God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep in Jesus.
For this we declare to you by the word of God: that we who are alive, who are left until the coming of the Lord, will not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep.
For the Lord himself will come down from heaven with a command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first.
And then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so from then on we will be with the Lord forever.
Comfort one another with these words.
Blessed is he who has understanding. To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul, into your hands.
At that time some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection of the dead, came to him and asked him, saying: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us thus:
if someone's brother dies, having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers among us. The first took a wife and died childless.
And the second, and the third, and so on up to the seventh, and they left no child. And after them the woman died.
Now then, in the resurrection of the dead, whose wife will she be of them? For all seven had her."
Jesus answered them and said: "The children of this world marry and are given in marriage;
but those who are counted worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage,
nor can they die any more, for they are equal to the angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
But that the dead are raised, even Moses made known at the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
For God is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all are alive before him."
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever hears my words and keeps them and believes him who sent me
has eternal life, and he will not come into judgment, but he passes from death to life.
Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the word of God, and those who hear will live.
Just as the Father has life in himself, so too he has granted the Son to have life in himself.
And he has given him authority also to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man.
Do not marvel at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice.
And they will come out: those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing of myself; as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of my Father who sent me.
I am the bread of life, which [?] so that he may live forever:
through the transgression of the commandment. Who [?] the all-holy temple of the heavens.
O God, doer of good and of countless mercy: the light which came down from heaven:
Pray and give glory to the Lord: he is made known in Judea:
Hear wisdom and become knowing, and do not stumble.
Blessed is the man who listens to me, and the son of man who keeps my ways, who keeps watch before my gates and guards the thresholds of my entrances.
For my ways out are the ways out of life, and the will of the Lord is fulfilled.
But those who sin against me act lawlessly against their own souls, and those who hate me love death.
Thus says the Lord Almighty:
Just as I resolved to do evil to you because your fathers provoked me to anger, says the Lord Almighty,
and they did not repent, so now I am ready and resolve in those days to do good to Israel and to the house of Judah; do not be afraid!
These are the things you shall do: let each of you speak the truth to his neighbor, and judge with true judgment in your gates;
and let none of you hold evil against his brother in your heart, and do not love false oaths, for I hate all these things, says the Lord Almighty.
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty:
The fourth fast and the seventh fast and the tenth fast shall become joy and gladness and feasts, good gladness, and they shall rejoice;
and let them love peace and truth, says the Lord Almighty.
Thus says the Lord: Now cry out with a loud voice and do not keep silent;
and declare to my people their sins, and tell Jacob his iniquities.
They seek me day after day, and their heart longs to know my ways, like a people that has done righteousness and has not forsaken the judgment of its God.
Now they ask me for righteous judgment and long to draw near to God, and they say:
Why is it that we fasted and you did not see? We humbled our souls and you did not take notice?
Because in the days of your fasting, when you were fasting, your own will is found carried out, and you oppressed all the [?] (possibly 'weak') who are under your authority.
Or you fast for the sake of judgment and quarrelling, and you strike your neighbour hard with your fists.
So now I have no need of such fasting, or of your coming and crying out before me, that I should listen to you.
For this is not the fast that I have chosen, nor the kind of humility people show when they bend their knees to be seen by others;
and now, even if you bend your neck like a hoop, put on sackcloth and spread ashes under you, I will still not count it as a fast, or as a day pleasing to the Lord.
I have not chosen such a fast, says the Lord. This is what is pleasing in my sight:
First, untie the knot of your heart and put away all falsehood. Set the prisoners free without taking a bribe, and tear up every document written in falsehood.
Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him, and do not neglect your own kin.
Only when you have done all this will your light break forth early, and your healing spring up quickly. Righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will surround you.
When you cry out, God will hear you, and before you even ask he will say to you, 'Here I am.'

If you put away from yourself false binding, the shameless raising of the hand and words of grumbling, and give bread to the hungry with an open heart, then light will shine out for you in the darkness, as at noon.
Your Lord will be with you always. You will be satisfied as your soul has desired, and your bones will be made fat,
and you will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose water never fails.
Your ancient cities will be rebuilt, and your dwellings will last forever, from generation to generation. You will be called the builder of your walls, and among your places light will go before you.
If you turn your foot away from the sabbaths so as not to do your own will on that holy day, and call the sabbaths a holy day, delightful and glorious to God,
your foot will not go out to work, and your mouth will not speak harsh words.
You will trust in the Lord your God. He will bring you into that good land and feed you with the portion of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
For now is the acceptable time; now is the day of salvation.
Give no one any cause to stumble in anything, so that the ministry may not be blamed. Instead, in everything commend yourselves as servants of God:
in great endurance, in afflictions, in sorrows, in hardships, in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in sleepless nights, in fastings, in purity,
in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love, in the word of truth, in the power of God,
