with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and for the left, through glory and dishonour, through blame and praise; as deceivers, and yet true;
as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as punished, and yet not killed;
as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
Take heed, my people.
Take care not to do your charitable deeds before others in order to be seen by them;
Otherwise you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
But when you do your acts of charity, do not proclaim it before you, as the hypocrites do in their synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be praised by people.
Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward. But when you do your acts of charity, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your charity may be in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will reward you openly.
And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, so that they may be seen by people.
Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward. But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret;
and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will reward you openly.
And when you pray, do not say many words, as the Gentiles do, for they think that they will be heard because of their many words.
Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward. But do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask.
But pray like this: Our Father, who are in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
Give us today our continual bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors,
and do not lead us into temptation, O Lord, but deliver us from evil, for yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, to the ages.
Amen. If you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will forgive you your trespasses.
If you do not forgive people their trespasses, neither will your heavenly Father forgive you your trespasses.
And when you fast, do not be like the hypocrites, gloomy, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people as fasting.
Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward. But when you fast, anoint your head with oil and wash your face,
so that you may not appear to people as fasting, but to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will reward you openly.
Do not store up your treasure on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal.
But store up your treasure in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not dig through and steal.
For where your treasures are, there also will your hearts be. The lamp of the body is the eye.
If your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. If the light that is in you is darkness, how great then is the darkness!
No one can serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other.
No one can serve God and mammon. Therefore I say to you: do not be anxious for your life, what we shall eat or what we shall drink;
nor for your body, what we shall wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow, they do not reap, and they do not gather into storehouses, and your heavenly Father feeds them.
Are you not better than the birds? Which of you can add a single cubit to his stature by worrying?
And why do you worry about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field and how they grow! They neither sow nor toil.
But I tell you: not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God clothes the grass of the field this way, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven to burn, will he not clothe you much more, you of little faith?
So do not worry and say, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?'
For the gentiles seek all these things, and your Father knows what you need of all these things.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
Let us begin, O peoples, the immaculate
We who, in the mystery of the cherubim
Let us put away the works of darkness, and
Let us hasten, O peoples, to the foreordination [?]:
In the time of favor: of your [?]. Hear me, O Lord, for your mercy is sweet:
Spiritual brothers, let us take up:
And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and said: I have gained a man through God.
And then she bore again: she bore his brother Abel. Abel was a shepherd of sheep, and Cain worked the ground.
And after those days Cain brought some of the fruits of the ground as a sacrifice to the Lord.
And Abel too brought some of the firstborn of his sheep and some of their fat. And God looked upon Abel and his sacrifices.
But God did not look upon Cain and his sacrifices. And Cain was greatly grieved, and his face fell.
And the Lord God said to Cain: Why have you become grieved, and why has your face fallen?
If you did not offer rightly and did not act rightly, you have sinned; be still. Its turning will be toward you, and you will rule over it.
And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go out into the field. And when they had gone out into the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.
And the Lord God said to Cain: Where is Abel your brother? And he said: I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?
And the Lord said to him: What is this you have done? The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me on the earth, and you think you can hide from me.
Cursed are you on the earth, which opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hands.
For you will work the ground, and it will no longer give its strength to you. And you will be on the earth groaning and trembling.
And Cain said to the Lord God: "Is my guilt too great to be forgiven?"
"If you drive me out from the face of the earth, I shall also be hidden from your face, and I shall be groaning and trembling on the earth."
"And will it be that whoever finds me will kill me?" And the Lord God said to him: "Not so."
"Whoever kills Cain shall receive sevenfold vengeance." And the Lord God set a sign, so that no one who found him would kill him.
And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord God and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
And Cain knew his wife; she conceived and bore Enoch. And he built a city and named the city after his son, Enoch.
And Enoch begot Gaidad (Irad), and Gaidad begot Malel, and Malel begot Methuselah, and Methuselah begot Lamech.
And Lamech took two wives; one was named Adah and the other Zillah. And Adah bore Jobel (Jabal).
He was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock. And his brother's name was Jobel (Jubal). He was the one who first brought forth the harp and the lyre.
And Zillah also bore Thobel (Tubal). He was a hammer-smith, a worker in iron and bronze; and Thobel's sister was Noema (Naamah).
Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah: "Hear my voice, you wives of Lamech, and listen to my words.
For I have killed a man to my wounding, and a young man to my bruising.
For if Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-seven times sevenfold."
Adam knew Eve his wife; she conceived and bore a son and named him Seth, saying: "For God has raised up for me offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed."
And a son was born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. He hoped to call on the name of the Lord God.
This is the book of the generations of humankind, on the day when Adam was created in the image of God.
He was created male and female, and He called his name Adam on the day He created him.
Adam lived two hundred and thirty years and begot a son in his own likeness and after his image, and named him Seth.
And the days of Adam after he begot Seth were seven hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters.
And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died. Seth lived two hundred and five years and begot Enosh.
And Seth lived after he begot Enosh seven hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died. Enosh lived one hundred and ninety years and begot Cainan.
And Enosh lived after he begot Cainan seven hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died. Cainan lived one hundred and seventy years and begot Mahalalel.
And Cainan lived after he begot Mahalalel seven hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters.
And all the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died. Mahalalel lived one hundred and sixty-five years and fathered Jared.
And after the birth of Jared, Mahalalel lived seven hundred and thirty years and had sons and daughters.
And all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he had sons and daughters.
Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years and fathered Enoch. And after the birth of Enoch, Jared lived eight hundred years and had sons and daughters.
And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died. Enoch lived one hundred and sixty-five years and fathered Methuselah.
And after the birth of Methuselah, Enoch was pleasing to God, and he lived two hundred years and had sons and daughters.
And all the days of Enoch were eight hundred and sixty-five years.
And Enoch was pleasing to God, and he was not found, for God took him away. Methuselah lived one hundred and sixty-seven years and fathered Lamech.
And after the birth of Lamech, Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two years and had sons and daughters.
And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.
Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-eight years and fathered a son. And he named him Noah and said:
"This one will give us rest from our works and from the toil of our hands, and from the ground which the Lord God has cursed."
And after the birth of Noah, Lamech lived five hundred and sixty-five years and had sons and daughters.
And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred and fifty-three years, and he died. Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it came about, when people began to multiply on the earth, that daughters were born to them.
And the sons of God saw the daughters of men, that they were beautiful, and they took for themselves as wives any of them they chose.
And God said: "My spirit shall not remain in these people, for they are flesh; let their days be one hundred and ten years."

Now the giants were on the earth in those days, and afterwards too, when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men and they bore children by them. These were the giants of old, the men of renown.
And the Lord God saw that their wickedness had multiplied on the earth, and that everyone was carefully devising evil in his heart every day.
And God repented that he had made man on the earth, and he considered it.
And God said: "I will wipe out from the face of the earth man whom I have made, from man to cattle, and from creeping things to the birds of the sky;
for I repent that I made them." But Noah found favor before God.
My son, let not evil counsel overtake you, the one that abandons the counsel of youth and forgets the divine law.
For she has set her house beside death, and her paths lead to hell, among the earthborn.
None of those who walk in it will return; instead they will regret it, and they will not reach the places of uprightness, for the years of life will not reach them.
If they had been perfect in good paths, they would have found the straight paths of righteousness.
For the upright will inherit the earth, and the holy will eat. But the ways of the ungodly will be destroyed from the earth, and the lawless will depart from it.
My son, do not forget my law; keep my words in your heart. For length of days and years of your life and of peace
will be added to you. Do not let mercy and faithfulness fail you; bind them around your neck, and you will find grace.
Plan what is good beforehand, before God and before people. Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not follow your own wisdom.
In all your ways acknowledge him, so that he may guide them and make your paths straight, and your foot will not stumble.
Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the Lord and turn away from all evil. Then there will be healing for your body and care for your bones.
Honour the Lord with your righteous labours, and offer him the firstfruits of your righteous fruits,
so that your storehouses may be filled with plenty of wheat, and your winepresses may overflow with wine.
My son, do not neglect the instruction of the Lord. For the Lord instructs the one he loves, and he disciplines every son whom he receives.
Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, and the mortal who has seen understanding.
For it is better to gain than treasures of gold and silver. It is more precious than precious gems; no evil thing will stand against it.
Its goodness is plain to all who come near to it; nothing precious is equal to it.
For length of days and years of life are in its right hand, and in its left hand are riches and glory.
Righteousness comes out of its mouth; it carries law and mercy on its tongue. Its ways are good ways, and all its paths are in peace.
There was a man in the land of Ausitis whose name was Job.
That man was true, blameless, righteous and a servant of God, and he kept away from every evil deed. He had seven sons and three daughters.
He had seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred grazing she-donkeys, and a very great number of servants. His works were great on the earth.
That man was a nobleman among the people of the east.
His sons would gather together and hold a feast day after day, and they would bring their three sisters with them to eat and drink.
When the days of their drinking were over, Job would send for them and purify them.
He would rise at dawn and offer sacrifices according to their number, and one calf for the sin of their souls, for Job said:
"Perhaps evil has come into the minds of my sons." Job did this all his days.
Then such a day came, and the angels of God came to stand before God, and the devil also came and stood among them.
The Lord said to the devil, "Where have you come from?" The devil answered the Lord, "I have gone around the whole earth and looked over what is under heaven, and now I am here."
And the Lord said to him: "Have you considered in your mind my servant Job?
For there is no one like him on the earth: a blameless man, true, a worshipper of God, who keeps away from every evil deed."
The devil answered before the Lord and said: "Does Job serve the Lord for nothing?
Have you not put a wall around him, and around the inside of his house and the outside, and surrounded everything that is his?
You have blessed the works of his hands and made his flocks many.
But stretch out your hand and touch everything he has. Will he still bless you to your face?"
Then the Lord said to the devil: "Look, I will give everything that is his into your hands, but do not touch him himself."
And the devil went out from the presence of the Lord. And a day like this came: Job's sons and his daughters were drinking in the house of their eldest brother.
And look, a messenger came to Job and said to him: "The yoked oxen were plowing, and the herd of she-asses was grazing near them.
And raiders came and carried them off as plunder, and they killed the servants. I alone escaped, and I have come to tell you."
And while he was still saying this, another messenger came and said to Job: "Fire came down from heaven and burned up the sheep, and it consumed the shepherds in the same way.
I alone escaped, and I have come to tell you." And while he was still saying this, another messenger came and said to Job:
"The horsemen divided into three bands and surrounded the camels, and they carried them off as plunder and slaughtered the servants with the sword. I alone escaped, and I have come to tell you."
And while he was still saying this, another messenger came and said to Job: "Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking at their eldest brother's house.
And suddenly a great wind came from the desert and struck the four corners of the house, and the house fell on your children, and they died. I alone escaped, and I have come to tell you."
And then Job got up and tore his clothes, and shaved the hair of his head, and fell to the ground. And he rose, and bowing down he worshipped the Lord with his face to the ground, and said:
"I came out completely naked from my mother's womb, and naked I will return there again, to the earth.
The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away. As he willed, so he has done. May the name of the Lord be blessed forever."
In all of this that happened to him, Job did not sin at all before the Lord, nor did he say anything foolish against God.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have grown weak through your falsehood.
Take words with you and return to the Lord your God. Say to him:
"You have the power to forgive sins, so that you may not receive falsehood but may receive good; and we will render the fruit of our lips.
Assyria could not save us. We will not ride on horses. We will no longer say 'Our gods' to the things made by human hands. The one who is in you will have mercy on the orphan."
"And I will heal their dwelling, and I will love them all together, for my anger has turned away from them.
I will be like dew in Israel. He will blossom like the lily and spread out his roots like Lebanon."
His branches will spread out, and his fruit will be like the olive, and his fragrance like that of frankincense.
They will return and sit under his shelter; they will live on wheat and be strengthened, and his memorial will blossom like a vine, like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what more has he to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a [?] fir tree; from me his fruit is found.
Who is wise and understanding, so that he will understand these things? Who is prudent, so that he will know them?
For the ways of the Lord are straight, and the righteous will walk in them, but the ungodly will grow weak.
The sacrifice to God is a spirit … will despise. Have mercy on me, O God, great …
Let us keep the spiritual fast:
And it came to pass after the death of Abraham that God blessed Isaac, his son.
And Isaac settled by the Well of the Oath. And these are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham: Abraham fathered Isaac.
And Isaac was forty years old when he brought Rebecca home as his wife. She was the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Mesopotamia and the sister of Laban.
And Isaac prayed to the Lord for his wife Rebecca, because she was barren. And God heard him, and Rebecca his wife conceived.
And the children leapt in her womb, and she said: If it is to be like this for me, why is this happening to me? And she went to inquire of the Lord.
And the Lord said to her: Behold, two nations are in your womb, and two sons will come from your womb, and the elder will serve the younger.
And the days for her to give birth were fulfilled, and there were twins in her womb.
And the firstborn came out completely red and hairy like a hide. And he was given the name Esau.
And after him his brother came out, and his hand was holding Esau's heel.
And he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when Rebecca bore them. And the boys grew up.
And Esau was a man skilled at hunting, a man of the field, but Jacob was a simple man who stayed at home.
And their father loved Esau, because his game was food for him. But Rebecca loved Jacob. And Jacob cooked a stew.
And Esau his brother came in from the field exhausted. And Esau said to Jacob: Let me taste that stew of wheat, for I am faint.
That is why he was called Edom. Jacob said to Esau: Give me your birthright today.
Esau said to him: Behold, I am about to die, so what use is this birthright of mine to me?
Jacob said to him: Swear to me today. And he swore to him and gave his birthright to Jacob.
And Jacob gave Esau bread and a stew of lentils. He ate and drank, got up, and went away. So he treated his birthright as worthless.
And there was a famine in the land, apart from the famine that had happened in the days of Abraham.
And Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, at Gerar.
And God appeared to him and said: "Do not go down to Egypt. Dwell in the land that I have told you of.

Live in it as a stranger, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all this to you and to your descendants, and I will establish my covenant and my oath, which I swore to Abraham your father.
I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and I will give all this land to you and to your descendants. Through your descendants all the tribes of the earth will be blessed,
because your father obeyed my voice and kept my commandments, my law and my ordinances."
And Isaac settled in Gerar. The men of that place asked about Rebecca his wife, and he said, "She is my sister."
For he was afraid to say, "She is my wife," in case they killed him because of Rebecca his wife, because she was beautiful in appearance.
And he was there a long time. Abimelech, king of the Gerarites, looked down and saw Isaac playing with Rebecca his wife.
Abimelech called Isaac and said to him: "So she was your wife! Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?"
Isaac said: "I said it in case I died because of her." And Abimelech said to him: "What is this you have done to us?
A little more, and someone of my people would have touched her, and you would have brought a sin of ignorance upon us."
And Abimelech commanded all his people: "Anyone who touches this man or his wife shall be liable to death."
And Isaac sowed in that land, and in that year he reaped a hundredfold of wheat. And God blessed Isaac.
And the man became great. He kept growing greater until he became very great.
He had flocks of cattle and sheep and a great deal of farmland under work. And the Philistines envied him.
And all the wells that the servants of his father Abraham had dug in his days, the Philistines stopped up and filled with earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac: "Go away from me, for you have become much stronger than I." And Isaac left that place, camped in the valley of Gerar and settled there.
And Isaac dug again the wells of water that his father's servants had dug, which the Philistines had stopped up after his father's death.
And he gave them the same names that his father had given them.
And Isaac's servants dug wells in the valley of Gerar and found there a well of living water.
And the herdsmen of the Gerarites quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen and said: "This water is ours."
And he named it Injury, because they had wronged him. And he moved on from there and dug another well.
And they disputed over that one too, and he named it Enmity. And he moved on from there as well and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it.
And he named it Broad Space, saying: "For now the Lord has made room for us and has made us increase in the land."
And he went up from there to the Well of the Oath. And God appeared to him and said: "I am the Lord, the God of your father Abraham."
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham, your father.
And he built an altar there and called there on the name of the Lord.
Love righteousness, you judges of the earth;
think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him with a sincere heart. For he shows himself to those who do not disbelieve in him.
For crooked thoughts separate people from the Lord; and when his power is put to the test, it exposes the foolish.
For wisdom will not enter a soul that does evil, nor will it dwell in a body worn down by sins.
For the holy spirit of instruction flees from deceit and withdraws from senseless thoughts, and it is put to shame when falsehood comes upon it.

For the spirit of wisdom loves humankind, and it will not leave the blasphemer unpunished for what his lips say; for God is witness of his inmost being, a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
For the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and the one who holds every spirit knows the meaning of every voice.
Therefore no one who speaks falsehood will be forgotten, nor will he escape when he is convicted by the law.
For there will be an inquiry into the plans of the ungodly, for his words will come before the Lord against his will, to convict him of his lawless deeds.
For the ear of his jealousy hears everything, and secret grumbling is not hidden.
So beware of useless grumbling, and keep your tongue from slander; for what is said in secret does not go unnoticed, and the mouth that speaks evil kills its own soul.
Do not strive [?] after death in the error of your life, and do not bring destruction on yourselves by the work of your hands.
For God did not create death, and he takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living.
For he created all things to exist, and life is the creation of the world. There is no deadly poison in it, and the kingdom of Hades is not on earth.
For righteousness is mortal [?] by the hands of the ungodly; with their words they summoned death, and they counted it a friend,
and today [?] they made a pact with it, for they deserve to be its portion. For they said in their heart, reasoning wrongly:
“Our life is short and sorrowful, and there is no remedy at a man's end, and no one has ever been known to return from Hades.
For we came into being by ourselves [?], as though we had never been; for the breath in our nostrils is smoke,
and our words [?] are a spark that dies out; the body turns to ashes, and the spirit dissolves like [?] air.
And in time our name will be forgotten, and no one will remember our deeds.”
And when such a day came, the angels of the Lord came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came with them.
And the Lord said to the devil, “Where have you come from?” Then the devil said before the Lord:
“I have gone about under heaven and looked over all of it; and now I am before you.” And the Lord said, “Have you seen my servant Job?”
For there is no man like him on the earth: blameless, true, a servant of God, keeping away from every evil deed;
and he still holds on to his innocence. Yet you told me to destroy his possessions for nothing.
The devil answered and said before the Lord: "Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has for his life.
But not like this. Rather, stretch out your hand and touch his bones, and see whether he will openly bow down to you, or whether he will bless you."
And the Lord said to him: "Look, I hand him over to you; only spare his life."
And the devil went out from the Lord and struck him with an evil sore from his feet to his head, and covered him with [?].
And Job took a potsherd to scrape away the pus, and he sat on the dung heap outside the city.
And after a long time had passed, his wife said to him: "How long will you endure this and say nothing?
'Look, I will wait just a little longer, and hope will come, his deliverance.' Look, your memory has perished from the earth:
the sons and daughters of my womb, my labor pains and my sufferings, for whom I wore myself out with grief for nothing.
And there you yourself sit in the stench of worms and spend your nights under the open sky, while I, a wanderer and a servant, go from place to place and from house to house, waiting for the sun
to set, so that I may rest from my labors and the pains that now surround me. Now say some word against the Lord, and die."
But Job looked at her and said to her: "You speak like one of the foolish women. If we have received good from the hand of the Lord, shall we not endure evil?"
In all this that happened to him, Job did not sin at all with his lips before the Lord.
And when his three friends heard of all the evil that had come upon him, each of them came from his own land to see him and what had happened to him:
Eliphaz, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans. And they came to him together to comfort him and to see him.
And when they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. They cried out with a loud voice and wept, and each of them tore his garment, and they poured dust on their heads.
And they sat with him for seven days, and none of them said anything, for they saw how great and terrible his affliction was.
After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his days. And he said: "Let the day on which I was born perish, and the night on which they said, 'It is a boy.'
Let that night be darkness; let the Lord not seek it out from above, and let no light come upon it.
Let darkness and the shadow of death seize it; let it not be a day of the year,
nor let it be counted among the days of the months. Rather, let that night be full of pain, and let no joy come upon it.
But let him curse it who curses that day, the one who is about to lay hands on the great sea monster.
Let the stars of that night be darkened; let it not stay, nor come to the light, nor see the rising sun.
For it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb, nor keep pain away from my eyes.
Why did I not die in the womb? Why, when I came out of the belly, did I not perish at once? Or why did knees receive me?
Or why did breasts nurse me? For now I would be lying down and at peace; I would have fallen asleep and been at rest,
with kings, the counsellors of the earth, who boasted of their swords,
or with rulers who had much gold, who filled their houses with silver;
or like a stillborn child that comes out of the womb, or like infants who never saw the light.
There the ungodly have burned out the fury of their wrath; there those worn out in body have found rest.
Together, those of the ages past no longer hear the voice of the tax collector. Small and great are alike there, and the servant does not fear his master.
Why, then, were light and life given to the embittered, to those whose souls are in pain?
They long for death but do not reach it, and they search for it as for treasure.
They rejoice when they reach it. For death is rest for a person, and God has hemmed them in.
Before my very food my sighs come [?]; I weep, held in by fear.
For the fear I was anxious about has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me. I was not at peace, I was not at rest, I had no relief, and wrath came upon me.
The Lord is long-suffering;
his power is great, and the Lord will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His way is in destruction and in earthquake, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
He will dry it up, and he has laid all the rivers waste. Bashan and Carmel have withered, and the blossoms of Lebanon have failed.
The mountains quaked because of him, and the hills were shaken. The whole earth and all who live on it were seized with trembling at his presence.
Who can stand before his wrath? Or who can withstand the fury of his anger?
His anger melts the mountains, and the rocks are shattered by him. The Lord is kind to those who wait for him in a time of trouble, and he knows those who fear him.
With the flood of his advance he will make an end of those who rose up against him, and darkness will pursue his enemies.
What are you plotting against the Lord? He will make an end of it; he will not take vengeance twice over in affliction.
It will be laid waste to its very foundation. Like tangled bindweed it will be devoured, and like a reed thicket full of dryness.
From it came forth anger against the Lord, people plotting evil and resistance.
Thus says the Lord, who rules over many waters: in this way they will be cut off, and they will hear no more news of you.
Now you will break his rod from off you, and I will burst your bonds. The Lord will give a command concerning you: no more offspring will be sown to bear your name.

From the house of your God he will destroy the molten idols, and I will lay your foundation, for it is soon. Look, here on the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news, who proclaims peace:
Keep your feasts, O Judah, and pay your vows, for they will never again pass through you to bring you to ruin. It is finished; it is destroyed.
One who breathes on you has come up from before your face to rescue you from distress. Watch the road, strengthen your loins, and take courage with all your strength.
For the Lord has turned away the insult done to Jacob.
Give ear to my prayer, O God. Turn your ear to me, O Lord.
Praise is fitting for you.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who went into Egypt with their father Jacob, each one with his whole household:
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Gad, Naphtali, Asher, and Benjamin. Joseph, however, was already in Egypt.
All the people descended from Jacob numbered seventy-five. Joseph died, and all his brothers, and that whole earlier generation.
But the sons of Israel increased, grew great, and became mighty, for the land made them multiply greatly.
A new king arose in Egypt who did not know Joseph, and he said to his people:
"Look, this people of the sons of Israel has multiplied greatly and is mightier than we are. Come, let us make a plan against them, so that they do not multiply further.
Otherwise, when war breaks out against us, they will join our enemies, fight against us, and then leave our land."
So he set taskmasters over them to oppress them with forced labor. They built strong cities for Pharaoh: Pithom, Raamses, and On, which is Heliopolis, the City of the Sun.
But the more he oppressed them, the stronger they grew, and the Egyptians came to loathe the sons of Israel.
They tyrannized them and made their lives bitter with hard labor in clay and brick and with every kind of work in the fields. In all their labor they enslaved them harshly.
Then the king spoke to the Hebrew midwives. One of them was named Shiphrah and the other Puah.
He said: "When you deliver the babies of the Hebrew women, if it is a boy, kill him; if it is a girl, let her live."
But the midwives feared God. They did not do what the king of Egypt had commanded them, and they let every boy live.
Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, summoned the midwives and said to them: "Why have you done this and let the boys live?"
The midwives said to Pharaoh: "The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. They give birth before we arrive, and only then do they call us in."
God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.
And because the midwives feared God, they made households for themselves.
Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: "Throw every boy born to the Hebrews into the river."
There was a certain man from the tribe of Levi who married one of the daughters of Levi, and she became his wife.
She conceived and bore a son. When they saw that the child was beautiful, they hid him for three months.
And since she could not hide him any longer, his mother took a little ark and coated it inside and outside with lime, naphtha and pitch. She put the child in it and set it in the reed-bed
there. And his sister watched from a distance to learn what would happen to him.
Pharaoh's daughter went down to the river to bathe, and her maidservants walked with her along the riverbank on this side and that.
She looked and saw the little ark in the reed-bed, and she sent her maidservant and took it.
She opened it and saw the child, for he was crying in the little ark. Pharaoh's daughter rescued him and said: "This is one of the Hebrews' children."
The child's mother's sister said to her: "Do you wish, my lady, that I call a nurse from among the Hebrew women, and she will nurse that child for you?"
Pharaoh's daughter said to her: "[?], go and call her." And she called the child's mother.
And Pharaoh's daughter said: "Keep this child for me and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages." And his mother took the child and nursed him.
And when the child had grown, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She called his name Moses, for "I drew him out of the water."
And it came to pass after many days that Moses grew up and went out to his brothers, the sons of Israel, and saw their suffering and their toil.
He looked and saw an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew man, one of his brothers, the sons of Israel.
He looked around, this way and that, and when he saw no one, he struck and killed the Egyptian and buried him in the sand.
Then he went out again on the second day and saw two Hebrew men who were fighting, and he said to them: "Men, you are brothers. Why are you harming each other?"
But the one who was wronging his neighbour pushed him away and said: "Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
Or do you want to kill me too, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" Moses was afraid and said: "Has this matter really become known like this?"
Pharaoh heard of this matter and sought to kill Moses. Moses fled from Pharaoh's presence.
He went and settled in the land of Midian, and he sat down by the well of water.
Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they were tending the sheep of their father Jethro.
The shepherds came and drove the sheep away. Moses arose and rescued the daughters from the shepherds. He drew up the water for them and watered their sheep.
And when they came in to Reuel their father, he said to them: "Why have you hurried to come back today?"
They said: "An Egyptian man rescued us from the shepherds and watered our flocks for us."
He said: "Where is he now? And why did you leave him outside? Call the man, and let him eat bread with us."
And Moses settled with that man, and he gave him his daughter Zipporah as a wife.
And the woman conceived and bore a son. He called his name Gershom, for he said: "I am a stranger in a foreign land."
And the name of the second son was Eliezer, for "the God of my father helped me and delivered me from the hands of Pharaoh."
And Noah began to work the land, and he planted a vineyard. And he drank wine from it and became drunk, and lay uncovered in his house.
And Ham the Canaanite saw his father's nakedness, and he laughed, and went outside and told his brothers.

And Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it on the knees of both of them, and they came walking backwards and covered their father's nakedness. They did not turn their faces toward him, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
Noah awoke from the wine and understood what his youngest son had done to him; and he said:
"Cursed be Ham, that boy, and let him be a servant to his brothers." And he said: "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Shem, and let him be his servant.
May God enlarge Japheth, and may he inherit the dwellings of Ham, and let Ham be their servant."
And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years. And all the years of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
These are the generations of the sons of Noah: of Shem, Ham and Japheth. And sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog, Madai and Javan, Eli and Tubal, Meshech, Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz and Riphath and Togarmah. And the sons of Javan: Elishah and Tarshish, the Kittim and the Rodanim.
From these the regions of the nations were divided in their land, each according to its own language, by their tribes and their nations.
And the sons of Ham: Ikus [? Cush] and Imes [? Mizraim], Trempos [? Put] and Nanti [? Canaan]. The sons of Cush: Seba and Havilah and Sabtah and Raamah and Bakatan [?].
And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Judah [?] and Dedan. And Cush begot Nimrod. He was the first mighty man on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the Lord God. Therefore they say: "Like Nimrod the mighty one."
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, Erech and Accad and Calneh in the land of Silan [? Shinar].
From that same land Asshur went out and built Nineveh, and Rehoboth the city, and the city [?], and Resen between the city of Nineveh and the city [?].
This is the great city. And Mizraim begot the Nodites [?] and the Kotomites [?]. And Calan [? Canaan] begot Sidon first, and the Hittites,
and the Jebusites and the Amorites and the Girgashites and the Sinite and the Aodite [? Hivite] and the Zemarite and the Hamathite. And after this these tribes of the Canaanites were scattered.
And the borders of the Canaanites were from Sidon as far as Gerar and Gaza, as far as Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham, by their tribes and languages, in their land and in their nations.
And to Shem also sons were born, the father of all the sons of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth. His sons: Elam and Asshur and Arphaxad and Lud and Aram and Cainan.
And the sons of Aram: Uz and Hul, Gether and Meshech. And Arphaxad begot Cainan, and Cainan begot Shelah, and Shelah begot Eber.
And to Eber were born two sons; the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; the name of his brother was Joktan.
To Joktan were born Almodad and Sheleph and Hazarmaveth and Jerah, and Hadoram and Jezreel, Diklah, and Ebal and Abimael and Sabel.
All these were the sons of Joktan. And their dwelling place was from Mesha as far as Sephar, toward the rising of the sun.
These are the sons of Shem, among their tribes, each by its language, in their lands. These are the tribes of the sons of Noah according to their generations.
From these the islands of the tribes, each tribe by itself, were scattered over the earth after the flood. And all the earth was one, and all had one speech.
And it came to pass, as they moved from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they settled there.
And a man said to his neighbour: “Come, let us make bricks and bake them with fire.”
“Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose top will reach up to heaven, and let us make a name for ourselves before we are scattered over the face of all the earth.”
And God came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men had built.
And the Lord said: “Behold, this people is one, and all have one language, and this they have begun to do. And now nothing that they set their heart to do will be withheld from them.
Come, and let us confuse our [?] languages, so that each one may not understand the voice of his neighbour.”
And the Lord scattered them over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city and the tower.
Therefore its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord confused the languages of all the earth, and the Lord dispersed them over all the earth.
And these are the generations of Shem: Shem was a hundred years old when he fathered Arphaxad, in the eighth year after the flood.
After fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived five hundred years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died. Arphaxad lived a hundred and thirty-four years, and he fathered Cainan.
And after fathering Cainan, Arphaxad lived three hundred and thirty years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Cainan lived a hundred and ten years, and he fathered Salah. And after fathering Salah, Cainan lived three hundred and thirty years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Salah lived a hundred and thirty years, and he fathered Eber. And after fathering Eber, Salah lived three hundred and thirty years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Eber lived a hundred and thirty-four years, and he fathered Peleg. And after fathering Peleg, Eber lived two hundred and seventy years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Peleg lived a hundred and twenty years, and he fathered Reu. And after fathering Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and thirty years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Reu lived a hundred and twelve years, and he fathered Serug. And after fathering Serug, Reu lived seven hundred years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Serug lived a hundred and thirty years, and he fathered Nahor. And after fathering Nahor, Serug lived two hundred years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Nahor lived sixty-nine years, and he fathered Terah. And after fathering Terah, Nahor lived a hundred and twenty-nine years, and he had sons and daughters, and he died.
Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abraham, Nahor and Haran. And Haran fathered Lot.
And Haran died before his father Terah, in the land where he was born, in the country of the Chaldeans.
And Abraham and Nahor took wives for themselves. The name of Abraham's wife was Sarah, and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Iscah.
And Sarah was barren and did not bear children. Terah took his son Abraham, and Lot the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarah,
[?] his son's wife, and he brought them to the land of the Chaldeans, and he came as far as Haran and settled there.
And the days of Terah in Haran were two hundred and five years, and Terah died in Haran.
Sanctify a fast, proclaim a service of worship,
gather the elders, all the inhabitants of the land, into the house of our God, and cry out to God together.
Alas, alas, for the day of the Lord is near, and it will come like misery upon misery.
For before our eyes the food has dried up, and from the house of the Lord our God, joy and gladness.
The heifers were restless at their mangers, and the storehouses were ruined and the winepresses were broken down, for the wheat has withered.
What shall we store up for ourselves? The herds of cattle wept, for they had no pasture; and the flocks of sheep were destroyed.
To you I cry, O God, for fire has consumed the beauty of the wilderness, and the flame has burned up all the beauty of Lebanon.
And the beasts of the earth looked up to you, for the springs of water have dried up, and fire has devoured all the beauty of the wilderness.
Have mercy on me, O God, great [?] my [?]: wash me thoroughly from my iniquities.
Let us keep the fast:
And Jacob went to the land of the east, to Laban the Syrian, the son of Bethuel, the brother of Rebecca, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
And he looked and saw a well of water in the field.
And there were three flocks of sheep lying there, for they watered their flocks from that well. And a stone lay over the mouth of the well.
And all the flocks and their shepherds would gather there, and they would roll the stone away from the mouth of the well and water their sheep, and then they would put it back in its place.
And Jacob said to the shepherds: "Where are you from, brothers?" And they said to him: "We are Canaanites."
Jacob said to them: "Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?" And they said: "We know him." Jacob said to them: "Is he well?" And they said: "He is well."
And while he was saying this to them, behold, Rachel, the daughter of Laban, came with her father's flocks.
And Jacob said: "It is still broad daylight, and it is not yet time to gather the flock. Water your flocks and go."
But they said to him: "We cannot, until all the shepherds gather and roll this stone away from the mouth of this well; then we will water our sheep."
And while they were still saying this, behold, Rachel was coming with the sheep.
And when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban, his mother's brother, he got up and rolled the stone away from the well and watered the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and she cried out with a loud voice and wept. And Jacob told her that he was her father's brother and the son of Rebecca.
Rachel hurried and went into the house and told her father what he had said.
When Laban heard the name of Jacob, his sister's son, he hurried out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him, and brought him into his house.
Jacob told Laban all these things. Laban said to him, "You are of my bones and of my flesh." And Jacob stayed with him one month and many days.
Laban said to Jacob, "Because you are my brother, do not serve me for nothing. Tell me, what is your wage?"
Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was lovely to look at and beautiful of face.
Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I will serve you for Rachel, your younger daughter."
Laban said to him, "It is better to give her to you than to another man. Stay with me."
So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and those years seemed to him like a few days because of his love for her.
When the seven years were completed, Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife, for the days of the appointed time are completed."
So Laban gathered all the men of that place and held a wedding feast.
When it was evening, Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her in to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her.
Laban gave his maidservant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her handmaid. And when it was morning, Jacob looked, and it was Leah who was with him.
Jacob said to Laban, "What is this you have done? Did I not serve you for Rachel? Why then have you treated me with contempt?"
Laban said to him, "It is not done this way in our place, to give the younger before the elder.
Now complete another seven years for this one, and I will give you this one as well, for the work that you will do with me for yet another seven years."
Jacob did so and completed the seven years. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
Laban gave his maidservant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her handmaid. Jacob went in to Rachel, and he loved her more than Leah.
God saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb. But Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived and bore a son. She named him Reuben and said, "For God has seen my humiliation and has given me a son.
Now my husband will love me." She conceived again and bore a second son, and said, "God has seen that I was hated, and he has given me this one too."
She named him Simeon. She conceived again and bore a son, and said, "From now on my husband will be mine, because I have borne him a son." She named him Levi.
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, "Now and from now on I will praise the Lord." Therefore she named him Judah.
Have troubles been spoken of to you many times? Yet who could withstand the force of your words?
If you have instructed many, and comforted weak hands, and raised up the sick, and given courage to the knees of the godless [?],
now pain has come upon you and touched you, and you are in haste.
Or is not that fear of yours now founded on folly, and your hope too, and the wickedness of your ways?
Now remember: who that was holy ever perished? Or when and where were the true uprooted, root and all?
As I have seen: those who plough what is improper, and those who sow it, will reap pain.
By the command of the Lord they perish, and by the breath of his wrath they are destroyed. The strength of the lion and the voice of the lioness, and the hissing of the dragons, were quenched.
The ant-lion perished, for there was no food for them. The lion's cubs abandoned one another.
If there had been any true word in what they said, no evil would have happened to you.
Now, is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? With fear and with the groaning of the night, fear falls on people.
Dread came over me, and great fear, and my bones trembled. A spirit came before my face. My bones and my flesh trembled.
I rose and did not know myself. I looked, and there was no form before my eyes. I heard only a breeze and a voice.
What now? Can a man really be pure before the Lord, or can a man be blameless in his deeds?
Does he not distrust even his own servants, and has he not found something crooked in his angels?
Then how much more those who live in houses of clay, we who are made of that same clay? How he has struck them down like a moth!
Between morning and evening they are gone, for they could not help themselves, and they perished.
He blew on them and they withered, for they had no wisdom. Call out, then, and see if anyone will heed you, or if you will see any of the holy angels.
For wrath kills the fool, and envy puts to death the one who has gone astray.
I have seen fools whose roots had spread out, but their provisions were suddenly devoured.
Their sons were cut off from life and crushed at the gates of their inferiors, and there was no one to rescue them.
For what they gathered, the righteous ate, and they were not rescued from evil. Their strength is drained away.
For darkness does not come out of the earth, and pain does not spring up from the mountains; rather, man is born to pain, and the young of the vultures [?] fly on high.
Not so. Instead I would plead with the Lord and call on God the Almighty, for he has done great and unspeakable things, glorious and wonderful things beyond number.
For he gives rain to the earth and sends water under heaven.
He makes the lowly high and lifts up those who were lost. He frustrates the schemes of the gentiles,
and their hands did not accomplish truth. He catches the wise in their own thinking and brings to nothing the counsel of those who weave many schemes.
Darkness will come upon them by day, and at noon they will grope as if at midnight. Let them perish in battle, and let the powerless be rescued from the hand of the mighty.
Let there be hope for the powerless, and let the mouth of the liar be shut. But blessed is the man whom God has rebuked;
do not turn away from the instruction of the Almighty. For he causes pain and then restores; he struck, and his hands healed him.
He will deliver you from six troubles, and in the seventh no evil will touch you.
In famine he will deliver you from death, and in war he will free you from the power of the sword.
He will shelter you from the lash of the tongue, and you will not be afraid of evil when it comes.
You will scorn the false and the lawless, and you will not be afraid of wild beasts, for the beasts of the field will be subject to you.
Then you will know that your house is at peace, and the order of your household will not fail.
Then you will know that your descendants are many, and your children like the flowers of the field.
And you will come to the grave like wheat that is ripe, reaped in its own time, and like a heap of sheaves on the threshing floor, gathered in its due season.
Look, this is what we have searched out, and this is what we have heard. But you must know for yourself what you have done.
And the children of Israel set out and camped on the east side of Moab, by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
And Balak son of Zippor saw everything that Israel had done to the Amorites;
and Moab was afraid of the people, because they were very many, and dread fell on Moab before the children of Israel.
And Moab said to the elders of Midian: "Now this assembly of Israel will lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the green grass of the field."
And Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time only.
And he sent the elders as messengers to Balaam son of Beor, at Pethor, which is on the river,
and in the land of his own people, to test him [?]. And he said to him [?] a narrow place, where it was impossible to turn aside either to the right or to the left.
And the donkey saw the angel of God and lay down on the ground under Balaam's feet.
And Balaam grew angry and beat the donkey with a staff. And God opened the donkey's mouth, and it said to Balaam: "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"
And Balaam said to the donkey: "Because you have mocked me. If I had a sword in my hand, I would have run you through right then."
And the donkey said to Balaam: "Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this very day?
Have I ever treated you with contempt?" And he said: "No."
And God opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in front of the donkey with a drawn sword in his hand. And he bowed down and worshipped [him] [?] with his face to the ground.
And the angel of God said to him: "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out to stand in your way.
This way of yours is not right before me. Your donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. By now I would have killed you and spared her."
And Balaam said to the angel: "Lord, I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing in the road to block me. And now, if it does not please you, I will turn back."
And the angel said to Balaam: "Go with the men, but keep the word that I have told you." And Balaam went with Balak's princes.
And Balak heard that Balaam was coming, and he went out to meet him at the city of Moab on the borders of the Arnon, which is at the edge of the borders.
Balak said to Balaam: "Did I not send to you to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I truly not able to honor you?"
Balaam said to Balak: "Behold, I have come to you. Now will I be able to say anything at all?
But the word that God puts in my mouth, that I will speak." And Balaam went with Balak, and they came to the cities of Balak.
And Balak slaughtered sheep and oxen and sent them to Balaam, and the princes were there.
Tell this to the house of Jacob, and let the house of Judah hear this, and say to them:
Hear now, you foolish and senseless people, who have eyes and do not see, who have ears and do not hear.
Do you not fear me, says the Lord, or do you not tremble before my face?

I who set the sand as a boundary for the sea by an everlasting decree, and it will not pass over it; it will stir itself and will not prevail against it; its waves will roar and will not pass over it.
But this people's heart has become disobedient and unbelieving; they have turned aside and gone away, and they did not say in their heart:
"Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives you early rain and late rain; only at the time of the fulfilment of his command was it kept for us."
Your iniquities have turned these things aside, and your sins have kept your good things away from you.
For among my people were found ungodly men, and they set snares like a hunter's trap to destroy men, and they caught them.
Like a trap that is set, full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and grown rich.
And they burst forth and transgressed my words for evil; they did not judge justly, nor did they make the cause of the orphan prosper, and they did not judge the cause of the widow.
Shall I not look upon this, says the Lord, and shall my soul not take vengeance on such a nation as this?
Do not cast me away, O Lord my God, from me [?].
I said: I will guard my ways, that [?]
Hear, O Israel: the Lord your God is the one Lord.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your strength. And these words, which I command you today, shall be in your heart.
And you shall speak of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, and when you lie down and when you rise up.
And you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be unshakable before your eyes. And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
And when the Lord your God brings you into the land which he swore to your fathers, to Abraham,
to Isaac and to Jacob, to give you great and good cities which you did not build, and houses full of every good thing which you did not fill,
hewn cisterns which you did not hew, vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant, and when you eat and are full,
Guard yourself, so that you do not forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him alone, and swear by his name.
Do not go after foreign gods, the gods of the nations that were around you.
For God is a jealous God, the Lord your God who is with you. Otherwise the Lord your God may become angry with you and destroy you from the face of the earth.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test, as they tested him at the place of testing.
Carefully keep the commandments of the Lord your God and his judgments, all that I command you.
And do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God, so that it may go well with you, and so that you may go in and inherit that good land
which God swore to your fathers, driving out all your enemies before you, as the Lord told you.
And when your son asks you in time to come and says, "What are these testimonies and judgments that the Lord commanded you?"
then tell your son: "I was Pharaoh's slave in Egypt, and the Lord brought me out with a strong hand and a high arm.
And he gave us great signs and wonders, evil ones against Egypt, against Pharaoh and against his house, before our eyes.
And he rescued us from there in order to bring us in and give us this land, which the Lord our God swore to our fathers to give to us.
And the Lord our God commanded us all these judgments, so that we would fear the Lord our God, so that it would go well with us all our days, and so that we would live, as we do today.
And there will be mercy among us if we keep all these commandments before the Lord God, as the Lord commanded us."
When the Lord your God brings you into the land that you are entering to inherit, and removes the great and many nations from before you,
and the Lord your God gives them into your hands, and you destroy them, do not make a covenant with them, and do not show them mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughter to his son, and do not bring his daughter to your son,
for he will turn your son away from me, and he will serve foreign gods, and the Lord your God will be angry with you.
Instead, do this to them: tear down their altars, smash their pillars and idols, cut down their groves, and burn their carved idols with fire.
For you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord chose you to be his own people, his possession, above all the nations
that are on the face of the earth. The Lord did not choose you because you are more numerous than other nations, for you are the fewest of all nations.
It was because the Lord loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your fathers
that he brought you out with a strong hand and a high arm. The Lord your God redeemed you from the house of bondage and from the hands of King Pharaoh. So know that the Lord your God
is the faithful God, who keeps his covenant and his mercy for those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations.
And he repays those who hate him to their face with destruction and retribution; he does not delay to repay them to their face [?]…
For the Lord God is among you, a great and mighty God. And the Lord your God will wipe out those nations before you little by little;
you will not be able to destroy them quickly, so that the land does not become desolate and the wild beasts multiply against you.
And the Lord your God will give them into your hands, and you will destroy them with a great destruction.
And he will give their kings into your hands, and he will wipe out their names by your hand, and they will perish from their place;
no one will stand against you before your face until you have destroyed them.
Burn their carved idols with fire. Do not set your heart on taking their gold and silver for yourself, lest you go astray, for it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
And do not bring the abomination into your house, or you will be accursed as they are. You shall utterly loathe it and utterly abhor it, for it is accursed.
If only someone would weigh my anger and lift my pains onto the scales together, they would be found heavier than the sand of the sea.
But, as I think, my words seem to be in vain.
For the arrows of the Lord are lodged in my body, and their fury drinks up my blood.
Whenever I begin to speak, they pierce me. What now? Does the wild donkey bray for nothing? No, it is looking for food.
Or does an ox low at the manger when it has fodder? Or is bread eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in empty words?
My soul cannot find rest, for my food seems foul to me, like the stench of a lion.
If only the Lord would grant it to me, and my requests would be fulfilled, and the Lord would give me hope.
The Lord began, and he has wounded me, but may he not kill me completely. Let this city, on whose walls I used to walk, be my grave;
I will not hold back, for I have not been false to the holy words of God. What is my strength, that I should endure?
Or how long is my time, that my soul should bear it?
Is my strength the strength of stone, or is my flesh made of bronze? Or did I not trust in him? Yet his help has gone far from me.
Your mercy has abandoned me, and the Lord's care has disregarded me. My neighbours have not looked on me;
I have dried up like a stream, and they have passed me by like a wave. Those who used to fear me now fall upon me like snow, and like frozen ice
that melts in the time of heat until its place can no longer be found. In the same way I have been left behind by everyone; I have perished and been driven out of my house.
Look at the roads of the Temanites and the paths of the Sabaeans, who are neighbours.
Those who trusted in cities and wealth will be put to shame.
Now look, you too have come at me without mercy. Seeing this wound of mine, you should have been afraid. What now?
Did I ask anything of you, or do I seek any of your strength, that you should rescue [?] me from the hands of enemies and deliver me?
Teach me and I will be silent; if I have gone astray in anything, tell me. But, it seems, true words are [to you] worthless, for I do not seek any strength from you.
Nor will the rebuke of your words silence me, and I have not taken upon myself what you have said.
But you come upon me as upon an orphan, and you assail your friend.
Now behold, I have looked upon your faces, and I will not lie. Sit down, and let there be no falsehood, and join yourselves again to justice.
For there is no falsehood on my tongue; or is my tongue not trained in understanding?
Now is not the life of man upon earth a trial, and his life like that of a day-laborer hired for wages?
Or like a servant who fears his master and trembles [?] at his shadow, like one hired for wages, who waits for his wages?
So I too have endured empty months, and nights of pain have been given to me. When I lie down, I say: When will it be morning?
And when I rise, again: When will it be evening? For I am filled with pain from evening until morning.
My flesh is defiled with the loathsomeness of worms, and I dissolve the clods [?] of the earth with the scraping of pus.
And my life is more [?] than speech; my hope has perished in vain.
I have remembered that my life is a breath, and my eye will not return again to see good.
Like a cloud that passes away from the sky: if a man goes down to hell, he will not come up again.
Nor will he return to his house, nor will his place know him.
Now therefore I too will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my soul; I will open my lips, held fast by bitterness.
Am I a sea, or a dragon, that you have set a guard over me? I will open [?] my words to myself upon my bed.
You frighten me with dreams in sleep, you terrify me with visions; you separate my soul from my body, and with death you crush my bones.
I am not to live forever, that I should endure; depart from me, for my life is vain.
What is man, that you have magnified him? Or that you regard him in your mind? Or that you visit him until morning and appoint him rest?
How long will you not let me alone, so that I may swallow my spittle in pain?
If I have sinned, what can I say to you, who know the mind of men? And why have you set me as a pleader [?] to you, and am I a burden to you?
And why have you not forgotten my iniquities and cleansed my sins?
Now behold, I go to the earth, and by morning I shall be no more.
And it came to pass in those days, when the judges judged, that there was a famine in the land.
And a man went from Bethlehem of Judah to live as a sojourner in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his sons.
And the man's name was Abimelech, and his wife's name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah.
And they came to the country of Moab and stayed there. And Abimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her sons.
And they took Moabite wives. The name of one was Orpah and the name of the other was Ruth; and they lived there for ten years.
And both her sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died, and the woman was left alone, without her two sons and her husband.
And the woman got up with both her daughters-in-law, and they went back from the country of Moab to the land of Judea,
because they had heard in the country of Moab that the Lord had visited his people to give them bread.
And she left the place where she had been living, and both her daughters-in-law went with her. And they set out on the road to return to the land of Judah.
And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law: "Go now, daughters, and return each of you to your mother's house;
and may the Lord show you mercy, as you have shown it to the dead and to me.
May the Lord grant it to you, and may each of you find rest in the house of her husband."
And she kissed them and said goodbye to them. And they raised their voices and wept. And they said: "We will go with you to your people."
And Naomi said to them: "Turn back, my daughters, and go; why are you coming with me?
Are there still sons in my womb who could become husbands for you?
Go back now, my daughters, because I have grown old and can no longer take a husband.
Even if I were to say, 'I have no strength left,' and yet I were joined to a husband again and bore sons,
would you wait for them until they grew up? Would you hold back for their sake from taking husbands?
Not so, my daughters, for it is more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the Lord has gone out against me." And they raised their voices and wept.
And they kissed their mother-in-law. And Orpah kissed her, turned back and went to her home, but Ruth followed her.
And Naomi said to Ruth: "Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods; now you go back too, after your sister-in-law."
Ruth answered and said to her: "May it not happen that I do that, that I leave you and turn back and go away from you;
but wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you are, there I will be too.
Your people will be my people, and your God my God. And where you die, there I will die too and be buried with you.
May the Lord do this to me, and add more to it, for death will make the separation between you and me."
And when she saw that Ruth was this determined to go with her, from then on she stopped speaking to her about it. And the two of them went on and came to Bethlehem.
And it came to pass, when they reached Bethlehem, the whole city groaned over them, and they said: "Is this really Naomi?"
And she said to them: "Do not call me Naomi any more, but call me Embittered, for he has embittered me very heavily."
"For I went away full and I have come back empty. Why do you call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me and the Mighty One has done me evil?"

So Naomi returned, and Ruth, her daughter-in-law, with her. They came from the land of Moab, and they came to Bethlehem just at the beginning of the barley harvest. And there was a man there known to Naomi's husband.
That man was rich and powerful, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz. And he gave Naomi a widow's house to live in.
And Ruth said to Naomi: "Let me go to the field and gather ears of grain behind the reapers, wherever I find favour in their sight."
And she said to her: "Go, daughter." And she went to glean in the field behind the reapers.
And by chance she happened upon the portion of the field of Boaz, which was part of the estate of Elimelech.
The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Sheri [?], in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah,
kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel. The beginning of the words of the Lord to Hosea.
And the Lord said to Hosea: "Go and take for yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry, for the land has gone whoring and turned away from following the Lord."
And he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim. And she conceived and bore him a son. And God said:
"Call him Jezreel, for in a little while I will take vengeance for the house of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel."
"And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel." And she conceived again and bore a daughter, and the Lord said to him:
"Name her 'Not Pitied', for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel; instead, I will set myself firmly against them."
"But I will receive the sons of Judah, and I will save them by the Lord God
their [God]. I will not save them by bow, or by sword, or by battle, or by horses, or by horsemen."
And when Not Pitied was weaned from the milk, she conceived and bore a son. And he named him 'Not My People', "and I am not your God, for you are not my people."
"And it will be that, even if the number of the sons of Israel is like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted, only a remnant will be saved."
"And it will be that in the place where [?] they will be called 'son of the living God'."
"And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will gather together and set one ruler over themselves, and they will go up out of the land,
for great is the day of Jezreel. Say to your brothers, 'My people', and to your sister, 'Received in favour'."
"Bring a case against your mother, bring a case, for she is not my wife and I am not her husband."
"Comfort, comfort my people," says the Lord.
"Priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem and comfort her, for her humiliation is complete,
And her sins are forgiven, for she has received from the hand of the Lord double recompense for her sins.
A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord, and make straight the paths of our God.
Every valley shall be filled up, and all the mountains shall be brought low; and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough places a plain.
And the glory of the Lord shall appear, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God, for the Lord has spoken.
A voice that said: Cry out! And I said: What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass.
The grass has withered, and its flower has fallen. But the word of the Lord stands and endures forever.
Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy. In the shelter of your wings.
You appeared as a good vine.
I went astray like a sheep. You are my portion:
Wisdom is better than precious stones; nothing precious is worthy of her.
I, Wisdom, have made knowledge my own; I have attended to counsel and understanding.
The fear of the Lord hates wickedness; insolence and arrogance and the counsel of the wicked, and perverse paths, I have hated.
Counsel is mine, prudence is mine, understanding is mine, strength is mine. Through me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
Through me princes are made great, and by me they hold the earth. I love those who love me, and those who seek me shall find me.
To gain me is better than gold and precious stones, and my words are better than gold and silver.
I walk in the ways of righteousness, and I dwell among the paths of the righteous, so that I may share out fruit to those who love me and fill their treasuries with good things.
If I tell you day by day how many things come to pass, you will remember to recount them from of old.
Who is like you, O Lord?
You are great, and great is your house in power. Who would not fear you, O King of the nations?
For they are yours; for among all the wise men of the nations and among all their kings, who is like you, O Lord?
For all at once they are kindled and become senseless [?]; the hearts of the blameless [?] are wood.
Beaten silver and gold of Uphaz, the work of craftsmen, all of it from the hands of goldsmiths: blue and purple are their clothing.
But the Lord our God is true, the living God and the eternal King.
I beseech you,
brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, pleasing to God, which is your spiritual worship.
And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may discern what the will of God is:
good, acceptable and perfect. For I say, through the grace that has been given to us, to all, whoever there may be:
Do not think more highly than you ought to think, but let each one think with purity, as God has apportioned to each the measure of faith.
For as one body has many members, but all the members do not have the same function,
so we all are one body in Christ Jesus, and each of us is a member of one another.
May the prayer draw near to you:
And all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to Jesus to hear him.
And the Pharisees and the scribes grumbled and said, "This man receives sinners and eats and drinks with them."
And he told them a parable, and said to them: "Which of you, having a hundred sheep, if he loses one of them,
does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
And when he has found it, he lifts it onto his shoulders with joy. And he comes home and calls together his friends and his neighbours and says to them:
'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.'
I tell you: in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search diligently until she finds it?
And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and her neighbours and says to them: 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I had lost.'
I tell you: in the same way there is joy in heaven before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
Disregard my sins.
We who [mystically represent] the cherubim [?].
Seek me, the sheep that has gone astray.
Let us hasten, O peoples, to [?] beforehand; he looked upon their prayer [?]. Lord, hear the prayer:
Have mercy on me, this sinner:
There was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, of Ramathaim.
He had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no child.
And that man would go up from his city, Ramathaim, from time to time to worship and to offer sacrifice at Shiloh.
And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the Lord there.
And the day came, and Elkanah offered sacrifice and gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her children, her sons and daughters.
But to Hannah he gave a single portion, because she had no child. Yet Elkanah loved Hannah more than Peninnah. The Lord had closed her womb and had not given her a child.
She spoke out of her grief and her affliction, because he had not given her a child but had closed her womb.
She did this year after year for a long time: she would go up with her husband to the temple of the Lord, and each time she would vex herself, weep, and not eat.
Her husband said to her: "Why do you weep and not eat, and why is your heart grieved? Am I not better for you than many children?"
