After they had eaten bread at Shiloh, she got up. Eli the priest was sitting on the seat in front of the doors of the temple of the Lord.
In bitterness of heart she prayed to the Lord, weeping bitterly. She made a vow to the Lord and said:
"Adonai, Lord, Eloi Sabaoth, if you will indeed look upon the lowliness of your handmaid, remember me, and give me male offspring,
I will surely give him to you, to be before you until the day of his death. He shall drink no wine or strong drink, and no iron shall come upon his head."
While Hannah went on praying at length before the Lord, Eli the priest was watching her mouth.
She was speaking in her heart. Only her lips moved, and her voice could not be heard, so Eli thought that she was drunk.
Eli's servant said to her: "How long will you be drunk? Get rid of your wine and go away from the presence of the Lord."
Hannah answered him: "No, my lord. I am a woman whose days are hard. I have not drunk wine or strong drink, and I am pouring out my prayers before the Lord.
Do not take your handmaid for one of the worthless daughters. I have been wasting away until now from great grief and faintness of spirit because of my affliction."
Eli answered her: "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you everything you have asked of him."
Hannah said: "Your handmaid has found favor in your sight, my lord."
The woman went her way. She ate and drank with her husband, and her face was no longer sad.
They rose early the next morning and worshiped the Lord, and they went back to their own town, Ramathaim.
Elkanah went in to his wife Hannah, and the Lord remembered her.
In the course of those days the woman conceived and bore a son. She named him Samuel, for she said: "I asked for him from the Lord Sabaoth."
Then the man Elkanah and all his household went up to offer sacrifice at Shiloh, and to offer all the tithes of his land to the Lord.
But Hannah did not go up. She said to her husband: "I will not go up until the child goes up.
When he has been weaned, he will go up with me and appear before the face of the Lord, and he will stay there."
Her husband Elkanah said to her: "Do whatever seems good in your eyes.
Stay here until you have weaned him. May the Lord establish everything that has come out of your mouth."
So the woman stayed there and nursed the child until he was weaned.

And she went up to Shiloh when she had weaned him, with a three-year-old bull, with bread, with a measure, and with three measures of wine. She went into the house of the Lord at Shiloh, and the child was with them.
And they brought him before the Lord. In those days his father slaughtered the sacrifices that he offered to the Lord from time to time.
And he brought the child and slaughtered the bull, and Hannah, his mother, presented the child to Eli.
And she said: "Look upon me, my lord; as your soul lives, I am the woman who stood before you when I was praying.
And the Lord has granted me my request, which I asked of him. I will have him serve the Lord all the days that he lives." And she worshipped the Lord there.

Hannah prayed and said: "My heart has been strengthened in the Lord, and my horn has been raised high in God. Through my Saviour I have known [?] my mouth over my enemies. I have rejoiced in your salvation.
For no one is holy like you, O Lord, and no one is holy besides you; and no one is righteous like our God.
Do not boast, and do not speak lofty things beyond measure, and let no arrogant word come out of your mouth.
For God is the Lord of knowledge, and God prepares his works. The bows of the mighty have become weak, and the weak have been clothed with strength.
Those who lived in luxury have run short of bread, and the hungry have taken possession of the land; for the barren woman has borne seven children, and she who had many children has become weak.
The Lord kills and makes alive; he casts down to Hell and brings up again. The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and lifts up.
He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the fallen from the dunghills, so that they may sit with the mighty of his people, and he makes them inherit thrones of glory.
He grants the request of those who pray to him and blesses the years of the righteous. A man's might is not strength. The Lord makes his adversaries weak.
The Lord is holy. Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the mighty man boast in his strength, nor the rich man boast in his riches; but let him boast in this,
he who boasts: in understanding and knowing the Lord, and in doing judgment and justice on the earth. The Lord has gone up into the heavens and has thundered.
He himself will judge the ends of the earth in his righteousness. He will give strength to our king, and the Lord will raise high the horn of his anointed."
And they left the child there before the Lord and went to their own city, to Ramah.
Who would make me as in those former days, in the years when my Lord watched over me?
When his lamp shone above my head, when I walked by his light in the darkness;
when I lived in luxury in my ways, when I walked in my ways in very great righteousness, and my servants were around me;
when butter flowed in my paths and milk poured out on my mountains; when I went out to the city and my seats were set up in the streets;
the young men would see me and hide, and all the elders would rise up for me; princes would stop speaking before me and lay their hand on their mouth;
and those who heard me called me blessed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth. For the ear that heard me called me blessed, and the eye that saw me held me in awe;
for I rescued the poor from the hands of the mighty, and I helped the orphan who had no helper;
The blessing of the perishing came upon me, and the mouth of the widow blessed me; and righteousness clothed me, I put on justice like a garment;
I was the eye of the blind and the foot of the lame; I was the father of the powerless; and the case that I did not know, I searched out;
I broke the jaws of the deceitful and took the plunder out from between their teeth; and they became glad whenever I spoke to them.
As thirsty earth that waits for water, so these waited for my words.
If I laughed with them, they did not believe it; and the light of my face did not fall.
I searched out their ways and sat as their ruler; I dwelt like a king among the mighty, and like one who comforts the sick.
But now, behold, those lesser than I laugh at me; now, behold, they admonish me in some part, whose fathers I despised, whom I did not count equal to the dogs of my flocks.
And the strength of my hands, how much is it to me? Upon them the end of the needy perished.
They were in hunger, who yesterday walked in the waterless land in distress and wretchedness; who gathered herbage in the mountains, whose food was greens;
dishonoured and worthless and lacking in every good thing, who even chewed the roots of trees because of great hunger.
Now, behold, thieves have risen up against me, whose houses were holes in the rock.
Among the [?] they cry out, who were raised in the [?] (brushwood?) of the field, children of fools and of a dishonoured house.
Now, behold, I am their lyre, and they have me as a byword. They abhorred me and stood far off from me, and did not refrain from spitting before my face.
The Proverbs of Solomon:
Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: I begot sons and raised them up, and they despised me.
The ox knew its owner, and the donkey the manger of its lord; but Israel did not know me, and my people did not understand.
Woe, erring nation and wicked seed, lawless offspring! They have forsaken the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger; they became estranged and turned back.
Why do you add wounds upon wounds by your lawlessness? The whole head is in pain, and the whole heart in grief.
From the feet to the head he is struck; there is no place of [?] (lit. 'fragrance', probably for 'soundness') in him, nor are the wounds open,
nor is there swelling of the bruises, nor is there a place to lay on a remedy, nor oil, nor bandage.
Your land is desolate, and your cities are burned with fire; strangers devour your country before you; and it is laid waste and overthrown by the hands of strangers.
The daughter of Zion shall be cast off and abandoned like a tent of [?] (vineyard keepers?), and like the shelters of fruit-watchers in a melon field, and like a besieged city.
Had the Lord of hosts not left us a seed of inheritance, we would have been overthrown like the Sodomites and made like the Gomorrhans.
Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom, and give heed to the law of God, you people of Gomorrah.
What [?] mine and yours, and of the multitude of your sacrifices? says the Lord. I am full now; the burnt offerings of rams are enough for me;
And I do not want the fat of lambs and of your goats. I do not want to see you, or your coming, or your appearing before me.
Who asked this from your hands, that you trample my courts? From now on you shall not come into my court again.
If you offer me fine flour, that sacrifice is useless to you. If you burn incense to me, that too is counted as loathsome to me.
Your new moons and your sabbaths, and the days of the year that you count as great, I will not bear.
My soul hates your fasts, your days of rest and your new moons, for I am now sick of you.
It cannot go on. From now on I will no longer forgive your sins. When you stretch out your hands to me,
I will turn my face away from you. Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
The word of God that came to Jeremiah,
[son] of Hilkiah, one of the priests, who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the Lord came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
It came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah,
king of Judah, until Jerusalem was carried into captivity in the fifth month. The word of God came to him and said:
"Before you were formed in the womb I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I made you holy. I appointed you a prophet to the nations."
And I said, "O you who are, Lord, Lord! Look, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth." And the Lord said to me:
"Do not say, 'I am only a youth.' For you shall go to everyone I send you to, and you shall speak everything I command you.
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord."
And the Lord stretched out his hand to me and touched my mouth, and said to me, "Look, I have put my words in your mouth.
Look, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot and to plant, to tear down and to build up."
Let your ears be [?]. Out of the depths we cry to you:
Have mercy on me, this sinner.
And the boy Samuel was serving before the Lord with Eli the priest.
But Eli's sons were wicked and did not know the Lord. They used to take the priests' share from all of that priesthood [?]. He would come when they were boiling [?] the meat,
holding a three-pronged fork in his hand. He would thrust it into the basin, or the [?], or the cauldron, or the pot, and the priest would take for himself everything the fork brought up.
And they did this to all Israel who came to sacrifice before the Lord at Shiloh.
And before the incense was burned before the Lord, the priest's boy would come and say to the man who was offering the sacrifice:
Give me meat to roast for the priest, and I will not take boiled meat from [?].
And the man who was offering the sacrifice said to him: “First let the fat be burned as incense, as is proper,
and then take from all of it whatever your soul desires.” And he said to him: “No, give it to us now, or else I will take it by force.”
And the sin of those men was great before the Lord, because they treated the sacrifices of the Lord with contempt.
And the boy Samuel was serving before the Lord, and he was clothed in a garment, a linen ephod.
And his mother made him a small double cloak and brought it to him from time to time, when she went up with her husband to offer the sacrifice of those days.
And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife Hannah and said:
“May the Lord give you offspring from this wife of yours in return for the loan that you lent to the service of the Lord.” And the man went away to his own place.
And the Lord visited Hannah, and she bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew great before the Lord.
And Eli was very old. And he kept hearing what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel.
And he said to them: “Why do you act like this, according to this report that I hear from the mouth of the people of the Lord?
If a man sins against a man, people will pray to the Lord for him. But if he sins against the Lord, who will pray for him?”
But they would not listen to the voice of their father, because the Lord willed to destroy them.
And the boy Samuel went on and kept growing greater, and he was pleasing to the Lord and to men. And a man of God came to Eli and said to him:
“Thus says the Lord: I plainly revealed myself to the house of your father while they were still in Egypt as slaves of Pharaoh,

and I chose the house of your father out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priests, to go up to my altar, to burn incense and to carry the ephod. And I gave the house of your father all the wheat of the sons of Israel for food.
And why have you looked upon my altar and my sacrifices with a shameless eye, and honored your sons more than me, blessing for them first all the produce of the sacrifices of the house of Israel?
Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I said that your house and the house of your father would walk before me forever;
but now the Lord God says: Far be it! Rather, those who glorify me I will glorify, and those who despise me I will despise.
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will destroy your descendants and the descendants of your father's house, and there shall be no old man in my temple.
And I will cut off from you a man from my altar, so that your eyes may grow dim and his heart may melt away; and all who remain of your house shall fall by the sword of men.
And this shall be the sign for you, which will come upon these two sons of yours: on one day Hophni and Phinehas shall both die together.
And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do everything that is in my heart, and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before my anointed one all his days.
And it shall be that everyone who is left of your house will come to bow down to you for a small silver coin and one loaf of bread, and will say:
‘Appoint me to just one of your priestly offices, so that I may eat bread.’” And the boy Samuel was serving before the Lord, in the presence of Eli the priest;
And the word of the Lord was precious in those days, and there was no vision of discernment.
And it came to pass in those days that Eli was sleeping in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see.
The lamp of God was not yet lit; and Samuel was sleeping in the temple, where the ark of God stood.
And the Lord called Samuel and said to him: "Samuel, Samuel!" And Samuel said: "Behold, here I am; why have you [?] me?"
And he went to Eli. And Eli said to him: "I did not call you; go and sleep, my son."
And he went and slept, and the Lord called him again, a second time, and said: "Samuel, Samuel!"
And Samuel rose, went to Eli and said to him: "Behold, here I am, for you called me." And he said to him: "I did not call you; go and sleep, my son."
And then the Lord called him again, a third time, and said to him: "Samuel, Samuel!" And he rose and went to Eli and said: "Behold, here I am, for you called me."
And Eli understood that the Lord was calling the boy. And Eli said to Samuel: "Go back and sleep, my son.
And if he calls you, say: 'Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.'" And Samuel went and slept in his place.
And the Lord came and stood over him and called in the same way and said to him: "Samuel, Samuel!" And Samuel said: "Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening."
And the Lord said to Samuel: "Behold, I will carry out my words in Israel, so that both ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.
On that day I will bring upon Eli everything that I have spoken against his house; I will begin and I will finish.
And tell him that I will take vengeance on his house forever for the wickedness of his sons, because they spoke evil against God, and he did not correct them.
And not so have I sworn to the house of Eli [?] with slaughtered offerings and sacrifices forever."
And Samuel slept until morning; and he rose early in the morning and opened the doors of the temple of the Lord; and Samuel was afraid to tell the vision.
And Eli said to Samuel: "Samuel, my son!" And Samuel said: "Behold, here I am, lord."
And Eli said to him: "What are the words that were spoken to you this night?
Do not hide anything of those words from me." And Samuel told him all those words and did not hide a single one of them from him.
And Eli said: "May the Lord himself do what is good in his eyes."
And Samuel grew great; and the Lord was with him; and none of his words fell to the ground.
And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was trustworthy as a prophet of the Lord.
And the Lord again gave revelation in Shiloh, for he revealed himself to Samuel.
And Samuel was trusted as a prophet of the Lord by all Israel, from one end of the earth to the other. And Eli was very old.
And his sons kept going on in their ways, and their way was evil before the Lord.
What, then, is the prelude [lit. 'fore-parable'], or the fear that comes from him who made all things entirely in the heights?
Let no one suppose that there is any respite for trials. Upon whom does such an ambush from him not come?
How can a man be righteous before the Lord, or who born of women can make himself pure?
If he commands the moon, it does not shine; the stars are not pure before him either.
Leave it, then: man is rottenness, and the son of man a worm. Whose side are you on, or whose help do you expect?
Is it not he who has great power, and whose arm is strong? Or whom have you counselled? Is it not he from whom all wisdom comes?
Will you not follow someone? Is it not he from whom comes all the wealth of strength? To whom have you told your words?
Whose is that breath that goes out from you? Will the giants make me [?] beneath the waters, and his neighbours?
Hell is naked before him, and destruction has no foundation.
He stretches out the north over nothing and hangs the earth upon nothing. He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the clouds do not burst beneath him.
He holds the face of the throne and spreads his clouds over it.
By his command he encircles the heaven. Before his face everything trembles [?], until the consummation of light in darkness.
And the pillars of heaven flew up and were astonished at his rebuke. By his power he calmed the sea, and by his command its surging was struck down.
And the bolts of heaven fear him. By his command he killed the apostate dragon.
Behold, this is a part of his ways, and further still I will hear in him the depth of words. And the power of his thunder, who knows when and where it will be?
My son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray. Do not consent to go with them.
If they entreat you and say to you: 'Come with us and share in blood, and let us falsely drench the earth with innocent blood,
and let us swallow him up as hell swallows a living man, and take away his memory from the earth; let us seize his many and varied possessions and fill our houses with plunder.
Cast in your lot with us, and let us all get a common purse [?]; let there be one bag [?] for all of us,'
do not walk on the road with them; turn your feet away from their paths. For not in vain are snares spread for birds.
For those who take part in murder store up evil for themselves, and the ruin of ungodly men is evil.
These are the ways of all who commit lawlessness, for by their ungodliness they destroy their own souls.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said: 'What do you see, Jeremiah?'
And I said: 'A rod of walnut.' And he said to me: 'You have seen well, for I have kept watch over my words to perform them.'
And the word of the Lord came to me a second time and said: 'What do you see, Jeremiah?' And I said: 'A cauldron [?] heated from beneath, its face turned from the face of the north.'
And the Lord said to me: From the north every evil will flare up upon all who dwell on the earth.
For behold, lo, I will summon all the kings of the earth from the north, says the Lord,
and each one will set up his throne before the gates of Jerusalem, and all around its walls, and against all its cities.
And I will speak to them in judgment for all their wickedness, for they forsook me and served foreign gods and worshipped the works of their own hands.
And you, gird up your loins, arise, and speak all the words that I command you.
Do not be afraid of their faces, and do not tremble before them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.
Hear, O Lord, the voice of my prayer. The Lord is my light and my Savior.
After those days the king of the Egyptians died, and the children of Israel were oppressed by the work of clay and brick, and they began to cry out and lament to the Lord.
And the Lord heard their groaning under the oppression the Egyptians laid on them.
And the Lord remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the Lord looked upon the children of Israel and revealed himself to them.
And Moses was tending the sheep of Jethro, his father-in-law, the chief priest of the Midianites.
He drove his flock away into the wilderness and went up to the high mountain, Horeb.
And the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from within the bush, and he saw that the bush was burning with fire yet was not consumed.
Moses said: I will go and see this great sight, for the bush is not burned up.
When he saw that Moses was coming to see it, the Lord called to him from within the bush and said: Moses! And he said: What is it, O Lord God?
And the Lord said to Moses: Do not come near here. Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
And he said to him: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
Moses turned his face away, for he was afraid to come near before the Lord. The Lord said to Moses:
I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I have seen their suffering.
And I have come down to deliver them from the hands of their enemies,
and to bring them out of that land, and I will bring them into a good and broad land, a land
flowing with milk and honey, the place of the Canaanites and the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Girgashites, the Jebusites and the Hittites.
And now the cry of the children of Israel has reached me, and I have seen their suffering and their groaning under the oppression the Egyptians lay on them.
Now come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, and you will bring my people, the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt.
And Moses said to the Lord: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, and bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt?
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him: "I will be with you, and this shall be a sign to you that I am sending you:
that you shall bring my people out of the land of Egypt, so that they may serve God on this mountain."
Moses said to the Lord: "Behold, I will go to the sons of Israel and say to them,
'The God of your fathers has sent me to you.' And if they ask me and say to me, 'What is his name?', what shall I say to them?"
The Lord said to him: "I am who I am." And he said: "Say this to the sons of Israel: 'He who is has sent me to you.'"
Then the Lord spoke again to Moses: "Say this to the sons of Israel:
'The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.'
This is my eternal name and my memorial from generation to generation. Go and gather the elders of the sons of Israel and say to them:
'The Lord God of our fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has appeared to us and said: I will surely look upon you because of the evil done to you by the Egyptians,
and I will bring you into the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Hivites, the Girgashites and the Jebusites and the Amorites, a land flowing with milk and honey.'
They will listen to your voice, and you and the elders of the sons of Israel shall go in to the king of the Egyptians and say to him:
'The Lord God of the Hebrews has summoned us. Let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness, so that we may offer sacrifice to the Lord our God.'
But I know that the king of the Egyptians will not let you go unless it is by a mighty hand and a high arm.
I will stretch out my hand against them and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I will do among them, and after that he will let you go.
And I will give my people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and when you go out, you shall not go out empty-handed.

Instead, each woman shall ask her neighbor and the woman who lodges with her for vessels of gold and silver, and for clothing, and you shall plunder those Egyptians; and you shall put these things on your sons and your daughters."
Moses answered the Lord and said: "If they do not believe me or listen to my voice, and they say to me, 'The Lord did not appear to you,' what shall I say to them?"
The Lord said to Moses: "What is that in your hands?" He said: "A rod." The Lord said to him: "Throw it on the ground."
He threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from it. The Lord said to Moses: "Put out your hand and take hold of its tail."
He put out his hand and took hold of its tail, and it became a rod again in his hands.
"This is so that they may believe you, that the God of your fathers has appeared to you, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob."
Then the Lord said to him again: "Put your hand into your bosom." And he put his hand into his bosom.
He took his hand out of his bosom, and his hand had become white as snow. The Lord said to him: "Put your hand back into your bosom."
He put his hand into his bosom and took it out of his bosom, and it had returned to the color of the rest of his flesh.
The Lord said to him: "If they do not believe you, and do not heed the first sign, they will listen to your voice because of the second sign."
If they do not listen to you because of both these signs, and do not heed your voice, take water from the river and pour it on the dry land, and it will become blood on the earth.
And Moses said: I beseech you, Lord, I have not been eloquent, neither yesterday nor the day before, nor since you began to speak to your servant.
The Lord said to Moses: Who gave man a mouth? Or who made the hearing and the deaf, the speaking and the blind and the seeing? Is it not I, the Lord?
Now go, and I will open your mouth for what you are to say. And Moses said: I beseech you, Lord, choose someone else, someone capable, whom you may send.
And the Lord was angered with wrath against Moses and said: Is not Aaron there, your brother the Levite?
I know that he will speak for you with words. And behold, he is coming out to meet you; he will see you and rejoice in his heart.
And you shall tell him and put my words in his mouth, and I will open your mouth and his mouth and teach you what you are to do.
And he will speak for you to the people, and he will be a mouth for you, and you will be to him as one toward God. And take this rod in your hands,
with which you will perform the signs. Moses went and returned to Jethro, his father-in-law, and said to him:
Let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive.
And Jethro said to Moses: Go in good health.
And behold, Boaz was coming from Bethlehem, and he said to the reapers: The Lord be with you!
And they said: May God bless you! And Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers: Who is this young woman?
The servant answered and said to Boaz: She is a Moabite woman who came with Naomi from the land of Moab, and she said:
Let me glean ears of grain and gather them among the sheaves behind the reapers. And she came and has stayed until now, and has not rested even a little in this field.
And Boaz said: I tell you, daughter: do not go to another field, and do not leave this place, but stay here with my maidservants.
And keep your eyes on this field; wherever they reap, follow them. Behold, I have commanded my servants not to say anything to you.
And when you are thirsty, come to the vessels and drink from what my servants drink. And she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground.
And she said to Boaz: For I have found favor in your eyes, and you have taken notice of me, though I am a foreigner. Boaz answered and said:

I have been told in full how much you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and that you left your father and your mother and your land and came to a people whom you did not know before.
May the Lord repay you for this deed of yours, and may your reward be full from the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.
And she said to him: May I find favor before you, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your maidservant, and from now on I will be like one of your maidservants.
And Boaz said: At mealtime come here and eat bread, and dip your bread in the vinegar.
And Ruth sat down beside the reapers, and Boaz heaped up roasted grain for her, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.
And she got up and began to glean ears of grain. And Boaz commanded his servants, saying that she should glean among the sheaves, and: Do not put her to shame.
Rather, take it upon yourselves to look after her: give her some of your food, and let her eat and glean, and do not scold her.
So she gleaned in that field until evening and threshed what she had gleaned, and the barley came to about one measure. She picked it up and went into the city.
Her mother-in-law saw what she had gathered. Ruth brought out and gave her the leftovers from the food she had eaten her fill of.
Naomi said to her: "Where did you glean, daughter? Where did you gather so much? Blessed be the one who took notice of you!"
Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had gleaned, and said: "The name of the man I gleaned with is Boaz."
Naomi said to her daughter-in-law: "May that man be blessed by the Lord, for he has not stopped showing kindness to the living and the dead."
Naomi also said to her: "That man is close to us; he is also our kinsman." Ruth said to her mother-in-law:
"The man told me: 'Stay close to my maidservants until they have finished all my harvest.'"
Naomi said to Ruth: "It is good, daughter, that you went out with his maidservants, so that no other men will bother you in someone else's field."
So Ruth stayed close to Boaz's maidservants to glean until they had finished the barley harvest. Ruth went home and lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her: "Daughter, should I not look for a place of rest for you, so that things will go well for you?
Now Boaz, whose maidservants you were with, is a relative of ours. Tonight he is gathering barley on his threshing floor.
So wash, anoint yourself, put on your clothes and go up to his threshing floor. Do not let the man see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go, take hold of the covering at his feet and lie down.
He will ask you [or: tell you] what you ought to do." Ruth said: "I will do everything you have told me."
So she went down to the threshing floor and did exactly as her mother-in-law had told her.
Boaz ate and drank, and he was in good spirits. Then he went to lie down in a corner of his sleeping place.
Ruth came quietly, lifted the covering at his feet and lay down.
At midnight the man woke up with a start and was frightened, because a woman was lying at his feet. Boaz said to her: "Who are you?"
She said: "I am Ruth, your maidservant. Spread your garment over your maidservant, because you are my kinsman."
Boaz said to her: "May you be blessed by the Lord, daughter. This last kindness you have shown is greater than the first,
because you have not gone after young men, poor or rich.
And now, daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you everything you have asked me, because all the kin of my people know that you are a woman of strength.
It is true that I am a kinsman, but there is another kinsman who is closer to you than I am.
Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he will take you as his own, let him do so. If he does not want to take you as his own, I will take you as mine. As the Lord lives!
And she lay down and slept at his feet until the morning, and she rose early, before a man could recognize his neighbour.
And Boaz said: Let no one know that a woman came to this threshing floor.
And Boaz said: Hold out to me the garment you are wearing, and spread it out! And she held it out to him.
And he measured out six measures of barley and laid it on her. And she went into the city to her mother-in-law.
Naomi said to her: How is it, daughter? And she told her everything that the man had said to her.
And she said to her: He gave me these six measures of barley and said to me: Do not go empty-handed to your mother-in-law.
And she said: Sit still, daughter, until you learn how the matter will not fall to the ground;
for the man will not rest until he has settled the matter this very day.
Love the righteousness of judges.
And now thus says the Lord your God:
Turn to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping and with mourning. Rend your hearts and not your garments;
turn to the Lord your God, for he is merciful and forgiving, long-suffering and abounding in mercy, and he relents from doing evil to people.
Who knows whether he will turn and relent and [?]
And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the Lord shall be made manifest, and it shall be established on the top of the mountains, and it shall be raised above all the hills;
and many peoples shall hasten and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob;
and he will show us his way, and we will walk in his paths, for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord;
and he shall judge many peoples and rebuke peoples even to all the earth, and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares and their spears into sickles.
And nation shall no longer lift up the sword against nation, and they shall no longer learn the work of evil.
And each one shall rest under his vine and under his fig tree, and there shall be no one to make them afraid, for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken this.
For each one will walk in his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and beyond.
I have sinned before you, O Lord, who [?]
Hear my worship, O Lord. I said: I will keep my ways.
And it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered to fight against Israel; and Israel went out to fight against them.
And the Philistines encamped on this side of Ebenezer, and Israel encamped at Aphek.
And they drew up in battle against Israel, and turned against Israel, and the battle went against them, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines.
And four thousand men from the battle line fell on the field.
And the people went into the camp, and the elders of Israel said: "Why has the Lord God struck us down before the Philistines [lit. 'the foreigners']?
Let us bring the ark of our God from Shiloh and take it into our midst, and it will save us from the hand of our enemies."
And the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought the ark of the Lord, upon which stood the cherubim of glory. And both sons of Eli were with it:
Hophni and Phinehas were with the ark. And when the ark of the Lord came into the camp, the sons of Israel shouted with a loud voice.
And the earth groaned greatly. And the Philistines heard it and said: "What is this shouting in the camp of the Israelites?"
And they learned that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp. And the Philistines were afraid and said: "These are gods who have come into their camp.
Woe to us! Deliver us today, O Lord, for there was no such shouting yesterday or the day before.
Woe to us! Who will deliver us from these mighty gods? For these are the gods who crushed Egypt and did wonders in the wilderness.
Be strong and be men, Philistines, and fight them." And they joined battle, and the sons of Israel were defeated, and each man fled to his own dwelling.
And there was a very great slaughter. And thirty thousand men in battle array fell from Israel.
And the ark of God was taken captive, and both sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were killed.
And a Benjaminite man ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh that same day. His garment was torn, and he had poured earth on his head.
And Eli was sitting on his seat before the gates of the temple of the Lord, watching the road, for his heart was trembling for the ark of the Lord. And the man cried out in the city.
And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said: "What is this outcry that I hear, and this noise?"
Now Eli was ninety years old, and his eyes had grown heavy, and he could not see.
And Eli said to the men who stood before him: "What is this sound of groaning?"
And the man came quickly to Eli and said to him: "I am the one who came from the camp, for I fled from the slaughter today."
And Eli said to him: "What is this thing that has happened, my son?" The young man answered and said:
"The men of Israel fled before the Philistines, and there was a great slaughter among the people, and both your sons were killed, and the ark of God has been taken."
And when the ark was mentioned to Eli, he fell backward from his seat near the gates, onto the threshold, and his back was broken and he died;
for the man was old and heavy, and he had judged Israel for twenty years. And his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near to giving birth.
And she heard the news that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died. She wept and gave birth, for her pains came upon her.
And she was dying. At that time the women who stood before her said to her: "Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son."
But she answered not a word, nor did she take it to heart.
And they named the child Ichabod, because of the ark of God and because of her father-in-law and her husband, and they said:
"The glory of Israel has been carried off into captivity, because the ark of God has been taken."
And the Philistines took the ark of God and carried it from Ebenezer to Ashdod. They brought it in and set it up in the temple of Dagon.
And the people of Ashdod rose early and went into the temple of Dagon and saw that Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of God.
They raised him up and set him back in his place. And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the people of Ashdod; he afflicted them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territory.
And when they rose early in the morning, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the covenant of the Lord;
and his head and both the soles of his feet had been broken off [?] and lay in front, and both arms of his hands lay toward the doorway; only his back was left.
For this reason the priests of Dagon, and everyone who enters the temple of Dagon in Ashdod, do not step on its threshold to this day, but step over it.
And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the people of Ashdod; he sent mice upon them and spread them out, and there was a great panic of death in the city.
And when the people of Ashdod saw this, they said: "This ark of the living God cannot stay among us, for because of it is [?]"
And they sent and gathered the rulers of the Philistines to that city and said: "What shall we do with this ark of the God of Israel?"
And the people of Gath said: "Let the ark of God come to Gath."
And when it came there, the hand of the Lord was upon that city, with very great terror, and he afflicted the men of the city, from the least to the greatest, and struck them with tumors.
And the people of Gath made golden tumors for themselves.
And they sent the ark of God to Ashkelon, and the people of Ashkelon cried out and said: "Why have you brought the ark of the God of Israel to us?"
"Let it go back to its own place, so that it does not destroy us and our city." For there was great destruction in that city.
And when the ark of the God of Israel came there, even those who were still alive were struck with tumors, and their cry rose up to heaven.
And the ark of God was in the land of the Philistines for seven months, and their land swarmed with mice.
Then the Philistines called their priests and said: "What shall we do with this ark of God? Tell us, so that we may send it back to its own place."
And they said: "If you send away the ark of the covenant of the Lord God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but give it an offering for the affliction."
"Then you will be healed, if his hand has not been withdrawn from you." And they said to them: "What shall we give for the affliction?"
And the diviners said to them: "Five golden tumors, according to the number of the rulers of the Philistines,
for there is sin among you, among your rulers and your people; and five golden mice, like the mice that are ravaging your land.
And why do you harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts?
Was it not after he had made sport of them that they at last let them go, and they went out?"
So now take and make a new cart, and two first-calving cows without their calves, and yoke them to the cart, and shut their calves away at home.
And take the ark and set it on the cart, and give the golden vessels as an offering for the torment. And do not [?] put them, placing them in a bersekhtan [?] beside it;
and watch the road to its border, which way it goes. If it goes toward Beth-shemesh, then he is the one who has done us this great evil;
if not, then we shall know that it was not his hand that touched us, but that something happened to us by chance.
And the Philistines did so: they took two first-calving cows and yoked them to the cart, and they kept the calves shut up at home.
And they set the ark on the cart, along with the tumours and the golden mice.
And the cows went straight along the road that leads into Beth-shemesh. They went along one road and did not grow weary,
and they did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the lords of the Philistines followed and went along with them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
And the people of Beth-shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted up their eyes and saw the ark coming, and they rejoiced and went out to meet it.
And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.
And they set the ark beside the great stone, and they cut up the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a sacrifice to the Lord.
And the Levites took up the ark of God, and the golden vessels with it, and set them beside the great stone.
And the men of Beth-shemesh offered sacrifice and offerings to the Lord on that day.
And the five lords of the Philistines watched, and returned to Ashkelon on that day.
And these are the golden tumours that the Philistines gave to the Lord as an offering for the torment:
one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron.

And there were five golden mice, for all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five principalities, from the fortified cities as far as the villages of the Perizzites, and as far as the great stone
on which they set the ark, in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.
Has he himself not seen my ways and counted all my ways?
If I have walked with mockers, or if my foot has hurried to deceit — for I have stood on a just yoke, and God knows my innocence.
If my foot has turned aside anywhere from his way,
or if my heart has followed my eyes, or if I have laid my hand on a bribe, then let me sow and let others eat, and let me be without root on the earth.
If my heart has followed another man's wife, or if I have sat somewhere lying in wait at her door, then let my wife please other men, and let my children be brought low.
For the fury of wrath cannot be restrained: the defiling of a man's wife.
For it is a fire kindled on every side, wherever it goes, and it destroys to the very root.
If I have despised the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant when they contended with me,
Wisdom is praised in the outlets of the streets, and in the squares she speaks openly.
On the tops of the mountains she is proclaimed, and at the gates of the city she speaks boldly: As long as the innocent hold to righteousness, will they not be kept from shame?
But the foolish desire insolence. They have become ungodly, have hated knowledge, and have become liable to rebuke.
Behold, I have set before you the words of my spirit, and I will teach you my word. For I called you, and you did not listen;
I spoke at length, and you did not heed me. Instead, you scorned my counsels and paid no attention to my rebukes.
Now therefore I too will laugh at your destruction, and I will rejoice when sudden turmoil comes upon you.
And ruin will come upon you like a storm wind, when distress and a siege by enemies come upon you.
It shall be that when you call upon me, I will not hear you; the wicked will seek me and will not find me. For they hated wisdom and did not seek the fear of God.
Nor did they want to obey the words of my lips, and they scorned my rebukes.
From now on they will eat the fruit of their own ways and be filled with their own ungodliness.
For because they wronged the little ones, they will be slain, and judgment will destroy the ungodly.
But whoever listens to me will dwell in hope and will rest without fear of any evil.
Behold, from this day I have made you like a chosen city and like a strong wall of bronze against all: against the kings of Judah, against its princes, and against the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to deliver you.
And he said: Thus says the Lord: I will remember the kindness of your youth, when you followed the Holy One of Israel, says the Lord.
Israel is holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of his produce. All who devour him will regret it, and evil will come upon them, said the Lord.
May you hear
my supplication, O God. I said: I will keep my ways.
All these commandments that I command you today
you shall keep and do, so that you may live and multiply and inherit the land that the Lord swore to your fathers.
And you shall remember all the way by which the Lord your God led you in the wilderness,
to afflict you and test you, and to test your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.
And he afflicted you, let you hunger, and fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, so that he might tell you
that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that comes out of the mouth of God.
Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your feet were not bruised.
And know in your heart that as a man teaches his son, so the Lord was teaching you.
And keep the commandments of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways and to fear him.
For the Lord your God is bringing you into a good and abundant land, where streams of water and springs of the deep flow out from its plains;
a land of wheat and barley, of vines and figs, of pomegranates, a land of olives, of oil and honey;
a land where you will eat your bread without scarcity, and you will lack nothing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose stones you will dig out copper.
You will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless the Lord your God for the good land that the Lord your God has given you.
Take care that you do not forget the Lord your God by failing to keep his commandments and his judgments, all those that I command you today.
Take care that when you eat and are satisfied, and build fine houses and live in them;
and your sheep and cattle multiply, and your gold and your silver and everything you have increase;
that your heart does not become proud, and you forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;
who led you through that great and terrible wilderness, where the serpent and the scorpion bit, and where there was no water; who made a spring of water flow out of the rock for you;
which neither you nor your fathers knew, so that he might afflict you and test you, and do you good in the end.
Do not say in your heart, “My power and the strength of my arm have gained me this great power.”
And remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gave you power to do mighty things, so that he might confirm his covenant, which he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
And if you completely forget the Lord your God and go off to follow foreign gods and serve them, I call heaven and earth to witness against you that you will utterly perish.
Like the other nations that the Lord God destroyed before you, so you will perish, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
Hear, O Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan to go in and take possession from many nations, great and stronger than you, and cities walled up to heaven;
a people great and numerous and tall, the sons of Anak, where you were and heard it said: “Who can stand against the sons of Anak?”
And know today that it is the Lord your God himself who goes before you. The Lord your God is a consuming fire.
He will destroy them, and he, the Lord himself, will overthrow them before you, and he will destroy them quickly, as he told you.
When the Lord your God has destroyed these nations before you, do not say in your heart:
“The Lord brought me in to take possession of this good land because of my righteousness.” No, the Lord destroyed them before you because of the ungodliness of those nations.
It is not because of your righteousness, nor because of the uprightness of your heart, that you are going in to take possession of their land,
But it is because of the ungodliness of those nations that the Lord destroys them from before you, and so that he may confirm his covenant, which he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
And know today that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is giving you that good land to inherit, for you are a stiff-necked people.
Truly I know that this is so. How can a man be righteous before the Lord?
And even if he should wish to go to judgment with him, he would not listen to him, so that he could not answer him one word out of his thousand.
For he is wise in mind, mighty and great. Who has hardened himself before him and held out against him?
He overturns mountains, and they do not know it; he brings them low in his wrath. He shakes everything under heaven from its foundations, and its pillars totter.
He speaks to the sun, and it does not rise, and he seals up the stars. He alone stretched out the heavens, and he walks on the sea as on dry land.
He made the Pleiades and the evening star, the Wain of the north, and the treasuries of the south.
He does great and unsearchable things beyond number, glorious and wondrous.
If he passes over me, I shall not see him; if he goes past me, even then I shall not know it. If he takes away, who will turn him back?
Or who will say to him, 'Why have you done this?' For he turns his wrath away, and the sea monsters under heaven bow down beneath him.
Even if he himself should listen to me, or should he judge my words, and even if I were righteous, he would not listen to me. I would plead for his judgment.
And even if he listened to me, I would not believe that he had listened to me. Perhaps he will crush me with darkness, for he has inflicted many wounds on me for nothing.
He does not let me catch my breath, for he has filled me with bitterness. And since he is mighty in strength, who can stand against his judgments?
And even if I were righteous, my mouth would still go wrong. Even if I were blameless, I would still be shown to be perverse.
And if I have acted ungodly, I do not know it in my soul. I know only this: my life has been taken away.
Therefore I said: wrath destroys the great and the mighty, for the wicked perish by a strange death, but the righteous become a laughingstock.
For they are handed over into the hands of the ungodly. Shame has covered the faces of its judges.
For my life is swifter than a runner. It flees away and does not see [good].
Is there a path or track for ships on their way, or for an eagle in flight as it looks for food?
And if I should say anything, I forget it as I speak. I bow my face, I groan, and I tremble in all my limbs.
I know that you will not leave me unpunished. And since I am ungodly, why did I not die?
Even if I wash myself with snow and cleanse myself with pure hands, you have plunged me deep into filth. My own clothing has loathed me.
You are not a man like me, so that I might give you an answer and we might come together to judgment.
If only there were someone between us to stand in the middle, someone to reprove us, who would hear us both!
Take his rod away from me, and do not let fear of him terrify me. Then I would not be afraid, and I would speak, for I do not know myself to be so.
How weary my soul is! With sighing I will pour out my words against him. Held in the bitterness of my soul, I will speak.
And I will say to the Lord: Do not teach me ungodliness! Why have you judged me like this?
Is it good for you if I sin against you, that you have cast off the work of your hands and have listened to the counsel of the ungodly?
Do you see the way a man sees? Is your life a human life, or are your years the years of a man?
For you have searched out my iniquities and looked into my sins.
You know that I was not ungodly. But who is there who will rescue me from your hands?
Your hands made me and formed me, and after that you turned against me and struck me down.
Remember that you made me of clay, and you are returning me to that same earth. You poured me out like milk and curdled me like cheese.
You clothed me with skin and flesh and made me firm with bones and sinews. You gave me life and mercy, and your care guarded my spirit.
These things I hold from you. I know that you can do all things and nothing is impossible for you.
If I sin, you watch me closely, and you have not held me innocent of my iniquities.
If I become ungodly, woe is me. And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head, for I am full of disgrace. I am hunted like a lion for the slaughter.
Again you turn back and torment me cruelly. You renew your judgments against me, for you have dealt with me in great wrath and brought trials upon me.
Why did you bring me out of the womb, and why did I not die? I wish no eye had seen me!
Why was I not carried from the womb straight to the grave, as if I had never been? Are not the days of my life few?
Leave me alone, so that I may rest a little before I go to the place I will not return from: the land of eternal darkness, where there is no light and no seeing of human life.
My son, pay attention to what I say, and turn your mind to my words.
Then your springs will not fail you. Keep them in your heart, for they are life to those who find them and relief to all flesh.
Keep every safeguard [?] within your heart, for out of it come the springs of life.
Put crafty theft away from you, and remove lying lips far from you. Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids bear witness to what is right.
Make the paths of your feet straight, and keep your ways on course. Do not turn to the right or to the left; turn your foot away from the evil way.
For the Lord knows the ways on the right, but the ways on the left are crooked.
He will make your paths straight and guide your steps in peace.
My son, seek my wisdom and turn your mind to my words, so that you may keep good understanding.
I give you the knowledge of my lips as a command: do not look at an evil woman, for honey drips from the lips of a harlot,
She makes your palate smooth for a moment, but in the end she will be found more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged sword.
For the feet of folly lead those who use her down to hell after death, and her steps are not firm.
For she does not come onto the path of life. Her tracks wander and cannot be known. Now, my son, listen to me, and do not disregard my words.
Keep your ways far from her. Do not go near the doors of her house, so that you do not give your life to others and your possessions to the merciless,
so that strangers are not filled with your strength and your labours do not go into the houses of others.
In the end you will regret it, when the flesh of your body is wasted away [?], and you will say: "How I hated instruction, and how my heart turned away from reproof!
I did not listen to the voice of my teacher, nor did I bend my ear to him. A little more, and I would have been found in every evil in the middle of the congregation and the assembly."
Drink water from your own vessels, and spring water from your own wells. Let water flow out for you from your own springs, and let your waters run in your streets.
Let them be your possession alone, and let no stranger share them with you.
Go up onto a high mountain:
Hear [us?], O God the Saviour [?]. Praise is fitting for you, O God, in Zion.
God is wonderful to the people: Let God arise, and let [his enemies?] be scattered:
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
Treasures do not profit the lawless, but righteousness delivers from death.
The Lord will not let a righteous soul die of hunger, but he will overturn the life of the ungodly.
Poverty humbles a man, but strong hands make rich. A son who has been taught is wise, but you will use the foolish as a servant.
A sensible son escapes the heat, but a lawless son is blasted by the scorching wind at the threshing floors.
The blessing of the Lord is on the head of the righteous, but untimely mourning will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
The memory of the righteous will be praised, but the name of the ungodly will perish.
The wise accept the commandments with their heart, but the ungodly man, stumbling with his lips, will be tripped up.
Whoever walks in simplicity walks in virtue, but whoever twists his ways will be found out.
If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
If the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead
will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit, which dwells in you.
So then, brothers, we are debtors, but not to the flesh, so that we should live according to the flesh.
If you live according to the flesh, you are bound for death; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
For those who walk by the Spirit of God are children of God.
For you have not received a spirit of slavery, so that you should be afraid again. You have received the Spirit of adoption, by which we cry out: "Abba, Father!"
That same Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God.
If we are children, then we are also heirs with God and joint heirs with Christ. If we suffer with him, we will also be glorified with him.
The saints will boast in glory.
A disciple is not greater than his teacher, and a servant is not greater than his master.
It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and for the servant to be like his master.
If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they call the members of his household so?
Do not be afraid of them, for nothing is hidden that will not be brought out, and nothing is secret that will not be revealed.
What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in your ears, proclaim upon the streets.
And do not be afraid of those who kill your bodies but cannot kill your souls.
Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna. Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion?
And not one of them falls to the ground without your Father. Even the hairs of your head are all counted.
Do not be afraid, for you are worth more than many sparrows.
Give ear, O God, to my prayer: I called upon God, and God heard me.
The glory of God conceals words, but the glory of the king honours the king.
The heaven is high and the earth is deep, but the heart of the king cannot be searched out. Hammer out untested silver, and it will be purified until it is completely pure.
And the heathen will be destroyed from before the king, and his throne will be set straight in righteousness. Do not behave boastfully before the king, and do not sit down in the place of the mighty.
It is better for you to be told, "Come up higher," than to be humbled before the mighty.
Speak about what your eyes have seen. Do not be quick to quarrel, so that you do not regret it in the end.
When a friend reproaches you, withdraw from him, or the friend may come to despise you.
And quarrelling and enmity will not leave you; they will be like death to you.
Kindness and friendship set you free. Keep them for yourself, so that you will not be open to reproach, and keep your ways well.
A golden apple in a necklace of sardius: that is speaking a word. A word of wisdom to an obedient ear is like a golden earring adorned with a precious carbuncle.
As snow falling in the heat of harvest brings coolness, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him, for he is a benefit to the hearts of those who remember him.
Like winds and clouds and violent rains, so are those who boast falsely of a gift.
Thus says the Lord: Turn to me and be saved,
you who are at the ends of the sea. I am, and there is no other besides me.
By myself I swear, says the Lord, that righteousness has gone out from my mouth, and my words will not turn back.
For to me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall swear by the true God.
And every tongue shall say: Righteousness and glory shall come to him. And all who separate themselves from the Lord shall be put to shame.
For all the generations shall be justified and shall be glorified by the Lord.
We have gifts by the grace of God, each in a different way: if it is prophecy, in proportion to faith;
or whoever serves, in that service; or whoever comforts, in that comforting; whoever gives, with generosity;
whoever presides, with diligence; whoever shows mercy, with cheerfulness. Let love be without hypocrisy. Turn away from evil and hold fast to what is good.
Be affectionate toward one another in brotherly love; outdo one another in showing honor; do not be lazy in zeal;
be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord; rejoice in hope; be patient in affliction; be constant in prayer;
share in the remembrance of the saints; pursue hospitality. Bless those who curse you; bless and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. Be of the same mind toward one another; do not set your mind on lofty things, but associate with the lowly.
Blessed is the man who is [?]. He sat [?]:
A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father:
Give me the share of my inheritance that falls to me. And he divided his living between them.
And not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and went away to a distant country, and there he squandered all his substance, for he lived in impurity.
And when he had wasted everything, a severe famine came on that country, and he began to be in want.
And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into the fields to feed pigs.
And he longed to fill his belly with the carob pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
He reflected within himself and said: How many of my father's hired servants have more than enough bread, and here I am perishing with hunger.
I will get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am not worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your laborers.
And he got up and went to his father. And while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion.
And he ran, fell on his neck and kissed him.
And the son said to him: "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers."
And his father said to his servants: "Bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
And bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and rejoice, for my son was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found."
And they began to celebrate. Now his elder son was out in the field, and as he came and drew near the house, he heard the sound of celebration and rejoicing.
And he called one of the servants and asked him, "What is this?"
And he said to him: "Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has come back alive."
But he became angry and would not go inside. His father came out and pleaded with him. He answered and said to his father:
"Look, I have served you for so many years and have never broken your commandments, and you have never given me even one young goat so that I could rejoice with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, who devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him."
And he said to him: "Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
But it was right to make merry and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found."
I have repented of my insolence.
Who … the cherubim.
The Father's gift:
I humbled [myself] with fasting … returned: Judge, O Lord, those who harm [me]:
Very many are the mercies:
Now Joseph was seventeen years old, and he was tending the flocks with his brothers.
He was still a boy, with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's concubines. And they brought an evil accusation against Joseph to Israel, their father.
Now Jacob loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the child of his old age. And he made him a robe of many colours.
When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his sons, his brothers hated him and could not speak to him peaceably at all.
Joseph had a dream and told it to his brothers. And he said to them: "Listen to this dream that I had:
I thought that you were gathering sheaves in the field, and my sheaf rose up and stood upright.
And your sheaves turned and bowed down to my sheaf." His brothers said: "Are you now really going to reign as king over us?"
And they hated him even more because of his dreams. Then he had another dream and told it to his father and his brothers, and said to them:
"Look, I have had another dream: the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
His father rebuked him and said: What is this dream that you have seen?
Shall I and your mother and your brothers really come and bow down before you to the ground? And his brothers were jealous of him.
But his father kept these words in mind. And his brothers went to pasture their father's sheep at Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph: Are not your brothers pasturing the flocks at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them. And he said: Here I am.
Israel said to him: Go and see your brothers, how they are faring, and the sheep, and bring me word. And he went from the valleys of Hebron and came to Shechem.
And a certain man found him wandering astray in the field. The man asked him: Whom are you looking for? And he said: I am looking for my brothers; tell me, where are they pasturing the flocks?
The man said to him: They have gone away from here, for I heard them saying: Let us go to Dothan.
And Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
They saw him coming from far off, before he drew near to his brothers, and they plotted evil, to kill him.
They said to one another: "Look, here comes that dreamer."
Now come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say that an evil beast has devoured him.
And we shall see what will become of his dreams. But Reuben heard this and rescued him from their hands, and said to them: Let us not take his life.
Do not shed blood. Throw him into that pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him. He said this so that he might rescue him and give him back to his father.
The word that came to Israel by the hand of his angel: lay it to your hearts.
I have loved you, says the Lord, and you said: In what way have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother?
says the Lord. Yet I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated, and I appointed his territory for destruction and his inheritance to be given over to desolation.
For they said: Idumea has been overthrown; let us return and rebuild what has been laid waste. Thus says the Lord Almighty:
They will build, and I will tear down; and they will be called the territory of lawlessness, and the people against whom the Lord is set in hostility forever.
And your eyes will see it, and you will say: The Lord has been magnified beyond the borders of Israel.
A son honours his father, and a servant his master. So if I am a father, where is my honour?
says the Lord Almighty. You who despise my name and say: In what way have we despised your name?
For you bring defiled bread to my altar and offer it, and you say: In what way have we defiled it?
Because you say: The table of the Lord is contemptible, and you have treated with contempt what is laid upon it.
Therefore if you offer a blind animal at my altar, is it not evil? If you offer a sick or lame one, is it not evil?
Bring it now to your ruler: will he accept it, or will he show you favour? says the Lord Almighty.
And now plead before the Lord your God, and he will have mercy on you. This has been done by your own hands; shall I show favour to any of you? says the Lord Almighty.
For among you too the doors will be shut, and you will not kindle my altar in vain.
I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.
For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is glorified among the nations, says the Lord Almighty.
And now entreat the face of your Lord, and he will have mercy on you. This was done by your hands; will he [?] regard you? says the Lord Almighty.
For among you too the doors will be shut, and you will not kindle my altar in vain.
I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.
For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is glorious among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my house, and a pure sacrifice,
for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord Almighty.
But you profane it, because you say: “The table of the Lord is defiled, and the food set on it is contemptible.”
And you say: “This comes from hardship,” and you have brushed it aside, says the Lord Almighty;
and you brought me what was seized by force, and the lame, and the sick, and you offered them as a sacrifice. I will not accept it from your hands, says the Lord Almighty.
Cursed be the man who was able, and who has a ram in his flock, and his vow is upon it,
and yet he sacrifices a blemished animal to the Lord. For I am a great King, says the Lord Almighty.
A merciful man does good to his own soul, but the merciless man destroys his own flesh.
The ungodly man does works of falsehood, but the seed of the righteous is the reward of truth.
A righteous son is born for life, but the pursuit of the ungodly leads to death. Crooked ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all the blameless are acceptable to him.
Whoever strikes hands in falsehood will not go unpunished, but whoever sows righteousness will receive a sure reward.
Like an earring in a pig's snout is beauty in an ill-natured woman. The desire of the righteous is wholly good, but the hope of the ungodly will perish.
There are those who sow seed and gather more; and there are those who gather what belongs to others and come to want.
Every blessed soul is upright, but a wrathful man is not seemly.

Whoever hoards grain, may he leave it behind to the [?] nations; and whoever makes grain hard to come by, may he be cursed by the people; but the blessing of the Lord is on the head of the generous man.
Whoever does good seeks good favor, but whoever seeks out evil, it will overtake him.
Whoever trusts in riches will fall, but whoever upholds the righteous will shine forth.
Whoever does not get along with his own household will inherit the winds, and the fool will serve the wise.
Whoever winks with the eye gathers sorrows for men, but whoever rebukes openly makes peace.
A fountain of life is in the hand of the righteous, but destruction will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
Hatred stirs up victory [i.e. contention], and love covers all who are not quarrelsome.
Whoever brings wisdom out of his lips strikes the senseless man. The wise keep knowledge, but the ruin of the weak [?] is poverty.
Righteous work brings about life, but the fruit of the lawless is sin.
Wisdom guards the way of these times [?], and the Lord guards the ways of life; but instruction that goes unreproved goes astray.
The righteous hide enmity with their lips, but those who bring out abuse are fools.
Sinners do not escape from much talk; be restrained, so that you may be sensible with your lips.
For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek me, and you will live.
Do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath, for Gilgal will surely be carried off into captivity, and Bethel will become as though it had never been.
Seek the Lord and you will live, so that [lest?] the house of Joseph blaze up like fire and devour it, and there be no one to put it out for the house of Israel.
He who makes judgment on high and has established righteousness on the earth;
he who makes all things, and turns the shadow of death into dawn, and darkens the day into night;
he who calls the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: the Lord is his name;
he who deals out ruin on the strong and brings misery on the fortress.
They hated the one who rebukes in the gates and loathed the holy word. Therefore, because they oppressed the poor and you took choice gifts from them,
you built houses for yourselves but you will not live in them; you planted pleasant vineyards but you will not drink their wine.
For I know your many acts of ungodliness, and your sins are great: you trample the righteous, take bribes, and drive the poor away from the gates.
Therefore whoever understands at that time will keep silent, for it is an evil time. Seek good and not evil, so that you may live.
And so it will be, says the Lord, and the Lord God Almighty will be with you, just as you said.
Hate evil and love good, and restore justice in the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.
For your name's sake, O Lord, be merciful. To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
I spread out repentance, which [?] standing [?].
And the Lord God said to Samuel: How long will you mourn for Saul, since I too have rejected him so that he no longer reigns over Israel?
And the Lord God said to Samuel: Fill that horn of yours with oil and come, and I will send you to Jesse in Bethlehem, for I have seen a king for myself among his sons.
And Samuel said: How can I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me. The Lord said to him:
Take a heifer from the cattle in your hand and say: “I am going to offer a sacrifice to the Lord.”
And call Jesse and his sons to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you are to do; and anoint for me as king the one I name to you.
And Samuel did as the Lord told him. He went to Bethlehem, and the elders of that city were astonished at his coming and said to him:
“Is your coming peaceful, O seer?” And he said: “In peace. I have come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord.
Sanctify yourselves and rejoice [?] with me today at this sacrifice.” And he sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice.
And when they came, he saw Eliab and said: “Surely the Lord's anointed is before him?”
The Lord said to Samuel: “Do not look at his face or at the form of his stature, for I have rejected him.
For God does not see as a man sees: a man looks at the face, but God looks at the heart.”
And Jesse called Abinadab, and he came before Samuel, and Samuel said: “The Lord has not chosen this one either.”
And Jesse brought his seven sons before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse: “The Lord has not chosen any of these.”
Samuel said to Jesse: “Are these all your boys?” Jesse said to him: “There is still one more, the youngest, and he is tending the flock.”
And Samuel said to Jesse: “Send and bring him, for I will not sit down [?] until he comes here.”
And Jesse sent and brought David before Samuel. He was ruddy of face, with beautiful eyes, and good in appearance before the Lord.
And the Lord said to Samuel: “Arise and anoint him before his brothers.” And the Holy Spirit came upon David from that day onward.
And Samuel arose and went to Armathaim. And the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord seized him and choked him.
And his servants said to him: “Behold, an evil spirit from the Lord is choking you.
Speak, lord, to your servants who are before you, and let them seek for our lord a man who knows how to play and sing on the harp.
And whenever the evil spirit from God is upon you, he will play and sing on his harp, and it will be well with you, and he will give you relief.”
And Saul said to his servants: “Find me a man who knows how to play and sing, and bring him to me.”
One of his servants answered and said to him: “I have seen one of the sons of Jesse in Bethlehem who knows how to play and sing.
The man is intelligent, brave in battle, mighty in strength, wise in speech, and good in deeds, and moreover the Lord is with him.”
And Saul sent a messenger to Jesse and said: “Send me David your son, who is out with the flock.”
And Jesse took a donkey [?], loaded on it a sack of bread, a skin of wine, and one kid of the goats, and sent them to Saul by the hand of David his son.
And David stood before him, and David became the bearer of his bow and quiver.
And Saul sent to Jesse and said: “Let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.”
And whenever the evil spirit from the Lord came upon Saul, David would take the harp in his hand and play,
and Saul would be refreshed and it would be well with him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
And in the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up onto the pillar of Balaam [?], and from there he showed him a small part of that people.
And Balaam said to Balak: "Build me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bull-calves and seven rams."
And Balak did as Balaam had told him, and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
