And Balaam said to Balak: "Stand by your sacrifice, and I will go. And God will appear to me in a vision, and I will tell you the word that he reveals."
And Balak stood by his offering. And Balaam went to inquire of God, and he went straight on.
And God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said: "I have prepared seven altars, and I have offered a calf and a ram on each altar."
And the Lord put a word in Balaam's mouth and said: "Speak thus."
And he returned to him, and Balak was standing by his whole burnt offerings, and all the princes of Moab with him. And the Spirit of God was upon him.
And he took up his parable and said: "Balak king of Moab summoned me from Mesopotamia, from the princes [?] of the East, and said:
'Come and curse Jacob, and come and curse Israel.' How shall I curse one whom the Lord does not curse? Or how shall I curse one whom God does not curse?
But from the tops of the mountains I see him, from the hills I behold him. Behold, a people will dwell alone and shall be reckoned among the nations.
Who has searched out the race of Jacob, or who will count the companies of Israel?
Let my soul die with the souls of the righteous, and let my offspring be like their offspring."
And Balak said to Balaam: "What is this you have done to us? I summoned you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them with a blessing."
And Balaam said to Balak: "Shall I not speak what God has put in my mouth? Shall I not take care to speak this?"
And Balak said to him: "Come with me again to another place, from which you will not see them all, but will see only a small part of them, and curse them for me from there."
And he took him to the field of the watchmen, to the top of the hewn rock, and built seven altars there, and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
And Balaam said to Balak: "Stand by that sacrifice of yours, and I will go to inquire of God."
And God met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said: "Return to Balak and speak thus." And he returned.
And Balak was standing by his whole burnt offering, and all the princes with him, and he said to him: "What did God say to you?"
And he took up his parable and said: "Rise, Balak, and hear; give ear, you witness, son of Zippor.
God is not like a man, that he should waver, nor like a son of man, that he should be angry. Shall he speak and not do it?
Shall he say and not abide by it? Behold, I have been brought to bless; I will bless and I will not turn it back. There shall be no trouble in Jacob.
He shall not see trouble in Israel. The Lord his God is with him, and glorious rulers are among him.
It is God who brought him out of Egypt; he is like the glory of the unicorn.
For there is no augury in Jacob, nor any divination in Israel. In due season it shall be told to Jacob and to Israel what God will do.
Behold, the people shall rise up like a lion's whelp and shall rage like a lion. It shall not lie down until it eats the prey and drinks the blood of the wounded.
And Balak said to Balaam: Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all.
Balaam answered Balak and said to him: Did I not tell you, saying: The word that God speaks to me, that I will do?
And Balak said to Balaam: Come, and I will take you to another place, in case it pleases God, and curse them for me from there.
And Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which stretches toward the wilderness.
And Balaam said to Balak: Build me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven calves and seven rams.
And Balak did as Balaam told him, and offered a calf and a ram on each altar.
And Balaam saw that it was good in the Lord's sight to bless Israel. So he did not go to seek the Lord through auguries as he usually did, and he turned his face toward the wilderness.
And Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and he saw the Spirit of God upon him.
And Balaam son of Beor took up his parable and said, the man who truly saw;
who saw the vision of God in sleep, with his eyes open: How good are your houses, O Jacob, and your tents, O Israel!
They are like shady glens and like gardens by the rivers, and like tents that the Lord pitched and not man, and like fir trees at the water's edge.
One shall come forth from his seed and shall rule over many nations, and his kingdom shall be exalted and shall increase.

God led them out of Egypt; his glory is like the unicorn's. He shall devour the nations of his enemies, he shall suck out their fat along with the marrow, and with his arrows he shall strike his enemies.
[?] he lay down and rested like a lion and like a lion's whelp; who shall rouse him?
Those who bless him shall be blessed, and those who curse him shall be cursed.
And Balak grew furious with Balaam and struck his hands together, and Balak said to Balaam:
I called you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them a third time.
Now flee to your own place. I said that I would honour you greatly, but now you have been deprived of my honour.
And Balaam said to Balak: Did I not also tell your messengers whom you sent to me, saying:
'Even if Balak should give me a house full of silver or gold, I could not go beyond the word of the Lord to do anything good or bad of my own accord;
but whatever the Lord tells me, that I will say'? And now I am going to my own place. Come, I will tell you what this people will do to your people in the last days.
And Balaam son of Beor said, he who truly heard the words of God,
and who knew with the knowledge of God, and saw a vision of God in sleep, his eyes being opened: "I shall show him, but not now; I call him blessed, but he is not near.
He will shine forth like a star out of Jacob, and a man will rise up out of Israel, and he will crush the rulers of Moab."
And hear this, what the Lord was saying. The Lord said: "Arise and plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
Hear the Lord's voice, you hills, the judgment of the Lord, and you valleys, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a case against his people, and he will argue it with Israel.
"My people, what have I done to you? How have I troubled you, or how have I wearied you? Answer me!
For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of bondage, and I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before you.
My people, remember what Balak king of Moab plotted against you, and how Balaam
son of Beor answered him, from the measuring-lines of the allotments as far as Gilgal, so that the righteousness of the Lord may be known."
With what shall I come before the Lord and take hold of my God Most High? Shall I come before him with sacrifices, with year-old calves?
Will the Lord accept thousands of rams, or tens of thousands of choice lambs?
Shall I give my firstborn for ungodliness, and the fruit of my womb for the sin of their soul?
I will tell you, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requires of you: only the fruit of righteousness, and that you love mercy and be ready to walk with your God.
The voice of the Lord will call out to the city, and he will save those who fear his name.
Give heed to the voice of prayer. To my words:
And after those days the king of the Egyptians died.
And the Lord said to Moses in Midian: "Go back to Egypt, for all those who sought your life have died."
So Moses took his wife and his children, set them on [?], and returned to Egypt. And Moses took the rod from God in his hand.
And the Lord said to Moses: "As you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the signs I have put in your hand.
But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will not let the people go. And you shall say to Pharaoh: Thus says the Lord: Israel is my firstborn son.
Let my people go, so that they may serve me. But if you refuse to let them go, beware: I will kill your son, your firstborn."
And on the way, at the lodging place, an angel of the Lord met him and sought to kill him.
And Zipporah took a sharp stone [?] and circumcised her son, and fell at his feet and said: "The blood of my son's circumcision has stopped."
And the angel went away from him, because she said: "The blood of my child's circumcision has stopped."
And the Lord said to Aaron: "Go out into the wilderness to meet Moses." And he went out and met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.
And Moses told all these words of the Lord, for which he had sent him, and all the signs which he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron came and gathered the elders of the children of Israel.
And Aaron spoke all the words which God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
And the people believed and rejoiced, because the Lord had looked upon the sons of Israel and had seen their affliction.
And the people bowed down and worshipped the Lord. And after this Moses and Aaron came before Pharaoh and said to him:
"Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Send out my people, so that they may serve me in the wilderness."
And Pharaoh said: "Who is the Lord, that I should listen to his voice and let the sons of Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go."
They said to him: "The God of the Hebrews has summoned us. Let us go a three days' journey, so that we may offer sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest death or the sword befall us."
Pharaoh, the king of the Egyptians, said to them: "Moses and Aaron, why are you turning my people away from their work?
Go, each of you, to your own work." And Pharaoh said: "See, the people of the land have now become numerous.
Let us not, then, give them rest from their work." And Pharaoh gave orders to the taskmasters and the scribes:
"Do not give straw any more for making bricks, as you did yesterday and the day before;
let them go and gather straw for themselves. The fixed quota of bricks which they made day by day, impose
on them; do not reduce it at all. For they are idle, and that is why they cry out and say: 'Let us go and offer sacrifice to the Lord our God.'
Make the work heavy on these men, and let them be occupied with it, and not be occupied with empty words."
And the taskmasters and the scribes hurried the people and said to them: "Thus says Pharaoh: Straw will no longer be given to you.
Go and gather straw for yourselves wherever you can find it, and you shall not reduce your quota by even one."
And the people scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
And the taskmasters pressed them, saying: "Complete your appointed work, just as when straw was given to you."
And the scribes of the sons of Israel, who had been set over them by Pharaoh's taskmasters, were beaten, and they were told:
"Why have you not completed your quota of bricks today, as you did yesterday and the day before?"
The scribes of the sons of Israel went in before Pharaoh, crying out and saying: "Why do you treat your servants like this?
They give us no straw, and yet you tell us to make the same number of bricks? And see, your servants are beaten; you are wronging your people."
Pharaoh said to them: "You are idle, you are idle, and that is why you say: 'Let us go and serve the Lord our God.'
Now go and work. For straw will not be given to you, and you shall deliver to me the quota of bricks."
And when the scribes of the sons of Israel saw that they were in trouble, as they were being told:
"You shall not reduce the daily quota of bricks," they met Moses and Aaron, who were coming to meet them, just as they were coming out from Pharaoh.
And they said to them: "May the Lord look upon you and judge, because you have made our scent loathsome before Pharaoh and before his servants, putting a sword into their hands to kill us."
Moses turned to the Lord and said: "Lord, why have you done evil to this people? Why did you send me?
Ever since I came to Pharaoh to speak to him in your name, they have done evil to this people, and you have not remembered your people."
And the Lord said to Moses: "See what I will do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand I will bring them out of the land of Egypt."
God spoke to Moses and said: "I am the Lord, who appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I am their God, but I did not make known to them that my name is Lord.
And I established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, in which they lived as strangers, in which they dwelt.
And I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered your covenant.

Go and say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from the oppression of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from their affliction, and I will redeem you with an uplifted arm and with great judgment.
And I will be your God, and you will know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
And I will bring you into the land over which I stretched out my hand to give it to Abraham. I, the Lord, will give it to you as your portion."
Moses spoke thus to the children of Israel, but they did not listen to him because of their discouragement and their harsh labors.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said: "Go and speak to Pharaoh the king, so that he lets the children of Israel go out of the land of Egypt."
Moses spoke before the Lord and said: "Look, the children of Israel have not listened to me. How then will Pharaoh listen to me, since I cannot speak well?"
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a command concerning Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, that they should bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
And the angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Salon [?], to Bethel, to the house of Israel, and said to them:
"The Lord brought you up into the land that he swore to your fathers to give to you, and he said to you: 'I will never break my covenant.'
And you must not make a covenant with those who live in this land, and you must not worship their gods,
but you must smash their idols and tear down their altars.' Yet you did not listen to my voice when you did this.
So I have said: 'I will no longer remove the people whom I said I would drive out before you, and they will become a stumbling block to you.'"
And when the angel spoke all these words to the children of Israel, the people raised their voices and wept.
For this reason that place was named Weeping. And they offered a sacrifice to the Lord there.
And Joshua sent the people away, and the children of Israel each went to their own home.
And the children of Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua,
who knew the work God had done for Israel. And Joshua son of Nun, the servant of God, died at the age of one hundred and ten.
And they buried him within the borders of his inheritance, in Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
And all those generations were gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know the Lord or the works that he had done for Israel.
And they did evil before the Lord and served Balaam [?].
And they abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they went after foreign gods,
the gods of the peoples around them, and they angered the Lord. And they served Baal and Astarte.
And the Lord's anger burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hands of those who took them captive, and they carried them off as captives.
And he gave them into the hands of their enemies, among all those with whom they had committed fornication. And the hand of the Lord was against them for harm,
as he had said and as he had sworn. And he afflicted them greatly. And he raised up a judge for them and rescued them from the hands of those who took them captive.
But they would not listen to their judges either, for they went whoring after foreign gods and worshipped them,
and they angered the Lord. They quickly turned aside from the way in which their fathers had walked, obeying the commandments of the Lord, and they did not do so.
And the Lord raised up a judge for them, and the Lord was with that judge, and he rescued them from the hands of their enemies all the days of that judge,
for God relented because of their groaning on account of those who oppressed them.
And when the judge died, they would turn back and become even more corrupt than their fathers, going after foreign gods to serve them and worship them,
and they would not turn back from their stubborn way. And the Lord's anger burned against Israel, and he said:
"Because this nation has abandoned my covenant so many times, the covenant I commanded their fathers, and they have not listened to my voice,
I will no longer go on driving out anyone before them from the nations that Joshua left."
And he left them in order to test Israel by them, to see whether or not they would keep the ways of the Lord and walk in them, as their fathers had kept them.
And the Lord left these nations. He did not destroy them quickly, and he did not give them into the hands of Joshua.
And these are the nations that Joshua left, so that he might test Israel by them: all those who had not known any of the wars of Canaan,
for the sake of the generations of the children of Israel, so that they might teach them war, since those who came before had not known it.
These were the five rulers of the foreigners, and all the Canaanites and the Sidonians and the Hivites who lived in Lebanon, from the mountain of Galbana [?] of Hermon as far as Lobeba [?].
And they remained among them so that he might test Israel, to see whether they would listen to the commandments of the Lord that he had commanded their fathers through Moses.
And the children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites and the Girgashites, the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Jebusites.
And they took the daughters of these peoples as wives for themselves and gave their own daughters as wives to their sons, and they served their gods before the Lord.
And they forgot the Lord their God and served Balaam [?] and the sacred groves.
And the Lord's anger burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hands of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Assyria, of Mesopotamia of the rivers, and they served him for eight years.
And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and he raised up a savior for Israel, and he delivered them: Othniel son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb.
And they listened to him. And the Spirit of God was upon him, and he went out to battle. And the Lord gave Cushan-rishathaim, king of Assyria, into his hands, and his hand was heavy upon him.
Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has done great things.
Do not be afraid, you beasts, for the plains of the wilderness have turned green, for the tree has brought forth its fruit, and the fig trees have given their strength.
And you children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, for he has given you food in righteousness;
and he will send rain down on you, the early rain and the late rain, as before.
And your threshing floors will be filled with wheat, and your presses will overflow with wine and oil.
And I will repay you for the years that the locust, the fly, the blight and the worm devoured, my great army, which I sent against you, said the Lord.
And you will eat your fill and praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonders among you; and my people shall never be put to shame.
And you will know that I am the Lord your God in the midst of Israel, and there is no other besides me; and my people shall never be put to shame.
In you, O Lord, I have put my hope; let me not be put to shame. Incline your ear to me.
Deliver me, O Lord my God, for you [?]
And it came to pass
that when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of the many-colored garment that he was wearing, and they took him and threw him into the pit.
Now the pit was empty; there was no water in it. And they sat down to eat bread, and they lifted up their eyes, and behold, they saw merchants, Ishmaelite travelers,
coming from Gilead, and their camels were loaded with gum and balm, and they were going down to Egypt.
Judah said to his brothers: "What profit is there if we kill this brother of ours and shed his blood?
Come, let us sell him to those Ishmaelites, but let our hand not be upon him, for he is our brother." His brothers listened to him.
And the Midianite merchants came by, and they drew Joseph up and handed him over to the Ishmaelites, and they took him down to Egypt.
Reuben returned to the pit and did not find him in the pit, and he tore his garments.
And he returned to his brothers and said: "The boy is not there, so where has he gone?"
Then they took Joseph's garment and slaughtered a young goat, and they stained his garment with the blood.
And they sent the many-colored garment, brought it to their father, and said: "We found this.
See whether it is your son's garment." And he said: "It is my son's garment.
An evil beast has snatched him from me, an evil beast has devoured him." And Jacob tore his garments and put on sackcloth, and he mourned for his son many days.
All his sons and his daughters gathered together and came to comfort him.
And he would not be comforted, and he said: "I will go down to my son in Hades." And his father wept for him.
But those Ishmaelite merchants sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, the eunuch, [?] (the word "matakaran-" is unclear).
And at that very time Judah went away from his brothers and went to a certain man of Adullam, whose name was Hirah.
And there Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite, whose name was Shua, and he brought her and took her as his wife.
She conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Er. And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
And she bore yet again a son, and she called his name Shelah. She was in Chezib when she bore them.
And Judah brought a wife for his firstborn son, whose name was Tamar. And Er, his firstborn son, was wicked before the Lord, and God killed him.
Judah said to Onan: "Go in to your brother's wife, marry her as her brother-in-law, and raise up offspring for your brother." Onan understood that the offspring would not be his.
And so, whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he spilled the seed on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
This deed was evil before God, because it was so, and the Lord put him to death too. Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law:
"Remain a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up," for he said, "Lest he too die like his brothers."
And Tamar went and remained a widow in her father's house.
At that time Joshua summoned the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
and said: "You have heard all that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded, and you have obeyed my voice in everything, just as he commanded you.
And you have not abandoned your brothers these days and many more, up to this very day.
You have kept the commandments of the Lord your God. And now the Lord your God has given rest to our brothers, as he told them;
now therefore turn back and go to your homes, to the land of your possession, which Moses gave you beyond the Jordan.
But take great care to do the commandments and the laws that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you: to love the Lord your God and to walk in all his ways,
to keep his commandments, to be an inheritance [?], and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul."
And Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their homes. To the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a portion in Bashan, and he sent them away.
And when he sent them away to their homes, Joshua blessed them and spoke to them thus.
And they went to their homes with great wealth and with very many flocks, for they had divided the spoil of their enemies with their brothers.
And the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh departed from the sons of Israel at Shiloh, from the land of Canaan,
to go to Gilead, to the land of their inheritance, which they had taken possession of by the command of the Lord through Moses.
And they came to Gilead of the Jordan, which is in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar by the Jordan, an altar great to look at. And the sons of Israel heard of it and said:
"Look, the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar at the borders of the land of Canaan, at Gilead of the Jordan, across from the sons of Israel."
And the sons of Israel gathered at Shiloh to go up and make war on them.
And the sons of Israel sent Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the high priest, to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead,
and ten chiefs with him, one chief from each father's house out of all the tribes of Israel. The chiefs of the fathers' houses were the commanders of thousands of Israel.
And they came to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead, and they spoke with them and said:
"This is what the congregation of the sons of Israel says: What is this sin that you have committed before the Lord God of Israel, turning away from the Lord today,
in building an altar for yourselves and rebelling against the Lord?
Is the sin of Peor a small thing to you? We have not been cleansed of it even to this day, and because of it wrath came upon this congregation of the Lord.
And you have turned away from the Lord. If you turn away from the Lord today, tomorrow wrath will be upon all Israel.
And now, if the land you have inherited is too small, cross over into this land that the Lord possesses, where the Lord's tabernacle dwells,
and settle among us. But do not rebel against the Lord by building yourselves an altar apart from the altar of the Lord our God.
Did not Achan son of Zerah sin in the matter of the devoted thing, and the wrath of God came upon the whole congregation of Israel? He was only one man. Did he die alone for his sin?"
The sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the commanders of thousands of Israel and said:
"God, God is the Lord! God, God the Lord knows, and Israel itself shall know: if we have sinned before the Lord by rebellion, may the Lord not save us this day.
If we have built ourselves an altar in order to rebel against the Lord our God,
to offer an offering of sacrifices on it, or to make an offering of peace on it, may the Lord himself call us to account.
Rather, we did this out of fearful concern, and we said: 'Some day your children may say to our children: "What do you have to do with the Lord God of Israel?
For the Lord has set the Jordan as a boundary between you and us, and you have no share in the Lord."'
And so your sons would make our sons strangers, so that they would not serve the Lord.
And we decided to do this: to build this altar, not for sacrifices, nor for offerings,
but so that it might be a witness between you and us, and between your children and ours after us,
so that they may perform the service of the Lord before him with our produce, our sacrifices and our offerings,
and so that your children may not say to our children: 'You have no share in the Lord.'
And we said: If it should ever happen that they say this to us or to our descendants in time to come,
then they will say: See now the likeness of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for offerings of produce nor for sacrifices,
but it is a witness between us and you, and between our children and yours.
Far be it from us to turn away from the Lord on this very day, as if we had turned away from the Lord and built an altar for offerings of produce and
for peace offerings and for sacrifices of salvation, apart from the altar of the Lord our God, which is before his tabernacle.
And when Phinehas the priest and all the leaders of the congregation who were with him heard
these words that the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh spoke to them, these words pleased them.
And Phinehas the priest said to the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
Today we know that the Lord is with us, because you have not committed a sin before the Lord God.

And Phinehas the priest and the leaders who were with him turned back and went from the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, out of the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and told them these words.
And this word seemed good to them, and they blessed the God of the sons of Israel. And Phinehas spoke to the sons of Israel and said to them:
Do not go up any longer to fight against them and to destroy the land of the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. And they settled on the mountain.
And Joshua gave the altar the name 'Altar of Reuben and Gad and of the half-tribe of Manasseh,' and said to them:
This is a witness between them that the Lord God is their God.
The thoughts of the righteous are just judgments, but the ungodly train themselves in deceit.
The words of the ungodly are deceitful, but the mouth of the righteous will deliver them. Wherever the ungodly man turns, he will perish, but the houses of the righteous will stand firm.
The mouth of the understanding man is praised by people, but the sick at heart is despised.
Better is a man in a lowly position who serves himself than one who seeks honor and lacks bread.
The righteous man takes care of the lives of his livestock, but the inner parts of the ungodly are merciless.
He who works his own land will have his fill of bread, but those who chase after vanity are senseless. Whoever takes pleasure in passing his time over wine will leave disgrace in his own dwellings.
The desires of the wicked are evil, but the roots of the godly are in strongholds.
Through the sin of his lips the sinner falls into a snare, but the righteous man escapes from it.
He who looks with sincerity will be shown mercy, but he who confronts others at the gates will bring distress even on people.
From the fruit of his mouth a man's soul will be filled with bread, and the reward of his lips will be given to him.
The ways of fools seem right in their own eyes, but the wise man listens to counsel.
The fool shows his anger day after day, but the sensible man hides an insult.
The righteous man declares open faithfulness, but the witness of liars is deceitful. There are those who speak words that cut like a sword.
But the tongue of the wise heals. The lips of the righteous make testimony straight, but a false witness has a lying tongue.
There is deceit in the heart of the one who does evil, but those who want to make peace will rejoice.
Nothing false pleases justice, but the ungodly are filled with evil.
Deceitful lips are hateful to the Lord, but the one who keeps faith is accepted by him.
A man of understanding is a throne of knowledge, but the heart of fools will meet with a curse.
The hand of the chosen will easily take hold, but the deceitful will be taken captive.
Thus says the Most High, who dwells in the heights, holy among the holy ones, whose name is Lord and Most High, who rests among the holy ones,
and he gives patience to the faint-hearted and gives life to those who are humble in heart.
"I will not hold resentment forever to take vengeance, nor will I always be angry with you, for the spirit will go out from me, and I have made the breath of life."
"Because of sin I afflicted him for a little while. I punished him and turned my face away from him. He was afflicted and went about his ways in sorrow."
"And I saw his ways and healed him, and I gave him true comfort, peace upon peace, and to those who are near"
Lord, hear me [?]. To my cry:
Remember, and do not forget
how much you angered the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious toward the Lord.
At Horeb, too, you angered the Lord God, and he was so angry with you that he was ready to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the two tablets of the commandments of the law, the law that the Lord gave you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
And the Lord gave me two tablets of stone, written by the finger of God, and on them were written all the words of God that the Lord had spoken to you.
At the end of the forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two tablets of the law.
And he said to me, "Get up and go down from here quickly, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have acted lawlessly.
They have turned aside from the way that you commanded them, for they have made themselves an idol."
And the Lord said to me, "I have spoken to you once and twice, and I said to you: I have seen this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people.
Let me alone, and I will destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. And I will make you into a great nation, much mightier than they are."
So I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire. The two tablets were in my hands.
And I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God. You had made yourselves an idol and had turned aside from the way that the Lord your God had commanded you.
And I took the two tablets and threw them out of both my hands, and I smashed them in front of you.
And I made supplication before the Lord, as before, a second time for forty days and forty nights.
I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all your sins that you committed by doing evil before the Lord God, to provoke him to anger.
And I was afraid of his wrath and his anger, for the Lord was angry with you, enough to destroy you completely.
And the Lord listened to me at that time. And the Lord was very angry with Aaron, enough to destroy him; and I prayed for Aaron at that time.
And your sin that you had made, the calf, I took and burned it with fire. I crushed it and ground it very fine,
until it became like dust, and I scattered it into the stream that comes down from the mountain.
And at the Burning, at the Testing and at the Graves of Craving you provoked the Lord your God to anger.
And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said to you, 'Go up and take possession of the land that I have given you,'
you disobeyed the Lord your God and his words. You did not believe him, and you did not listen to his voice. You have been disobedient to the Lord ever since he revealed himself to you.
And I made supplication before the Lord for forty days and forty nights, the whole time that I made supplication, because the Lord had said he would destroy you.
And I prayed to the Lord and said: 'O Lord God, King of gods, do not destroy your people and your portion,
whom you redeemed by your great power, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and a raised arm.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their ungodliness and their sin,
or else the inhabitants of the land you brought us out of might say:
"The Lord was not able to bring them into the land that he promised to give them. He hated them, and that is why he led them out, to destroy them in the wilderness."
These are your people and your portion, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt by your great power and your raised arm.'
At that time the Lord said to me: 'Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain, and make an ark of wood.
And I will write on those tablets the words that were written on the first tablets, which you smashed, and you will put them in the ark.'
So I made the ark of wood that does not rot, and I cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I went up the mountain, with the two tablets in my hands.
And he wrote on the tablets, as in the first writing, the ten words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire.
And the Lord gave them to me. Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark that I had made.
And they stayed there, as the Lord had commanded me. And the children of Israel set out from Beeroth of the sons of Joakim.
And there Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
And from there they set out for Gadgad, and from Gadgad for Itabed (Jotbathah), a land of the valley of portions [?].
At that time the Lord appointed the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord, to minister and to pray in his name, to this day.
For this reason the Levites have no portion or inheritance among their brothers; the Lord God is their portion, as he told them.
And I stood on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and the Lord heard me at that time and did not wish to destroy you.
And the Lord said to me: "Go, set out before this people, and let them go in and take possession of the land which I swore to their fathers to give them."
And now you, too, are only men; or has wisdom come to an end with you?
For my heart, too, is like yours; I am not more foolish than you. For a righteous and blameless man has become a byword.
For at an appointed time he was made ready to fall at the hands of others, and his houses to be plundered by the lawless.
But let no one who is wicked trust that he will be innocent, nor anyone who provokes the Lord, as though there would be no judgment for him.
But ask the four-footed beasts, and see whether they will tell you anything. Speak to the earth, and see whether it will say anything to you, or whether the fish of the sea will tell it to you.
Who among all these does not know that the hand of the Lord made this?
Is not the soul of all living things in his hand, and the breath of every man?
For the mind judges words, and the palate tastes food. Is not wisdom found through long time, or knowledge through length of days?
From him come wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his. If he tears down, who will build up?
Or if he shuts men in, who else will open? If he holds back the water, he dries up the earth; if he lets it loose, he destroys the earth all at once and overturns it.
From him come strength and power; knowledge and understanding are his.
He sends counselors into captivity and confounds the judges of the earth. He seats kings on thrones and girds them with the belt of might.
He sends priests away into captivity and overthrows the mighty of the earth. He alters the lips of the faithful, and he knows the understanding of the elders.
He pours contempt on rulers and heals the lowly. He brings the depths of darkness out into light from the shadows of death.
He leads the nations astray and lets them go; he brings down the sons of the tribes and leads them.
He alters the hearts of the rulers of the earth and makes them stray on a road they did not know.
They walk in darkness and not in light, and they wander like drunkards.
Behold, my eye has seen all this, and my ear has heard it. And I know as much as you know, and I have no less understanding than you.
Not only that, but I would speak to the Lord, and I will argue my case before him, if he wishes.
But you are all false physicians and evil comforters. If only you would keep silent, and it would be counted to you as wisdom.
Hear the reproofs of my mouth, and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
What is this? Do you not speak before the Lord, and plot deceit in his presence?
Or will you hold yourselves back and make yourselves judges? Would it be good if he searched you out as well?
Even if you do everything and attach yourselves to him, he will rebuke you no less, even if you have secretly shown partiality [?].
Will not fear of him make you tremble? Then that boasting of yours will become like ashes, and your bodies like clay.
Be silent, so that I may speak and find relief from my anger. I will take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hands.
If the Mighty One lays hands on me, as he knows, I will still speak and argue my case before him.
And this will be your salvation, for deceit will not come before him.
Hear my words, hear them, for I will tell you, if only you will listen to me.
Look, I have drawn near to my judgment. I know that I will be shown to be righteous. Who is the one who will contend with me?
For then I would fall silent and perish. It is right for me to keep still, and then I will not hide from your face.
Take your hand away from me, and do not let fear of you terrify me. Then call me, and I will listen to you; or speak to me, and I will answer you.
How many are my sins? Teach me where they come from. Why do you hide from me and count me as your adversary?
Am I afraid of a leaf stirred by the wind? Or do you oppose me as you would a [?] that the breeze carries away?
For you write down all evils against me, the sins of my youth. You have set my feet in a stumbling block,
you have watched over all my deeds and reached the soles of my feet, which grow old like a wineskin, or like a garment eaten by moths.
For a man born of woman lives a short time and is full of wrath. He is like a flower that blooms and falls; he passes away like a mere shadow and does not remain.
Or have you taken account even of him?
But his flesh [?] and his soul mourned.

For there will be a visitation upon the idols of the nations, because among created things they have become a profit [?] and a temptation for the souls of men, like a snare for the feet of the foolish.
For the idol is the beginning of apostasy, and their invention is the corruption of life. They did not exist anywhere from the beginning, and they will not exist forever.
For they entered the world through the vain imagination of men; because of this a swift end was sent upon them.
For a father, lamenting in untimely grief because his child was taken early, made an image of the person who had once died,
and now honours him as a god, and he handed down mysteries of worship to those under him.
Then, over time, that ungodliness and the [?] became established in this way, as though it had been laid down as a law, and idols were worshipped by command of rulers.
People could not honour these rulers face to face because they lived far away, so they portrayed the distant face and made a visible image of the king,
So that they might eagerly flatter him, though far away, as if he were present there, by the command of the law, until the honour paid by the craftsman later drew in even those who did not know him,
for he, perhaps wishing to please the ruler, used his craft to make the likeness better than it was.
So that righteousness [?] might come to be hated through that more excellent work, he counted as an object of worship a man who had been honoured only a short time before.
And he made this a snare for this world, for people serve some evil or some tyranny, and they gave the name that may not be shared to stones and wood.
And then this snare of ignorance about God was no longer enough for them. Instead they lived in a great war of ignorance, and they call such great evils peace.
And they [practise] the [?] of children for idols, or secret mysteries, or mockery with altered laws, and they hold gatherings.
And they no longer keep either life or holy marriage pure; one man kills his neighbour or [his neighbour's] offspring.
And they have everything mixed together: blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption and faithlessness, and the defilement of souls,
disorder in marriage, adultery and licentiousness. And the worship of lawless idols is the beginning, the cause and the end of every evil.
For either they rejoice and go astray, or they prophesy falsehood, or they live by lies, or they swear falsely again and again.
For they trust in lifeless idols, and they swear wickedly and expect no harm.
But judgement will come upon them for both things together, because they thought wickedly about God when they looked to idols, and because they swore wickedly.
It will not be the power of those [idols] that comes against them, but [against] those who sin: punishment comes upon the liars for breaking the law.
But you, our God, are kind and true and patient, and you govern all things with mercy.
And even if we sin, we are yours, and we know your power. But if we do not sin, we know that we are counted as yours.
For knowing you is complete righteousness, and your righteousness is the root of immortality.
To Jacob my servant.
We will give thanks to you, O God, we will give thanks. Let us tell of wonders.
All the earth. The heavens declare.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, and whoever keeps it will be filled with the spirit.
A fool despises his father's instruction, but whoever keeps the commandment will be wiser.
Where righteousness abounds there is great strength, but the ungodly will utterly perish from the earth.
In the house of the righteous there is great strength, but the fruits of the ungodly will perish. The lips of the wise are bound by knowledge, but the hearts of the wicked are not careful.
The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of the righteous are acceptable before him.
The ways of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but he loves those who look to righteousness.
The instruction of the innocent will be recognized by those who pass by; but those who hate reproof die in disgrace.
Hell and destruction are plain before the Lord; how much more the hearts of men!
The uninstructed man will not love the one who reproves him, and he does not take counsel with the wise.
When the heart is glad, the face is glad too; but those who are in sorrow have a sorrowful face as well.
An upright heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of the uninstructed knows evil.
At all times the eyes of the wicked look out for evil, but the good are always at rest.
A small portion with the fear of God is better than great treasures without fear.
Hospitality with vegetables, with love and gratitude, is better than calves slaughtered from the stalls with enmity.
A hot-tempered man prepares himself for killing, but a patient man calms even what is about to happen.
A patient man puts out judgment, but the ungodly man stirs it up all the more.
The ways of the ungodly are strewn with thorns, but the ways of the brave are smooth.
And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it;
and if one member is glorified, all the members are glorified with it. You are the body of Christ, and individually members of it.
And God has appointed some in the churches: first apostles, second prophets,
third teachers, then powers, then gifts of healing, helps in struggles, and various kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Or are all prophets?
Or are all teachers? Or are all powers? Or do all have the gift of healing?
Or do all interpret? Be eager for the greater gift, and further, I will show you a more excellent way.
To all the Gentiles:
But I say to you, my beloved:
Do not be afraid of those who kill your body and after that have nothing more that they can do to you.
But I will show you whom you should fear: fear him who, after killing you, has power to cast you into Gehenna.
I tell you, fear him. Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten before God.
But the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid, for you are worth more than many sparrows.
And I tell you: everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
And whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
And when they bring you to the synagogues and before rulers and authorities, do not worry about how or what you will say, for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that hour what you ought to say.
Hear me, O Lord, for sweet [?]
[?] from you; for I am in distress, [?] until [?] deliver this [?]
My son, if you receive the commandments spoken by my soul and keep them hidden with you,
and your ear listens to wisdom, and you make them known beforehand as signs to your son, and you give your heart to understanding;
if you call out to wisdom and give your voice to understanding,
and if you search for it, then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from his mouth comes knowledge.
And he stores up life for those who walk uprightly; he helps them on their way, to guard the paths of righteousness, and he guards the ways of those who fear him.
Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and you will walk straight in all the paths of good.
If wisdom comes into your mind and knowledge into your soul, you will desire to do good, and good counsel will guard you,
and a pure mind will preserve you, to deliver you from the evil way and from the man who speaks what is not trustworthy.
Woe to those who have forsaken the paths of light and walked in places of darkness, who rejoice in wickedness and delight in evil perversity,
whose ways are crooked and whose places are perverse, so as to lead you away from the straight way and make you a stranger to righteousness of mind.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts:
Now I will bring back the captivity of Jacob and have mercy on the house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy house.
And they shall bear their disgrace, by which they were false to me, at the time when I settle them in their own land in peace, and there will no longer be anyone to make them afraid.
When I bring them back from the nations and gather them from all the lands of their enemies, I will be exalted before that great people.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God; I will reveal myself among the nations and gather them into their land, where I will leave none of them behind with them.
Because I have poured out the wrath of my anger on the house of Israel, said the Lord of hosts.
Do not be wise in your own eyes.
And let none of you repay evil for evil; take thought beforehand for what is good before God and before people.
If it is possible on your part, live in peace with all people.
Do not seek vengeance by yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath, for it is written: "Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord."
Rather, if your enemy is hungry, give him bread; and if he is thirsty, give him drink. By doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let every person submit to the higher authority, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.
Therefore whoever rises against that authority rises against God's command, and those who rise against it of their own accord will receive judgement.
For rulers are not a terror to those who do good, but to those who do evil.
Do you want to have no fear of the one in authority? Do good, and you will receive praise from him. For he is God's servant for your good.
But if you do evil, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God's servant, an avenger of wrath on those who do evil.
Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath, but also for the sake of conscience.
For this reason you also pay tribute, for they are servants of God, and they attend diligently to this very labour.
Pay all that is owed: tribute to whom tribute is due, toll to whom toll is due, fear to whom fear is due, honour to whom honour is due.
Owe nothing to anyone, except to love one another, for whoever loves his neighbour has fulfilled the law.

"You shall not commit adultery, you shall not kill, you shall not steal, you shall not covet," and whatever other commandment there is, is fulfilled in this one saying: "You shall love your neighbour as yourself."
Love does no evil to a neighbour; love is the fulfilment of the law.
In you, O Lord, I have hoped; let not [?]
And he also told them a parable, to show that they ought always to pray and not lose heart in prayer.
And he said: "There was a certain judge in a city who did not fear God and was not ashamed before men. There was a certain widow in that same city.
She kept coming to him and saying to him, 'Give me justice against my adversary.' And for some time he would not listen to her.
Afterwards he said in his heart, 'Even though I do not fear God and am not ashamed before men, yet because this widow is always causing me trouble,
I will give her justice, so that she will not keep coming and wearying me.'" And the Lord said to them: "Hear now what that unjust judge says.
And will not God avenge his elect, who cry to him day and night, and is he long-suffering toward them?
I tell you, he will avenge them speedily. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised others:
"Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. The Pharisee stood and prayed thus by himself:
'Lord, I thank you that I am not like other men, robbers, liars, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.'
I fast twice in the week, and I give a tenth of everything I own.
But the tax collector stood far off and did not dare to lift up his eyes. Instead he beat his breast and said: "God, have mercy on me, this sinner."
I tell you: this man went down to his house justified rather than that Pharisee. For whoever exalts himself will be humbled;
and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
O Almighty, Most High, you know [?].
Those who [?] the cherubim:
For they are sweet to my palate. [Your word] is a lamp to [my] feet.
Who has sinned and repented [?].
And it came to pass,
when Isaac had grown old and his eyes had grown dim so that he could not see, that Isaac called his elder son Esau and said to him: "My son Esau."
And Esau said: "Here I am, lord." And Isaac said to him: "Look, I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death.
Now take your gear, your bow and your quiver, and go out to the field and hunt game for me. Bring it to me and make me a meal,
so that I may eat and be satisfied, and my soul may bless you while I am still alive and not yet dead."
Rebekah heard this while Isaac was speaking to his son Esau. And Esau went out to hunt for his father.
Rebekah called her son Jacob and said to him: "I heard your father speaking to your brother Esau. He said to him: 'Bring me game and make me a meal.
I will eat and bless you before the Lord your God while I am still alive and not yet dead.' Now, my son, listen to me and do as I tell you:
Go to your father's flock and bring me two young, fat kids, and I will make them into a meal for your father, the way he likes it.
Take it to your father so that he may eat, and your father may bless you while he is still alive and not yet dead."
Jacob said: "My brother is a hairy man, but I am smooth [note 1].
What if my father touches me? Then I will appear to my father as someone who mocks him, and I will receive a curse from my father and not a blessing."
His mother said to him: "Let that curse be on me, son. Just listen to me, and go and bring me what I am asking you for."
Jacob went to his father's flock and brought them to his mother. And his mother made a meal, the way his father liked it.
And Rebekah took the good clothing of her son Esau, which she had with her in the house, and dressed her son Jacob in it.
She wrapped the skins of the kids around his arms and his bare neck. And she put the meal and the bread into Jacob's hands.
And he brought it in to his father and said: "Father." And he said: "Here I am. Who are you, son?" And Jacob said: "I am Esau, your firstborn son."
I have done as you told me. Arise and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me.
Isaac said to his son: "How is it that you found it so quickly, my son?" And he said: "Because the Lord God put it in my way."
Isaac said to Jacob: "Come near, so that I may touch you with my hand, my son, to know whether you are my son Esau or not."
And Jacob came near to his father, and he touched him with his hand and said: "This voice is the voice of Jacob, but these hands are the hands of Esau."
And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau. And he blessed him.
And he said: "Are you my son Esau?" And he said: "I am." And he said: "Bring me some of your game, so that my soul may bless you."
And he brought it to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank. And Isaac said to him: "Come near to me so that I may kiss you, my son."
And he came near to him and kissed him. And he smelled the fragrance of his garments, and he blessed him and said:
"Behold, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a full field that the Lord has blessed.
May the Lord give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth, and an abundance of wheat and wine.
May nations serve you and princes bow down to you; be lord over your brother, and may your father's sons bow down to you.
May those who curse you be cursed, and may those who bless you be blessed!"
And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob and Jacob had gone out from his father's presence, that Esau his brother came in from hunting with his game.
He too prepared food for his father, and he came and said to him: "Let my father arise and eat of his son's game, so that your soul may bless me."
And Isaac his father said to him: "Who are you?" And he said: "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau." Isaac was astonished with great astonishment and said:
"Who then was it who hunted game for me and brought it to me? I ate of all of it before you came, and I blessed him, and he shall be blessed."
And it came to pass, when Esau heard these words of Isaac his father, that he cried out with a loud and bitter cry and said: "Bless me too, father."
Isaac said to him, "Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing."
And Esau said: "His name was rightly called Jacob, for this is the second time he has deceived me: first he took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing."
Esau said to his father: "Have you not kept even one blessing for me, father?" Isaac answered Esau and said:
"Since I have made him lord over you, made all his brothers his servants, and strengthened him with wheat and wine, what now shall I do for you, my son?"
Esau said to his father: "Do you have only one blessing? Bless me too, father." And because Esau was distressed, he cried out with a loud voice and wept.
Isaac his father answered and said: "Behold, your dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth and of the dew of heaven from above.
By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother. But the time will come when you break free and throw his yoke off your neck."
And Esau bore a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and Esau said in his heart:
"The days of my father's death are coming, and then I will kill my brother Jacob." These words of her elder son were told to Rebekah.
And she sent and called her younger son and said to him: "Behold, your brother Esau intends to kill you."
Now, my son, listen to my voice: get up and flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.
And stay with him until your brother's anger and wrath turn away from you and he forgets what you did to him.
And I will send and call you back from there. Otherwise he may kill you, and I would be bereaved of you both in one day.
And Rebekah said to Isaac: I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth.
If Jacob also takes a wife from the daughters of this land, what will my life be worth?
And the land was at rest for fifty years.
And Othniel, son of Kenaz, died. And the sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord.
And the Lord strengthened Eglon, king of Moab, against Israel, because they had done evil before the Lord.
And he brought with him all the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he came and struck Israel and took possession of the city of the Phoenicians.
And the sons of Israel served Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.
The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and God raised up for them a savior, Ehud, son of Gera, son of Jemini, a man who could use both hands equally well.
And the sons of Israel sent a gift by his hand to Eglon, king of Moab.
And Ehud made himself a two-edged sword, one span in length, and he girded it under his tunic
beneath his right thigh. And they presented the gift to Eglon, king of Moab; and Eglon was a very stout [?] man.
And when he had finished presenting the gift, he sent away the men who had carried the gift.
Eglon turned back from the carved images that were at Gilgal. Ehud said to him: I have a secret word for you.
Eglon said: Everyone go out. And all his attendants went out from him. And Ehud went in to him, and he was sitting in his summer upper chamber.
Ehud said to him: I have a word of God for you, O king. And King Eglon rose from his throne, close to him.
And as he rose, Ehud put out his left hand, drew the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into Eglon's belly,
and he drove even the hilt in after the blade, and the fat closed over the mouth of the wound, for the sword did not come out of his belly.
Ehud went outside and shut the doors of the upper chamber and locked them.
And he went away. And his servants came and looked, and saw that the doors of the upper chamber were shut, and they said:
Perhaps he is sitting alone inside on the seats of rest. And they waited until they were ashamed, and no one opened the doors of the upper chamber.
And they took the key and opened them. And behold, their lord had fallen to the ground and was dead.
And Ehud escaped while they were still in an uproar, and there was no one who took notice of him. And he passed beyond the carved images and escaped to Seirath.
And when Ehud came, they blew the horn trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went down, and he went before them.
And he said to them: "Come after me, for the Lord God has given your enemies, Moab, into your hands."
And they went down after him. They hurried and seized the fords of the Jordan and of Moab, and did not let anyone cross over.
And at that time they struck down about ten thousand men of Moab, all of them warriors and every one of them strong, and not a man escaped.
And on that day Moab was humbled under the hand of Israel, and the land was at rest for eighty years.
And Ehud judged them until his death.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
"Son of man, what is this proverb among the sons of Israel, which they repeat: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'?
As I live, says the Lord, from now on this proverb shall no longer be a saying in Israel.
For all souls are mine: as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine.
And the soul that sins, that soul shall die. But a man who is righteous, who does what is right,

who does not eat on the mountains, and does not let his eyes go after the desires of the house of Israel, and does not defile his neighbour's wife, and does not touch a woman while she is in her impurity;
who does not oppress anyone, and gives back the pledge to the debtor, and does not commit robbery, and gives his bread to the hungry and clothes the naked;
who does not lend his silver at interest and does not take increase, who turns his hand away from wrongdoing, and carries out righteous judgement between one man and his neighbour;
and who is perfect in my commandments and keeps my judgements so as to do them — such a man is righteous; he shall surely live, says the Lord.

If he fathers a son who is vile, a shedder of blood and a doer of sin, who does not walk in the righteous ways of his father, but eats on the mountains and defiles his neighbour's wife, oppresses the destitute
and the poor, commits robbery, does not give back the pledge, sets his eyes on idols, commits lawlessness,
lends silver at usury and takes increase — this one shall not live. Because he has done all these lawless deeds, he shall surely die, and his blood shall be upon him.
If he fathers a son, and the son sees all the sins that his father has committed, and is afraid and does not do the same:
he does not eat on the mountains, and does not set his eyes on the desires of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbour's wife,
does not oppress anyone, does not take a pledge, does not commit robbery, but clothes the naked and gives his bread to the hungry, and turns his hands away from wrongdoing;
he does not take usury or increase, but does what is right and walks in my commandments — he shall not die for his father's sin, but shall surely live.
If his father has inflicted hardship on someone, and committed robbery, and done evil among my people, such a man shall die in his own wrongdoing.
And you say: 'Why is this, that the son does not bear the sin of the father?'
Because that son has done what is right, has kept all my law and done it; he shall surely live.
The soul that sins, it shall die. The son shall not bear the sin of the father, nor shall the father bear the sin of his own son.
The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the lawlessness of the lawless shall be upon him.
I will pay my prayers to the Lord. I believed, and therefore:
I, a sinner, take refuge in you.
Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath and went to Haran.
And he came to a place and slept there, for the sun was setting. And he took a stone from among the stones of that place and put it under his head, and lay down in that place.
And he saw in a vision: behold, a ladder set up on the earth, whose top reached to heaven, and the angels of God were going up and coming down on it.
And the Lord stood above it and said: I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac.
Do not be afraid! The land on which you are sleeping I will give to you and to your offspring.
And your offspring shall be like the sand of the sea, and they shall spread out to the sea, to the north, to the south, and to the east.
And all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in you and in your offspring. And behold, I am with you wherever you go.
And I will bring you back to this same land, for I will not leave you until I have done everything that I have told you.
And Jacob woke from his sleep and said: How fearful is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
And Jacob rose at dawn and took the stone that he had put there as a pillow, and poured oil on the top of that stone.
And he called the name of that place House of God, for at first the name of that land was Ulamaus.
And Jacob prayed a prayer and said: If God will be with us, and will keep me on this road on which I am going, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,
and will bring me back alive to my father's house, then the Lord shall be my God.
And this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be a house of my God, and of everything that you give me I will give a tenth to you.
And the whole house of Israel turned to the Lord on that day.
And Samuel said to the whole house of Israel: If you turn to the Lord with all your heart and mind, and put away from among you those foreign idols and
the sacred groves of your places of worship, and prepare your hearts to serve God alone, then he will deliver you from the hands of the Philistines.
They took it to heart, and the sons of Israel cast away from themselves the Baal, the sacred groves of their places of worship, and the idols of Astarte, and they served the Lord.
Samuel began to speak to them and said: Gather all the people of Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.
And all the people of Israel gathered at Mizpah. They drew water and poured it out on the ground before the Lord, and they fasted on that day and said: We have sinned before the Lord.
For Samuel was judging the sons of Israel at Mizpah. And all the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered at Mizpah.
And all the lords of the Philistines gathered an assembly of the people, and the Philistines came up against Israel.
When the children of Israel heard this, they were afraid and trembled before the Philistines.
And the children of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not stop praying to the Lord all the days, so that he may save us from the hands of the Philistines."
And Samuel said, "Far be it from me to give up praying to the Lord God for Israel." And the Lord heard him.
And while Samuel was offering the sacrifice, the Philistines came and drew near, ready to do battle against Israel.
And the Lord thundered against the Philistines with a terrible, crashing voice. The Philistines trembled and were afraid, and they were defeated before Israel.
And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued them, overtook them and struck them down, and put the survivors to flight as far as Beth-car.
And Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and the place of the battle line,
and he called its name Ebenezer, which is translated "stone of help," for "up to now the Lord has helped us."
And he humbled the Philistines, and they no longer came into the territory of Israel. And the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
Whoever turns away from instruction hates himself, but whoever keeps it will gain wisdom.
The fear of the Lord is instruction, and he will gain wisdom and the rule of glory.
All the works of the humble are plain to see before the Lord, but the ungodly will be destroyed on the evil day.
Everyone who is proud in heart is unclean before the Lord, and whoever strikes hands on a deal falsely will not go unpunished.
The beginning of a good way is to do what is right. It is more pleasing before the Lord than offering sacrifices.
Whoever seeks God will find knowledge of righteousness, and those who seek him will find peace.
For all the works of God are done in righteousness, but [?] is kept for the day of evil.
Knowledge is on the lips of a king, and his mouth will not go wrong in judgment. The [?] of the scale comes from the Lord, for his works are a scale of righteousness.
A person who does evil is hateful to a king, for the throne of rule is established by righteousness.
Knowing lips are pleasing to a king, and he loves right words.
A king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise man will calm it.
A king's son is in the light of life, and those who please him are like a cloud of late rain.
The nests of wisdom are better and more to be chosen than gold, and the nests of understanding are more choice than silver. The paths of life turn one away from evil.
And the ways of righteousness are length of days. Whoever accepts instruction will have good things, and whoever heeds correction will become wise.
Whoever keeps the ways of the Lord guards his own soul, and whoever loves life will guard [?] his mouth.
Pride comes before destruction, and an evil [?] comes before a fall.
It is better to be gentle in mind, with humility, than to be one who divides spoil with the insolent.
One who is understanding in his affairs finds what is good, and one who trusts in the Lord will be blessed.
The wise and prudent are called understanding, but those who are sweet in their words will be listened to all the more.
Thus says the Lord:
Keep justice and do righteousness, for my salvation has drawn near to come, and my mercy to be revealed.
Blessed is the man who does this, who keeps my sabbaths undefiled and guards his hands so that they do no falsehood.
Let not the eunuch who has come over to the Lord say, "The Lord will surely separate me from his people"; and let not the eunuch say, "I am a dry tree."
For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: "Those who keep my sabbaths and who seek out what I desire,
and who hold fast to my covenants, I will give them in my house a place of renown, better than those who have sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name."
Hear, O Lord, the voice of my prayer. To you, O Lord, I have cried.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, "I am the Lord. Speak to Pharaoh everything that I speak to you."
And Moses said, "Behold, I am weak of voice. How will Pharaoh listen to me?"
And the Lord said to Moses, "Behold, I have made you a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
You will speak everything that I command you, and Aaron your brother will speak to Pharaoh, so that he will send the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
But I will harden Pharaoh's heart and multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt. And Pharaoh will not listen to you.
And I will lay my hand upon Egypt and bring out my people, the children of Israel, with power from the land of Egypt, with great vengeance.
And all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord, when I stretch out my hand over Egypt and bring the children of Israel out from among them."
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded them. Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, at the time when they spoke to Pharaoh.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said, "If Pharaoh speaks to you and says to you, 'Show us a sign or a wonder,' then say to Aaron your brother:
'Take that rod which is in your hand and throw it down before Pharaoh and before his servants,' and it will become a serpent."
Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and before his servants and did just as the Lord had commanded them.
And Aaron threw down the rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent. Pharaoh summoned the wise men and sorcerers of Egypt.
And they did the same by their sorcery: each of them threw down his rod, and they became serpents.
And Aaron's rod swallowed them up, those rods of theirs. And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not believe them, just as the Lord had told them.
The Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart has become heavy, so that he will not let my people go."
Go to Pharaoh in the morning, for he will be going out to the water tomorrow. Stand before him on the bank of the river, and take in your hands the rod that was turned into a serpent.
And say to him: The Lord God of the Hebrews has sent me to you and said: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness.
And see, you have not listened until now. Thus says the Lord: See, with this rod that is in my hand I will strike the water of the river, and it will turn into blood.
And the fish of the river will die, and the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to drink the water of the river.
The Lord said to Moses: Take your rod and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers and over all their pools of water,
and there will be blood over all the land, in trees and in stones. Moses and Aaron did so, just as the Lord had commanded them.
And Aaron raised his rod and struck the waters of the river in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants, and the water of the river was turned into blood.
And the fish of the river died, and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river.
And there was blood in all the land of Egypt. And the sorcerers of Egypt did the same by their sorceries.
And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had told them.
Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his mind even on this.
All the Egyptians dug around the river so that they might drink water from the river.
And seven days passed after the Lord struck the river. The Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says the Lord:
Let my people go, so that they may serve me. If you refuse to let them go, see, I will strike all your territory with frogs.

And frogs will swarm out of the river and come up and enter your house, the inner rooms of your bedchamber, and your beds, and the houses of your servants and of your people, and your kneading troughs [?] and your ovens.
And the frogs will come up on you, on your people and on your servants.
The Lord said to Moses: Say to your brother Aaron: Stretch out your hand over the streams and the channels, and bring up the frogs.
And Aaron stretched out the rod in his hand over the waters of the sea and brought up the frogs, and they covered the land of Egypt.
The sorcerers did the same and brought up frogs over all the land of Egypt. Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Pray to the Lord for me, so that these frogs may be taken away from me and from my people, and I will let the people go, and they may serve the Lord.
Moses said to Pharaoh: Set a day for me when I should pray for you, for your servants and for your people,
so that the frogs may be taken away from your houses and from your people, and frogs will remain only in the rivers.
And he said: Tomorrow. Moses said to him: It will be as you have said, so that you may know that there is no other besides the Lord.
And the frogs will be taken away from your house and from your courtyards, and they will remain only in the rivers.
Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. And he cried out to the Lord for deliverance from the frogs, as Pharaoh had asked.
And Moses did so, as the Lord had told him, and the frogs died out of their houses and their fields. And they were gathered together in heaps, and the land stank.
When Pharaoh saw that relief had come to him, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, as the Lord had told him.
And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron your brother: Stretch out that rod with your hand and strike the dust of the earth.
And there will be gnats among people and livestock and in all the land of Egypt.
Aaron stretched out the rod with his hand to the dust of the earth, and there were gnats on people and four-footed beasts, and in the dust of the earth, and in all Egypt.
The magicians of Egypt did the same with their sorceries, to bring forth gnats, and they could not.
And the gnats were on people and on beasts. The magicians said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God.
And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had said.
And Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there.
And behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. And Boaz said: Turn aside and sit here, O hidden one.
And he turned aside and sat down there. And Boaz brought ten men from the elders of the city and said to them: Sit down! And they sat down.
Boaz said to the kinsman: The portion of land that belongs to our brother Elimelech is to be given to Naomi, who has come from the land of Moab.
And I said: I will make it known to your ears. He said to him: Acquire it before these who are sitting here and before the elders of my people.
If you will redeem it, redeem it; if you will not redeem it, tell me, for there is no kinsman apart from you, and after you, I am next.
And he said: I am; I will redeem it. And Boaz said: On the day that you acquire the land from the hand of Naomi and from Ruth the Moabitess,
her son's wife, whose husband died, you must acquire her inheritance for yourself,
by whom you will raise up an heir for the dead man on his inheritance.
The kinsman said: I am not able to redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance.
But you redeem in place of my right of redemption, for I am not able to redeem. And this was the custom formerly in Israel concerning redemption:
to confirm every matter, a man would take off his sandal and give it to his neighbour, who would redeem in place of his right of redemption.
And this was the form of attestation in Israel. And the kinsman said to Boaz: Take my right of redemption for yourself.
