And he took off his sandal and gave it to him. Boaz said to the elders and to all the people:
You are witnesses today that I have acquired everything that was Elimelech's, and everything that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, from the hand of Naomi.
And Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, I have acquired for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead man on his inheritance,
so that the name of the dead man will not be blotted out from among his brothers and from the tribes of his place.
"You are witnesses today." All the people who were sitting at the gates answered and said, "We are witnesses."
And the elders said to him, "May the Lord make the wife who is coming into your house like Rachel and Leah,
the two who built up the house of Israel. And they did mighty things in Ephrathah, and a name was to be called in Bethlehem.
And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, your kinsman, and may the Lord give you offspring from this maidservant of yours."
And Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went in to her, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son. And the women spoke to Naomi and said to her,
"Blessed is the Lord, who has secured offspring for you today, so that your name may be called in Israel.
And he will be to you a restorer of soul in your old age, for your daughter-in-law, who loved you, has borne a son, and she is better to you than seven sons."
And Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became his nurse. And they called his name Obed.
He is the father of Jesse, the father of David. And these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron. Hezron fathered Ram.
Ram fathered Amminadab. Amminadab fathered Nahshon. Nahshon fathered Salmon. Salmon fathered Boaz. Boaz fathered Obed.
Obed fathered Jesse. Jesse fathered King David.
"And it shall come to pass afterward," says the Lord, "that I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh,
and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your old men shall see visions, and to your young men it shall be revealed in visions.
And upon my menservants and maidservants in those days I will pour out of my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.
And I will give signs in the heavens and wonders on the earth: blood and fire and smoke of the earth.
The sun shall be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the coming of that great and appointed day.
And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance,
as the Lord has said, and those who bring good news, whom the Lord our God calls.
For behold, in those days and at that time, when I bring back the captivity of Judah and of Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will enter into judgment with them there on behalf of my people Israel, who were scattered among the nations, and they divided up my land.
And they cast lots over my people, and gave boys to harlots, and sold girls for wine.
What have I to do with you, Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners? Are you paying me back some recompense? Or are you bearing some grudge against me?
Swiftly and speedily I will return your recompense upon your own heads, because you took my gold and my silver, and carried my choice and good things into your temples,
and you sold the sons of Israel to the sons of the nations, in order to drive them out of their borders.
Behold, I will raise them up from the land where you sold them, and I will return your recompense upon your own heads.
And you shall give your sons and your daughters into the hands of Judah, and they will sell them as captives to nations far off and distant, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
With my voice to the Lord. In the day of my distress.
To you, King and Lord:
And Jacob lifted up his eyes and saw the camp of God encamped, and the angels of God met him.
When Jacob saw them he said: "This is the camp of God." And he named that place Camps.
Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
He commanded them and said: "Thus shall you say to my lord Esau: 'Thus says your servant Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban and stayed until now.'"
"'And I have acquired oxen and sheep, male servants and female servants, and I have sent to tell my lord Esau, so that your servant may find favor before you.'"
And Jacob's messengers came back and said to him: "We went to Esau your brother, and behold, he too is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him."
Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed, and he divided the people who were with him, and the sheep and the cattle, into four camps.
And Jacob said: "If Esau comes to this one camp and destroys it, the second camp will escape."
And Jacob said: "O God of my father Abraham and of Isaac, O God who said to me, 'Go to the land of your birth, and I will do you good':
I have had enough of all the righteousness and all the truth that you have shown to your servant, for with this staff alone I crossed this river.
Now behold, I have become two camps. Deliver me from the hands of my brother Esau, for I am afraid of him, lest he come and kill me, and the mother together with the children.
And you said, 'I will do you good, and I will make your descendants like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted for multitude.'" And he slept there that night.
And he took from what he had brought a gift and sent it to Esau his brother: two hundred she-goats, twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes, twenty rams,
thirty milch camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-asses and their foals.
And he gave his flocks into the hands of his servants and said to them: "Go on ahead of me, and keep a space between flock and flock."
And he commanded the first and said: "If Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying,
'Whose are you, or where are you going, or whose are these that go before you?', you shall say: 'Your servant Jacob's. He has sent a gift to Esau, and behold, he himself is coming after me.'"
In the same way he commanded the second and the third and all who went ahead of him, and said:
"Speak to Esau according to these words when he finds you, and say to him: 'Behold, your servant Jacob is coming behind us.'"
For he said: "I will appease his face with the gift sent ahead of me, and after that I will see his face;
who knows, perhaps he will receive me." And the gift went on ahead of him, but he himself slept that night in the camp.
And he rose up and took his two wives and his eleven children, and brought them out, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.
And he brought across everything that he had. And he remained there alone. And a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
When he saw that he could not prevail against him, he touched the broad part of his thigh, and the broad part of Jacob's thigh went numb as he wrestled with him.
And the man said: Let me go, for the dawn has risen.
But Jacob said to him: I will not let you go until you bless me. And he said to him: What is your name? And he said: Jacob.
He said to him: From now on you shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name, for you have shown strength with God, and with men you were strong.
Jacob asked him and said: Tell me, what is your name? And he said: Why do you ask my name? It is wonderful.
And he blessed him. And he called the name of that place "Vision of God", for I have seen God face to face, and my soul was saved.
If you sit down, you will sit without fear, and if you sleep, you will sleep in rest.
And you will not be afraid of terror when it comes, nor of the onslaught that falls upon the ungodly.
for the Lord will be in all your ways and will make your feet firm, so that you will not be shaken.
Do not hold back from doing good to the needy when your hand has the means to help.
Do not say, "Go away now, and come back tomorrow, and I will give to you," when you have the power to do good.
And do not plot evil against your friend who lives alongside you and trusts in you. Do not delight in enmity with a worthless man, lest he do you harm.
Do not take a wicked man as one who reproaches you, and do not imitate their ways, for he is not pure before the Lord, and he does not dwell among the righteous.
The curse of the Lord is in the house of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous will be blessed. The Lord crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly have exalted dishonor. Hear, children, a father's instruction, and pay attention so that you may know understanding.
For I give you a good gift. Do not forget and do not forsake my law.
For I too was a son to my father, obedient, and beloved in my mother's sight. They taught me and said to me:
Let my word be fixed in your heart, and keep the commandments, and do not forget them; and do not disregard the words of my mouth;
and do not forsake them, and they will help you; love them, and they will keep you. Put a fence around them, and they will exalt you;
honor it, so that it may receive you and place on your head a crown of grace, and adorn you with a crown of glory.
And on that day, says the Lord, she will call me "My husband" and will no longer call me "Alaam" [?].
And he will take the name of Balaam out of her mouth, and their names will no longer be remembered.
And in those days he promised them their covenant with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth;
I will break bow and battle and sword from the land, and I will make you dwell in hope.
And I will betroth you to myself forever, and I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and in judgment and in mercy.
And I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you shall know the Lord. And on that day, says the Lord, I will listen to the heaven, and the heaven will listen to the earth;

And the earth will hear the wheat and the wine, and they will hear Jezreel. And I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on the one who was not shown mercy, and I will say to "Not my people":
"You are my people"; and he will say to me: "You are the Lord my God."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel and say to its shepherds:
Thus says Adonai the Lord to the shepherds of Israel: Is it not themselves that those shepherds feed? Do those shepherds not feed my sheep?
Look, you eat the milk and clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the fat ones, and you do not feed my sheep.

You have not strengthened the weak, and you have not fattened the sick, and you have not bound up the broken, and you have not brought back the one that went astray, and you have not sought the lost, and you have worked the strong with hard toil.
And my sheep were scattered, because they had no shepherd, and they became food for all the beasts of the field.
And my sheep were scattered over all the mountains and all the high hills, and they were scattered over the face of the whole earth, and there was no one to seek them and no one to bring them back.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord: As I live, says Adonai the Lord, because my sheep have become plunder and food for the beasts of the earth,
because there were no shepherds, and the shepherds did not seek out my sheep, and the shepherds fed themselves and not my sheep, therefore, shepherds, thus says Adonai the Lord:
Behold, I will require my sheep from the shepherds, and I will take them out of your hands and turn them back, so that you will no longer shepherd my sheep;
and the shepherds will no longer feed them hereafter, and I will rescue my sheep from their mouth, and they will no longer be food for them.
For thus says the Lord:
I will bring them out from among the nations and gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land, and I will feed them on the mountain of Israel;
and in the valleys and in every inhabited place of the land I will feed them in good pasture; and their folds will be there;
they will lie down and rest in a good resting place, and they will graze in rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
Thus says Adonai the Lord: I will seek the lost, and bring back the one that went astray, and bind up the broken, and strengthen the lame, and guard the strong, and I will feed them with justice.
And I will remove the evil beast from the land; they will dwell in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.
And I will give them the side of my mountain; and I will give you a rain of blessing.
And I will give fruit to the trees of the field; and they will dwell in their land in hope of peace, and they will know that I am the Lord.
Let my prayer be heard by God [?] prayer. [?] prayer. From the ends of the earth to you:
And now, Israel, what does the Lord God ask of you?
Only that you fear him and walk in all his ways, and love him and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
And keep the commandments of the Lord your God and his ordinances, all that I command you today, so that it may go well with you.
Behold, the heavens and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord your God, and the earth and everything that is in it. For he chose your fathers, to love them.
And after them he chose their descendants, you, above all nations, as it is this day.
And now circumcise your hardness of heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer.
For the Lord your God is the great and mighty God, God of gods and Lord of lords, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe.
He executes justice for the stranger, and he loves strangers, giving them bread and drink.
You also must love strangers, for you too were strangers in the land of Egypt.
Fear the Lord God, serve him alone, and swear by his name.
For he himself is the Lord your God, who did great and mighty things, which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy-five souls, but now, behold, the Lord your God has made you as many as the stars of heaven.
And you shall love the Lord your God and keep his charges, his ordinances, his commandments and his judgments all your days.

And you shall know (for it is not your children, who knew nothing, and who do not know the instruction of your Lord) his majesty, his signs and his wonders, which he did in the midst of Egypt and in their land,
and what he did to the people of Egypt: how the water of the Red Sea overwhelmed their chariots and their horses before your face
when they were pursuing after you, and how the Lord your God destroyed them, down to this present day;
and all that the Lord your God did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place;
and all that he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben:
how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households, their tents and all their possessions, in the midst of all Israel.
Your eyes have seen all the great and mighty works of the Lord God, all that he did among us. Keep all his commandments,
all that I command you today, so that you may live and multiply and take possession of the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess,
so that you may live long in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them and to their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land that you are going to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where, when they sow, they water it by foot like a vegetable garden.
But the land that you are entering to possess is a land of mountains and plains; they drink water from the rain that comes down from heaven.
It is a land that the Lord your God watches over always; the eyes of the Lord your God are on it from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
If you truly obey all his commandments that I command you today, to love the Lord your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
he will give rain to your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather in your grain, your wine and your oil.
And he will give grass of the fields for your cattle, and you will eat and be satisfied.
Take heed to yourself, lest your heart be led astray, and you turn aside to worship foreign gods.
And the Lord your God will be angry with you in his wrath, and he will shut up the sky, and the earth will not give its fruit,
and you will quickly perish from the good land which the Lord has given you.
And lay these words in your hearts and in your souls, and bind them as a sign on your hands, and let them be fixed before your eyes.
And teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in the house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you rise up.
And write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that you and your sons may live long on the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to you, as the days of heaven upon the earth.
And it shall be, if you listen to all the commandments which I command you to do today, to love the Lord your God and to walk in all his ways and to cling to him,
the Lord God will drive out all these nations from before you, and you will take possession of many nations, mightier than you.

Every place on which you set the sole of your feet, from the wilderness before Lebanon, and as far as the great river, the Euphrates, and as far as the sea of the setting sun, shall be your territory.
No one will stand against you before your face; the Lord your God will lay fear and dread of you on all the face of the land
on which you go, as he told you. Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you truly listen to the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you today;
and the curse, if you stray from the way which I commanded you, and go to serve foreign gods whom you have not known.
I have heard many such things; you are all evil comforters. Now what?
Is there any order in words of wind? Or what has troubled you, that you answer?
I too could speak as you do, if only your soul were in place of my soul.
And then I would leap upon you with words, and I would [?shake] my head over you. May there be strength in my mouth,
and I would not hold back the movement of my lips. If I speak, will my wound not pain me? And if I keep silent, will I be wounded any less?
But now he has given me toil, stupefied and decayed as I am; you seized me, and it became a witness. And my lies rose up against me; it answered me back to my face.
Wrath came upon me and cast me down, and he gnashed his teeth at me. He fixed the arrows of trials upon me.

The points of his arrows pierced [?] my eyes; he struck me on the knees with a sword, and together they rushed upon me. The Lord delivered me into the hands of the false and cast me among the ungodly.
When I was at peace he destroyed me; he seized me by my hair and crushed me, and set me up as a lookout.
Spearmen surrounded me and pierced my kidneys; without sparing they poured out my gall on the ground.
They struck me down blow upon blow; the mighty ran at me. They sewed sackcloth onto my skin, and my strength was spent on the ground.
My belly is burned up with weeping, and the shadow of death is on my eyelids. There was no falsehood in my hands; my prayer was pure.
O earth, do not cover the blood of my flesh, and let there be no place for my cry.
And now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high.
Let my prayer reach the Lord, and let my eyes weep before him. Let there be one who pleads for a man before the Lord, as a son of man pleads for his neighbour.
My numbered years have come, and I am going on the way from which I will not return. I am perishing, swept away in spirit;
I beg for burial and do not obtain it. I toil, I grow weary, and what am I to do? For strangers have stolen my possessions.
Who is this? Let him give me his hand. For they have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore you will not exalt them.
He will declare a portion of wickedness; his eyes have melted away over his sons. You have made me a byword among the nations, and I have become their laughingstock.
My eyes are blinded by wrath; I am greatly besieged by all. The truthful were amazed at these things, and let the righteous rise up against the lawless.
Let the faithful one keep to his way, and let the one who is pure of hands take comfort.
Not so, but come down [?]; come, for I do not find truth among you.
My days have passed away in stench, and the membrane of my heart has burst. They have turned night into day; light is near, in the face of darkness.
And even if I endure, hell is my home, and my bed is spread in the deep darkness.
I have called death my father and my mother, and corruption my sister. Where, then, is my hope?
Will I ever see my good? Or will they go down with me to hell, or shall we go down together into the earth?
And Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho, and the Lord showed him
all the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, as far as the furthest sea,
and all the wilderness and all the surrounding country in the plains of Jericho, the cities of palm trees, as far as Zoar.
And the Lord said to Moses: "This is the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying: 'I will give this land to your descendants.'
Now I have shown it to you, and your eyes have seen it, but you will not go in there." And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died in the land of Moab at the word of the Lord.
And he was buried in Gai, near the house of Peor, and no one knows his grave to this day.
And Moses was about a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eyes had not grown dim, and the appearance of his face had not changed.
And the children of Israel mourned for Moses in the plains of Moab, on the bank of the river Jordan, opposite Jericho; they mourned for thirty days.
And the days of mourning for him came to an end. And Joshua the son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom,
For Moses had laid his hands upon him, and all the children of Israel obeyed him and did what God had commanded Moses.
And there did not arise a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face, in all the signs and wonders
which the Lord sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh and all his servants and all his land;
those very great wonders, the strong hand and the uplifted arm, which Moses performed before all Israel.
Thus says the Lord God, who created the heavens and established them;
who established the earth and all that is in it, and gave breath to his people, and spirits to those who walk upon it.
I am the Lord God, who called you in righteousness and held your hand and strengthened you, and gave you as a covenant to the peoples and a light to the Gentiles,
to open the eyes of the blind and to bring out of prison those who are bound, who sit in darkness.
I am the Lord, and this is my name. Thus says the Lord, who made the heaven and established it;
who founded the earth and all that is in it, and gave spirit to his people who are upon it, and breath to those who walk upon it.
I, the Lord, called you in righteousness and held your right hand and strengthened you, and gave you as a covenant to the peoples and a light to the Gentiles,
to open the eyes of the blind and to bring out of bonds those who are bound, and out of the prison house those who sit in darkness.
I am the Lord God, and this is my name, and my glory I will not give to others, nor my praise to graven images.
The things from the beginning, behold, are coming, and the new things I will tell you; before they are told, they will be made known to you.
Sing to the Lord a new song; for his beginning is glorified on high,
and his name is glorious from end to end of the earth, the sea and those who go upon it, the islands and all who dwell in them.
Know [?] for [?] your name. O God, who will be like you?
Good is the Lord; he did not [?] me. Be delivered [?]: for our help by the name [?].
To that one among the holy ones [?]. We passed through fire.
Shout to God, all the earth, to his [?].
From the great counsel of strength the righteous will run to him and be exalted.
The wealth of a rich man is like a walled city, and its glory greatly overshadows it.
Before humiliation a man's heart is exalted, and before glory it is humbled.
Whoever answers a word before hearing it, it is folly and reproach to him.
Prudent service [or: servant] calms a man's anger, but who will bear with a faint-hearted man?
The heart of the prudent gains knowledge, and the ears of the wise seek understanding. A man's gift makes room for him and seats him among the mighty.
The righteous man becomes his own accuser at his very first word; but as soon as the judge lays down the case, he is refuted.
A prudent man quiets disputes and settles matters among the mighty.
A brother helped by a brother is like a strong and lofty city, and he is as strong as a walled kingdom.
A man fills his belly from the fruit of his mouth, and he is satisfied from the fruit of his lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue; and those who guard it will eat its fruit.
He who has found a good wife has found grace and has received gladness from God.
He who drives out a good wife drives out his own good; and he who keeps an adulteress is foolish and ungodly.
Therefore thus says the Lord, those who serve me:
By faith they were cut off: all this came to pass:
Remember the word that I spoke to you. For I was with you
O spiritual offerings.
a sacrifice to you:
Direct my steps. Show your face:
A man's folly ruins him through his own scheming, and in his heart he blames God.
Wealth gains many friends, but from the poor man, who has no one, even [his friend] withdraws.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who accuses unjustly will not escape judgment.
Many pay court to the king's face, but everyone turns wicked at his giving [?] and becomes a reproacher of a man.
Everyone who hates a poor brother will be far from love as well; good counsel is near to those who know it,
and a wise man will find it. He who does much evil carries wickedness to completion [?], and he who stirs up provoking words will not be saved.
He who acquires prudence loves himself; and he who keeps wisdom will find good.
A lying witness will not go unpunished; he who kindles evil will himself perish.
Luxury does not befit a fool; likewise, if a servant rules over his masters, they are driven out with abuse.
A merciful man is long-suffering, and his boast overtakes the ungodly.
The king's command is like the roaring of a lion, and like dew on the grass, so is his favor.
A foolish son is his father's shame, and prayers paid for with a strange woman's wages are not pure.
Fathers divide house and possessions among their children, but a good wife is given to a husband by the Lord.
Fear takes hold of the heart of adulterers, and the soul of the idle goes hungry.
Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his own soul safe, but whoever is careless about his ways will perish.
Whoever is merciful to the poor lends to the Lord, and he will be repaid according to what he has given. Instruct your son, and in this way there will be good hope.
And do not lead his soul into insolence. If you strike him with the rod, he will not die; rather, you will deliver his soul from death.
A man of evil character will be severely punished, and if he goes on acting lawlessly, he will forfeit his own soul as well.
You who are the Lord, O Lord, behold,
you made heaven and earth by your great power and your outstretched arm. Nothing is hidden from you.
You show mercy to a thousand generations, and you repay the sin of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them.
O mighty God, the Lord of hosts is your name. Great in counsel and mighty in deed, Almighty, Lord of great name, O Lord,
your eyes see all the ways of men, to give each one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
Know this: the hour has already come for us to wake from sleep.
Our salvation is now nearer than when we first believed.
The night has moved away from us, and the light has drawn near. So let us now put away the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
And let us walk decently, as in the daytime, not in revelry and drunkenness, nor in beds of filth,
not in quarreling and envy. Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh to satisfy its desires.
Welcome the one who is weak in faith, without doubts or disputes over opinions. One person believes he may eat anything, but the weak one eats vegetables.
The one who eats must not despise the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats, since God has welcomed them.
Who are you to judge another person's servant? It is before his own master that he stands or falls. And he will stand, for God is able to make him stand firm.
One person keeps a day by setting it apart, and another keeps every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
Whoever observes the day observes it for the Lord, and whoever does not observe the day does not observe it for the Lord as well.
And whoever eats, eats for the Lord, and he gives thanks to God.
Your mercies are many:
At that time a certain lawyer stood up to test Jesus and said to him:
"Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?" And the Lord said to him, "What is written in the Law? How do you read it?"
And he said, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."
Jesus said to him, "You have answered rightly. Do this and you will live." But he wished to justify himself and said to Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
Jesus answered and said to him, "A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers fell upon him. They stripped him, wounded him, and left him half dead.
A certain priest was going down that same road. He saw him and passed by. Likewise a Levite came to that same place, saw him, and passed by.
Then a certain Samaritan was traveling and came to that same place. He saw him and had compassion on him.
He went to him and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own beast, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
And the next day, as he was leaving, he gave two denarii to the innkeeper and said to him,
'Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.' Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?"
And he said to him, "The one who showed mercy." Jesus said to him, "Go, and you do likewise, and you will live."
Like the one who fell into the hands [?].
Those who [?] the mystery of the cherubim. Like the robbers:
Look [?]; you have heard [?] unto death [?]. Sing to the Lord of the good [?]:
Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean:
But I speak to you, you Gentiles:
Since I am a teacher of the Gentiles, I glorify my ministry, so that I may make my own flesh jealous and save some of them.
For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, how much more will their acceptance be?
If the firstfruits are holy, so too is the [?]; and the roots, so then the branches also are holy.
If some of the branches have been broken off, and you, who were a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became a sharer in the roots and the richness of the olive tree,

do not boast over those branches. If you boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root that supports you. Now perhaps you will say, "The branches were broken off and I was grafted in."
Good! They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand firm through faith. Do not be proud, but fear.
If God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either. Now see the kindness and the severity of God:
severity toward those who fell, but kindness toward you, if you continue in that kindness. Otherwise you too will be cut off.
And they too, if they do not remain in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
If you were cut from this wild olive tree and went and were grafted into the good cultivated olive tree, how much more will those who are the true branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
…who had fallen into the hands of robbers:
And when those days were completed, Shua, the wife of Judah, died,
and Judah was comforted after his mourning and went up to the shearers of his sheep at Timnah, he and Hirah, his Adullamite shepherd.
And they told Tamar, his daughter-in-law, saying to her: "Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."
And Tamar took off her widow's garments and put on a garment and adorned herself, and sat by the gates of Enaim,
which is on the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah, his son, had grown up, and he had not given her to him as wife.
And Judah saw her and thought that she was some harlot, for she had covered her face and he did not recognize her.
And he turned aside to her from the road and said to her: "Let me come in to you." But she said to him: "What will you give me if you come in to me?"
And Judah said: "I will send you a kid of the goats from the flock." But she said: "Give me a pledge until you send it."
And Judah said: "What pledge shall I give you?" And she said: "That ring of yours, and the necklace, and the staff that you have in your hand."
And he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him. And she arose and took off that garment and put on her widow's garments again.
And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his shepherd, the Adullamite, to get back the pledge from the woman.
But he did not find her. He asked the men of that place: "Where is the harlot who was at Enaim by the road?"
And they said: "There is no harlot here." And the shepherd returned to Judah and said to him: "I did not find her; and the men of that place said: 'There is no harlot here.'"
Judah said: "Let her keep them, lest we be ridiculed. I sent this kid, but you did not find her."
And it happened after three months that they told Judah, saying: "Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has played the harlot, and she is pregnant through harlotry."
Judah said: "Bring her out and burn her with fire." And as she was being brought out, she sent to her father-in-law and said to him:
"By the man to whom this pledge belongs, by him I am pregnant. Recognize whose are this ring and necklace and staff."
And Judah recognized them and said: "Tamar is more righteous than I, for I did not give her as wife to my son Shelah."
And he did not know her again. And it happened, when she was giving birth, there were twins in her womb.
One put out a hand. And the midwife took it and tied scarlet thread on his hand, and said: "This one came out first."
And he drew back his hand, and immediately his brother came out, and the midwife said: "Why has a way been broken open for you?"
And she called his name Perez. And after him his brother came out, and she called his name Zerah.
Now Joseph was brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, an Egyptian man, acquired him from the hands of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
And the Lord was with him, and he was a man who prospered, and he was in the house in the presence of that Egyptian man.
His master knew that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made everything he did prosper.
And Joseph found favour before him and was pleasing to him. He put him in charge of his own [household], and everything he had he gave into Joseph's hands.
And it came to pass, after he had put him in charge of his house and had given everything he had into his hands,
that God blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake, and the blessing of the Lord was on all his possessions, in the house and in the fields.
He gave everything into Joseph's hands, and he did not know what Joseph was doing, except only the bread that he ate.
And Joseph was handsome in form and very fair of face.
After this, the wife of the Egyptian, his master, cast her eyes on Joseph and said to him, "Lie with me."
But he refused, and said to his master's wife, "If my master knows nothing about my concerns in his house, and everything
that is his he has given into my hands, and no one in this house is greater than I, and nothing is kept back from my hand
except you alone, because you are his wife, then how could I do this evil thing and sin before my lord?"
She spoke to him day after day, but Joseph would not agree to lie with her or be with her.
One such day Joseph went into the house to do his work, and no one was in the house.
She caught hold of his garment and said, "Lie with me." But Joseph left his garment, went out, and fled from her.
And when he had left his garment in her hands and fled, she called those who were in the house, spoke to them and said,
"See now, he has brought this Hebrew servant in to us to mock us. He came in to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.
And when he heard my voice, that I raised it, he left his garment with me, went outside, and fled."
She kept Joseph's garment with her until her husband came home.
And she said to him, "This Hebrew servant whom you brought in came in and said to me, 'I will lie with you.'
When he heard that I raised my voice, he left his garment with me, fled, and went outside."
When he heard the words his wife told him, "This is what your servant did to me," he was enraged with anger.
He took Joseph and put him in the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were held.
But the Lord was with Joseph and showed him mercy, and he found favour before the chief jailer.
The chief jailer gave the prison into Joseph's hands, and all the prisoners who were in the prison.
And of everything that was done in the prison, the chief jailer himself knew nothing, not a single thing,
because everything was in his hands, since the Lord was with him. And whatever Joseph did, [the Lord] made it prosper in his hands.
And the Lord opened his quiver and afflicted me, and loosed the reins before my face.
And at the right of the shoot they have risen up; he stretched out his foot and made a way against me, to the paths of my destruction.
And my paths were broken, for he stripped off my garment and shot his arrows at me. And he does to me whatever he wishes.
I am worn down in my pains. And my pains turn back upon me again.
My hope has passed away like the wind, and my life like a cloud. And now my soul has gone out of me.
And days of pain and nights of groaning have been given to me. My bones burn, and my sinews come loose.
With his great strength he has seized my garment, and he has bound me about like the collar of my tunic.
He has counted me the same as clay, along with the earth, and he has set my portion the same as ashes. I cry out to you, Lord, and you do not hear me.
They stood and examined me. And they fell upon me without mercy; you torment me with a strong hand. And you have ordained pains for me and cast me out of my life.
I know that death has crushed me, for the earth is the house of everyone who dies.
If only I had the power to lay hands on myself, or if I could beg someone else, and he would do this for me.
For I used to weep over the helpless and sigh when I saw a man in distress.
I waited for good, and look, evil days have come upon me. My belly boils and is not still; days of poverty have overtaken me.
And I go about sighing, without a muzzle. And I have stood in the assembly and I cry out. I have become a brother to [?] (dedach'uavi; perhaps sirens or jackals) and a companion to ostriches.
My skin has wasted away badly, and my bones from the heat. My joy has turned to mourning for me, and my gladness to weeping.
I made a covenant with my brothers and did not look with desire on a virgin. And then would the Lord give me from above an inheritance without lack, from on high?
Woe! Destruction is for the false, and a strange fate for those who do lawless deeds!
For the day of the Lord is near; that day of the Lord is near and coming very swiftly, and it is bitter and harsh; the mighty one has been appointed.
A day of wrath, a day of misery and ruin, a day of gloom and darkness, a day of cloud and mist, a day of the trumpet and the battle cry against the strong cities and against the high corner towers.

And I will bring distress on people, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the Lord. And their innocent blood was poured out on the earth like [?] (mats'a; perhaps dust), and their flesh like dung.
And their silver and their gold will not be able to save them on that day of the Lord's wrath.
And the whole earth will be consumed by the fire of his jealousy, for there will be a swift end for all who live on the earth.
Come together and gather yourselves, you undisciplined nation, before you become like flowers, and your days pass away,
before the wrath of the Lord comes upon you, before that day of the wrath of the Lord's anger comes upon you.
Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth. Do justice, seek righteousness and speak what is right, so that you may be sheltered on that day of the Lord's wrath.
Hear, O God, my prayer.
to you. From fear of the enemy of lawlessness [?]:
The soul that sins shall itself die;
the son shall not bear the sin of the father, nor shall the father bear the sin of his son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the lawlessness of the lawless shall be upon him.
And if the lawless one turns from all his lawless deeds that he has done, and keeps all my commandments, and does mercy and righteousness,
he shall surely live and shall not die. None of his transgressions, however many he committed, will I remember; in the righteousness that he has done he shall surely live.
For I do not at all desire the death of the lawless one, says the Lord, but rather that he turn from his evil way and live.
And if the righteous one turns away from his righteousness and commits lawlessness according to all the lawlessness that the lawless one commits,
none of the righteous deeds that he has done will I remember; in the transgression that he committed, in it he shall die.
And you said: 'The ways of the Lord are not upright.' Hear, O house of Israel: is it that my ways are not upright? Is it not rather your ways that are not upright?
If the righteous one turns away from his righteousness and commits sin, in the transgression that he has committed, in it he shall die.
And if the lawless one turns from the lawlessness that he has done and does judgment and righteousness, he has preserved his soul.
And he has turned from all his lawlessness that he committed; he shall surely live and shall not die.
And the house of Israel said: 'The way of the Lord is not right.' Is it that my way is not right, O house of Israel? Rather, it is your way that is not right.
I will judge you, each one according to your way, O house of Israel, says the Lord.
I make known to you, brothers, the gospel.:
From my counsels [?]:
And the foreigners gathered their camps to fight against Israel, and they gathered at Socoh of Judea and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephermem.
And Saul and the men of Israel gathered and encamped in the valley of the oak, these on this side and those on that side.

And they drew up in battle array before the foreigners to fight. And the foreigners drew up in array and stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel on the mountain on this side, and the valley was between them.
And a man came out from the battle line of the foreigners; his name was Goliath, of Gath. His height was four cubits and a span.
And a bronze helmet was set on his head, and he was clothed in a coat of chain mail; and the weight of the coat was five hundred shekels of bronze and iron;
and bronze greaves were fastened on his loins, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders;
and the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the spearhead on it was six hundred shekels of bronze.
And the one who carried his armor went ahead before him.
And he shouted to the ranks of Israel and said to them: "Why do you come out to draw up for battle and to fight before us?
Am I not a Philistine, and are you not Hebrews of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and send him down to me.
If he is able to fight with me and kills me, we will be your slaves; if I prevail and kill him, you will be our slaves and serve us."
And that Philistine said: "Behold, today I have taunted the ranks of Israel; give me a man, and let the two of us fight alone."
And Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and greatly afraid. And David was the son of a man, an Ephrathite;
he was from Bethlehem of Judah, and his name was Jesse, and he had eight sons. And in the days of Saul this man was old and advanced in many years.
And his three eldest sons went out with Saul to battle.
And these are the names of his three sons who had gone out to battle: Eliab the firstborn, next Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
And David was the youngest, and these three eldest went out with Saul to battle.
And David went away from Saul and returned to his father's flock, to tend his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
And that Philistine came forward morning and evening and stood before the ranks of Israel, and he did so for those forty days.
And Jesse said to his son David: "Take to your brothers this measure of parched grain and these ten loaves of bread, and go to the camp to your brothers;
and take these ten curd cheeses to the commander of the thousand, and ask after your brothers' welfare, and bring me news and tell me how they are."
And Saul and all Israel were fighting the Philistines in the valley.
And David rose early in the morning and left his sheep with a keeper, and took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him;
and he came into the camp of the army that had gone out to battle, and there was a great shouting in the camp.
And the sons of Israel drew up for battle, and the Philistines drew up facing the sons of Israel.
And David put down his baggage and gave it into the hands of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the camp, to the battle line, and greeted his brothers and asked after their welfare.
And while he was still speaking with them, behold, that man, the Amalekite, was coming up, whose name was Goliath the Philistine, who was from Gath,
from the ranks of the Philistines, and he spoke the same words as before, and David and every man of Israel heard these words.
And a man of Israel said: "Do you see that man who is coming up? For he comes up to taunt Israel;
and the man who kills him, the king will enrich him with his own riches, and they will give him his daughter as wife, and he will make his father's house free in Israel."
And David said to the men who stood with him: "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes the reproach from Israel?
And who is this uncircumcised Philistine, who has taunted the ranks of the living God?"
And the people answered him in the same words, and said to him: "Thus will it be done for the man who kills him."
And Eliab, his eldest brother, heard this while he was speaking to those men, and he grew angry with David in his wrath and said to him:
"Why have you come here, and with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness?
I know your arrogance and the wickedness of your heart, for you have come for no other reason than to see the battle." And David said, "What have I done now?
Was I not only speaking words?" And he went to another place and said the same thing, and they answered him just as before.
And the words that David was speaking were heard, and they reported them to Saul, and they brought him before Saul.
And David said, "Let not the heart of my king be troubled because of this, for your servant will go out and fight him."
And Saul said to David, "You are not able to go out and fight with that Philistine, for you are a boy, and he is a man and has been a warrior since his youth."
And David said to Saul, "Your servant was a shepherd of his father's flock, and whenever a lion or a bear came and took a sheep from the flock,
I would go out after it and strike it and take the sheep out of its mouth; and if it turned on me, I would seize it by the throat, strike it, and kill it.
Your servant has killed both lion and bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them.
I will go out and kill him and remove the reproach from Israel. And who is this uncircumcised one, that he reproaches the army of the living God?"
And David said, "The Lord, who delivered me from the mouth of the lion and from the paws of the bear, will himself deliver me from the hands of this uncircumcised Philistine."
And Saul said to David, "Go, and may the Lord be with you."
And Saul clothed David in his own armor, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in a coat of mail.
And David girded the sword on over the coat of mail, and David struggled to walk in it, for he was not used to it.
And David said to Saul, "I cannot go out in these, for I am not used to them." And he took them off.
And he took his staff in his hands and chose five smooth stones and put them in the shepherd's bag,
which served as his pouch; and he had his sling in his hands, and he approached the Philistine.
And the Philistine kept coming forward and drew near to David, and the man who carried his shield went before him.
And the Philistine Goliath looked and saw David and despised him, for he was only a boy, and he was ruddy and had handsome eyes.
And the Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you have come out against me with a staff and stones?" And the Philistine cursed him by his idols.
And the Philistine said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth."
And David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword and spear and shield,
but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the army of Israel, which you have reproached today.

And today the Lord God will deliver you into my hands, and I will kill you and take your head from you, and this very day I will give your corpse and the corpses of the Philistine camp as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
and all the earth shall know that there is a God in Israel;
and all this assembly shall know that God does not save by sword or by spear, for the battle is the Lord's, and he has delivered you into our hands.
And the Philistine rose up and drew near to fight David, and David hurried and went out from the battle line to meet the Philistine.
And he put his hand into the bag, took out one stone, slung it, and struck the Philistine on the forehead. The stone went through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell face down on the ground.
And on that day David prevailed over the Philistine with the sling and the stone. He struck the Philistine and killed him, and there was no sword in his hand.
And David ran and stood over him, took hold of his sword, drew it out of its sheath, and cut off his head with that sword.
And when the Philistines saw that their mighty man was dead, they fled.
And the men of Israel and of Judah rose up, raised a shout, and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance of Gath and as far as the gates of Ashkelon.
And the wounded fell along the road of the gates, as far as Gath.
And the men of Israel turned back and came back from pursuing the Philistines, and they plundered their camp.
And David took the Philistine's head and brought it into Jerusalem, and he put the Philistine's armor in his own dwelling.
And when Saul saw David going out to fight the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of his army: "Whose son is this young man?"
Abner answered and said: "As your soul lives, my lord king, I do not know." And Saul said: "Ask whose son this young man is."
And when he returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, and he had the Philistine's head in his hands.
And Saul said to him: "Whose son are you, young man?" And David said: "I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."
And David went in before Saul and finished speaking his words to him;
and Jonathan, the king's son, saw him, and his soul was bound to David's soul, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
And from that day Saul took him and did not let him return to his father's house any more.
And Jonathan and David made a covenant, for he loved the soul of his friend as his own soul.
And Jonathan stripped off the garment he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his coat of mail, and even his sword, his bow, and his belt.
And Saul set him over the men of war. And David went out and came in, and he acted wisely in every matter wherever Saul sent him;
and he was pleasing to all the people and in the eyes of Saul's servants.
And when they came in, when David had returned from killing the Philistine,
women dancers and singers of praise came out from all the cities of Israel to meet David and to meet King Saul,
to praise, dance, and sing with tambourines, pipes, songs, and lyres.
And the women who were dancing sang out with joy and said: "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands."
And Saul was angered with wrath, and this saying seemed very evil to him, and Saul said:
"They have given David tens of thousands, and me thousands; what more does he lack but the kingship?"
And from then on Saul looked askance at David, from that day to the end.
Whoever made me in those days.
Fear my words, my son, and receive them and repent.
Thus says the man to those who believe in God: "I will be silent, for I am more foolish than all men, and I do not have human wisdom.
God has taught me wisdom, and I have understood the knowledge of the holy ones, and I know holiness.
Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the winds in his bosom? Or who has bound up the waters in his garment?
Who has taken hold of the ends of the earth? What is his name? Or what is the name of his son, that you may know?
For all the words of God are tested and choice, and he takes care of those who fear him.
So that he may not rebuke you and you be found a liar. Two things I ask of you: do not take them away from me before I die.
Remove false and vain words far from me; give me neither riches nor poverty, but set my portion in due measure,
so that I may not become rich and turn false, or, if I am poor, steal and swear falsely by the name of my God.
Do not hand a servant over into the hands of his master, lest he curse you and you be destroyed. An evil offspring curses his father and does not bless his mother.
An evil offspring counts himself among the righteous, and does not cleanse away his blameworthiness.
The eyes of an evil offspring are haughty, and he lifts himself up with his eyelids.
The teeth of an evil offspring are like swords, and his jaw teeth are like knives, to crush and devour the lowly of the earth and poor men.
This I say to you who are wise, for you to know: do not be ashamed of justice; partiality in judgment is not good.
Whoever says to the ungodly, "You are righteous," let him be cursed by the people and abhorred among the nations;
but those who rebuke them will prove the better, and blessing will come upon them.
And the word came to me:
O God, save me by your name. O God, hear:
And I will sprinkle water upon you:
Or do you not know:
The Lord said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, for behold, he is going out to the waters, to the bank of the river. And say to him:
Thus says the Lord: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness.
If you will not let them go, behold, I will send the dog-fly upon you, upon your servants and upon your houses, and I will fill the houses of the Egyptians with the dog-fly.
And on that day I will glorify the land of Goshen, where my people live.
And there will be no dog-fly there, so that you may know that I am the Lord, the God of all the earth.
And I will make a distinction between my people and your people. And tomorrow this sign will come about.
And the Lord did so. The dog-fly came in very great numbers into Pharaoh's house, into the houses of his servants and into all the land of Egypt, and the land was ruined by the dog-fly.
Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them: Go and offer sacrifice to the Lord your God here in your own land.
Moses said to him: It is not possible to do that. We would be sacrificing to the Lord our God what is an abomination to Egypt.
If we sacrifice what is an abomination to Egypt before him, we will be stoned.
Rather, let us go out into the wilderness and sacrifice to our God there, as the Lord told us.
And Pharaoh said: I will let you go, and you may serve the Lord your God in the wilderness.
But do not go far away when you go out. And pray to the Lord for me too.
Moses said to him: Behold, I will go out from you and pray to God, and tomorrow the dog-fly will depart from you and from your people.
But do not deceive us again, Pharaoh, by not letting the people go to serve the Lord. Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God, as Moses had said.
And the dog-fly was removed from him, from his servants and from his people, and not a single one of them remained.
And Pharaoh hardened his heart at that time, and he would not let the people go.
The Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says the Lord of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness.
If you will not let my people go, but still keep holding them, behold, the hand of the Lord will be upon your livestock
that are in the field: upon the horses and upon the [?], upon the camels, the sheep and the cattle, a very great death.
And I will go [?] among the flocks of the children of Israel, and not one of the livestock of the children of Israel will die.
And the Lord set a fixed time and said: Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land.
And the Lord did this thing, and all the livestock of the Egyptians perished, but not one of the livestock of the children of Israel died.
And Pharaoh saw that not one of the livestock of the children of Israel had died. And Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not let the people go.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said: Take handfuls of ash from the furnace and scatter it before Pharaoh and before his servants.
And let it become dust over all the land of Egypt, and it shall become boils on men and four-footed beasts, bursting out in blisters upon men and four-footed beasts and in all the land of Egypt.
And they took the ashes from the furnace before Pharaoh and scattered them toward heaven. And boils came, bursting out in blisters upon men and four-footed beasts.
And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians too and in all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to him, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord said to Moses: Rise early tomorrow and stand before Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness,
for now, at this time, I will send all my plagues upon your heart, and upon your servants and upon your people,
so that you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth. And now I will send out my hand and strike you down from the earth.
For this very reason you have been preserved: that I may show my power in you, and that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth;
for you still go on holding my people and do not let them go.
Behold, at this very hour tomorrow I will rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in the land of Egypt from the day it was founded until this day.
Now therefore hurry and gather in your livestock and whatever you have out in the field; whatever does not go into a house, the hail will fall on it and it will die.
Those of Pharaoh's servants who feared the word of the Lord gathered their livestock into houses.
But those who did not take the word of the Lord to heart left their livestock in the field.
The Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and there will be hail in all the land of Egypt, on man and on livestock and on every green plant of the field.
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and water ran about over the earth;
and the Lord rained hail on all the land of Egypt. There was the hail, and fire was blazing within the hail.
The hail was very great, such as had never been in Egypt since there had been a nation upon it.
And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt, from man to beast; the hail destroyed every green plant, and the hail shattered every tree of the field.
But in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, there was no hail.
Pharaoh sent and summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them: Now I have sinned against the Lord. The Lord is righteous, but I and my people have sinned.
Pray to the Lord for me, and let these thunders of the Lord, and the hail and the fire, cease. I will let you go, and you shall not stay any longer.
Moses said to him: As soon as I go out of the city, I will spread out my hands to God, and these voices will cease, and there will be no more hail or rain,
so that you may know that the earth is the Lord's. But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not fear God.
The flax and the barley were struck, for the barley had just come up and the flax was going to seed. But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late.
Moses went out of the city, away from Pharaoh, and spread out his hands to the Lord. The thunder stopped, and the hail and rain no longer poured down on the earth.
When Pharaoh saw that the thunder, the hail and the rain had stopped, he went on sinning, and he hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not let the children of Israel go, as the Lord had told Moses.
As the Lord lives, who has judged me in this way, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
as long as this breath is still in me and the divine spirit is in my nostrils, my lips shall not speak lawlessness, and my soul shall not speak falsehood.
Far be it from me to declare you in the right as long as I live, for I will not give up my innocence,
while I hold on to righteousness and do not let it go. I do not know of any lawless deed in myself.
Not so; rather, let my enemies be like the overthrow of the ungodly, and let those who have risen up against me be like the destruction of the lawless.
What hope does the ungodly man have when he holds on? Will he go on hoping in the Lord, and will he be saved? Will the Lord hear my prayer?
When distress comes upon him, will he have any boldness before him? If he calls, will he hear him?
But now I will tell you what is in the hand of the Lord, and I will not lie about what is with the Almighty.

See, all of you know that you attack me for nothing and in vain. This is the portion that the ungodly man receives from the Lord, and the inheritance of the mighty will come upon them from the Almighty.
Even if their children become many, they will be handed over to slaughter. Even if they grow up, they will become beggars for bread.
Those of them who are still alive, their children will be wiped out by death. No one will have pity on their widow.
Even if they pile up silver like earth and pile up gold like clay, the righteous will gather all of it, and they will truly carry off their wealth.
His house will become like a moth and like a spider's web. The rich man has lain down and will gain nothing more. He opened his eyes, and he is no more.
For pains have come upon him like waters, and a whirlwind carried him off in the night. A burning heat will lift him up and carry him away and scatter him from his place.
It will fall upon him and will not spare him. He will run in flight from its hand. Its hands clapped over him, and it will carry him away from his place.
For there is a place for silver, where it comes from, and there is a place for gold, where it comes out.
For iron comes out of the earth, and bronze is dug out like stone.
He set a limit for darkness, and he searches out every end: the stone of darkness and the shadow of death, the cutting of a ravine out of the dust.
Those who forget the right ways have grown weak and fallen away from among people.
Wisdom is better.
Proclaim this among the nations: make the war holy, stir up the warriors, bring them near, and let all the men of war go up.
Beat your plowshares into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak man boast, saying, "I am strong."
Gather together and come, all you nations round about, and gather there; let the meek become a warrior.
Rise up, and let all the nations go up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge the nations round about.
Send out the sickles, for the grape harvest has come;
go in and tread, for the winepresses are full and the vats overflow, for their wicked deeds have multiplied.
Let them cry out with loud cries in the valley of judgment. Let the sun and the moon be darkened, and let the brightness of the stars be hidden.
But the Lord will roar from Zion and utter his voice from Jerusalem, and the heavens and the earth will shake; but the Lord will spare his people and will strengthen the children of Israel.
And you will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwell in Zion, my holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will no longer pass through it.
And on that day the mountains will drip sweetness and the hills milk, and water will flow in all the streambeds of Judah,
and a spring will come out from the house of the Lord and water the valley of the portions.
Egypt will be a desolation, and Edom a plain of desolation, because of the wrongs done to the sons of Judah, because they shed innocent blood on the earth.
But Judea will remain forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
And I will take vengeance for their seed [?], and I will not hold them guiltless; and the Lord will dwell in Zion.
