And it came to pass,
after these things, that the chief cupbearer offended the king of Egypt, and the chief baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh was angry with his two eunuchs, the cupbearer and the chief baker, and he put them in the prison of the chief cook, the place where Joseph was imprisoned.
And the chief jailer entrusted them to Joseph, and he attended them. And they were in the prison for many days.
And both of them had a dream, each of them on the same night, a dream-vision:
the cupbearer and the chief baker, who belonged to the king of Egypt and who were in the prison.
Joseph went in to them in the morning and saw them, and they were troubled.
He questioned Pharaoh's eunuchs who were with him in the prison of his lord, and said to them, "Why are your faces sad?"
They said to him, "We have had a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." Joseph said to them, "Does not their interpretation come from God?"
…tell it to me." And the cupbearer told him his dream and said to him: "In my sleep I was seeing, and there was a vine before me.
And on the vine were three branches, and it sprouted, and a shoot grew, and the clusters were ripe.
And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup and put the cup into his hand."
Joseph said to him: "This is its interpretation: the three roots are three days.
"Three more days will pass, and Pharaoh will remember your office and will restore you to your post as cupbearer,
and you will put Pharaoh's cup into his hand as in your former office, when you were his cupbearer.
And remember me yourself when things go well for you, and show me mercy and mention me before Pharaoh, so that he may bring me out of this prison.
For I was carried off by theft from the land of the Hebrews, and here I have done nothing evil, and yet they threw me into this house of the dungeon."
And when the chief baker saw that he had interpreted rightly for him, he said to Joseph:
"I too saw a dream: it seemed to me that three baskets of white bread were set on my head.
And in the uppermost basket there was some of every kind of food that King Pharaoh eats,
the work of the chief baker, and the birds of the sky were eating from the basket that was on my head."
Joseph answered and said: "This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
Three more days will pass, and Pharaoh will cut off your head from you and hang you on a tree, and the birds of the sky will eat your flesh."
And it came to pass on the third day that it was Pharaoh's birthday, and there was a great feast for all Pharaoh's servants;
and he remembered the office of the cupbearer and the office of the chief baker among his servants.
And he restored the cupbearer to his office, and he put the cup into Pharaoh's hands.
But the chief baker he hanged on a tree, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
But the cupbearer did not remember Joseph; instead he forgot him.
What shall I do if the Lord brings judgment upon me? Or if he makes a visitation, and speaks to me, what word shall I answer him?
Were they not in the womb just as I was? Were we not in the same belly? When did the helpless ever need anything anywhere, and I withheld it?
Or when did I ever bring grief to the eyes of the widow? Or did I ever eat bread alone and not give to the orphan?
For from my youth I raised them like a father; from my mother's womb I guided them.
Or did I ever disregard the naked, and not clothe the afflicted?
And all the helpless blessed me, for their shoulders were warmed by the fleece of my sheep.
Or did I ever raise my hand against the orphan with confidence, thinking that I had much support?
Then let my arm fall from my shoulder, and let my hand be broken off at the elbow.
For I was held by the fear of the Lord, and I could not withstand his words. Did I hide gold in the earth, or did I put my trust in precious stones?
Did I rejoice over my great wealth, or did I lay my hand on riches without number?
Did I not see the sun rising and setting, and the moon waning and full, for it is above these?
Was my heart ever secretly led astray, so that I put my hand to my mouth and kissed it?
That too would be counted against me as great iniquity, for I would have lied before God Most High.
Did I ever rejoice at the fall of my enemy, and did my heart ever say, "Aha!"?
Then let my ear hear my curse, and let me become a byword for evil among the people.
Did I often say to my maidservants, "Who will give us his flesh so that we may be filled?"
I was very kind. Did a stranger from outside ever fail to lodge in my house? For my door was open to all who came.
Or did I ever sin willingly and hide my sin?
For I was not ashamed to confess before the whole crowd of people. Or did I send the helpless away empty-handed? Who will give me a hearing?
For I feared the hand of the Lord. If I held a written bond from anyone, I placed it on my shoulders,
and I tore it up and gave it back to them, and I took nothing of the debt from him.
The land never groaned because of me, and its furrows never wept together.
If I ate its produce by myself alone, or seized land and grieved the soul of the land's owner, then let nettles grow up for me instead of wheat, and brambles instead of barley.
"Return to me, and I will return to you," says the Lord Almighty. "But you said, 'How shall we return?' Will a man defraud God?
For you are defrauding me. And you said, 'How are we defrauding you?' Because the tithes and the firstfruits of your produce are still with you.
You look at me with downcast eyes, and you defraud me. The year has ended, and you brought the produce into the storehouses, and there was plunder in your houses.
Turn back from this," says the Lord Almighty, "so that I may open the floodgates of heaven for you and pour out my blessing on you until there is enough.
I will provide food for you by my command, and I will not destroy the produce of your land, and the vine in your field will not wither," says the Lord Almighty.
"All the nations will call you blessed, for you will be favoured in the land," says the Lord Almighty.
I love him, because he heard me, because he turned his ear to me.
Lord, who [?] has believed the report?
Faith is a power [?], the proof of things that are not seen. For by it the elders received God's approval.
By faith we understand that the ages were established by the word of God, so that what is seen was made from what is not visible.
[?] By faith Abel offered a greater sacrifice than Cain's. Through it he was attested to be righteous, by the testimony given about his sacrifices.
And because of it, even though he died, he still speaks. By faith Enoch was taken away so that he would not see death;
and he was not found, because God had taken him away. Before he was taken away, it was attested that he had pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever comes to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

By faith Noah, when he received a command about things not yet seen, was afraid and built an ark to save himself. Through it he condemned the world, and through that faith of righteousness he became an heir.
By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and went out to the place he was to receive as an inheritance. He went out from there without knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a sojourner in the land of promise, as if in a foreign land, dwelling in a tent with Isaac and Jacob, who were co-heirs of the same promise;
for he was waiting for the city that has foundations, whose master builder and maker is God.
By faith Sarah herself also, though she was barren, received power to conceive offspring, and she gave birth when she was past the age, because she considered faithful the one who had promised her.
Therefore these too came from one man, and from one as good as dead: as many as the stars in number, and as countless as the sand of the sea.
All these died in faith without having received what was promised. But they saw it from far off, greeted it, and confessed
that they were strangers and passers-by on the earth. For people who say such things make it plain that they are seeking a homeland.
If they had been thinking of the land they had left, they would have had a chance to return there. But as it is, they set their hearts on a better one, that is, a heavenly one.
Therefore God was not ashamed to be called their God, for he prepared a city for them to dwell in.
By faith he offered up Isaac when he was tested. The one who had received the promise was offering up his only son, about whom it had been said: "Through Isaac your offspring will be named."
He reasoned that God is able even to raise people from the dead, and from there, figuratively speaking, he did receive him back.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob concerning things to come.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and bowed in worship over the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, when he was near his end, spoke of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's command.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing to suffer mistreatment with the people of God rather than enjoy the short-lived pleasure of sin.
He considered the reproach of Christ to be greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, because he was looking ahead to the reward.
By faith he left Egypt and did not fear the anger of the king, for he regarded the invisible as though it were visible.
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if on dry land; when the Egyptians attempted it, they were drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell after being encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with the disobedient, for she had received the spies in peace.
And it shall be, when the Lord God brings you into the land that you are crossing over into to inherit it, that you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not there beyond the Jordan, toward the road of the setting sun, in the land of Canaan,
which lies to the west, near the tall oak? For you are crossing the Jordan.
Go in and inherit the land which the Lord your God is giving you as a portion for all the days that you live on the earth.
You shall utterly destroy every place where the nations serve their idols, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every tree of the grove.
Tear down their altars, cut down their sacred groves, burn their carved idols with fire, and wipe out their names from that place.
But you shall not do so to the Lord your God;
rather, seek out the place which the Lord your God chooses in one of your tribes, to put his name there, and go in there.
And offer there your sacrifices and offerings, and your firstfruits, and your freewill offerings, and your offerings of confession, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your flocks.
And you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice in everything
to which you put your hand, you and your household, as the Lord your God has blessed you.
You shall not do as we are doing here today, each one doing what is right in his own eyes;
for you have not yet come to the place of rest which the Lord your God is giving you.
Cross the Jordan and settle in the land which the Lord your God is giving you, and he will give you rest from your enemies all around, and you will dwell in safety.
And there shall be a place which the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called upon it; there you shall offer all that I command you today:
your sacrifices, your offerings, the firstfruits of your hands, your gifts, and all the choicest of your gifts, whatever you vow to the Lord your God.
And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your sons and your daughters, your servants, and the Levite
who is within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance among you: the Lord God is their portion.
Take care that you do not offer your sacrifice in just any place you see;
but in the place which the Lord your God chooses in one of your cities, there you shall offer your sacrifice, and there you shall do all that I command you.
But with all eagerness you shall sacrifice and eat meat, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which he has given you, in all your cities.
The unclean among you and the clean shall eat it alike, as the gazelle and the deer. But you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
You may not eat within your cities the tithe of your wheat and of your wine,
and of your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle, and any of your vows, as many as you have vowed, and your confession offerings, and the first fruits of your hands.
But you shall eat them before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose: you, and your son, and your daughter,
your male servant and your maidservant, and the stranger who is in your cities; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God in everything to which you have put your hand.
Take care that you do not abandon the Levite as long as you live on the earth.
If the Lord your God enlarges your borders, as he told you, and you say,
"I will eat meat," if your soul desires to eat meat, then with all the desire of your soul you shall eat meat.
If the place which the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there is far away,
then you shall sacrifice from your cattle and from your sheep, and from whatever the Lord your God gives you, as he commanded you, and you shall eat within your cities according to your desire.
As the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it; the unclean among you and the clean among you shall eat it alike.
Be very careful not to eat the blood, for its blood is its life, and the life shall not be eaten with the flesh. You shall not eat it; you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
But your holy things, and whatever belongs to you, and your vows, you shall take and go to the place which the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.
And there you shall make your sacrifices, and offer the flesh to the Lord your God on the altar; but the blood you shall sprinkle around the altar, and you shall eat the flesh.
How long will you wear out my soul and break me down with words? But only know this: that the Lord has done this to me.
You plot evil against me and shamelessly fall upon me. Yes, truly I have gone astray, and error rests upon me, to speak words that were not fitting.
My words go astray and are untimely. Let it be, for you exalt yourselves over me and come against me with reproaches.
Know that it is the Lord who has stirred things up like this; he has raised his harsh things [?] against me.
Behold, I laughed at reproach and did not speak; I cry out, and there is no justice.
I am walled in all around, for he has laid darkness on my face, and stripped my glory from me, and taken the crown from my head.
He has torn me down all around, and I am gone. He has cut down my hope like a tree, and has dealt with me harshly in wrath. You have despised me as an enemy.
And his trials came upon me all together; those lying in wait surrounded me on my ways.
My brothers have gone far from me; they acknowledged a stranger rather than me; my friends have become merciless to me.
My neighbours have counted me as nothing, and those who knew my name have forgotten me. The kinsmen of my household and my servants: I have become a stranger before them.
I called my servant, and he did not listen to me. My mouth pleaded, and I begged my wife.
I appealed to the sons of my concubines, but they rejected me forever. Whenever I rose up, you plotted evil against me.
Those who knew me have come to loathe me, and those whom I loved have risen up against me.
Within my skin my flesh has rotted, and my bones are held in your teeth.
Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, my friends, for the hand of the Lord has struck me.
Why do you persecute me as the Lord does, and why can you not get enough of my flesh?
Who would let me write down my words and set them in a book forever, with a pen of iron and lead, or carve them on a rock?
I know that the one who means to deliver me from the earth is everlasting.
he will raise up my skin, which has endured these things. For these things have been done to me by the Lord,
These things I know of myself; my own eye has seen them, and no one else's. For all things have been fulfilled in my bosom.
If you should say, “What shall we say before him?”, it is because we have found the root of the matter in him.
You too should be afraid because of what is hidden, for wrath will come upon the lawless, and then they will know where their righteousness is.
Do not oppress the downtrodden,
for he is poor; and do not treat the helpless with contempt at the gates. For the Lord will judge his case, and you will save your soul from harm.
Do not make a friend of a hot-tempered man, and do not keep company with an angry companion, or you may learn his ways and take a snare for your soul.
Do not give yourself as surety out of shame before someone's face. If he has nothing, what will he pay? They will take your bed out from under you.
A man who is capable and quick in his work is worthy to stand before kings, and not before men who lack understanding.
If you sit down to dine at the table of a powerful man, consider carefully what is set before you, and only then put out your hand.
Know that you will have to provide such things in return, if you are greedy. Do not long for his food, for it holds a life of falsehood.
If you are poor, do not try to match a rich man, but keep your mind away from it. If you fix your eyes on his wealth, it will be gone.
For wings like an eagle's are made ready for it, and it will return to the house of its master.
Do not eat with an envious man, and do not long for his food. For he will eat and drink with you the way someone swallows a hair;
do not bring him in with you, and do not eat bread with him, for he will vomit it up and mock your good words.
Say nothing in the hearing of fools, or they may scorn your wise words.
Do not move the ancient boundaries, and do not take over the land of orphans. For their redeemer is the Lord, who is mighty, and he will plead their case against you.
Give your heart to instruction, and make your ears ready for words of knowledge.
Do not hold back instruction from young children. If you strike a child with a rod, he will not die.
You will strike him with the rod, but you will deliver his soul from death.
Thus says the Most High:
Let my prayer come in before you, O Lord God of my life.
To all the earth: the heavens declare the glory.
My son, if your heart is wise, you will gladden my heart as well.
And let the words of my lips be in your mouth, if they are upright.
Do not let your heart be zealous for sin, but let your heart be in the fear of God all the days.
If you keep these things, you will have offspring, and your hope will not be taken away from you. Listen, my son, and become wise, and direct the understanding of your heart.
Do not be a wine-drinker, and do not look to the company of others or to the buying of meat. For every drunkard and fornicator and sluggard will become poor, and will be clothed in rags.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, for he begot you; and do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
A righteous father raises his children well, and his heart rejoices over a wise son.
Let your father and your mother rejoice over you, and let the one who bore you be glad.
Give me your heart, my son, and let your eyes keep my ways. For another's house is a pierced jar, and a narrow and strange pit.
For she will perish suddenly and quickly, and every lawless person will be destroyed. Who has turmoil?
Woe! Who has turmoil? Who has judgement? Who has sorrows and troubles? Who has bruises for no reason?
Whose eyes are bleary, if not those who linger over wine, who go searching for wine, wherever there are drinking parties?
Do not get drunk with wine. Instead, look to righteous men, and talk with one another as you walk.
For this reason let me take care:
Lift up [?], all the nations.

When day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas;

of Tyre and Sidon, who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. And those who were troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
The whole crowd tried to come near him, because power went out from him, and he healed them all.

Hear, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be multiplied, so that you may have many ways of life.
For the ways of life will teach you and will set you on the paths of righteousness. If you walk, your steps will not falter; and if you run, you will not grow weary.
Hold fast to your instruction and do not abandon it, but keep it for the life of your soul. Do not walk in the way of the ungodly, and do not imitate them.
Wherever they set up camp, do not go there; turn away from it and leave it. For they do not sleep until they have done evil;
their sleep has been taken from them, and they do not sleep, those who share in the food of ungodliness and get drunk on the wine of lawlessness.
But the ways of the righteous shine like lights; they go before and give light until the day is fully come.
But the ways of the ungodly are dark, and they do not know it until their feet stumble.
I am the Lord your God, and there is no other besides.
I made light and darkness; I created peace and evil. I am the Lord your God, who made all these things.
Let the heavens rejoice from above, and let the clouds rain down righteousness; let the earth bring forth mercy, and let righteousness spring up together with it.
I am the Lord your God, who made you and created you. And moreover I prepared you like the potter's clay.
Does the ploughman plough the earth all day long? Or will the clay say to the potter: "What are you making?" or "What are you doing?"
Or will the thing that is made say: "You have no hands"? Or will the creature talk back to its creator?
Woe to the one who says to his father: "Why did you beget me?" or to his mother: "Why did you go through labour for me?"
For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, who created you, who made the things that are to come in times ahead:
Ask me about my sons, and command me about the works of my hands. I made the earth and humankind upon it;
with my hand I established the heavens, and I commanded all the stars to exist. I raised him up as king in righteousness, and all my ways are straight.
For he will build my city and bring back the captives of my people, not for ransom nor for bribes, says the Lord Almighty.
Therefore put away falsehood; let each of you speak the truth with his neighbour, for we are members of one another.
Be angry, but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger. And do not give the devil a foothold.
Let the thief steal no more, but rather let him work hard, doing good with his own hands, so that he may have something to give to anyone in need.
Let no foul word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as the need requires, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness and anger, wrath and shouting and slander be removed from you entirely, together with all malice.
Be kind to one another, merciful, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ has forgiven us.
Be therefore imitators of God, as beloved children, and let us walk in love,
just as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us as an offering, a sacrifice to God, for a fragrant aroma.
O God, [come] to my help. Make haste.
There was a certain rich man, and he was always clothed in purple and fine linen, and he rejoiced splendidly.
There was a certain poor man named Lazarus, who lay fallen at his gates with grievous sores; he would look and long,
and his heart desired to be filled with the crumbs of that rich man. But even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
And it came to pass, when the poor man died, that the angels took him and brought him and placed him in the bosom of Abraham. The rich man also died and was buried.
And in hell he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham from afar and Lazarus in his bosom.
He raised his voice, began to speak, and said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus,
so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and touch it to my lips and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame.
Abraham answered and said to him: Remember, son, that you received good things in your lifetime, and likewise Lazarus bore evil things.
Now behold, he is comforted here, and you there are suffering. And further, what more shall I tell you? Besides all these things, between you and us there is a chasm,
so that if anyone wishes to cross from here to you, he is not able, nor can anyone cross over from there to here.
Then he began to speak and said: Then I beseech you, father Abraham, to send him to my father's house,
for I have five brothers, so that he may go and tell them, and they may not come to this place of torment.
Abraham said to him: There, son, are Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them. But he said to him: No; if someone goes to them from the dead, will they not believe?
Abraham said to him: If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, even if someone rises from the dead, they will not believe.

They did not understand, those who carry their carved wood and pray to gods who cannot save them.
Or let them declare something. Let them draw near and say together: Who made these things known, since from the very beginning it was told to you then?
I am the Lord, and there is no other besides me, righteous and a Saviour, and there is no one apart from me.
Turn to me and be saved, you who are at the end of the earth. I am God, and there is no other besides me, says the Lord.
Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.
You know that when you were still Gentiles, you followed after mute idols and were led astray.
Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed"; and no one can say "Lord Jesus" except by the Holy Spirit.
There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit. There are varieties of ministries, and the same Lord himself.
There are varieties of workings, and it is the same Lord himself who works all things in all.
And to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for what is better. To one is given the word of wisdom;
to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; to another faith from the same Spirit; to another the gift of healings from the same Spirit;
to another the working of mighty powers; to another prophecy; to another discernment of spirit; to another various kinds of tongues; to another interpretation of tongues.
All this is worked by one and the same Spirit, who distributes to each person individually as he wills.
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members, though many, are one body, so also is Christ.
By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether slaves or free;
and we have all been given one Spirit to drink. For the body is not one member, but many.

And the Spirit of God strengthened Gideon, and he blew the horn trumpet; and Abiezer cried out and gathered behind him.
And he sent a messenger throughout all Manasseh, and it too cried out and gathered behind him. And he sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali, and they came up to meet him.
And Gideon said to God: "If you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said, look, I will lay a fleece of wool on the threshing floor.
If there is dew on the fleece only, and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said."
And so it happened. Gideon rose early the next morning and wrung out the fleece, and the dew squeezed out of the fleece filled a bowl with water.
And Gideon said to God: Do not be angry with me in your wrath, and let me speak just once more; let me test once again with the fleece:
let there be dryness on the fleece alone, and on all the ground let there be dew.
And God did so that night: there was dryness on the fleece alone, and on all the ground there was dew.
And Jeroboam, that is, Gideon, rose early, he and all his people, and they camped in the land of Aloed;
and the camp of Midian and of Amalek was to the north of him, from the hills of Abor, in the valley.
And the Lord said to Gideon: The people who are with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel boast against me and say:
'My own hand has saved me.' And the Lord said to him: Now speak in the hearing of the people and say to them:
Whoever is fearful and afraid, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead. And twenty-two thousand men of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.
The Lord said to Gideon: The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and test them there.
And whoever I tell you is to go with you shall go, and whoever I do not tell you about shall not go with you. And he brought the people down to the water.
And the Lord said to Gideon: Everyone who laps the water with his tongue like a dog, set him apart by himself, and everyone who kneels down on his knees to drink, set him apart by himself.
And the number of all who lapped with their tongues was three hundred men; and all the rest of the people knelt down on their knees to drink water.
And the Lord said to Gideon: With these three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hands; and let all the rest of the people go back, each man to his own place.
And they took the people's provisions in their hands, and their trumpets; and he sent every man of Israel away to his own home and kept only the three hundred men.
Now the camp of Midian was below, in the valley.
And that night the Lord said to him: Get up and go down quickly from here to the camp, for I have given it into your hands.
If you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp, you and Purah your servant, and you will hear what they are saying;
after that your hands will be strengthened and you will go down against the camp. And he went down with Purah his servant to the edge of the companies of fifty that were in the camp.
And Midian and Amalek and all the people of the east were camped in that valley, as many as locusts,
and their camels could not be counted; they were as many as the sand on the seashore. And Gideon went in.
And there was a man telling his companion a vision, and he said: Here is a dream I dreamed:
there was a loaf of barley bread rolling through the camp of Midian, and it came all the way to the tent of Midian, struck it and overturned it, and it fell.
His companion answered and said: This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite; for God has given Midian and this whole camp into his hand.
And when Gideon heard the account of the vision and its interpretation, he bowed down to the Lord, went back to the camp of Israel, and said to them:
Get up, for the Lord has given the camp of Midian into our hands.
And he divided the three hundred men into three companies. He put horn trumpets into their hands, along with empty jars and torches inside the jars.
And he said to them: "Watch me and do the same. Look, I will go into the middle of the camp, and whatever I do, you do the same.
I will blow the trumpet, and all who are with me, and you also will blow the horn trumpets all around the camp and say: 'The sword of God and of Gideon!'"

And Gideon and a hundred men with him went in at one side of the camp, at the very start of the first watch of the night, and they roused the watchmen fully awake. They blew the horn trumpets and smashed the jars.
They held the torches in their left hands and the horn trumpets in their right hands.
And each man stood in his own place around the camp, and the whole camp ran.
And they blew the trumpets, and the enemy fled; and the three hundred blew the horn trumpets.
And the Lord turned each man's sword against his fellow throughout the whole camp. The camp fled as far as Beth-shittah, and as far as the edge of Abel-meholah, toward Tabbath.
And the men of Naphtali and of Asher cried out, and all of Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.
And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the territory of Ephraim, saying:
"Come down to meet the Midianites, and get ahead of them to seize the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan."
And the men of Ephraim cried out and seized the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.
They captured the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at Surub [?], and they killed Zeeb at Jakeb-zeeb.
And they pursued Midian and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon.
Do not bring an ungodly man to the dwelling
of the righteous; do not be led astray by a full and satisfied heart. For even if the righteous man falls seven times, he will rise again; but the ungodly will grow weak in evil.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and do not exalt yourself when he stumbles,
or else the Lord may see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
Do not rejoice over evildoers, and do not envy sinners. For the wicked will have no offspring, and the brightness of the ungodly will be put out.
My son, fear God and the king, and do not disobey either of them. For the ungodly will be called to account suddenly, and who can know the punishment that these two will bring?
A son who keeps the word will quickly and soon be saved from destruction; the Lord will surely receive him.
And no lie will come out of his mouth.
But I will hope in the Lord and wait for God my Savior, and my God, my Savior, will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy. I have fallen, but I will rise; and even if I walk in darkness, the Lord is my light.
I will endure the Lord's anger, because I sinned against him, until he sets my case right and gives me justice. He will bring me out into the light, and he will see my righteousness.
And my enemy will see me, and shame will cover her who said to me: Where is the Lord your God?
My eyes will look upon her. Now he will make her like mud to be trampled on the road.
A day of plastering, as with mud brick. He will blot it out on that day, and that day will remove your law.
And your cities will come to confinement and to destruction by the Assyrians, and your fortified cities will be cut off, from Tyre to the river, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
And the land will be given over to destruction together with those who live in it, because of the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your rod, the sheep of your inheritance, who dwell [apart?] from the mountains in a forest in the midst of Carmel;
let them graze among Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old; and as in the days of your coming out of Egypt, you will show them wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might, and they will lay their hands on their mouths; their ears will be deafened;
and they will lick the dust like snakes and crawl on the earth; they will tremble in their confinement before the Lord our God.
Who is a God like you? You blot out iniquities and pass over the falsehoods of the remnant of his inheritance.
And he did not keep his anger as a witness, for he is one who delights in mercy.
He will turn back and have mercy on us and cover our sins, and he will cast all our sins into the depth of the sea.
He will give truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, as the Lord swore to our fathers in the days of old.
O Lord God of hosts of Jacob. For they are beloved:
I, Daniel, was watching a vision in the night, and behold, the four winds of heaven burst upon the great sea.
And four beasts were coming up out of the sea, each greater than the other. The first was like a lioness, and it had wings like an eagle's;
I watched until its wings were plucked off, and it came out onto the earth and stood on a man's feet, and a man's heart was given to it.
And behold, the second beast came out, like a bear, and it stood on one side, and there were three ribs in its mouth between its teeth;
and they said this to it: Arise and devour the flesh of many. And after this I watched, and behold, another beast, like a leopard.
And it had four bird's wings on its back, and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.
After this I watched, and behold, a fourth beast was coming out, terrible and astonishing and mightier than all; its teeth were of iron;
it ate and crushed, and trampled what was left with its feet.
It was greater and mightier than all the beasts that came before it, and it had ten horns. And behold,
a small horn came up among its horns, and three horns were plucked out before it, from in front of it;
and behold, there were eyes like a man's in that horn, and a mouth that spoke great things.
I kept watching until thrones were set up, and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head was like pure wool.
His throne was like a flame of fire, and its wheels blazed like fire. A river of fire flowed before him.
Thousands upon thousands stood before him, and tens of thousands upon tens of thousands served him. The court sat for judgment, and the books of record were opened.

Then I kept watching because of the sound of the boastful words that the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was destroyed and done away with, and its body was handed over to be burned with fire.
The dominion of the other beasts was taken away, but they were allowed to go on living for a long time.
I kept watching in the vision of the night, and behold, one like a son of man was coming with the clouds of heaven. He came as far as the Ancient of Days and was brought before him.
He was given dominion and the honour of kingship, and all tribes, peoples and languages served him.
His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
My heart trembled within my body, and the vision in my head terrified me, Daniel.
I went up to one of those standing there and asked him for the exact truth about all this.
He told me truthfully and made known to me the interpretation of the words. He said to me: “These four beasts are four kings who will arise on the earth.
But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever.”
Then I asked for the exact truth about the fourth beast, which was greater and larger than all the other beasts and far more terrifying.
Its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze. It devoured and crushed, and it trampled what was left with its feet.
I also asked about the horns on its head, and about the one horn that came up last and uprooted the first three.
That horn had eyes and a mouth that spoke boastful things, and it looked greater than the other beasts. I kept watching, and that beast was waging war against the saints of the Most High
and was overpowering them, until the Ancient of Days came. Judgment was given in favour of the saints of the Most High, the time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom.
“The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on the earth. It will be greater than all the kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it and crush it.
The ten horns are ten kings who will arise. After them another king will arise who will be more evil than the others
who came before him, and he will bring down those other kings. He will speak words against the Most High and make war on the saints of the Most High.
He will intend to change the times and the law, and they will be handed over to him for a time, times and part of a time.
Then the court will sit in judgment, and his dominion will be taken away, to be destroyed and wiped out.
The kingdom, the authority, the glory and the greatness of all the kings on the whole earth
will be given to the saints of the Most High, along with an everlasting kingdom. All rulers will serve him and obey him.”
This is the end of the account.
For this reason I bend my knees before the Father,
from whom every tribe in heaven and on earth is named, so that he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory,
to be strengthened by his Spirit in the inner man, so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith,
being rooted and grounded in love, so that you may be able to grasp, together with all the saints, what is the breadth and the depth,
the height and the length, and to know the love of Christ, which surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him who is able to do far more than all things, beyond what we ask or understand, according to the power of his help at work among us,
to him be glory in the church through Christ Jesus, to all generations of the ages. Amen.
Let us purify ourselves:
When Joseph made himself known to his brothers, he raised his voice in weeping. All the Egyptians heard it, and it was heard in Pharaoh's house.
Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph. Is our father still alive?" His brothers could not answer Joseph a word, because they were afraid and greatly terrified.
Joseph said to his brothers, "Come near to me." And they came near. He said to them, "I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
But now do not grieve, and do not take it hard that you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to save your lives.
This is only the second year of famine in the land, and there are still five more years to come, in which there will be no ploughing and no threshing.
God sent me ahead of you so that a remnant of you would survive on the earth, to keep you alive as a great remnant.
So now it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me like a father to Pharaoh, lord over all his house, and ruler over all Egypt.
Hurry now, go up to my father and tell him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt.
Come down to me, and do not delay. Settle in the land of Goshen, which belongs to Arabia, and be near me,
you and your sons and your sons' sons, your sheep and your cattle and all that you have. I will provide for you there,
for there are still five years of famine to come, so that you and your sons and all your possessions will not perish.'
Look, your eyes see, and so do the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
Tell my father about all my glory in Egypt, everything that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father here."
Then he threw his arms around Benjamin's neck and wept over him, and Benjamin wept on Joseph's neck.
He kissed all his brothers and wept with them. After that his brothers talked with him.
The news reached Pharaoh's house, and they told him, "Joseph's brothers have come." Pharaoh and all his household rejoiced.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers to do this: 'Fill your sacks with wheat and go to the land of Canaan.'"
And bring your father and come to me. And I will give you all the good things of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
But you, command them thus: that they take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and wives, and bring your father and come to me.
And do not let your eye spare your belongings, for all the good things of Egypt shall be yours.
And the sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons according to the command of Pharaoh the king, and provided them with food for the road.
And to each of them he gave two sets of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave two hundred drachmas and five pairs of garments of various colours.
And to his father he likewise sent ten donkeys, loaded with all kinds of good things, and ten mules carrying bread as provisions for the journey for his father.
And he sent his brothers away, and they went. And Joseph said to them: Do not quarrel on the way.
And they went up from the land of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
And they told him, saying: Your son Joseph is alive, and he rules over all the land of Egypt.
And he was astonished in his mind and did not believe them. And they told him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them.
And when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, then the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
Israel said: This is a great thing for me, if Joseph my son is alive. I will go and see him before I die.
Israel set out, he and all that was his, and came to the Well of the Oath, and offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
God spoke to Israel in a vision of the night: Jacob, Jacob! And he said: Here I am, Lord.
God said to him: I am the God of your fathers. Do not be afraid to go down into Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
And I will bring you up again from there in the end. And Joseph shall lay his hands on your eyes.
Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, and do not be loose with your lips.
Do not say: As he did to me, so I will do to him, and I will repay him for as much as he harmed me. A foolish man is like a field for tilling, and a man lacking in understanding is like a vineyard.
If you abandon it, it will become desolate; grass will spring up in it and it will become completely desolate, and its stone walls will be torn down.
Afterwards I repented and looked to choose instruction: "I sleep a little, and I fold my hands on my breast a little."
If you do this, your poverty will come upon you like a forerunner, and your want like a good runner.
The leech had three daughters, dearly loved, and all three of them could not satisfy her, and the fourth was not content to say, "Enough."
Hell, and the love of women, and Tartarus, and the earth that is never filled with water. Water and fire have not said, "Enough."
The eyes that mock a father and despise a mother's old age: let the ravens of the valley pluck them out, and let the young of the eagle devour them.
There are three things that are impossible for me, and the fourth I could not understand:
the track of an eagle in flight, the way of a serpent on a rock, the paths of a ship's passage, [?] [one that is appointed?], and the ways of a man in his youth.
Such is the way of an adulterous [?] woman: when she has done it, she washes herself and then says, "I have done nothing wrong."
By three things the earth is shaken, and the fourth I cannot bear: if a slave becomes king, and if a fool is filled with bread;
and if a maidservant drives out her mistress, and if a hateful wife gets a good husband.
There are four things that are the smallest on the earth, and they are wiser than the wise: the ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
and the rock badgers, a feeble kind, which make their nests in the rocks; the locust has no king, yet at a single command it marches in good order;
the lizard [?] holds fast to the wall with its hands, and though it is easy to catch, it lives in royal palaces.
There are three things that walk well, and a fourth that goes along well: the lion's cub, strongest of beasts, which does not turn back and is not terrified by any wild animal;
the cock, which walks at ease among the hens; the he-goat, leader of the flocks; and the king who makes proclamation to the nations.
If you give yourself over to pleasure and put out your hand in a quarrel against your own face [?], you will be disgraced. Churn milk and it becomes butter.
If you squeeze the nose [?], blood comes out. If you draw out empty words, judgments and quarrels come out.
The words were spoken by God: the command of a king, which his mother taught him. What, my son, is keeping God's word before everything else?
I tell you, my son, what is it, son of my womb? What is it, son of our prayers?
Do not give your wealth to women, or your mind and your life to deficient counsel. Do everything with counsel; drink wine with counsel.
The mighty are quick to anger when they drink wine. So let them not drink, or they will forget wisdom and be unable to judge the weak rightly.
Strong drink is given to those in grief, and wine to drink to those in distress, so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their sufferings.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge the poor and the weak with righteousness.
Thus says Adonai the Lord:
Behold, I will bring the whole house of Israel out from among the nations to which they went, and I will gather them from all the lands around them and bring them into the land of Israel.
And I will make them one nation in my land and on the [?mountains] of Israel.
And there shall be one ruler, and they shall no longer be two nations, and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms.
So that they no longer defile themselves with their idols; and I will deliver them from all their lawless deeds by which they sinned,
and I will cleanse them, and they shall be my people, and I the Lord will be their God. And my servant David [?] among them as ruler.
And there shall be one shepherd over them all, for they shall walk in my commandments and keep my judgments and do them.
And they shall dwell in their land, which I gave to my servant Jacob, where their fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell in it;
and David my servant shall be their ruler forever. And I will make with them a covenant of peace; an everlasting covenant shall be with them;
and I will establish my sanctuary among them forever.
May your mercy, O Lord, go with me. I will not fear evil.
O God, great and almighty, Lord of great name, your eyes are on the ways of the sons of men, to repay each one according to his own way.
You did signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this very day in Israel and among those born of the earth, and you made a name for yourself,
as it is this day. And you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an uplifted arm, and with great sights.
And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey; and they came in and took possession of the land,
but they did not listen to your voice and did not walk in your commandments; and they did not do all that you commanded them, and all this has come upon them.
Behold, now, a people is coming against this city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword and the famine;
as God said, so it has come about. And you say to me: Buy a field for yourself with silver and write a deed;
and I sealed it and called witnesses to testify, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans.
For many [?].
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Go in and speak to Pharaoh, for I will harden his heart and the hearts of his servants, so that my signs may come upon them one after another,
so that you may tell in the ears of your children how I mocked the Egyptians, and the signs that I did among them, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and said to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself?
Let my people go, so that they may serve me. If you refuse to let my people go, behold, at this very hour tomorrow I will send a great swarm of locusts into all your territory.

And they shall cover the earth, and you will not be able to see the ground; and they shall eat all that remains, which was left over from the hail, and they shall eat every tree, the plants of the earth.
And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your servants, and all the houses of all the land of Egypt, such as your fathers have never seen since the day they came to be upon the earth.
And Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh. Pharaoh's servants said to him: How long shall this affliction be upon us?
Let these men go, so that they may serve the Lord their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined? And they brought Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to them: Go and serve the Lord your God. Who exactly are the ones I am to let go?
Moses said to him: We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and daughters, with our flocks and our cattle, for it is a feast of the Lord our God.
Pharaoh said to them: So be it, the Lord be with you! For I am letting you go, but surely not your belongings as well?
You see that evil lies before you. Not so; go, the men only, and serve the Lord your God, for that is what you yourselves are asking for.
And they drove them out from Pharaoh's presence. The Lord said to Moses:
"Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let locusts come up and devour every green plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees, everything that the hail left."
And Moses lifted up the rod in his hand toward heaven, and the Lord sent a wind from the south over the land all day and all night.
And when it was morning, the south wind brought up the locusts.
And it brought them over all the land of Egypt in very great numbers. Before that there had never been so many locusts, and after it there were never such again.
And they covered the face of the land, and the land was ruined. They devoured every green plant of the land and every fruit-bearing tree, everything that the hail had left.
Nothing green was left on the trees, and not one of all the green plants was left in all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them: "I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you.
Bear this sin of mine, and pray for me to the Lord your God, and take this death away from me."
Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord.
And the Lord sent a fierce and mighty wind from the sea, and it lifted up the locusts and threw them into the Red Sea, and not a single one was left in all the land of Egypt.
But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go.
The Lord said to Moses: "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness, gloom and murk over all the land of Egypt."
And for three days no one saw his brother, but the sons of Israel had light in every place where they went.
Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them: "Go and serve the Lord your God, but leave your sheep and your cattle behind, and take your belongings with you."
But Moses said: "No, you too must give us sacrifices and offerings to offer to the Lord our God,
until we arrive there." But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let them go.
Pharaoh said to Moses: "Go away from me, and be careful not to see my face again, because on the day you appear before me, you will die."
And Moses said: "As you have said, I will not appear before your face again."
And the Lord said to Moses: "I will bring one more plague on Pharaoh and on all Egypt, and after that they will send you away from here.
And when they send you away, they will drive you out completely.
Speak secretly in the ears of the people, and let every man ask his neighbor, and every woman her neighbor, for articles of gold and silver and for clothing, and you will plunder the Egyptians."
And the Lord gave his people great favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and in the sight of Pharaoh and his servants.
And Moses said: "Thus says the Lord: 'About midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt.
And every firstborn in Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sits on the throne, to the firstborn of the maidservant who sits at the flour, and to the firstborn of all the cattle.'"
And there shall be a great cry throughout all Egypt, such as there has never been, nor shall be again.
But among all the children of Israel not a dog shall move its tongue, against man or beast, so that you may see how great a thing the Lord will do between Egypt and the children of Israel.
And all these will come to me and bow down to me and say to me: Go out, you and all your people whom you lead.
And after that I will go out. And Moses went out from Pharaoh in anger.
The Lord said to Moses: Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that I may multiply my wonders and signs in Egypt.
And Moses and Aaron did these wonders and signs in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh,
but the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the children of Israel go out of the land of the Egyptians.
And the men who had caught up with Gideon said to him:
What is this thing that you have done to us, that you did not call us when you went out to fight Midian?
And they quarrelled with him fiercely. And Gideon said to them: What have I done now, as you say?
Is not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
For the Lord has given the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, into your hand; and what more have I been able to do, compared with you?
Then he calmed their hearts with these words. And Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men with him, exhausted and hungry.
And Gideon said to the men of Succoth: Give bread as food to these people of mine who are with me, for they are hungry, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.
And the men of Succoth said to him: Are the heads of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hands now, that we should give bread to your army?
Then Gideon said to them: Not so; but when the Lord has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with bull's-head [?].
And he went on from there and came to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way. The men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had spoken.
And Gideon said to the men of Penuel: When I return in peace from the battle, I will tear down this tower.
And Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their army with them, only about fifteen thousand, who had escaped from the whole army of the sons of the east.
And those who had fallen by the sword were a hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
And Gideon went up by the road of the tent-dwellers, east of Nobah and opposite Nabea [Jogbehah?], and attacked the army and destroyed it,
for their army was off its guard on that side, and they fell on them suddenly.
And Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and Gideon pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and all their army was scattered.
And Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
And he caught a young man from among the men of Succoth and asked him the names of the men of Succoth.
And Gideon wrote down the names of the princes and elders of Succoth, seventy-seven men.
And Gideon came to the princes of Succoth and said to them: "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna in my hands. You taunted me about them and said:
'Are the heads of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hands, that we should give bread to your army?'"
Then Gideon seized the princes and elders of the city. He took thorns and bull's-head [?] and tormented them with these, the men of Succoth.
And he tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of that city.
And he said to Zebah and Zalmunna: "Where [?] are the men whom you killed at Tabor?"
And they said to him: "They were like you, and you look like them. They looked like the sons of kings."
And Gideon said: "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the Lord lives, if you had not killed them, I would not kill you."
And Gideon said to Jether, his son: "Get up and kill them." But the boy did not draw his sword, because he was afraid, for he was still a boy.
And Zebah and Zalmunna said to him: "Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength."
And Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna. And he took the collars that were on the necks of their camels.
And the men of Israel said to Gideon: "Rule over us, you and your sons and your sons' sons, for you have saved us from the hands of Midian."
And Gideon said to them: "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The Lord will rule over you."
And Gideon said to them: "I ask one request of you:
let each one of you give me one earring from his plunder." For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
And they said to him: "We will certainly give them." And Gideon spread out his garment, and each man threw [?] into it a gold earring from his plunder.
And the weight of the gold earrings that he asked of them was

one thousand seven hundred shekels, not counting the collars, the beads, the purple garments and whatever else had belonged to the kings of Midian, and not counting the [?] that were on the necks of their camels.
And Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, Ophrah. And all Israel turned there to worship it, and it became a snare for Gideon and his house.
And Midian was humbled before the sons of Israel, and they could no longer raise their heads. And the land was at peace for forty years in the days of Gideon.
And Jeroboam [?Jerubbaal], son of Joash, who is the same person as Gideon, went off and lived in his own house.
And Gideon had seventy sons who were his own offspring, for he had many wives.
And his concubine who lived in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
And Gideon, son of Joash, died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of Joash, his father, in Ophrah of Abiezer.
And after Gideon died, the sons of Israel turned away and prostituted themselves by following Baal. And they made a covenant with Baal-berith that he would be their god.
And the children of Israel did not remember the Lord their God, who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies round about.
And they did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, in return for all the good that he had done in Israel.
Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; proclaim it, O daughter of Jerusalem.
Behold, your king is coming to you, righteous and a savior; he himself is meek, and he is mounted on a beast of burden and a new colt.
And he will destroy the chariots from Ephraim and the horses of Israel, and he will cut off the bow of war;
and there will be an abundance of peace from the nations, and he will rule over the waters as far as the sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
And you, by the blood of the covenant, have sent forth [your prisoners] from the pit in which there is no water.
And you will sit in the prison, you prisoners of the congregation, and in place of one day of your bondage I will repay you double.
For I have bent you for myself as a bow, and I have filled Ephraim; and I will raise up your children, O Zion, against the children of the Greeks, and I will wield you like the sword of a warrior.
And the Lord will be over them, and his arrows will go forth like lightning; the Lord Almighty will sound the trumpet, and he will go forth in the shaking of his heart.
And the Lord Almighty will help them.
Long-suffering, greatly merciful, and they ate [?]. [?] my soul and deliver me.
Who is this who hides [?] me, bowing [them?] down to the ground [?]:
I am writing these things to you, and I hope to come to you soon as well;
but if I am delayed, [I write] so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
And by common confession great is the mystery of godliness: he who was revealed in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels,
was proclaimed among the nations, was believed on in the world, and was taken up in glory.
