And Saul and his men went to seek David.
And they told David, and he went down to the rock in the wilderness of Maon. And Saul heard of it, and pursued after David into the wilderness of Maon.
And Saul and his men were going along one side of the mountain, and David was going secretly away from the presence of Saul.
And Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men, wanting to seize them.
And a messenger came to Saul and said to him: "Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on our land."
And Saul turned back and pursued David no longer, and went to meet the Philistines. For this reason that place was called the Rock of Separation.
And David went up from there and stayed in the narrow places of En-gedi.
And when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, they told him, saying: "Behold, David is in the wilderness of Engedi."
And he took with him three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to search for David and his men in front of the hunting-ground of the deer.
And he came to the sheepfolds of the flocks, which were by the road.
And there was a cave there, and Saul went in to prepare himself. And David and his men were sitting in the inner part of the cave.
And David's men said to him: "Behold, this is the day of which the Lord said to you:
'I will give your enemy into your hands, and do to him whatever is pleasing in your eyes.'"
And David arose and secretly cut off the edge of Saul's cloak.
And after this David repented in his heart, because he had cut off the edge of his cloak. And David said to his men:
"Far be it from me before the Lord that I should do this thing to my lord, the Lord's anointed, to lay my hand on him, for he is the Lord's anointed."
And David persuaded his men with these words and did not let them rise up and kill Saul. And Saul arose and went out of the cave on his way.
And David also came out of the cave after him, and David cried out to Saul and said: "My lord the king!"
And Saul looked behind him, and David bowed down with his face to the ground and did obeisance.
And David said to Saul: "Why do you listen to the words of the people who tell you, 'David seeks your life'?
Behold, this day your eyes have seen how the Lord gave you into my hands in this cave, and I did not wish to kill you, but spared you and said:
'I will not lay my hand on my lord, for he is the Lord's anointed.'
And behold, the edge of your cloak is in my hand. I cut off the edge of your cloak and did not kill you.
Know and see today that there is no falsehood in my hands, nor insult, nor lawlessness, and I have not sinned against you in anything; yet you have pursued my life to take it.
May the Lord judge between you and me, and may he avenge me on you; but my hand shall not be upon you.
As the proverb of the ancients says: 'From the lawless comes forth sin.' But my hand shall not be upon you.
And now whom do you pursue, king of Israel? Or after whom do you come out? After a dead dog and a flea.
May the Lord be arbiter and judge between you and me; may the Lord see and judge my cause, and deliver justice to me out of your hands."
And when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said: "Is this your voice, my son David?"
And David said: "I am your servant, my lord the king." And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
And he said to David: "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good, and I have repaid you with evil.
And you yourself have told me today the good you have done me, how the Lord delivered me into your hands,
And you did not kill me. For who, finding his enemy in distress, would let him go safely on a good road?
May the Lord also repay you with good, as you have done today. And now, behold, I know that you will reign, and the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.
And now swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my descendants after me, and that you will not blot out my name from my father's house.
And David swore to Saul, and Saul went to his house; and David and his men went up to Messara, the narrow place.
Whoever leads the upright astray into an evil way will himself be given over to corruption;
but the lawless will pass by good things and will not enter into them. A rich man seems wise to himself, but a poor man with understanding will condemn him.
Through the help of the righteous much glory comes about, but in the place of the ungodly men are destroyed.
Whoever hides his lawlessness will not prosper; but whoever tells it and reproves it will be loved.
Blessed is the man who is wary of all things out of the fear of God, but the hard-hearted will fall into evil.
A hungry lion and a thirsty wolf: so is he who, being [?], rules over a poor nation.
A king lacking in revenue is a slanderer of great slander, but those who hate falsehood will live long.
A man on whom lies the guilt of murder, and someone takes it upon himself (as surety), that one will be a fugitive and not secure; he will fall into evil.
Instruct your son, and he will give you rest and will give adornment to your soul, and he will not obey a lawless nation.
Whoever walks in justice will be given help, but whoever walks in crooked ways will be entangled in them.
Whoever works his own land will be filled with bread, but whoever gives himself to idleness will be filled with poverty.
A man worthy of trust will be greatly blessed, but the evildoer will not go unpunished.
Whoever is ashamed to rebuke the face of the false is not good; such a one will hand over a man for a morsel of bread.
An envious man hastens to grow rich and does not know that a merciful man will take hold of it.
Whoever reproves a poor man for his ways will have more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
Whoever sells off his father or mother and thinks that he does not sin is a partner of the ungodly man.
An insatiable man judges rashly; whoever trusts in the hardness of his own heart is foolish, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be under care.
Whoever walks in wisdom will be saved. Whoever gives to the poor will not be in want;
but whoever turns his face away from the poor will be in great destitution.
In the place of the ungodly the poor groan, but at their destruction the righteous will multiply.
A man who reproves is better than a stiff-necked man; when he suddenly flares up, there will be no healing.
And you, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Hear the word from my mouth and tell it to them from me.
When I say to the lawless man, "You shall surely die," and you do not tell him, and do not speak to warn the lawless man to turn away,
so that he may turn from his ways and live, that lawless man shall die in his lawlessness.
And you will save your own soul. And if the righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits sin,
I will set torment before his face and he shall die, for I will remember his righteous deeds, and I will require his blood at your hands.
If you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he listens and does not sin, that righteous man shall surely live.
Lord, hear [?] the prayer: [?] hear.
And the hand of the Lord was upon me:
Now concerning the eating of food offered to idols, I know that there is no idol in the world, and there is no god except the one God.
For even if there are things called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, as there are many gods and many lords,
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we are for him.
And there is one Lord, Jesus Christ, from whom are all things, and we are through him. But not everyone has this knowledge.
Some, with doubt about the idol even until now, eat it as food offered to idols, and their nature, being weak, is defiled.
But our food will not bring us before God. If we do not eat, we lack nothing, and if we eat, nothing is added to us.
But take care that this freedom of yours does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
If someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not the mind of the one who is weak be corrupted into eating food offered to idols?
And that weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
When you sin against the brothers in this way and wound their weak mind, you sin against Christ.
Therefore, if food makes my brother stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I do not make my brother stumble.
Keep and hear all the words that I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your sons forever.
And if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God, and if the Lord your God destroys those nations
before your face, whose land you are entering to possess, and you possess it and settle in their land,
take care for yourself, lest you follow in their track after they have been destroyed before your face. Do not seek after their idols and say:
"As these Gentiles do toward their idols, so I will do as well."
You shall not do so to the Lord your God, for they do for their idols the abomination that the Lord your God hated: they burned their sons and their daughters with fire for their idols.
Every word that I command you today, keep it and do it. Do not add to them and do not take away from them.
If a prophet or a seer of visions rises up among you and gives you a sign or a wonder, and says to you:
"Let us go and serve other gods, whom you have not known," do not listen to that prophet or that seer of visions.
For the Lord your God is testing you, so that you may know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart.
Walk after the Lord your God and fear him. Keep his commandments, listen to his voice, and hold fast to him.
And that prophet and seer of visions shall die, because he spoke to you to lead you astray, so that you would not follow the Lord your God,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt and who redeemed you from slavery. He spoke to turn you aside from the way in which the Lord your God commanded you to walk.
So you shall remove the evil from among you. If your brother, the son of your father or the son of your mother, or your son, or your daughter entreats you,
or your wife who is in your bosom, or your friend who is as your own self, and says to you secretly:
"Let us go and serve other gods," whom neither you nor your fathers have known, from among the gods of the nations
who are around you, whether near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth,
do not consent to him and do not listen to him. Your eye shall not spare him, and you shall not shelter him from it.
Instead, you shall surely report him, and your hand shall be the first against him to kill him, and afterward the hands of all the people.
And stone him with stones, and he shall die, because he sought to make you fall away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear and be afraid, and no one shall ever again do such an evil thing among you.
If you hear about one of the cities that the Lord your God has given you to dwell in
that lawless men from among us have gone out and led astray all the inhabitants of their city, saying:
"Let us go and serve other gods, whom you have not known,"
then you shall inquire and search the matter out thoroughly. And if it is truly and clearly so that this abomination has been done among you,
you shall utterly destroy all the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword. You shall devote it to destruction as accursed, together with everything that is in it.
And you shall gather all its plunder on the road with the [?], and all the people shall burn the city and all its plunder with fire before the Lord your God.
And that city shall be a desolation forever and shall never be built again. You shall take nothing for yourself with your hands from what has been devoted to destruction,
so that the Lord may turn from the wrath of his anger, show you mercy, have compassion on you and multiply you, just as he swore to your fathers.
If you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and doing everything that I command you today,
then you will do what is pleasing and good before the Lord your God.
Be children of the Lord God. Do not cut yourselves for the dead, and do not make a mark of baldness on your face.
For you are a holy people of the Lord your God, and the Lord God has chosen you out of all the nations to be his own people, a people acquired for himself,
out of the nations that are on the face of all the earth. And you shall not eat anything abominable.
Listen, listen to my words, so that this may not be the comfort I get from you.
Let me be, so that I may speak, if you will not laugh at me. Now, is this reproof of mine a man's? Or why should I be angry?
Look at me and be amazed, and lay your hand on your mouth. If I call it to mind, I hurry in this way, for pains have taken hold of my flesh.
Why do the ungodly live and grow old in their wealth? Their offspring are as they wish, and their children are before their eyes.
Their houses are full. There is no fear anywhere, and no punishment from the Lord is upon them.
Their cow conceived and did not miscarry. Their pregnant cow gave birth safely and did not fail.
And they remain like everlasting sheep. Their children sing. They have taken up the harp and the lute, and they rejoice at the sound of joy.
For they have spent their life in good things, and they have fallen asleep in the rest of hell. They said to the Lord: "Depart from me!
I do not wish to know your ways." For good was in their hands, but he does not look upon the deeds of the ungodly.
Not only that, but the lamp of the ungodly too will be put out, and destruction will come upon them, and pain will seize them because of wrath.
And they will be like chaff before the wind, or like dust that the breeze carries away.
May their sons lack fruit. May he repay them, and he will know it. May his eyes see his own slaughter, and may he not get away from the Lord.
Now is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? And does he himself judge the wise?
Their insides are full of fat, and their marrow is spread out. But the other man dies in bitterness of soul, and they eat nothing good.
Together they sleep on the ground, and rot has covered them. Since I know you, you set upon me boldly.
How do you comfort me in vain? But you will not silence me.
The righteous man knows the cause of the poor.
But the ungodly man does not understand knowledge, and the poor man has no mind for knowledge.
Lawless men set a city on fire, but the wise turn away wrath.
A wise man judges the nations, but a foolish man is rebuked in [?], and he is not ashamed.
Bloodthirsty men hate a holy man, but the upright seek his soul.
The fool shows all his anger, but the wise man stores it up from time to time.
When a king listens to lying words, all who serve him are lawless.
The lender and the borrower meet each other, and the Lord watches over them both.
When a king judges the poor with truth, his throne will be set up as a testimony.
Blows and rebukes give wisdom, but a foolish son brings shame on his father and mother.
Though the ungodly are many, they commit many sins, but the righteous become fearful at their fall.
A stubborn servant cannot be taught by words, and even if he understands, he will not obey.
If you see a man who is hasty in his words, know that a fool has more hope than he does.
Whoever lives in luxury from his youth will become a servant, and in the end he will grieve over himself.
An angry-hearted man digs up victory [?], but a wrathful man digs up sin.
Insolence brings a man low, but the Lord upholds the humble with glory.
Whoever shares with a thief hates his own soul. If an oath is put before them and they say nothing, they are afraid because of men.
Such a one has stumbled by God's doing [?], but whoever trusts in the Lord will rejoice forever.
Ungodliness brings a man to stumbling, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be saved.
Many seek the favor of rulers, but a man's justice comes from the Lord.
A righteous man is detestable to a sinful man, and whoever has walked straight in the good way is detestable among the lawless.
Who can find a valiant woman? She is worth more than very precious carbuncles.
Her husband's heart trusts in such a woman. Such a man will not lack spoil, for she helps her husband in all good things throughout this life.
She got wool and flax and made useful things with her own hands. She became like a ship coming from far away; she gathers all the means of living.
She gets up at night and gives food to her household, to the workers and to the maidservants.
She saw a useful field and bought it, and with the fruit of her hands she planted a [?] (literally 'root' or 'foundation').
She girded her hands firmly and set her arms to work. She tasted that work is good.
Her lamp did not go out all night. She put her hands to the spindle and stretched out her arms to what is profitable.
She opened her hands to the poor and held out her arms to the sick.
Her husband has no worries about his house when he stays somewhere [?], for all her household are clothed.
She made double cloaks for her husband, of purple and fine linen, and clothing for herself.
Her husband is renowned in the gates when he sits in the council with the elders who dwell in the land.
She made [?] and sold them, and girdles to the Canaanites. She opened her mouth with wisdom and set order upon her tongue.
She clothed herself in strength and beauty, and she rejoiced in the last days.
The places of her house are dry; she did not eat the bread of the idle [?]. She opened her mouth wisely and lawfully.
Her children rose up and praised her, and her husband praised her.

Rejoice, you hymns: The righteous, like a palm tree: It is good to give thanks:

For to each and every man: Rejoice, you righteous, in the Lord:
I am the good shepherd:
The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. But the hired hand, who is not the shepherd,
and to whom the sheep do not belong, when he sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf scatters them.
For he is a hired hand and does not care for the sheep. I am the good shepherd; I know my own, and my own know me,
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for my sheep.
And I have other sheep that are not of this fold; I must bring them too,
and they will listen to my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.

Glory, glory to you.
Glory to the coming: Blessed are you, O Lord, who have come: O Lord, you brought up: I will exalt you, O Lord, for you:
The fear of the Lord adds to one's days, but the years of the ungodly will be shortened.
Joy abides with the righteous, but the hope of the ungodly will perish. The fear of the Lord is a stronghold for the holy, but ruin for those who do evil.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the ungodly will inherit the land.
From the mouth of the righteous comes forth wisdom, but the lawless tongue will be destroyed. The lips of the righteous drop grace, and the mouths of the ungodly will be overturned.
False scales are an abomination before the Lord, but a just scale is pleasing before him.
Where there is insolence, there is also disgrace; the mouths of the righteous meditate wisdom. Integrity guides the righteous, but stumbling destroys those who are [?] (self-willed?).
Wealth will be of no use on the day of wrath, but righteousness will deliver from death.
But everything that is exposed by the light becomes visible, for everything that is made visible is light. Therefore it says:
"Wake up, you who are sleeping, rise from the dead, and Christ will give you light."
Be very careful how you walk: not as fools, but as wise people. Make the most of the time, because the days are evil.
So do not be foolish, but understand what the will of God is.
Turn my soul [?]; I shall be afraid:
The Jewish feast of Passover was near,
and many went up to Jerusalem from the countryside before the Passover, which is called the Passion, to purify themselves.
The Jews were looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple they said to one another, "What do you think? Will he not come to the feast?"
For the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, he should tell them, so that they could arrest him.
Six days before the Passion, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, who had died and whom he had raised from the dead.
They prepared a supper for him there. Martha served him, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him.
Then Mary took a pound of ointment of pure, very costly nard, anointed Jesus' feet, and wiped his feet with her hair,
and the whole house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
One of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, who was going to betray him, said,
"Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?"
He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief; he kept the money bag and carried what was put into it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial. For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me."
The whole crowd of the Jews learned that Jesus was there, and they came not only because of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
The chief priests plotted to kill Lazarus as well, because many of the Jews were coming and believing in Jesus.
Mary and Martha to the Saviour.
The mountains will rejoice. Sing to the Lord with a song:
The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast,
hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took palm branches and went out to meet him, crying out and saying, "Hosanna!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!" They brought him a donkey and he sat on it, as it is written:
Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion! Behold, your king is coming to you, and he is sitting on a donkey's colt.
His disciples did not understand this at first, but when Jesus was glorified, they remembered that this had been written about him, and that they had done this to him.
And the crowd that was with him bore witness to him, that he had called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead.
This is why the crowd went out to meet him: they had heard that he had performed this sign.
But the Pharisees said to one another: "Do you see that you are getting nowhere at all? Look, the whole world has gone after him."
Among those who had come up to worship at the feast there were also some Gentiles.
These came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him, saying: "Sir, we wish to see Jesus."
Philip came and told Andrew; then Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.
And Jesus answered and said to them, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
He who sits at the right hand of the Father: today it has been fulfilled:

and said to them: "Go into the village ahead of you. When you enter it you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat.

say this: 'The Lord needs it.'" And those who had been sent went and found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: "Why are you untying that colt?" And they said: "The Lord needs it."
And they brought the colt to Jesus, threw their garments on the colt, and set Jesus on it.
And as he went along, they spread their garments on the road.
And as he came near the approach to the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to praise him joyfully with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,
and they said: "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
And some of the Pharisees in the crowd spoke to him and said: "Teacher, rebuke your disciples!"
But Jesus answered and said to them, "I tell you, if these were silent, the stones would cry out."
Seated at the right hand of the Father: today the Savior has entered:

And when they drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples,
and said to them: "Go into the village that is ahead of you, and as you enter it you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat.
Untie it and bring it to [?] (the text reads "son"; probably an error for "me"). And if anyone says anything to you, tell him: 'Its Lord needs it,' and he will send it here at once."
And they went and found the colt tied at the door, outside at the entrance, and they untied it.
And some of those standing there said to them, "What are you doing? Why are you untying that colt?" And they spoke to them as Jesus had commanded them, and they let them go.
And they brought the colt to Jesus and threw their garments on it, and he sat on it. And many spread their garments on the road.
And those who went ahead and those who followed behind cried out and said, "Hosanna in the highest!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the king, the son of David! Peace in the heavens and glory in the highest!"
And Jesus entered Jerusalem, into the temple, and looked around at everything, for the hour was already evening.
And he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
Blessed is he who comes:
Blessed is the King of glory. On a colt, with branches: Hosanna to the Son of David:
The resurrection of all before the Passion: The mountains rejoice: Let us sing to the Lord with song:
I grew tall like a cedar in Lebanon, and like a cypress on the mountains of Hermon.
I grew tall like a palm tree in En-gedi, and like a rose plant in Jericho. Like a beautiful olive tree in the plain, I grew tall like a plane tree.
And like cinnamon, like aspalathus among spices, and like choice myrrh, I spread forth fragrance;
like galbanum and onycha and frankincense, the incense in the tabernacle. Like a terebinth I spread out my branches, and my branches, branches of glory and of grace.
Like a vine I put forth grace, and my blossom is the fruit of glory and riches.
Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits.
For the memory of me is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance sweeter than the honeycomb.
Those who eat me will hunger for more, and those who drink me will thirst for more. Whoever obeys me will not be put to shame, and those who boast in me will not sin.
Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion!
Proclaim it, Jerusalem! Rejoice and be glad with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
For the Lord has taken away your falsehoods; he has rescued you from the hands of your enemies.
The King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst, and from now on you will see evil no more.
At that time the Lord of Israel said: Do not be afraid, Zion; do not let your hands grow weak!
The Lord your God is in your midst; the Mighty One will save you and bring gladness upon you;
he will renew you in his love and rejoice over you with gladness, as on a feast day.
And they gathered the crushed. Woe to whoever brings reproach upon her.
Behold, I will act for your sake at that time. I will save the crushed one and take back the one who was driven out.
And I will make them a source of pride and renown before all the peoples of the earth on the day when I bring back your captives before you, says the Lord.
Awake, awake, O Zion!
Awake, O Zion, and rouse your strength. And you too, Jerusalem, holy city, put on your glory!
From now on, the uncircumcised and the unclean shall no longer pass through you. Shake off your dust, Jerusalem; arise and sit down!
Loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion!
For thus says the Lord: You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed here without silver.
Thus says the Lord: At first my people went down into the land of Egypt to live there as sojourners, and they were carried off to Assyria by force.
And now, what are you seeking here? says the Lord. For my people were carried off for nothing; so they wailed.
Thus says the Lord: Because of you my name is continually blasphemed among the gentiles.
Therefore my people shall know that I myself am the one who was speaking, and now I have come and I stand among you.
Look toward the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy coming to you from those who are on their way to you.
Behold, those who were sent away from you are coming to you. They will come, gathered from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Look toward the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy from God that has come to you. Behold, your sons who were sent away are coming to you.
They are coming, gathered from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Take off, Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and your affliction, and put on forever the beauty of the glory that comes from God.
Put on the robe of the righteousness that comes from God, and set the crown of eternal glory on your head.
For God has shown your splendor to everything under all the heavens.
For God will call your name forever: "Peace of Righteousness and Peace of Godliness."

Arise, Jerusalem, stand upon the heights and look toward the east, where the sun rises. See your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.
For they went out [?], led away by their enemies, but God has brought them back to you, coming in glory as on a royal throne.

For God has commanded that every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low, and that the valleys be filled up and the ground made level, so that Jerusalem may walk safely in the glory of God.
The forest and every fragrant tree will give shade to Jerusalem at God's command.
For God will lead Jerusalem with joy in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.
[?], go on, walk about, come in through my gates;
clear the ways, make ready the places for my people, and throw the stones out of the road; raise up a sign among the nations.
For the Lord has made it heard from end to end of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion:
Behold, your Saviour comes and draws near, and his reward is with him and his works are before him.
And he will call them a holy people, redeemed by the Lord; and you shall be called a city sought out and not forsaken.
Behold, like a cypress of Lebanon with fine shoots, I rose high in greatness, and its top was among the clouds.
The water made it grow, and the deep raised it high.
It made its rivers flow around its plantings, and sent out the thickness of its branches to all the trees of the field.
Therefore its greatness was exalted above all the trees, and its branches spread out from many waters.
All the birds of the sky nested in its shoots, and under its branches all the wild beasts of the field gave birth; in its shade all the families of the tribes dwelt.
And it was fair in its uprightness and in the multitude of its branches, for its roots were established upon many waters. The firs that are in the garden of God were not like it;
and the pines did not equal all its shoots, and the tree that is in the garden of God does not resemble it.
Because of the multitude of its branches the trees of delight of the garden of God envied it.
Therefore the Lord says this: Behold, I made you glorious in your greatness, and [?] your tops among the clouds, and I saw it in its exaltation,
and I gave it into the hands of the rulers of the nations, and they will cut off its branches from among the trees.
And they will take them up with their hands, and in the cutting off of the branches of the trees all the peoples of the earth will find rest.
For under that tree were all the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, and they rejoiced in it on that day.
Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavens through Christ.
Even as he chose us in him before the creation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love.
He predestined us beforehand for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, according to his good pleasure, which he graciously bestowed on us through the Beloved,
in whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our sins, according to the riches of his glory, which he lavished upon us in all wisdom and understanding;
he made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure, which he prepared beforehand in him,
for a plan according to the fullness of the times, to bring all things under one head, in the heavens and on the earth;
in him in whom we also have received an inheritance and were predestined by his will, he who made all things according to the counsel of his will,
so that we, who first hoped in Christ, should be to the praise of his glory;
In whom you also heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, in which you believed and were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the promise,
who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the redemption of our help [?], to the praise of his glory.
O Lord our God, how wonderful [...]. Praise.
And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two of his disciples and said to them:
Go into that village which is before you, and at once you will find a donkey tied up and a colt with it;
untie them and bring them to me. And if anyone says anything to you, you shall say to him: 'The Lord needs them,' and at once he will send them.
All this took place so that the word of the prophet might be fulfilled, which said:
Tell the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, meek, and seated upon a donkey and a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.
And the disciples went and did just as Jesus had commanded them.
And they brought the donkey and the colt with it, and put garments on them, and he sat upon them.
And the greater part of the crowd spread their garments on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
And the crowd that went before him and that followed behind cried out and said: Hosanna to the Son of David!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest! And Jesus entered Jerusalem, and the whole city was stirred, and they said: Who is this?
And the crowd said: This is the prophet Jesus from Nazareth of Galilee.
And Jesus entered the temple and drove out from there all who sold and all who bought in the temple,
and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and threw down the seats of those who sold doves.
And he said to them: It is written: My Father's house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers.
And the blind and the lame came to him, and he healed them.
And when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonder that had been done, and the children who were crying out in the temple and saying:
Hosanna to the Son of David, they became angry and said to him: Do you hear what these are saying?
And Jesus said to them: Yes; have you never read: Out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you have established praise?
And he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there.
Wondrous and glorious is what he saw: he who sits upon the thrones of the cherubim:
Today he enters in humility:
Again, the grace of the Savior:
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel. So be it. O God, give your judgment to the king:
Delight your heart in the Lord; make it known before the Lord:
And on the next day he was coming into the city, and he was hungry.
And he saw a fig tree by the road and came to it, and found no fruit on it, but only leaves.
And he said to it: "Let there be no more fruit from you forever!" And immediately that fig tree withered.
When the disciples saw it, they marvelled and said: "How immediately this fig tree has withered!"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Amen, I say to you: if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to this fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain,
'Be uprooted from here and fall into the sea,' it will be so. And whatever you ask in prayer with faith will be done for you."
And when he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to him as he was teaching the people, and said to him:
"By what authority do you do this, and who gave you this authority?"
In the beginning God made: And Jacob called his sons and said to them:
"Gather to me, and I will tell you" — and Jacob called his sons and said: "Gather to me, and I will tell you what will befall you in the last days."
The sons of Jacob came and listened. And he said: "Listen to Israel, your father.
Reuben, my strength and my firstborn, the beginning of my children, you went rashly, rashly and insolently. You boiled over like water.
Do not boil over [?], for you went up onto your father's bed. Then you defiled the bed onto which you went up.
Simeon and Levi, for they carried out wrongdoing by their rising [?]; may my soul not enter into their counsel,
for in their anger men were slain, and in their desire they hamstrung bulls.
Cursed be their desire, for their cunning was in insolence; for I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
1 Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hands will be upon the gates [? backs] of your enemies. The sons of your father will bow down to you.
Judah is a lion's whelp; from a shoot, my son, you have come up. Lying down he will sleep like a lion and like a lion's whelp. Who will rouse him?
A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until he comes for whom it has been prepared, and he is the expectation of the nations.
He will tie his mount to the vine, and the colt of his donkey to the branch of the vine.
He will wash his finery in wine and his garment in the blood of grapes. His eyes are merry with wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
Zebulun will dwell by the seashore, and he will send out ships and reach as far as Sidon.
Issachar's heart desired what is good, resting among his portion. And he will see his resting place, that it is good, and the land rich.
He gave his shoulders to labour and became a man who tills the land. Dan will judge his people as one tribe in Israel.
And let Dan be a serpent on the road, sitting in ambush, and let him bite the horse's heel, and the rider shall fall backward.
And he waited for the salvation of the Lord. Gad: a raiding band shall raid him, and he shall raid them, following at their heels.
Asher: his bread is rich, and he shall give food to rulers. Naphtali, a tree, a plant [?], shall yield fruits of goodness.
A son grown great, Joseph, my youngest son, return to me. They plotted against him; they reviled him, and the masters of the bows were hostile to him.
And their bows were shattered by might, and the sinews of their arms were loosed by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob, by him who made you strong, Israel, through the God of your father.
[…] of the Hittites. 1. And Jacob finished giving commands to his sons, and he drew his feet up onto the bed, and he died and was gathered to his people.
And Joseph fell upon his father's face, weeping, and kissed him.
And Joseph commanded his servants, those who prepare the dead for burial, to embalm his father. And those who prepare the dead embalmed Israel.
And they completed forty days, for so are the days of burial reckoned. And all Egypt mourned for him seventy days.
And when the days of his mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's officials and said to them, "If I have found favor in your sight,
speak in Pharaoh's ears and say to him: 'My father made me swear an oath and said to me, "In the tomb that I made for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me."'
Now therefore let me go up and bury my father, and I will come back here again."
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear." And Joseph went up to bury his father.
And with him went up all Pharaoh's servants, and the elders of his household, and the elders of all the land of Egypt,
and the whole household of Joseph, and all his brothers, and all his father's household, and all his kin.
But the sheep and the cattle they left in the land of Egypt. And chariots and horsemen went up with him, and the company was very great.
And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they lamented for him with a great and very loud lamentation.
And Joseph mourned for his father seven days. And the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad.
Therefore that place was called "The Mourning of Egypt." And the sons of Israel did for him just as he had commanded them.
And his sons carried him up to the land of Canaan, and they buried him in the double cave,
which Abraham had bought as a burial place from the sons of Ephron the Hittite, facing Mamre.
And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.
And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.
The Proverbs of Solomon:
Comfort, comfort:
Who will give me a small lodging in the wilderness, so that I may leave this people of mine and go away from them?
For they all commit adultery, an assembly of lawless men. For they have bent their tongues like bows, and they would not obey the words of my mouth;
instead, falsehood and faithlessness have grown strong among them. For they have gone out from evil to evil, and they have not known me, says the Lord.
Let each one beware of his neighbour, and do not trust your brothers, for every brother deals in lies and every friend walks in deceit.
And each one mocks his neighbour because of this, for they have abandoned the truth.
Their tongue has learned to speak falsehood. They have plundered, and they have not stopped adding falsehood to their tongue,
increase upon increase [?] and deceit upon deceit. And they would not know me, said the Lord.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will refine it and I will test them. For what shall I do because of the wickedness of the daughter of my people?
For their tongue is a wounding arrow, and the words of their mouth are deceitful. They speak peace to their neighbour, but in their hearts they have laid up enmity.
Shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord? Or shall my soul not take vengeance on such a people as this?
On the mountains they raised a voice of weeping, and on the paths of the wilderness a lament, for they have become desolate because no one passes through.
No sound of cattle was heard there; from the birds of the sky to the livestock, [all have gone], says the Lord of hosts.
Come, O faithful:
Tone: "Of the Passion": Hear us, O God our Saviour. Deliver us from fear of the enemy.
And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples with him, and on the way he said to them:
"Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners, and they will condemn him to death."
and they will hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and tortured and crucified, and on the third day he will rise.
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, bowing down before him and asking something of him. And he said to her, "What do you want?"
And she said to him, "Say, Lord, that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom."
Jesus answered and said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
They said to him, "We are able." Jesus said to them, "You will indeed drink my cup, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized,
but to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give; rather, it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
When the ten heard this, they became angry with the two brothers.
And Jesus answered and said to them, "Do you know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great ones exercise authority over them?
But it shall not be so among you. Rather, whoever wishes to be great among you, let him be your servant.
Just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many."
Before the Passion, [?]:
In the same tone: You give light marvelously. The earth was afraid, and [?]
Now my soul has been shaken, as though it were about to die.
If that servant says in his heart, 'My master is delaying his coming,' and begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and put his portion with the faithless.
And that servant who knows the will of his master and does not get ready according to his will shall be punished severely.

But the one who does not know, and does something deserving punishment, shall be beaten lightly. For of everyone to whom much was given, much will also be required, and from the one to whom much was entrusted, even more will be demanded.
I came to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I wish, but that it were already kindled!
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you think, then, that I came to bring peace upon the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
For from now on there will be five in one house divided: three against two and two against three.
Father will be divided against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.
Jesus also said to the people: When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, 'It is bringing rain,' and so it happens.
And when the south wind blows, you say, 'There will be heat,' and so it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to examine the face of the earth and of the sky, but how is it that you do not examine this time? Or why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?
For when you are going with your adversary before the ruler, make an effort on the way to be set free from him,
lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will not come out from there until you have paid even the last mite.
These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man and perfect in his generation; and Noah was pleasing to God.
And he fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with their iniquities.
And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
And the Lord God said to Noah: The time of every man has come before me, for the earth has been filled with their iniquities.
And behold, I will destroy them and the earth. Make yourself an ark of wood that does not rot; make it with compartment upon compartment, and coat it with pitch inside and outside with naphtha.
And this is how you shall make the ark: make the length of the ark three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
Make the ark narrowing toward the top, and finish it off at one cubit above; and put the door of the ark in its side; build it with lower and upper rooms, partition by partition.
And I, behold, will bring a flood of water upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which there is the breath of life under heaven, and whatever there is under heaven shall perish.
And I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall go into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you, into the ark.
And of all the cattle and of all flesh, two of every kind, male and female, of all the animals you shall bring into the ark, so that you may keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.
Of the creeping things according to their kinds, two of every kind shall go in with you, male and female, to be kept alive.
Take with you some of every kind of food for you to eat, and gather it to yourself, so that it may be food for you and for them.
And Noah did as the Lord God commanded him. And the Lord God said to Noah:
"Go into the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen that you alone are righteous before me in this generation.
And of the clean cattle you shall bring in with you seven, male and female, and of the unclean animals two, male and female,
to keep seed alive upon the earth. For in seven more days I will bring the flood upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out from the earth every living thing that exists."
And Noah did so, as the Lord God commanded him. Now Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came upon the earth.
And Noah went into the ark, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him, because of the flood.
And of the birds and of the unclean cattle and of all the creeping things of the earth, two by two they went into the ark, male and female, as the Lord God had commanded Noah.
And after seven days the flood came upon the earth. In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the thirtieth day of the month,
on that day the fountains of the deep burst forth and the floodgates of heaven were opened, and the rain fell for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah went into the ark, with Shem, Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife and his sons' wives with him.
And every wild beast according to its kind and all the cattle according to their kinds went in with Noah, and every creature that moves on the earth and every bird according to its kind.
They went into the ark, two of all flesh in which there was the breath of life.
And they all went in. Male and female of all flesh went in, as the Lord had commanded Noah. And the Lord God shut the ark from outside.
And the flood was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and the waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth.
And the water prevailed over everything and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark was carried about on the waters.
And the waters prevailed greatly over the earth and covered the high mountains that were under heaven. The water rose fifteen cubits above them and covered the mountains.
And all flesh that moved upon the earth perished: birds, cattle, wild beasts, and all the creatures that move upon the earth, and every human being,
and everything that had the breath of life, and everything that was on dry land, perished.
And every living thing that was on the face of the earth was wiped out, from humans to animals, and the creeping things and the birds of heaven were wiped out from the earth.
And only Noah remained, with those who were with him in the ark. And the water rose upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah and all the beasts and all the birds that were in the ark;
and God sent a wind over the earth, and the water abated.
And the springs of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the water kept decreasing.
As it flowed off the earth, the water grew less and kept decreasing.
And after the one hundred and fifty days the ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on the mountain of Ararat.
And the water went on decreasing until the tenth month; and in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
And after the fortieth day Noah opened the door of the ark that he had made.
And he sent out a raven to see whether the water had abated. And it went out and did not return until the water had dried up.
And after it he sent out a dove to see whether the water had abated from the face of the earth.
And the dove found no place for its wings to rest, and it came back to Noah in the ark, because the water was over the face of the whole earth.
And Noah put out his hand and brought it back into the ark. And he waited another seven days and sent it out of the ark again.
And the dove came back to him in the evening, and it had an olive leaf with its twig in its mouth.
Then Noah understood that the water had abated from the earth. And he waited yet another seven days and sent out the dove again, and it did not return to him any more.
And in the six hundred and first year of Noah's life, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the water was gone from the earth.
And the Lord God spoke to Noah and said to him: Come out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives.
And all flesh that is with you, every beast, from the birds to the cattle, and every creeping thing that moves on the earth, bring out with you; and increase and multiply on the earth.
And Noah went out, with his wife and his sons and his sons' wives.
And all the beasts and all the creeping things and all the birds that move on the earth went out of the ark, each according to its kind.
And Noah built an altar to the Lord God, and took from all the cattle, from every kind, and from all the clean birds. And Noah did so, and Noah offered a sacrifice to God on the altar.
And the Lord smelled the sweet fragrance. And the Lord God said: I have repented; I will not again curse the earth because of the deeds of human beings,
for the inclination of the human heart is bent toward evil from youth. I will not again come upon all flesh as I have done now.
As long as the earth lasts, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will not cease.
And the Lord God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them: Increase and multiply, fill the earth and rule over it;
and let the fear of you be upon all the birds of the sky, all the creeping things of the earth and the fish of the sea; I have put them under your hand and given them to you;
Every creeping thing that is alive shall be food for you; as with the green plants of the field, I give it all to you for food.
But you shall not eat flesh with its blood. For I will also require your blood, the blood of your souls, from every hand of yours,
and from the hand of a man's brother I will require the living soul of the son of man, from whoever sheds this blood of man;
in return for his blood, his own blood shall be shed, for I made man in the image of the Godhead.
As for you, increase and multiply and fill the earth, and have dominion over it.
And the Lord God spoke to Noah and to his sons and said to them: Behold, I am establishing my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
and with every living soul that is with you, the birds and the cattle and every wild beast of the earth, as many as are with you, all that came out of the ark with you.
And I will confirm my covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by a flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy all the earth.
The Lord God said to Noah: This is the sign of my covenant, which I have set between me and you and every living soul, for all generations forever.
I set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of my covenant between me and you.
And it shall be, when I send a cloud over the earth and my bow appears in the clouds,
that I will remember my covenant which is between me and you and every living creature of flesh, and there shall no longer be the water of a flood to destroy all flesh.
And my bow shall be in the clouds; I will see it and remember my everlasting covenant between me and every living soul and all flesh that is on the earth.
The Lord God said to Noah: This is the sign of my covenant, which I have set between me and all flesh that is on the earth.
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three are the sons of Noah; from them people spread out over the whole earth.
Go up onto a high mountain:
Fearsome is the Lord [?]:
To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul. Let them not laugh at me. Teach me:
Jesus came out of the temple and was going away. And his disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
But Jesus answered and said to them: Do you see all these things? Amen, I say to you, not one stone will be left here on another; all of it will be thrown down.
And as Jesus sat on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him privately and said to him: Tell us, when will this happen, and what is the sign of your coming?
Jesus answered and said to them: Take care that no one leads you astray. For many will come in my name and say, 'I am the Christ,' and they will lead many astray.
And you will hear of wars and rumours of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for this must happen, but it is not yet the end.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines, plagues and earthquakes in various places. All this is the beginning of the birth pains.
And then they will hand you over to affliction and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations for my name's sake.
And then many will stumble, and they will betray one another and hate one another.
And many false prophets will arise and will lead many astray.
And because lawlessness will multiply, the love of many will grow cold. But whoever endures it to the end will be saved.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place (let whoever reads understand),
then let whoever is in Judea flee to the mountains. And let whoever is on the roof not come down to take any goods out of his house.
And let whoever is out in the field not turn back to take his clothes. But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
But pray that your flight may not be in winter or on the Sabbath day.
For there will be great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning until now, and never will be.
And if those days were not shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Here is the Christ,' or 'He is there,' do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform very great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if it were possible, even the elect.
Behold, I have told you beforehand. If they say to you, 'He is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Behold, he is in the inner rooms,' do not believe it.
For as the lightning flashes from the east and is seen as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For wherever the carcass is, there the vultures will gather. And immediately after the affliction of those days the sun will be darkened,
and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the heavens, and then all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts in mourning, and they will see the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
And he will send out his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the earth to the other.
Now learn this parable from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and it puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the very doors.

If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
These things I have spoken to you, so that my love may be with you, and that your love may be complete.

Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. Pilate said to the Jews: "Here is the man!"
When the chief priests saw him, they cried out and said: "Crucify him! Crucify him!"
Pilate said to them: "Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no fault in him."
The Jews answered and said: "We have a law, and according to our law he must die, because he made himself the Son of God." When Pilate heard this, he was afraid.
And he went back into the praetorium and said to Jesus: "Where are you from?" But Jesus gave him no answer. Pilate said to him: "Will you not speak to me?
Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you, and I have authority to release you?"
Jesus said to him: "You would have no authority over me at all, if it had not been given to you from above.
Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin." Because of this Pilate wanted to release him, but the Jews cried out and said:
"If you release this man, you are not a friend of Caesar, for everyone who calls himself a king rises up in opposition to Caesar."
When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat, at the place called the Pavement, and in Hebrew Gabbatha.
It was the Friday of the Passover, and it was the sixth hour. Pilate said to the Jews: "Here is your king!"
But they cried out and said: "Take him away, take him away, and crucify him!" Pilate said to them: "Shall I crucify your king?"
The chief priests answered and said to him: "We have no king but Caesar."
Then he handed him over to them to be crucified.
They cried out for the crucifixion. O God, my God, look upon me.
You stood before the ruler like an innocent lamb.
Then Judas took a band of men, and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and they came there with torches and lamps and weapons.
But Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them: "Whom are you looking for?"
They answered and said to him: "Jesus of Nazareth." Jesus said to them: "I am he." Judas, who betrayed him, was also standing with them.
And when he said to them, "I am he," they drew back and fell to the ground. Then he asked them again: "Whom are you looking for?"
And they said: "Jesus of Nazareth." Jesus said to them: "I told you that I am he. If you are looking for me, let these men go."
This was so that the word Jesus had spoken to them might be fulfilled: "Of those whom you gave me, I have not lost a single one."
Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear.
The servant's name was Malchus. Jesus said to Peter: "Put your sword into its sheath! The cup that the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?"
Then the band and the commander and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him.
And they led him first to Annas, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
This was the Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people. Simon Peter and the other disciple followed Jesus.
That one disciple was known to the high priest, and he went in with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest. But Peter stood outside at the door.
So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.
The servant girl who kept the door said to Peter, "Surely you are not also one of this man's disciples?" But Peter said, "I am not."
The servants and the attendants were standing there. They had lit a fire because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter was with them, standing and warming himself.
Then the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching. Jesus answered him and said:
"I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I said nothing in secret.
Why do you question me? Ask those who heard me what I taught them. Look, these people know what I said to them."
When he had said this, one of the attendants standing by struck Jesus on the cheek and said, "Is that how you answer the high priest?"
Jesus said to him, "If I have spoken wrongly, testify about the wrong. But if I have spoken rightly, why do you strike me?"
Then Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest. And Simon Peter was standing and warming himself.
Those standing there said to him, "Surely you are not also one of his disciples?" He denied it and said, "I am not."
One of the high priest's servants, a relative of the man whose ear he had cut off, said to him, "Did I not see you in the garden with him?"
Then Peter denied it again, and at once a cock crowed.
They seized the Lord among the disciples:
You who for envy [?]. Thus says the Lord:
I will sing to my beloved vineyard a song of love. The beloved had a vineyard on fertile ground, on a choice site.
I put a fence around it and walled it in strongly. I planted a vine of Sorek, pruned it, and [?] strengthened it. I raised a tower in its midst and a winepress
I prepared [?], and I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns and thistles [?].
Now, you men of Judah who live in Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard. What more should I have done for my vineyard?
And now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will tear down its strong wall, and it will be trampled. I will abandon the vineyard and not prune it;
it will not be hoed, and thorns will spring up as on wasteland. And I will command the clouds not to rain on it.
For the vineyard of the Lord God is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are his beloved plants, from whom he expected justice.
When they had seized Jesus, they led him away and brought him to the house of the high priest.
Peter followed at a distance. They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down around it, and Peter sat down among them.
A servant girl saw him sitting in the light. She looked at him closely and said, "This man was with him too." But he denied it and said, "Woman, I do not know whom you are looking for."
A little later someone else saw him and said, "You are one of them too." But Peter said, "Man, I am not one of them."
About an hour later another man insisted, saying, "Truly this man was with him too, for he is a Galilean."
But Peter said to him, "Man, I do not know what you are saying." And immediately, while he was still saying this, the cock crowed. And the Lord turned and looked at Peter.
And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, which he had said to him: "Before the cock crows you will deny me three times, saying, 'I do not know him.'"
And he went outside and wept bitterly. And the men who had seized Jesus mocked him and beat him.
And they covered his head, ridiculed him and insulted him, and they kept asking him, saying, "Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?"
And they said many other blasphemous things against him.
And when day dawned, the elders of the people, the chief priests and the scribes gathered together, and they brought him up to their council and said to him:
"If you are the Christ, tell us." Jesus said to them, "If I tell you, you will not believe;
and if I ask you, you will not answer me, nor will you release me. From now on the Son of Man will be seated at the power of God."
And they all said to him, "Are you the Son of God?" Jesus said to them, "You say that I am."
And they said, "What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from his own mouth."
And their whole multitude rose up and brought him to Pilate. And they began to accuse him, saying:
"We found this man perverting our nation, forbidding the paying of tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is the Christ and a king."
And Pilate asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" And he said to him, "You say so."
Then Pilate said to the chief priests and to the people, "I find no guilt in this man."
But they grew all the more insistent and said, "He stirs up the people and teaches throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place."
When Pilate heard "Galilee," he asked them whether this man was from Galilee.
And when he learned that he was from Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, for he too was in Jerusalem at that time, in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had been hearing about him and wished to see some sign done by him.
And he questioned him with many words, but he answered him nothing. The chief priests and the scribes stood by and vehemently accused him.
And Herod with his soldiers treated him with contempt, and they mocked him and clothed him in a splendid robe, and he sent him back to Pilate.
And Pilate and Herod became friends with each other that very day, for before they had been enemies.
Then Pilate called together the chief priests and the people and said to them:
"You brought me this man as one who perverts the people, and behold, I examined him before you and found nothing in this man of which you accuse him.
Neither did Herod, for I sent him to him, and nothing deserving death has been done by him. I will therefore discipline him and release him."
For he was obliged to release one man to them at the feast. The whole multitude of the people cried out, saying:
"Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us," who had been thrown into prison for causing an insurrection in the city and for murder.
Pilate called to them again, because he wanted to release him. But they cried out and said, "Crucify him!"
And he said to them a third time, "What evil has this man done? I have found in him no crime worthy of death. I will chastise him and release him."
But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified. And their voices and those of the chief priests prevailed.

Then Pilate gave judgment according to their demand. He released to them Barabbas, whom they were asking for, who had been thrown into prison for rioting and murder; but Jesus he handed over to their will.
And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the field, and laid the cross on him, and he carried it behind Jesus.
And a great crowd of the people followed him, and of women who beat their breasts and mourned for him.
Jesus turned to them and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
For the days are coming in which you will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nurse.'
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us!' If they do these things to the green tree, what will they do to the dry?"
Today he is hung upon the tree. Blessed is the man who has not walked:
He was led as a sheep to the slaughter. Why have the nations raged:
Thus you spoke, O Lord, to the Jews: Lord, why have they multiplied:
For fear of the Jews; my calling was heard:
And the Canaanites knew the sheep that were kept, for it is the word of the Lord.
And I said to them, "If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; and if not, declare it to me." Wait, and they promised me as my wages those thirty pieces of silver.
And the Lord said to me, "Cast that silver into the furnaces of the smelters and see whether it is pure, just as I was tested for them."
And I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them into the house of the Lord, into the furnaces of the fire.
And I cast away the rod of the second portion, to break the covenant that is between Judah and Israel.
But far be it from me to boast,
except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
From now on neither circumcision is anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
And as for those who walk by this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy upon the Israel of God.
From now on, brothers, let no one cause me trouble, for I bear the sufferings of our Lord Jesus Christ in my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
To the lawless who seized you: Give ear to my words:
Woe to their soul, for they have plotted an evil plot and said: “Let us bind the righteous one, for he is troublesome to us.”
Now therefore they shall eat the fruit of their deeds. Woe to the lawless one, for the evil of their deeds shall befall him.
O my people, your tax-collectors strip you, and those who extort from you rule over you.
O my people, those who call you blessed lead you astray and unsettle the path of your feet.
And now the Lord will rise up for judgment and bring his people to judgment. Why have you burned my vineyard, and why is the plunder of the poor in your houses?
Why do you wrong my people and put the face of the poor to shame? Thus says the Lord of hosts.
Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus,
who, being in the form of God, counted it [?] robbery for himself to be equal with God,
but humbled himself, and took the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men, and was found in form as a man.
He humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name which is above every name,
that at the name of Jesus Christ every knee should bow, of things in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue should confess Jesus Christ as Lord, to the glory of God the Father. Amen.
His heart gathered to itself: Blessed is he who has understood:
Lawgivers of Israel. O Lord, not in your wrath:
The Lord has given me the tongue of the learned, to know when it is fitting to speak a word.
He appointed me in the morning and gave me also an ear to hear. And the instruction of the Lord opened my ear; and I was not disobedient, nor did I answer back.
I gave my back to the scourges and my cheeks to blows, and I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.
And the Lord was my helper, and therefore I was not put to shame; but I set my face like a firm rock, and I knew that I was not put to shame.
For he who justifies me is near; my [?] against me; and who is my judge? Let him draw near to me.
Behold, the Lord has helped me; and who is he that will do me harm?
For while we were still weak, at the appointed time Christ died for the ungodly.
For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous man; yet for a good man perhaps someone would dare even to die.
But God showed his own love toward us, in that while we were still ungodly, Christ died for us.
How much more, having been justified by his blood, have we been saved through him from wrath.
For if, while we were still enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, how much more, now that we have been reconciled, shall we be saved by his saving power.
And not only this, but we also boast in God, our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received this reconciliation.
For I am ready for scourging. O Lord, not in wrath: Your hand:
Fearful was the sight of the heavens: O Lord my God, in you I trust; save me:
And on that day, says the Lord, the sun shall go down at noon, and darkness shall come upon the earth, and the light shall fail on that day.
And I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation, and I will bind sackcloth on all loins and dust [?] on every head;
and I will make it like mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of anguish.
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send a famine upon the earth: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of God.
And the waters shall be stirred up as far as the sea, and from the north to the east, and they shall run to and fro and seek the word of God, and shall not find it.
For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are being saved it is the power of God.
For it is written: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the understanding I will bring to nothing." Where is the wise man?
Where is the scribe? Or where is the debater of this world? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
For since the world through its own wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe.
For the Jews ask for a sign, and the Gentiles seek wisdom. But we preach Christ crucified:
a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles, but to those same chosen Jews Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God,
for the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
I have become like a man without help: O Lord, God of my salvation:
When the lawless nailed him to the cross. O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful:
Behold, my servant shall understand, and shall be exalted and greatly glorified.
Just as many were astonished at you, so shall your appearance be without glory among men, and your glory among the sons of men.
So shall many nations marvel at him, and kings shall shut their mouths, for those to whom nothing was told about him shall see, and those who have not heard shall understand.
Lord, who [?] has believed your report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
And we announced this before him like a child, and like a root in thirsty ground.
He has no form nor beauty; rather, his appearance was more lacking than that of all men.
He was a man under scourging, and he knows how to endure sufferings, for he did not turn his face away; [?] and he was not esteemed.
He bore our sins and suffered for us, and we reckoned him to be in pains, in wounds and in afflictions.
But he was wounded for our transgressions and was beaten for our sins; the chastisement of our peace was upon him; by his wounds we were healed.
All of us went astray like sheep; each man went astray in his own way.
And the Lord gave him up for our sins; and because of his affliction he does not open his mouth.
Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and as a lamb stands voiceless before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. And who will declare his generation?
For his life is taken away from the earth, and for the transgression of his people he was given over to death.
I will give the wicked in return for his death and the rich in return for his burial.
For he committed no lawlessness, nor was deceit found in his mouth. And the Lord wills cleansing from sins.
If you give [an offering] for sins, your soul will see that offspring, long-lived.
And the Lord wills to take away the pain from his soul, to show him light, to form him with understanding, and to justify the righteous one, the servant
who serves many well, and he himself bore their sins. Therefore he himself will inherit many, and he will divide the spoils of the strong.
For this reason he gave his soul to death and was counted among the lawless; and he blotted out the sins of many and was given over for their transgressions.
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one,
for which reason he was not ashamed to call them brothers, saying: "I will declare your name to my brothers, and in the midst of the congregation I will sing praise to you."
And again he says: "I will put my trust in him." And again: "Here am I and the children whom God has given me."
For he also shared with the children in blood and flesh, and he himself took on the same likeness as theirs, so that through his death he might destroy the one who had the power of death,
that is, the devil, and might set free all those who through fear of death were subject to oppression all their life.
For it was nowhere from the angels that he took his beginning [?], but he took it from the seed of Abraham.
Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every way, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest before God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
