Since he himself suffered and was tested, he is able to help those who are being tested.
Before the Precious Cross. I will confess you, O Lord, with my whole heart:
They divided the garments. O Lord God of salvation.
Then, when Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned, he repented and brought the silver back to the chief priests and the elders and said to them:
"I have sinned, for I have betrayed righteous blood." But they said: "What is that to us? See to it yourself!" And he threw the silver down in the temple, went away and hanged himself.
But the chief priests took the silver and said, "It is not lawful to put this silver into the treasury, for it is the price of blood."
They took counsel and with it bought the potter's field as a burial place for strangers. For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this very day.
Then what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, when he said:
"I took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who was sold, whom they bought from the sons of Israel,
and I gave it for the potter's field, as the Lord commanded me." Now Jesus stood before the governor.
The governor questioned him and said, "Are you the King of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him, "You have said it."
And when he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him, "Do you not hear how many things they accuse you of?" And he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor marvelled greatly.
Now at the feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner, whomever the people wanted.
And at that time there was a certain prisoner whose name was Barabbas. And when they had gathered together, Pilate said to them:
"Which of the two do you want me to release to you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?" For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
And while he was sitting on the judgement seat, his wife sent to him and said, "What have you to do with that righteous man?
For I have suffered much in a vision because of him." But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the people to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus.
The governor answered and said to them, "Which of the two do you want me to release to you?" They cried out and said all together, "Barabbas."
Pilate said to them, "Then what shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?" And they all said, "Let him be crucified."
When Pilate saw that it was doing no good, but rather that a riot was arising, he then asked for water and washed his hands before them all and said:
"May I be innocent of this blood; see to it yourselves." All the people answered and said, "His blood be on us and on our children."
Then he released Barabbas to them, but he had Jesus flogged with a whip and handed him over to them to be crucified.
Then the soldiers [lit. men of the host] took Jesus and led him into the palace [lit. temple; i.e., the praetorium], and the whole company [lit. all the kindreds] gathered around him.
And they stripped him and put a purple cloak on him.
And they wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and they put a reed in his right hand, and kneeling before him they mocked him and said:
"Hail, King of the Jews!" And they spat on him, and took the reed from him and struck him on the head.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped the cloak off him and put his own clothes on him, and led him away to be crucified.
And they found a man of Cyrene named Simon; him they compelled to carry his cross.
And they came to the place called Golgotha, which is the Place of the Skull. And they offered him wine mixed with gall.
And he tasted it and would not drink. And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments and cast lots,
so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: "They divided my garments among them, and for my tunic they cast lots."
They kept watch over him there. And they put the charge against him over his head and wrote a board: "This is the King of the Jews."
Then they crucified two robbers with him, one on the right and one on the left. And those who passed by reviled him, wagging their heads and saying:
"Look, you who would destroy this temple and build it on the third day, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from that cross!"
In the same way the chief priests, with the scribes and the elders, mocked him and said: "He saved others; he cannot save himself.
If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from that cross, so that we may believe in him. For he said,
'I am the Son of God.'" In the same way the robbers who had been crucified with him also reproached him.
And from the sixth hour darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?"
That is: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" Some of those standing there heard it and said: "This man is calling Elijah."
And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink.
But the others said: "Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to save him." And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook, and the rocks were split;
and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
and they came out of the tombs, and after his resurrection they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
And the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and what had happened, were greatly afraid and said: "Truly this man was the Son of God."
Many women were also there, watching Jesus from a distance; they had followed him from Galilee and had served him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
Who is this who comes from Edom, with his garments crimson, from Bozrah?
This one is glorious in his apparel, mighty in strength. I speak righteousness and the judgment of salvation.
Why are your garments red, like those of one who treads the winepress, so trampled?
And of the nations there is no man with them; and I trampled them like earth, and I will pour out their blood like water.
For the day of their recompense has come upon them, and the year of redemption has arrived.
And I looked, and there was no helper; I watched, and no one helped me.
And my arm delivered it, and my wrath came upon them, and I trampled them in my anger, and I will pour out their blood upon the earth.
But Christ came,
the high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is,
not of this creation; not through the blood of calves, but through his own blood he entered the holy place and obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of calves and goats, and the ashes of heifers sprinkled on those who were defiled, sanctified them for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ,
who through the Holy Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify the mind from dead works to serve the living God.

And for this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, since a death has taken place for redemption from the first covenant, those who are chosen for the eternal inheritance may receive the promise.
For where a will is written, the death of the one who wrote the will must necessarily take place. For every written will is valid only after people are dead.
Otherwise it is never valid while the one who wrote the will is still alive. For this reason not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.
For when Moses had spoken all the commandments according to the law to all the people,
he took the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled the book itself and all the people, and said:
"This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you." In the same way he sprinkled blood on the tabernacle itself and on all the vessels used in worship.
And according to the law everything was purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there was no forgiveness.
So the copies of the heavenly things are purified by these, but the heavenly things themselves are purified by better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter holy places made with hands, which are copies of the true ones, but he entered heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God on our behalf.
Nor did he enter in order to offer himself many times, as the high priest enters the holy place once a year with blood that is not his own.
Otherwise he would have had to suffer many times since the creation of the world. But now he has appeared once, at the end of the ages, to set aside sins by his own sacrifice.
And just as people are appointed to die once, and after that comes the judgment, so also Christ was offered once to blot out the sins of many.
And he will appear a second time, without sin, to those who wait for him in faith as Savior.
Come, you who have put on Christ. In the Lord I put my trust; how [?]
They gave me vinegar for my food. Save me, O God, for [?] have come in.
And the soldiers led Jesus into the inner courtyard, which is the palace, and gathered the whole [?] (literally "the seeds/kindreds").
And they dressed him in a purple cloak and put a crown of thorns on him. And they began to salute him, saying to him: "Hail, King of the Jews!"
And they struck his head with a reed and spat on him, and they knelt down and worshipped him.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped off the purple cloak, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him out to crucify him.
And they forced a passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was coming in from the field, to carry his cross.
And they brought him to the place Golgotha, which translated is the Place of the Skull. And they offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments and cast lots over them, to see who would take what.
It was the third hour, and they crucified him. And there was an inscription of the charge against him, on which was written: The King of the Jews.
And with him they crucified two robbers, one on the right and one on the left.
And the scripture was fulfilled which says: He was numbered with the lawless. And those who passed by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying:
"Ah, you who would destroy this temple and build it on the third day, save yourself and come down from the cross!"
In the same way the chief priests, with the scribes, mocked him and said: "He saved others; he cannot save himself."
"If he is the Christ, the King of the Jews, let him come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe in him."
And those who were crucified with him reproached him. And when it was the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out and said: "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?"
which translated is: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" Some of those standing there heard it and said: "He is calling Elijah."
And one of them ran and filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink.
But the others said: "Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to set him free."
But Jesus cried out with a loud voice and gave up his spirit. And the curtain of the temple was torn from top to bottom.
When the centurion who stood facing him saw that he had cried out and given up his spirit, he said: "Truly this man was the Son of God."
And there were also some women watching him from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joses, and Salome,
who, when Jesus was in Galilee, had followed him and served him; and many other women as well, who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem.
O Lord, make it known to me and I will know it; for then I saw their schemes.
I, like an innocent lamb led to the slaughter, did not perceive it; they plotted an evil plot against me and said:
"Come, let us put wood into his bread, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name may no longer be remembered."
O Lord, judge of righteousness, who tests the heart and the kidneys, may I see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have laid open my cause.
Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek my life, who say:
"Do not prophesy in the name of the Lord, or else you will die at our hands."
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: "Behold, I will punish them: their young men shall die by the sword, their sons and their daughters shall perish by famine.
And there shall be no remnant of them, for I will bring evil upon the inhabitants of Anathoth, in the year of their punishment."
Righteous are you, O Lord, and I will plead my case with you; yet I will speak of justice to you.
Why does the way of the ungodly prosper? All who have dealt falsely with you in falsehood have gone far off. You planted them, and they established their roots.
I have forsaken my house and abandoned my inheritance; I have given my beloved soul into the hands of her enemies.
My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; it raised its voice against me; therefore I have hated it.
Therefore, brethren, we have boldness to enter the holy place by the blood of Jesus, which [?] …
[?] … and a great high priest over the house of God, let us draw near to him with a true heart and in full assurance of faith,
our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the confession of hope rightly, for he who promised is faithful.
And let us consider one another, to stir one another up to love and good works.
Do not forsake your own assembly, as is the custom of some, but encourage one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near.
For on account of willful sins, after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,
but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a zeal of fire that will devour the presumptuous.
Whoever despises the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses; how much worse a punishment does he deserve
who despises the Son of God, counts as unworthy the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and insults the Spirit of grace?
For we know him who said: "Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord." And again he says: "The Lord will judge his people."
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Today the veil of the temple [?]: Save me, O God, for [?] has failed.
And they were also leading two others, robbers, to be put to death with him.
And when they brought him to the place called Golgotha, which is the Place of the Skull, they crucified him there along with the evildoers, one on the right and one on the left.
And Jesus said: "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." And they divided his garments and cast lots. And the people stood watching.
The rulers also mocked him, saying: "He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the chosen one of God."
Some of the people also reviled him, coming up to him, offering him vinegar and saying: "If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself."
And there was an inscription over him, written in Greek, Latin and Hebrew letters: "This is the King of the Jews."
One of the evildoers who were hanging there blasphemed him and said: "If you are the Son of God, save yourself and us too."
His companion answered, rebuked him and said to him: "Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
We are receiving justly for what we did, but this man has done nothing lawless."
And he said: Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom. Jesus said to him: Amen, I say to you: today you will be with me in Paradise.
And it was the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole earth until the ninth hour. And the veil of the temple was torn in two.
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit. And when he had said this, he gave up the spirit.
Then, when the centurion saw this thing, he glorified God and said: Truly this man was righteous.
And all who were watching that sight and what had happened beat their breasts and went away.
But all who knew him stood at a distance; and the women who had followed him from Galilee also saw all this.
And the Lord my God will come, and all his holy ones with him. On that day there will be no light.
And there will be light on that one day, and that night will be made known to the Lord. It will be neither day nor night, and at evening there will be light.
On that day living water will go out from Jerusalem, half of it to the first sea and half of it to the last sea;
in the [?] of summer it will be so. And the Lord will be king over all the earth.
It will go around over all the earth; they will guard [?] all the land, the desert and the settled land, from Galad [?] to Rimmon;
to the south of Jerusalem it will be raised up; and in that very place [?] it will occupy the ground from the gates of Benjamin to the first gates,
and from the corner gates to the gate of Hananel, and to the winepress [?] of the diadems [?].
And they will dwell in it, and there will be no more curse; and Jerusalem will dwell in peace and in hope.
I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus,
who bore witness to the good confession under Pontius Pilate, that you keep this commandment spotless and undefiled until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which in his own time the blessed and only mighty King and Lord of lords will show, he who alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light,
whom no one among men has seen or is able to see; to whom belong glory and honor and power forever and ever.
Amen.
At your coming to the Cross: How long, O Lord, will you forget me:
Into your hands I commit: In you, O Lord, I have hoped; let [me] not [?]:
And those from among the people led Jesus away.
And he carried his own cross, and they went out to the place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
And there they crucified him, and with him they crucified two robbers, one on each side, and Jesus in the middle.
And Pilate wrote a placard and put it on the cross. And the writing was: Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews.
Many of the Jews read this board, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city.
And it was written in Hebrew, in Latin and in Greek. The chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate:
"Do not write 'King of the Jews', but that he said, 'I am the King of the Jews.'" Pilate said to them: "What I have written, I have written."
Then the soldiers who had crucified Jesus took his clothing and divided it into four parts, a part for each soldier.
But the tunic was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.
The soldiers said to one another: "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it, to see whose it will be," so that the scripture might be fulfilled:
"They divided my clothing among them, and for my tunic they cast lots." This is what the soldiers did.
Standing by the cross were his mother and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing by, he said to his mother: "Woman, behold your son!"
Then he said to the disciple: "Behold your mother!" From that time the disciple took her to his own home.
After this, when Jesus saw that everything was now accomplished, so that the scripture might be fulfilled, he said: "I thirst."
A vessel full of vinegar stood there. They filled a sponge, together with hyssop, put it on a reed, and held it to his mouth.
And when he had received the vinegar, he said: "Everything is accomplished." He bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
Then the Jews, because it was Friday, so that his body would not remain on the cross until the Sabbath, asked Pilate that his legs be broken.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, and likewise of the second, who had been crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus and saw
that he was already dead, they did not touch his legs; but one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
And he who saw it has testified, and his testimony is true, and he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you too may believe.
He did this so that the scripture might be fulfilled, which says: "Not a bone of his shall be broken."
And again another prophet says: "Look and see Christ, the one whom you pierced."
After this Joseph, who was from Arimathea, asked Pilate,
for he too was a disciple of Jesus, secretly, for fear of the Jews, that he might take away the body of Jesus; and Pilate gave him permission. They came and took away his body.
Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to him by night; and he brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
They took the body of Jesus down from the cross and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the burial custom of the Jews.
Now in the place where Jesus was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb.
And there they laid the body of Jesus, because of the Jews' Friday, since the tomb was nearby.
"Lord, cry out" [?]: this is the nobility [?] of our Lord:
See how the righteous one has perished, and no one takes it to heart, and righteous men are taken away,
and no one considers it, for justice has been taken away from the face of falsehood. And his grave will be in peace, for he has been taken away from the midst.
But you, come here, you lawless sons, offspring of adulterers and harlots. In what were you delighting?
Against whom did you open your mouth, stick out your tongue, and plot your evil?
And when God saw this, it did not please him, for there was no justice.
He looked, and there was no one to help; and he overcame them with his own arm and established his mercy.
And he put on righteousness like a coat of mail, set his salvation on his head like a helmet, and put on the garment of vengeance, with which he will repay reproach to his enemies in recompense.
And those of the setting of the sun will fear the name of the Lord, and those of the rising of the sun will fear his great name,
for the name of the Lord has come forth like a fierce river, and it will come with wrath.
And the deliverer will come from Zion and will turn away [?] ungodliness from Jacob, said the Lord. And this is my covenant with them, says the Lord Almighty:
my Spirit, which is upon you, and my words, which I have put in your mouth, said the Lord, from now and forever.
My enemies hunted me down like a sparrow, without cause, and they put my life to death in the pit; they laid a stone on me.
And water flowed over my head, and I said: Have I been cast off? I called on your name, O Lord, from the lowest pit.
You heard my voice; now do not make your ears heavy. Come near to me on the day when I called to you, and I said [?]: Do not fear.
Judge, O Lord, the judgments of my soul, and redeem my life. See, O Lord, all their acts of vengeance and all their plots against me.
See all their agitations against me, and they have multiplied [?] my judgments.
You have heard their reproach, O Lord, all their words, the rising [?] of their lips, and their plots every day, at their sitting down and their rising up.
Look, for I have become a byword to them. Repay them their recompense, O Lord, the snare of their heart.
Repay them according to the works of their hands; let the help of their heart be their toil.
Pursue them in your wrath, O Lord, and destroy them under heaven.
They put me in the lowest pit: O Lord, God of life.
And when it was evening,
a rich man came from Arimathea named Joseph, who had been a disciple of Jesus. He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Then Pilate ordered that his body be given. And Joseph took his body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
And he laid it in his new tomb, which he had hewn out of the rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary; they were sitting before the tomb.
Joseph asked for the body: Come, you faithful, today: Notable knowledge [?]: Source of life: Come, you faithful, and let us learn:
Lord, you appeared in honour among the people:
Let us oppress the poor and righteous man; let us not spare the old man, nor feel shame before the aged of many years.
Let our strength be our law of righteousness, for weakness is shown to be useless.
Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, for he is a burden to us and opposes our deeds,
and he reproaches us for sins against the law, and accuses us of sins against our training.
He professes that he has knowledge of God, and he calls himself son of God. He has become to us a reproof of the thoughts of our heart.
He is grievous for us even to look at, for his life is not like that of others, and his ways are different.
We are held by him in contempt as something loathsome, and he keeps away from our ways as from unclean things; he calls the end of the righteous blessed, he boasts and calls God father.
Let us see whether his words are true, and let us test what his end will be.
If the righteous man is the son of God, he will help him and deliver him from the hands of his adversaries.
Let us examine him with insult and torture, so that we may learn his gentleness and test his endurance of ill-treatment.
Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for, according to his own words, he will be looked after.

These things they planned, and they went astray, for their wickedness blinded them, and they did not know the mystery of God, nor did they hope for the reward of holiness, nor did they seek out the honour of blameless souls.
For God created man for incorruption and made him an image of his own nature.
Through the envy of the devil death entered the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.
Lord, have mercy on us, for we trust in you;
the race of the disobedient has been given over to destruction, for our salvation is through you in the time of distress.
By the hand of the fear of you the peoples were terrified, and before your majesty the nations were scattered.
But now your spoils will be gathered, from small to great; as someone gathers locusts, so they will mock you.
Holy is God, who dwells on high; Zion has been filled with judgment and righteousness.
And they will be given over to the law; our salvation is in treasuries; wisdom and knowledge and godliness toward the Lord are coming; these are the treasures of righteousness.
Behold now, those whom you feared will be afraid with fear of you; and envoys will be sent to plead for peace;
They were weeping bitterly, for their ways have been laid waste. The fear of the nations has ceased, and the covenant with the fathers has been taken away, and they are not counted as men at all.
The land mourned; Lebanon was put to shame; Sharon became marshland; Galilee and Carmel were laid bare.
"Now I will arise," says the Lord, "now I will be glorified, now I will be exalted. Now you will see, and you will be put to shame."
For you will not abandon my soul.
Keep me, O Lord, for I have hoped in you. Yours among them [?]:
On the next day, which is after Friday, the Pharisees and the chief priests gathered before Pilate and said to him:
"Lord, we have remembered that that deceiver said, while he was still alive, 'After three days I will rise.'
Now give orders for the tomb to be made secure until the third day, so that his disciples do not come by night, steal him away, and tell the people:
'He has risen from the dead.' Then the last deception will be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them: "You have a guard. Go and make it as secure as you know how."
So they went and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone and setting the guard.
Praise is fitting for you, O God, in Zion:
"Now I will arise," says the Lord, "now." Sing to the Lord a new song. For his beginning is on high.
Sing to the Lord a new song. Sing to the Lord, all the earth:
May the name of the Lord be blessed from this time on: Praise, O children.
Sing to the Lord a new song, for wondrous...
O Lord, I have cried out. Shine, shine:
Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; sing praise:
Arise, O God, judge the earth. God stood in the assembly of gods:
In the beginning God made: In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth.
The earth was invisible and unformed, darkness was over the deeps, and the Spirit of God was moving over the waters. And God said: "Let there be light."
And there was light. And God saw that the light was good. And God separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light "day," and he called the darkness "night." There was evening and there was morning, the first day. And God said:
"Let there be a firmament among the waters, and let it divide the waters from one another." And it was so. And God made the firmament.
And God separated the waters that were below the firmament from the waters that were above the firmament.
And God called the firmament heaven. And God saw that it was good. And there was evening and there was morning, the second day.
And God said: Let the waters that are under heaven be gathered into one gathering, and let the dry land appear.
And God called the dry land earth, and the gathering of the waters he called seas. And God saw that it was good.
And God said: Let the earth bring forth the green of the grass, seed-bearing, each according to its kind and each according to its likeness,
and the fruitful tree that bears fruit whose seed is in it, each according to its likeness and each according to its kind.
And God saw that it was good. 1 And there was evening and there was morning, the third day.
And God said: Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light to the earth and to divide between the day and the night.
And let them be for signs, for days and for years. And let them be for giving light in the firmament of heaven, so that they may shine upon the earth.
And God made these two great lights: the great light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.
And God set them in the firmament of heaven, so that they might shine upon the earth, and rule over the day and the night, and divide between the light and the darkness.
And God saw that it was good. And there was evening and there was morning, the fourth day.
And God said: Let the waters bring forth creeping things having living souls, and winged birds over the earth, along the firmament of heaven. And it was so.
And God made the great sea-monster and all the creeping things that the waters brought forth, according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.
And God blessed them and said: Increase and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas; and you birds, multiply upon the earth.
And there was evening and there was morning, the fifth day. And God said:
Let the earth bring forth living souls according to their kinds: four-footed creatures, creeping things, wild beasts of the earth, and all cattle according to their kinds.
1 And God said: Let me make man in our image and likeness.
Let him rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, and all the cattle and the creeping things that go upon the earth.
And God made man in his own form, and in the image of God he made him; male and female he made them.
He blessed them and said: Increase and multiply and fill the earth and have dominion over it, and rule over the fish of the sea and over all moving things.
And God said: Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing herb that is upon the face of all the earth;
and every tree that has in it seed-bearing fruit according to its kind shall be food for you.
And to all the creeping things that go upon the earth, which have in them a living soul, every seed-bearing herb shall be for food.
And God saw everything that he had made, and behold, everything was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
1 And the heavens and the earth and all their adornment were completed in their making. And God completed his work which he had made on the sixth day.
And God rested from all his works on the seventh day. And he made it holy, and he rested.
This is the book of the creation of heaven and earth, when God made heaven and earth on the seventh day;
every green plant of the field before it had sprung up, for God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to work the earth.
And God formed man, dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life, for that man became a living soul.
And God planted a paradise in the east, toward the rising of the sun, and placed there the man whom he had formed.
And then God made to spring up every tree beautiful to look upon, good, [and the tree] of knowing good and evil [?] in the midst of paradise.
A river goes out from Eden to water paradise, and from there it is divided into four heads. The name of the first river is Pishon.
This is the one that flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold. And the gold of that land is good; there is gold there, and the stone kapoet [?].
And the name of the second river is Gihon. This is the one that flows around the whole land of India.
And the third river is the Tigris. This is the one that flows before Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
And the Lord God brought out the man whom he had formed and placed him in the paradise of delight, to work it and to keep it.
And the Lord God commanded Adam and said to him: You may eat of every tree of paradise.
But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat of it, for on the day you eat of it you shall surely die.
And the Lord God said: It is not good for this man to be alone; let us make for him a helper like him.
And God further formed from the earth every wild beast of the field and every bird of the sky, and brought them before Adam to see what he would call them.
And whatever Adam called each one, that is its name.
And Adam gave names to all the livestock and to all the birds of the sky and to all the wild beasts of the earth, but for Adam there was not found a helper like him.
And the Lord God cast a trance upon Adam and put him to sleep.
And he took one rib out of his side and filled up [the place] with flesh, and the Lord God built the rib which he had taken from Adam [text: "from the night" ?] into a wife, and brought her to Adam.
And Adam said: This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called woman, for she was brought out of her husband.
Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and shall cleave to his wife, and the two of them shall be one flesh.
And the two of them, Adam and his wife, were naked, and they were not ashamed. [?] upon [?], which God made.
And the serpent said to the woman: What is this that the Lord your God has said to you, namely:
"You may eat of every tree of paradise, but of the tree of knowing good and evil, which is in the midst of paradise, you shall not eat"?
And the woman said: Of every tree that is in paradise we may eat, but of the tree of knowing good and evil we shall not eat.
And the serpent said to the woman: "God knew that you will surely not die on the day you eat of it;
your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil."
And the woman saw that it was good for the eyes to look at and beautiful to behold.
And she took of the tree and ate, and she also gave to her husband. They ate, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked.
And they sewed fig leaves together and made clothing for themselves. And they heard the voice of the Lord God as he was walking in paradise.
And Adam and his wife hid from the face of the Lord God in the midst of paradise.
And the Lord God called to Adam and said: "Adam, Adam, where are you?" And he said: "Behold, here I am, Lord.
I heard your voice as you were walking in paradise, and I was afraid, because I am naked, and I hid."
The Lord said to him: "Who told you that you are naked? Is it not that you have eaten of the tree from which I commanded you not to eat?"
He answered and said: "This woman whom you gave me, she gave to me and I ate." And the Lord said to the woman: "What is this that you have done?"
The woman said: "The serpent deceived me and I ate." The Lord said to the serpent: "Cursed are you among all the creeping things that go upon the earth."
You shall go on your breast and belly, and you shall eat earth all the days of your life.
I will put enmity between you and the woman, between you and her offspring. He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel.
And to the woman he said: I will greatly multiply your sorrows and your sighs, and your turning shall be toward your husband,
and he shall rule over you. And to Adam he said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife, and because you ate from the tree
from which I commanded you not to eat, cursed be the earth in your works; in sorrow you shall eat all the days of your life.
It shall bring forth thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the grass of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth there, for you are earth and to earth you shall return.
And Adam called the name of his wife [?] Life, for she is the mother of all the living.
And God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and clothed them.
And God said: Behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil.
Now then, he may put forth his hand and eat from the tree, and live forever.
And the Lord sent him out of the garden of delight, and set there the cherubim and the flaming, turning sword to guard the way of the tree of life.
And he set there the flaming cherubim and the turning sword to guard from the tree of life.
And it came to pass after these words that God tested Abraham and said to him: Abraham, Abraham. And Abraham said: Here I am, Lord.
And he said to him: Take your beloved son Isaac and go to a certain high land, and there offer him as a sacrifice on a certain mountain, which I tell you.
Abraham rose at dawn and saddled his donkey, and took with him two servants and Isaac his son;
and he split wood for the sacrifice, rose, and went to the place which God had told him.
Abraham lifted up his eyes, and behold, he saw the place from afar. And Abraham said to his servants:
Sit here with the donkeys; I and this boy will go to a certain place, worship the Lord, and come back to you.
And Abraham took the wood for the sacrifice and laid it on Isaac his son. And he took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them went on together.
Isaac said to his father: Father. And he said: What is it, my son? And he said: Here are the fire and the wood; where is the sheep for the sacrifice?
Abraham said to him: God will see to a sheep for himself for the sacrifice, my son. And the two of them went on to the place which God had told him.
And Abraham built an altar of the Lord there, laid out the wood, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.
And he put out his hand to take the knife and to slay his son. And the angel of God spoke to him from heaven and said: Abraham, Abraham.
And he said: Here I am, Lord. And he said: Do not lay your hand on the boy, and do him no harm at all.
"Now I know that you fear God, since you have not spared that beloved son of yours for my sake."
And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a ram was caught by its horns in a sabek bush.
And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a sacrifice in place of Isaac his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place "The Lord saw," for they say today: "On the mountain the Lord appeared."
And the angel of the Lord called to Abraham from heaven a second time and said: "By myself I swear, says the Lord: because you have done this and have not spared your beloved son for my sake,
I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore;
and your descendants shall possess the cities of your enemies; and in your descendants all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed."
Abraham turned back and went to his servants. They arose and went away together, and Abraham dwelt at the Well of the Oath.
The Lord began to speak to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt and said:
"This first month shall be for you the head of the months, the first month among the months of the year. Now go and tell the whole congregation of the sons of Israel:
On the tenth of this month let each one take a lamb, by families and by tribes; let them divide it up and take out a lamb for each household.

If they are too few in the household and are not able to eat the lamb, let them bring their neighbor into the house; according to the number of persons let each one take, as much as the lamb will suffice for.
Your lamb shall be a male, a yearling, without blemish; they shall take it from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats.
And you shall keep it carefully until the fourteenth of the month, and the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening."
And let them take some of its blood and mark both doorposts of the gate and the threshold of the house in which they will eat it.
And let them eat the lamb that same night, at evening, roasted with fire; and let them eat unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

But let them eat the lamb in this way: do not let them eat it unleavened [? probably "raw"], nor boiled in water, but let them eat it roasted with fire. Let them eat it hot and eat it quickly; let them eat the head and feet together with the entrails.
And leave none of it over until morning; do not tear it apart [?]; do not break a bone. Burn with fire whatever of it is left over.
And eat it in this way: staff in your hands, belt on your loins, sandals on your feet; eat it quickly, in great haste, for it is the Lord's Passover.
And that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast, and on all the land of Egypt I will bring vengeance, for I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where the children of Israel are, the houses in which they are living.
I will look at the blood marked on the doors and will shelter you, to protect you from the plague of wrath, when I pass down and destroy the firstborn of Egypt.
And that day shall be a memorial for you, a feast, a Passover celebration to the Lord for all generations, a law of joy forever, the chief of their yearly feasts.
For seven days eat unleavened bread, and from the first day until the [?] remove all leaven from your house.
Whoever eats bread from leavened [?] dough, that person shall be utterly cut off from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
For the first day is called: holy to the Lord. And the day of the Lord is called holy to the Lord.
None of you shall do any work of servile labor on those days, except that one work without which nothing can be managed for anyone's needs; only this shall be done by you.
And keep this commandment, for on this day I am bringing you out of the land of the Egyptians. Keep that day from generation to generation as an everlasting law for you.
You shall begin to eat unleavened bread from the twelfth day of the first month, from evening until the twentieth day [?] of that month, at evening.
And for seven days let there be no leaven in your houses.

Whoever eats anything leavened, that person shall be cut off from the people of the children of Israel, whether among the strangers who have come from outside or among the native-born children of the servants of your land.
Let no one at all eat anything leavened in any of your dwellings; eat unleavened bread instead.
Moses summoned the elders of the children of Israel and said to them: "Hurry, each of you take a lamb for yourselves, tribe by tribe, and slaughter it as the Lord's Passover.
Take one bunch of hyssop for sprinkling, dip it in the lamb's blood, and mark the doorposts of the gates and their thresholds,
but none of you shall go out of the door of your house until morning.
When the Lord comes down to destroy the Egyptians, they will see the blood on all three sides of the door, and he will pass by your doors and will not send the destroyer,
the executioner of death, to enter your houses and slay your firstborn."
And you shall keep this word as a law for yourselves forever, to the end of the ages.
When you enter the land which the Lord your God will give you, as he told you, keep this service. And you shall say to him:
“This is the sacrifice of the Passover of the Lord, who protected the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when he struck down Egypt, for he delivered our houses.”
And the people bowed down and worshiped the Lord. And they went, and the sons of Israel did as Moses and Aaron had commanded; so they did.
And at midnight the Lord struck down every firstborn of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne,
to the firstborn of the maidservant who sits at the mill, and to the firstborn of every beast.
And Pharaoh rose up in the night, and all his servants and all the Egyptians;
and there was a great cry in all Egypt, for there was no house in which there was not one dead. Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron in the night and said to them:
“Rise up and go out from among my people, you and the sons of Israel; go and serve the Lord your God, as you say.
And drive out your sheep and your cattle and go, as you said; but bless me too.”
And the Egyptians urged the people to hurry and send them out of their land, for they said, “Otherwise we shall all die.”
And the people took their dough before it was leavened, bundled in their garments, and loaded it on their backs.
And the sons of Israel did as Moses had ordered them. And they asked the Egyptians for vessels of gold and silver and for clothing.
And the Lord gave his people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and they gave them whatever they asked. And they plundered the Egyptians.
And the sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, six hundred thousand men on foot, besides their baggage.
And a great many strangers went out with them, and sheep and cattle and a very great amount of livestock.
And they baked the dough which they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened cakes [?], without leaven, for they had not been able to leaven it,
for the Egyptians had driven them out, and they could not delay, nor had they prepared food for the journey.
Now the sojourning of the sons of Israel and of their fathers in Egypt and in Haran was four hundred and thirty years.
And after four hundred and thirty years the people went out of Egypt by night. This is the first vigil of the Lord: their being brought out of the land of Egypt.
That night is the first watch of the Lord; it shall be so among all the sons of Israel and their generations.
And the word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
“Rise up and go to the city of Nineveh and cry out there, for the cry of their wickedness has gone up.”
And Jonah rose up to flee toward Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, and he went down to Joppa and found there a ship that was bound
and going toward Tarshish. And he paid the fare of the ship and went on board to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord.
And God raised up a fierce wind on the sea, and the ship was on the point of breaking apart.
And the sailors were seized with terror and great fear, and each man began to cry out to his own god. They threw their cargo from the ship into the sea to lighten the ship.
And Jonah had gone down into the hold of the ship and was asleep and snoring. The ship's captain came to him and said to him: "What is this, that you are asleep and snoring?
Get up and call on the Lord your God; perhaps he will save us and we will not perish." Then each man began to speak to his neighbour, and they said:
"Come, let us cast lots and find out on whose account all this has come upon us." They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
And they said to him: "Tell us, what is this evil that has come upon us? What is your business? Where are you from? What country are you from, or what people?"
And Jonah said to them: "I am a servant of God, and I serve the Lord God, who made heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land."
And the men were afraid with great fear, for they understood that he was fleeing from the presence of God, because he had told them.
And they said to him: "Now what shall we do to you, so that this sea will calm down for us?"
For this sea was growing more and more turbulent, and these waves were raging more and more against us.
Jonah said to them: "Take me up and throw me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you, for it is because of me that all this trouble has come upon you."
And the sailors strained at the ship to turn it back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea grew more and more turbulent and fierce against them.

They began to cry out to the Lord and said: "Let it not be so, O Lord! Do not destroy us for the life of this man, and do not bring righteous blood upon us, for you, O Lord, have done whatever you willed."
And they took Jonah up and threw him into the sea, and at once the sea ceased from its turbulence.
And the men were afraid with great fear. They began to worship God and offer sacrifice to him and make vows.
And the Lord God commanded the great whale to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights.
Jonah began to pray to the Lord his God from inside the belly of the whale.
And he said: "In my distress I cried out to the Lord, and God heard me; from the depths of hell you heard my voice.
For they cast me down into the depth, into the heart of the sea, and the currents of the water surrounded me; all your surges and your waves passed over me.
And I said: Have I been cast away from the sight of your eyes? Or will I yet again look upon your holy temple?
The waters poured over me up to my very soul, and the depths surrounded me; my head sank down.
I went down into the clefts of the mountains, into the earth, where I saw its bars, like everlasting locks.
Now let my life come up out of corruption to you, O Lord my God.
When my soul was failing I cried out, and you, O Lord, saved me; let my prayer reach your holy temple. For those who keep to falsehood have perished.
But I will sing to you with a voice of blessing and confession, and I will offer sacrifice and fulfil my vow to the Saviour."
And the Lord God commanded the great sea monster to spit Jonah out onto dry land.
And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, and he said: "Arise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and cry out there as I told you before."
Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, as the Lord had commanded him. Now Nineveh was a city whose size measured a journey of three days.
When Jonah had gone into the city a day's journey, he began to cry out and said: "Behold, only three days more, and Nineveh will be overthrown."
And the people of Nineveh believed God, and a herald cried out: "Proclaim a fast!" And they put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
And this word reached the king of the Ninevites. At once he rose from his thrones, stripped off his robe of splendour, put on sackcloth, and sat down in ashes.
And he ordered a proclamation to the whole city and said to them: "Let neither man nor flock, neither beast nor cattle, be allowed to taste anything at all, neither to graze nor to drink water."
And every man put on sackcloth, and they held back their flocks, and they called upon God with all their heart.
And each one turned from his evil way and from the wickedness that was in their hands.
They said: "Perhaps God will see this and relent concerning us, and turn away the anger of his wrath, and we will not perish."
God looked upon their deeds, for they had turned away from their wicked deeds,
and God relented of the anger of his wrath that he had intended to bring upon them, and he did not do it. When Jonah saw this, he was greatly distressed and was displeased.
He rose to worship God and said: "Ah, Lord, are these not the words that I was saying while I was still in my own country?
That is why I hastened to flee toward Tarshish, for I knew that you are merciful and forbearing and abounding in mercy, and that you relent from doing harm to people.
Now, O Lord my God, take my life from me, for death is better for me than life."
And the Lord God said to Jonah: "Are you truly so distressed?"
Jonah went out of the city; he went out and sat down before the city, and he made there a [?] and sat in it, until he should see what would happen to the city.
And the Lord God commanded a gourd to spring up at Jonah's head, so that it might shade his head from the heat of his distress.
And Jonah rejoiced over the gourd with great joy.
Then God commanded a worm at dawn to attack that gourd, and on the following day it struck it and withered it.
And the sun beat down, and God commanded a scorching wind to blow, mingled with heat, upon his head, and it oppressed him until he fainted [?], and his breath grew short.
And Jonah said: "My death is better than life. Am I any better than my fathers?"
And the Lord God said to Jonah: "Are you truly distressed over that gourd?" And Jonah said: "I am greatly distressed, even to death."
The Lord said to him: "Now you have pitied this gourd, for which you did not labour, which you did not water and did not make grow; it sprang up in a night and perished in one night.
And should I not pity Nineveh, the great city, in which more than twelve myriads (120,000) people live who do not know their right hand from their left, and their livestock?"
And when the Lord brought out his people, he did not lead them by the way
And when the Lord brought out his people, he did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, because it was near, and he said:
"Perhaps this people may change their minds when they see war, and turn back to Egypt."
And God led the people around by the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea. In the fifth generation the sons of Israel came out of the land of Egypt.
And Moses brought the bones of Joseph out with him, for Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear an oath, and had said:
"The Lord will surely visit you, and you shall carry my bones away with you."
And the sons of Israel set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, beside the wilderness.
And God went before them by day in a pillar of light and showed them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire.
The pillar of light by day and the pillar of fire did not depart from before all the people. The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
"Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them turn back and encamp before the ravine between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon.
And let them encamp before it, toward the sea. And Pharaoh said to his people: 'The sons of Israel have gone astray in the land, for they are shut in in the wilderness.'
But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue after them.
And I will be glorified over Pharaoh and over all his people, and the Egyptians shall know that I am God." And they did so.
And the king of the Egyptians was told that the one [?] had fled. And the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said:
"What is this that we have done, that we have let the sons of Israel go? Why should they not serve us?" And Pharaoh harnessed his chariots and took all his people with him.
And he took six hundred chosen chariots and all the horses of Egypt, and commanders over them all.
And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, and of his servants, and he pursued the sons of Israel; but the sons of Israel went out with an uplifted arm and a strong hand.
And the Egyptians pursued after them and found them encamped by the sea,
and all the chariots and horses of Pharaoh and the horsemen and all his people, before the ravine opposite Baal-zephon. And Pharaoh was drawing near.
The sons of Israel lifted up their eyes and saw that the Egyptians were drawn up behind them, at the mountain [?], and they were greatly afraid.
The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord. And they said to Moses: "Were there no graves in Egypt, that you have brought us out to die in this wilderness?
What is this that you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt? Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, when we said to you:
'Leave us alone, and let us serve the Egyptians,' rather than our being destroyed in this wilderness?"
Moses said to the people: "Do not be afraid. Stand firm and watch for the voice [?] from the Lord that will come for us today.
For as you have seen these Egyptians today, you shall never see them again, for all time to come.
The Lord will fight for you, and you shall keep silent. The Lord said to Moses: Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them set out.
And you, take up that rod of yours and stretch out your hand over the sea, and let it be divided, and let the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea as on dry land.
And I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, and they will go in after you.
And I will be glorified over Pharaoh and over all his people and over his horses, and all the Egyptians shall understand
that I am God, who have been glorified over Pharaoh and over his chariots and his horsemen.
The angel of the Lord, who went before the camp of the sons of Israel, rose up and stood behind them.
And the pillar of cloud moved from before their face and stood behind them,
and it went in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of the sons of Israel and remained there, and there was thick darkness.
That night passed, and they did not move toward one another that night. Moses stretched out his hand over the sea,
and the Lord sent a fierce wind from the south over the sea all night long, and the sea dried up.
And the sons of Israel went into the sea on dry ground, and the water was a wall on their right and a wall on their left.
And the Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh's horses and his chariots and horsemen went in after them into the midst of the sea.
Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to the Lord, and they said:
And it came to pass, in the [?] of daybreak (the morning watch), the Lord looked down upon the camp of the Egyptians, and it came to pass,
in the [?] of daybreak (the morning watch), the Lord looked down upon the camp of the Egyptians with the pillar of fire and of cloud, and threw the camp of the Egyptians into panic.
And he bound the wheels of their chariots, and they drove them with difficulty.
And the Egyptians said: Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord fights for them against the Egyptians.
And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the waters return and cover the Egyptians, their chariots and their horsemen.
And he stretched out the rod in his hand over the sea, and the waters returned to their places, and the Egyptians were covered.
The water of the Red Sea turned back and covered them, all their chariots and their horsemen, all the host of Pharaoh that had gone down into the sea.
But the sons of Israel walked through the midst of the sea as on dry land, and the water was a wall for them on the right and on the left.
And the Lord delivered Israel with a strong hand and an exalted arm. And all Israel saw the mighty hand which the Lord had used against the Egyptians.
The people feared the Lord and believed God and Moses his servant.
At that time Moses and the sons of Israel praised the Lord with this song; they spoke and said:
1 At that time the sons of Israel sang this song to the Lord. Tone: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified; horses and horsemen he has cast into the sea.
Be our helper and protector, as a savior to us. This is our God. Let us glorify him, and let us exalt the God of our father.
This is the Lord, who shatters wars; the Lord is his name.
The chariots of Pharaoh and all his host he cast into the sea; the chosen horsemen of their commanders he drowned in the Red Sea.
The sea covered them; they sank and were cast down into the depth of the abyss like stones.
Your right hand, O Lord, is glorious; by your power your right hand, O Lord, slew your enemies.
In the greatness of your glory you shattered those who rose against you; you sent forth the wrath of your anger, and it devoured them like reeds.
By the breath of the might of your anger the waters were parted; the waters of the sea were walled up and stood like walls; the waves froze and were walled up in the midst of the sea.
The enemy said: I will pursue, I will overtake, I will strike, I will divide the spoil, I will glut myself with plunder.
I will slay him with my sword; my hand shall rule and be exalted over him.
You sent forth your spirit; the sea covered them; they sank, they were cast down in the mighty waters.
Who is like you among the gods, O Lord? Or who is like you, glorious in holiness?
You are wondrous in glory, you who worked signs and wonders. You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
In your righteousness you led your people, this people whom you redeemed; by your strength you comforted the camp of your holiness.
The nations heard and were enraged; anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom hastened, and the princes of the Moabites; fear and trembling seized them, and all the inhabitants of Canaan were dismayed.
Fear and trembling fell upon them, and by the might of your arm they became as stone.
Until your people pass over, O Lord, until this your people whom you have chosen pass over.
Until they bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your holiness, the place prepared and to be built for your dwelling,
the sanctuary which you acquired from the beginning, O Lord, which your hands prepared, O Lord. The Lord is King forever and for ever and ever.
For Pharaoh went in with his chariots and horsemen into the midst of the sea, and he brought back the water of the Red Sea upon them, and it covered them;
but the children of Israel walked as on dry land in the midst of the sea.
And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Moses and Aaron, took timbrels in her hand, and all the women went out with her with timbrels.
And Miriam led them and said: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified: horsemen and horses he cast into the sea.
Miriam led them and said: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified: horsemen and horses he cast into the sea.
Be illumined, be illumined, O Jerusalem:
Who is this who hides his counsel from me, who gathers up thoughts in his heart and thinks to conceal them from me?
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me: Where were you when I was laying the foundations of the earth?
Tell me, if you have understanding. Who set its measurements, do you know? Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
Or on what are its rings fastened? Or who is it that laid the corner stone upon it?
When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice. I shut up the sea with gates when it was being born, when it came forth from its mother's womb.
I put a cloud on it as a garment and wrapped it in mists.
I set boundaries for it and fixed bars and gates for it, and I said to it: This far you shall come and no farther, but your waves shall be broken within you.
Or was it in your time that I appointed the light of dawn, and did the morning star learn its proper place from you, so as to reach the edges of the earth and scatter the ungodly from it?
Or did you take soil from the ground and make clay into a living, speaking being, and set it on the earth?
Or did you take away the light from the ungodly, and do you crush the arms of the proud?
Have you come to this spring of the sea, or have you walked in the tracks of the abyss?
Did the gates of death open to you in fear, or did the gatekeepers of hell see you and tremble?
Or have you been taught the breadth of what lies under heaven? Tell me, then, what it is like: in what place does the light dwell, and which place belongs to the darkness?
If only you could bring me to their boundaries, or do you know their places? Do you have knowledge? Who knows, were you born then, and are the years of your life so many?
Have you gone into the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail? For they are stored up for the day of enemies, of strife and of battle.
Or where does the frost come from, which spreads southward under heaven? Tell me. Or who prepares the course for the violent rain, and the path of the wild beasts?
Who is the father of the rain, or who is it that begot the brands of light? From whose womb does the ice come, or the hoarfrost in the heavens?
Who begot what comes down like the water of a river, or who silenced the mouths of the ungodly?
Have you understood the bonds of the Pleiades, or did you open the barriers of Orion?
Or do you know the courses of heaven, or how many things have been made together under heaven?
Will you call to the clouds with your voice, and will they obey you, trembling with much fierce water? Or will you send out the thunderbolts?
Will they go and say to you, 'Here we are'? Or who gave women the wisdom of weaving, or skill in embroidery?
Or who counted the clouds by number and bent the heavens down to the earth? It is spread out like dusty earth; I have made it firm like a cubed stone.
Or will you hunt food for the lions and satisfy the appetites of the dragons, when they cower and lie in their lairs in the thicket, lying in wait?
Or who prepared food for the raven, when its young cry out to the Lord and wander about looking for food?
Do you know the time when the wild goats give birth among the rocks? Or did you watch over the birth pangs of the deer?
And did you count the full months of their bearing, or did you ease their birth pangs?
And did you raise their young without birth [?], and did you send them their birth pangs?
They cast out their young and multiply by giving birth. Their young go out and do not come back on their own.
Or who let the wild ass go free and loosed its bonds? I made the desert its food and the salt land its dwelling.
It scorns the crowds of the city and does not hear the reproach of the tax collectors.
It searches the mountains for its pasture and goes after the trail of every green plant.
Or will the unicorn be willing to serve you, or to lie down at your manger? Or will you tie its yoke on with a rope, or will it pull your plough across the field?
Or will you trust it because its strength is great, and leave your work to it? Do you believe that it will bring in your seed and gather it onto your threshing floor?
The [?] (mčurinavi) rejoices with its wings, if the ostrich and the duck [?] draw near to it. For it leaves its eggs on the earth and warms them in the ground.
And it forgot where it scattered them, and the beasts of the field trample them. It has become hard toward its young, as though they were not its own; it has laboured in vain, without fear.
For God has silenced wisdom in it and has not given it understanding.
From time to time it lifts itself up on high; it mocks the horse and its rider. Did you clothe the horse with strength and gird its neck with terror?
And did you put armour on it, and glory and boldness in its chest? It paws the plain with its hooves, it cries out, and it goes out onto the plain in strength.
It laughs when the arrow comes and does not turn back from the sword. Above it the bow rattles, along with the blade of the spear and the shaking of the [?] (torni).
And in its fury it tears up the ground, and it does not believe it until the trumpet sounds.
When the trumpet signals, it says, "Aha!" From far off it catches the scent of battle, the charge and the shouting.
Does the hawk stand still because you taught it? Does it spread its wings and stand unmoving, looking toward the north?
Do the eagle and the heron rise up at your command and settle on their nests? Do they dwell on the peaks of the rock and stay hidden there?
And it looks for food: if the food is far off, its eyes see it. And its young are smeared with blood; wherever there is a carcass, they are found there at once.
And the Lord God answered Job and said: Now will you really shrink from judgment with the Almighty? Whoever rebukes God must answer for his word.

Job answered and said to the Lord: Why should I go on being judged in instruction and rebuking the Lord, when I have heard such great things, I who am nothing? And what word shall I find to answer such things?
I will lay my hand on my mouth. I have spoken once, and I will add nothing a second time.
And it came to pass, when the Lord was taking Elijah up by [?] as though into heaven, that Elijah and Elisha went out from Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha: Stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel.
And Elisha said: As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they came to Bethel.
And the sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came to meet him and said to him:
Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master away from over you? And Elisha said: I know it too; be silent.
And Elijah said to Elisha: Stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as Jericho.
And Elisha said: As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they came to Jericho.
And the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him:
Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master up from over you? Elisha said: I know it too; be silent.
And Elijah said to Elisha: Stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan.
And Elisha said: As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And the two of them went on.
And fifty men, sons of the prophets, came and stood at a distance opposite them, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
And Elijah took his mantle, folded it up and struck the waters, and the water was divided to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
And when they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha: "Ask what I should do for you before I am taken up from you."
And Elisha said: "Let a double portion of the spirit that is upon you be upon me."
And Elijah said: "You have asked a hard thing. But if you see me taken up from you, it will be so for you; if not, it will not be."
And as they were still walking and talking, behold, chariots of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated them from each other.
And Elijah was caught up in a whirlwind as if into heaven. And Elisha cried out: "Father, father, chariot of Israel and its horseman!"
After that he saw him no more. And Elisha took hold of his garment and tore it in two.
And Elisha took the mantle of Elijah, which had fallen upon him, and struck the waters, and the water was not divided. And Elisha said: "Where is the God of Elijah, apphō [?]?"
And he struck the waters in this way a second time, and the waters were divided to one side and the other, and he crossed over on dry ground.
And the sons [?] saw him
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make an everlasting covenant with the house of Israel.
Not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt,
for they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, said the Lord.
For this is my covenant that I will make with the house of Israel and the house of Judah after those days, said the Lord:
I will put my chosen [?] into their minds and write them on the tablets of their hearts, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.
And they will no longer teach each one his brother, saying, "Know the Lord," for all of them will know me, from the least of them to the greatest,
for I will be merciful toward their falsehoods, and I will no longer remember their lawless deeds.
And after the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, the minister of Moses, and said:
"Moses my servant has died. Now arise and cross over the Jordan, you and your people, to the land that I gave to your fathers.
Every place on which the soles of your feet tread, I will give to you, as I said to Moses.
From the wilderness before Lebanon as far as the great river Euphrates, and as far as the sea at the end, and from the rising of the sun, shall be your border.
No one shall stand against you all the days of your life.
As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not forsake you or neglect you.
Be strong and courageous to keep and do as Moses my servant commanded you, and do not turn aside from it, either to the right
nor to the left, so that you may understand in all things. Then your ways will prosper, and then you will understand.
Behold, I have commanded you: be strong, be courageous, and do not be afraid, for the Lord your God is with you in every place wherever you go.
And the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of God and set me down in the middle of a plain; and it was full of human bones.
And he led me over them; and behold, there were very many on the face of the plain, and they were very dry.
And he said to me: Son of man, prophesy over these bones. And say to them: You dry bones, hear the word of the Lord!
Thus says the Lord to these bones: Behold, I will send the spirit of life into you.
And I will put sinews on you, and make flesh grow on you, and spread skin over you;
and I will put my spirit in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as the Lord commanded me.
And it came to pass that as soon as I prophesied, behold, there was a shaking, and the bones were brought together, from both sides, each to its own joint. And I saw:
behold, sinews grew on them, and skin was spreading over them, but there was not yet any spirit in them.
And the Lord said to me: Prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead, and let them live!
And I prophesied as the Lord commanded me. The spirit entered into them, and they stood up on their feet, a very great multitude.
The Lord spoke to me and said: Son of man, these bones are the house of Israel, and they have all said:
'Our bones have dried up, and all our hope has perished, for we have died.' Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to them:
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will open your graves and bring you out of your graves, and I will bring you into the land of Israel.
And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I open your graves and bring my people out of their graves,
and I will put my spirit in you and bring you into your own land, and you shall know that I am the Lord, says the Lord of hosts.
And it came to pass after those words:
Who is this who hides his counsel from me, who gathers up thoughts in his heart and thinks to conceal them from me?
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me: Where were you when I was laying the foundations of the earth?
Tell me, if you have understanding. Who set its measurements, do you know? Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
Or on what are its rings fastened? Or who is it that laid the corner stone upon it?
When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice. I shut up the sea with gates when it was being born, when it came forth from its mother's womb.
I put a cloud on it as a garment and wrapped it in mists.
I set boundaries for it and fixed bars and gates for it, and I said to it: This far you shall come and no farther, but your waves shall be broken within you.
Or was it in your time that I appointed the light of dawn, and did the morning star learn its proper place from you, so as to reach the edges of the earth and scatter the ungodly from it?
Or did you take soil from the ground and make clay into a living, speaking being, and set it on the earth?
Or did you take light away from the ungodly, and did you break the arms of the proud?
Have you reached the source of the sea, or have you walked in the tracks of the abyss?
Have the gates of death been opened to you in fear, or did the gatekeepers of hell see you and tremble?
Or have you been instructed in the breadth that lies under heaven? Tell me how great it is. In what place does the light dwell, or which is the place of darkness?
Can you lead me to their boundaries, or do you know their paths? Do you know, who knows, whether you were born then, and whether the number of your years is great?
Have you reached the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail? For they are stored up for the day of enemies, of tumult and of battle.
Or where does the frost come from, which spreads from the south under heaven? Tell me. Or who prepared the course for the violent rain, and the way for the wild beasts?
Who is the father of the rain, or who is it who begot the brands of light? From whose womb does the ice come forth, or the hoarfrost in the heavens?
Who begot that which comes down like flowing river water, or who silenced the mouths of the ungodly?
Have you understood the bonds of the Pleiades, or have you opened the barriers of Orion?
Or do you know the courses of heaven, or how many things have been made together under heaven?
Will you call to the clouds with your voice, and will they obey you with the trembling of much fierce water? Or will you send out thunderbolts?
Will they go and say to you, 'Here we are'? Or who gave women skill in weaving, or knowledge of embroidery?
Or who counted the clouds by number and bent the heavens down to the earth? It is spread out like the dust of the earth; I made it firm like a cube of stone.
Or will you hunt food for the lions and satisfy the appetites of the dragons? They are fearful; they lie on their beds in the forest and lie in wait.
Or who prepared food for the raven? For its young cry out to the Lord, wandering about in search of food.
Do you know the time when the wild goats give birth among the rocks, or did you watch over the labour of the deer?
And have you counted the full months of their bearing, or have you relieved their birth pangs?
In the eighteenth year King Nebuchadnezzar made an idol of gold,
sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura, in the province of the Babylonians.
And King Nebuchadnezzar sent out to gather all the princes, the governors of the provinces, the officials and the satraps, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the idol
that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up. And all the princes came and gathered together, the satraps, the officials, the governors and the great men,
who were under his authority, to come to the dedication of the idol that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up; and they stood before the king and the idol.
And the herald cried aloud: "To you I say, peoples and nations and tribes and languages: when you hear the sound of the horn and of the lyre, of the cymbal and of the harp,
of the singing together and of every kind of musical instrument, fall down and worship the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
And whoever does not fall down and worship will at that same hour be thrown into the furnace of blazing fire."
