And so, as the people heard the sound of the trumpet, of the pipe and of the lyre and of the cymbal and of the singing together and of every kind of musical instrument, all
the people, the tribes and the languages, fell down and worshipped the golden idol that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then certain Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews. They answered and said to the king: "O king, live forever!
You, O king, have issued a decree that every man who hears the sound of the trumpet and of the lyre,
of the cymbal and of the harp and of the singing together and of every kind of musical instrument, must fall down and worship the golden image;
and if anyone does not fall down and worship, he will immediately be thrown into the furnace of blazing fire.
Now there are certain Jewish men here whom you have appointed over the affairs of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.
These men have not obeyed your decree, O king; they have not served your gods, and they have not worshipped the image that you set up."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was filled with anger, and in his wrath he ordered that Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego be summoned; and these men were brought before the king.
King Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them: "Is it really true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods and do not worship the golden image that I set up?
Now if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the trumpet and of the pipe,
of the sambuca and of the harp and of the singing together and of every kind of musical instrument, to fall down and worship the golden image that I have set up, [well and good].
But if you do not worship, at that same hour you will be thrown into the furnace of blazing fire; and who is the god who will deliver you out of my hands?"
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego answered Nebuchadnezzar and said to him: "We have no need to answer you a word about this, O king, for our God is in heaven,
whom we serve, who is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire, and he will rescue us from your hands as well, O king.
But if not, let it be known to you that we do not serve your gods and we do not worship the golden idol that you have set up."
Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with great anger, and the color of his face was changed against Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and he said:
"Heat that furnace seven times over, until it is completely [?]."
And he ordered strong men to bind Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and to throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.
Then these men were bound together with their trousers and tunics, and they were thrown, bound, into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire, for the king's command was growing ever more severe,
And the furnace blazed up all the more, and the flame from around it destroyed the men who had thrown in Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, were thrown bound into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.
They walked about in the midst of the flame of the fire, singing hymns to God and blessing the Lord.
And Azariah stood up and prayed thus. He opened his mouth in the midst of the fire and said: "Blessed are you, O Lord God of our fathers, and your name is praised and glorified forever.
For you have done all this to us with justice, for you are righteous, O Lord; all your works are in truth, your ways are upright, and all your judgment is righteous.
You have sent a righteous punishment upon us for everything that you have sent upon us,
and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem. Truly, in righteousness you have sent all this upon us today because of our sins.
For we have sinned against you; we have become lawless in everything and have turned away from you; we have sinned in all things.
We did not listen to your commandments; we did not keep them, nor did we do as you commanded us, so that it might go well with us from you.
Now all that you have sent upon us, and all that you have done to us, you have done by a righteous judgment.
You have handed us over into the hands of our enemies, lawless, harsh apostates, and into the hands of a lawless king, the most wicked in all the earth; you have handed us over.
And now there is no occasion for us to open our mouths, for shame and reproach have come upon your servants and those who worship you.
Do not hand us over completely, for your name's sake. Do not cancel your covenant,
And do not take your mercy away from me, for the sake of Abraham your beloved, Isaac your servant, and Israel your holy one,
to whom you spoke and said: 'I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore.'
Now, O Lord, we have become fewer than all the nations, and we are brought low in all the earth today because of our sins.
At this time there is no prince, prophet or leader, no burnt offerings of sacrifices, no incense,
no place of sacrifice to make an offering before you and to find mercy. But with a humbled head and a spirit of lowliness
may we be offered up like burnt offerings of sacrifices of rams, and like tens of thousands of fattened lambs.
So let this our sacrifice be offered before you today, so that we may be perfect in following you, and so that none of those who trust in you may be put to shame.
Now we follow you with all our heart; we fear you; we seek your face, O Lord.
Do not put us to shame, but deal with us mercifully in your kindness and in your great mercy.
Deliver us by your wonders, and glorify your name, O Lord,
so that all who do evil to your servants may be put to shame. Let their tyrannies be disgraced, and let all their strength be crushed.
And let them understand that you alone are the Lord God, exalted and glorious over all the world."
And the king's servants who had thrown the three youths into the burning furnace did not stop.
They kept the furnace burning with naphtha, pitch, tow and vine cuttings. The flame went up and rose forty-nine cubits above the furnace.
It came out, spread around, and burned up all the Chaldeans it found around the furnace.
At that time the angel of the Lord came down among Azariah and his companions and scattered the flame out of the fiery furnace.
Inside the furnace of fire and flame, he made something like a dewy wind, a breeze. The fire did not touch them at all. It did not trouble them, and it did them no harm at all.
Then all three youths sang as if with one mouth. In the furnace they blessed and glorified God, saying:
Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers. You are praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed is the holy name of your glory. It is praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in the holy temple of your glory. You are praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you who sit upon the cherubim and look into the depths. You are praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you upon the thrones of your kingdom. You are praised, glorified and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in the firmament, in the heaven of heavens. You are praised, blessed, glorified and exalted above all forever.
Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord. Bless the Lord, you heavens and angels of the Lord.
Bless the Lord, all you waters above, you heavenly powers of the Lord. Bless the Lord, sun and moon and stars of heaven.
Bless the Lord, rain and dew and all you winds. Bless the Lord, fire and heat, nights and days.
Bless the Lord, light and darkness, cold and warmth. Bless the Lord, frost and snow, lightnings and clouds.
Bless the Lord, O earth, you mountains and hills. Bless the Lord, every plant of the earth, the sea and the rivers.
Bless the Lord, you springs, you sea monsters, and everything that moves in the waters. Bless the Lord, you birds of the sky, wild beasts and all cattle.
Bless the Lord, you children of men, O Israel. Bless the Lord, you priests of the Lord, you servants of the Lord.
Bless the Lord, you spirits and souls of the righteous, you who are worthy and humble of heart. Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael,
for he has rescued us from hell and saved us from the hands of death. He has brought us out of the burning furnace and rescued us from the fire.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
When Nebuchadnezzar heard their song, he was amazed. He came quickly to the door of the furnace and said:
"Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out of that furnace and come to me!"
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego came out of the fire and came to him.
The [?] (literally "countries" or "villages"), the marzbans (governors), the commanders, and all the king's rulers and rich men gathered to see those men,
For the fire had no power over them at all. The hair of their heads was not singed, their garments did not change colour, and there was no smell of fire on them at all.
Nebuchadnezzar began to speak and said: "Blessed is the Lord, the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego,
who sent his angel and delivered his servants, because they trusted in him and treated the king's command with contempt.
They gave themselves up to the fire so that they would not serve a foreign worship or bow down to any other object of fear, but only to their own God.
Now I publicly lay down this decree: that every people and every race, of every kindred, and every tongue
that dares to speak a blasphemous word against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego shall be given over to destruction, and their houses shall be given over to plunder.
For no other god is able to show such power as he did when he delivered these men."
From then on the king honoured Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the land of the Babylonians. He raised them up and blessed them,
so that they would be rulers over all the Jews who were in all his lands.

I make known to you, brothers, the gospel that I preached to you, which you also received and in which you stand,

yet not I, but his grace that was with me. So whether it was they or I, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.

On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came early in the morning,
while it was still dark, to the tomb. She ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said to them:
"They have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him." Peter and the other disciple went out and came to the tomb.
The two of them ran together. But the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and came to the tomb first.
He looked down into the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
Simon Peter also came after him, went into the tomb, and saw the linen cloths lying there, and the face-cloth
that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths but folded up by itself in one place.
And the disciples went back again to their own homes. But Mary stood outside the tomb, weeping. And as she wept, she looked down into the tomb,
and she saw two angels clothed in white, sitting one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of the Lord Jesus had lain.
And the angels said to her: "Woman, why are you weeping? Or whom are you seeking?" And she said to them: "They have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him."
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus. Jesus said to her: "Woman, why are you weeping? Or whom are you seeking?"
She thought that he was the gardener, and she said to him: "Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, so that I may take him away."
Jesus said to her: "Mary!" She turned around and said to him in Hebrew: "Rabbi!" which means Teacher, and she ran to meet him.
Jesus said to her: "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. Go and tell my brothers:
I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."
Mary Magdalene came to tell his disciples that she had seen the Lord and that he had said these things to her.

And when there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them: Men, brothers!
You yourselves know that from the first days God chose me from among you, so that the Gentiles would hear the word of the gospel from my mouth and believe.
And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving the Holy Spirit to the apostles, just as to us.
And he made no distinction between us and them; he purified their hearts by faith. So now why are you testing God by putting a yoke on the neck of the disciples,
which not even our fathers were able to bear? But we believe through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Do not speak evil
of one another, my brothers. Whoever speaks evil of a brother or judges a brother condemns the law. And if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you to judge your neighbor?
Now you too, who say: Today or tomorrow let us go to such-and-such a city, spend a year there and trade,
you who do not know what tomorrow will bring: what is your life worth? You are like smoke, which lasts a little while and then vanishes.
Therefore what you ought to say is: If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.
But now you boast in your arrogance; all such boasting is evil. Whoever knows the good thing to do and does not do it, for him it is sin.
And now you too, you rich, weep and wail over the miseries that are coming upon you. Your wealth has rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes.
Your gold and your silver have rusted, and their rust will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire.
You have stored up treasure for the last days. Behold, the wages of the laborers who threshed your field

Then he went out to Tarsus to look for Saul, and he found him and brought him, and they came to Antioch.
And they were there for a whole year, gathering the church and teaching that great multitude, and it was in Antioch that the disciples were first given the name of Christians.
In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and foretold through the Holy Spirit that there would be a severe famine over the whole world. This happened in the days of Claudius Caesar.
And the disciples decided that each one of them, as he was able, would send help to the brothers
who lived in Judea. This they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Paul.
Rejoice with joy:
And since all these things are going to be dissolved in this way, what kind of people ought you to be? People of holy conduct, good works and service.
Wait for and hasten the coming of the day of God, when the burning heavens will be dissolved, and the elements will burn up and melt.
As he promised, we wait for new heavens and a new earth, where abundance [?] dwells.
Be exalted, O Lord, in your strength.
If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true.
There is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.
You sent to John, and he testified to the truth. But I have not received testimony from a man; I say this so that you may be saved.
He was a burning and shining lamp, and for a time you were willing to rejoice in his light.
But I have a testimony greater than John's, for I have accomplished the work that the Father gave me, and these works testify about me,
that the Father has sent me. And the Father who sent me has testified about me. You have never heard his voice, nor have you seen his form.
And his word does not abide among you, for you do not believe the one whom he sent.
Search the scriptures, for you think in yourselves that you have eternal life in them, and it is they that testify about me.
And you do not want to come to me so that you may have life. I have not received glory from men.
But I know that you do not have the love of God in yourselves.
I have come in the name of my Father, and you did not receive me. If another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
How then can you believe, you who receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you have set your hope.
If you had believed Moses, you would have believed me also, for he wrote about me.
If you do not believe his writings, believe my words!
Jesus said to them again: I am going away, and you will look for me, and you will die in your sins. Where I am going, you cannot come.
The Jews said to one another: Is he perhaps going to kill himself, since he says, 'Where I am going, you cannot come'?
And he said to them: You are of the earth, but I am from heaven. You are of this world, but I am not of this world.
I have told you that you will die in your sins. If you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.
They said to him: Who are you? Jesus said to them: First of all, what I am telling you.
I have many things to say about you and to judge, but the one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, that I speak in the world.
They did not understand that he was speaking to them about his Father. Jesus said to them again:
When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but I speak as the Father taught me.
And the one who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, for I always do what pleases him. As he was saying these things to them, many believed in him.
From you comes my praise; I will fulfil my vows.
Paul stood up, motioned with his hand for them to be silent, and said: "Men of Israel, you who fear God, listen to me!
The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and raised up the people during their stay as sojourners in the land of Egypt, and with a mighty hand he brought them out of there.
For a period of forty years he nourished them in the wilderness. He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave them their land as an inheritance.
This took about four hundred and fifty years. After that he gave them judges until the days of Samuel the prophet.
From then on they asked for a king, and he gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin; he reigned for about forty years.
God removed him and raised up David to be their king, about whom he himself bore witness and said:
'I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who will do and carry out all the will of my heart.'
From this man's descendants God, according to his promise, raised up for Israel a Saviour, Jesus,
before whose coming John the Baptist proclaimed in advance a baptism of repentance to all Israel.
As John was completing his course, he said to them:
'Whoever you suppose me to be, I am not he. But behold, one is coming after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.'
Men and brothers, children of the race of Abraham, and those among you who fear God: to you the word of life has been sent.
For those who live in Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognise this, and the voices of the prophets,
which are read out every Sabbath, they fulfilled by condemning him. Although they found no cause for death, they then asked Pilate to have him killed.
When they had carried out everything that had been written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead. For many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses to the people.
And we bring you the good news of the gift that he promised to your fathers: he has raised up Jesus for us,
as it is written in the second psalm: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you.'
And because he raised him from the dead, never again to return to corruption, he spoke in this way:
'I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.' Therefore he also says in another place: 'You will not let your Holy One see corruption.'
For David served his own generation and, by the will of God, was gathered to his fathers; he fell asleep with them and saw corruption.
But the one whom God raised up did not see corruption.
Let it be known to you, then, that through this man forgiveness of your sins is proclaimed to you."
Paul stayed there for many days. Then he took leave of the brothers and sailed for Syria, and Priscilla and Aquila were with him.
He had his hair cut at Cenchreae, because he had taken a vow. He arrived at Ephesus and left them there. He himself went into the synagogue [?] and spoke with the Jews.
When they begged him to stay there, he would not, but parted from them and said, "I will come again, by the will of God"; and he boarded a ship from Ephesus.
And he went down to Caesarea, went up and greeted the church, and went to Antioch. And he spent some time there and departed.
[?] in the synagogue. Aquila and Priscilla heard him, and they took him and explained the way of God to him more accurately.
And as he intended to cross over to Achaia, the brethren urged him on and wrote to the disciples to receive him;
he came and greatly helped the believers by grace [?] [?] he refuted the Jews before the people [and showed] from the Scriptures [?]
Purify yourselves; be watchful in prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another fervent, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each one has received grace from God, so let them serve one another, as good stewards of the manifold gift of God.
Whoever speaks, let it be as with the words of God; whoever serves, let it be as from the strength that God supplies,
so that in this the Lord may be glorified through Christ Jesus, to whom belong the power and the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
The kingdom is the Lord's:
On the next day the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea knew that there had been no other boat there
except one only, which his disciples had entered, and that Jesus had not gone into the boat with the disciples, but his disciples had gone in alone.
And other boats also came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread which the Lord had blessed, giving thanks.
When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they brought up the boat and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
And they found him on the other side of the sea and said to him, "Rabbi, when did you come here?" Jesus answered and said to them, "Amen, amen, I say to you:
you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
Do not labour for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for on him the Father, God, has set his seal."
They said to him, "What shall we do, so that we may do the work of God?" Jesus answered and said to them, "This is the work of God: that you believe in him whom the Father has sent."
And they said to him, "What sign do you perform, so that we may see it and believe you?
Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
Jesus said to them, "Amen, amen, I say to you: it was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven, but my Father has given you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is that which came down from heaven and gave life to the world." They said to him, "Lord, give us this bread always."
Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst.
But I told you that you have seen me and do not believe. All that the Father gives me will come to me; and whoever comes to me I will not cast out.
For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
For this is the will of my Father who sent me: that of all whom the Father has given me I should lose none of them, but should raise him up on the last day.
For this is the will of my Father: that whoever sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
Praise befits you, O God: hear [?], O God, the prayer.
The high priest rose up, and all who were with him, which was the sect of the Sadducees,
and they were filled with jealousy, and they laid their hands on the apostles and put them in prison, intending to keep them until the next day.
But an angel opened the doors of the prison at night and brought them out and said to them: Go, stand, and speak to the people in the temple
all the words of this life. And when they heard this, they went into the temple at the very break of dawn and were teaching the people.
Then the high priests came, and all who were with him, and they called together the council and the elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have the apostles brought.
But when the servants went, they did not find them in the prison; they returned and told them:
We found the prison secured with all care and the guards standing before the doors of the prison; but when we opened it, we found no one inside.
And when the captain of the temple and the high priests heard these words, they deliberated about them, as to what this might come to.
Someone came and told them: The men whom you put in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people.
Then the captain went with the servants and brought them, not by force, for he feared the people, lest they stone them.
He brought them and set them in the midst of the council. The high priest questioned them and said: We strictly commanded you not to teach in this name.
And now, behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring upon us the blood of this righteous one.
Peter answered and said: One must obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, on whom you laid hands and whom you hanged on a tree.
Him God has exalted by his right hand as Leader and Savior for us, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
And we are witnesses of these words of his, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who fear him.
Therefore gird up the loins of your mind, be watchful, and set your hope fully on the grace that is coming to their [?] at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, do not be conformed to the desires of your former ignorance,
but, like the Holy One who called you, you too be holy in all your conduct. For it is written: Be holy, for I am holy.
2 And if you call on him as Father who judges each one's work impartially, spend the time of your sojourning in fear.
Know that it was not with perishable silver or gold that you were redeemed from the futile way of life handed down from your fathers.
but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, who was foreknown before the creation of the world and was revealed in the last days for your sake,
you who believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith may be in God.
Purify your souls by obedience and by truth. For the sake of brotherly love, be sincere in heart, and love one another earnestly,
for you have been born a second time, not of corruptible seed, but by the incorruptible and eternal word of God.
For all flesh is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the grass: the grass has withered, and its flower has fallen.
but the word of the Lord abides forever.
O Lord, by your strength:
Now he had to pass through Samaria.
And he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of land that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
And Jacob's well was there. Jesus, tired from the journey, was sitting by the well.
It was about the sixth hour. And a Samaritan woman came to draw water.
Jesus said to her, "Give me water." His disciples had gone into the city to buy food.
The Samaritan woman said to him, "How is it that you, a Jew, ask water of me, a Samaritan woman?"
For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans. Jesus answered and said to her, "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you,
'Give me water to drink,' you would have asked him for water, and he would have given you living water."
The woman said, "Lord, you have nothing to draw with, and this well is deep. Where do you get the water of life?
Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well? He himself drank from it, and his sons and his flocks."
Jesus answered and said to her, "Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again.
But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst; rather, it will become in him a spring of water flowing to eternal life."
The woman said, "Lord, give me this water, so that I may not thirst and may not come here to draw."
Jesus said to her, "Go, call your husband and come here." The woman answered and said, "I have no husband." Jesus said to her,
"You have said well that you have no husband, for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband. What you have said is true."
The woman said, "Lord, I see that you are a prophet.
Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that Jerusalem is the place where one ought to worship."
Jesus said to her, "Believe me, woman, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.
But the hour is coming, and is already here, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father seeks such as these to be his worshippers.
God is spirit, and his worshippers must worship in spirit and in truth.
The woman said to him: "I know that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything."
Jesus said to her: "I am he, who am speaking to you." And just at this word his disciples came, and they were amazed that he was speaking with a woman.
And no one said to him: "What are you seeking?" or "Why are you speaking with her?" And the woman left her water jar.
She went into the town and said to the people: "Come and see a man who told me everything that I have done. Could this be the Christ?"
They came out of the town and came to him. And at just this word his disciples were speaking to him and said: "Rabbi, eat!"
But he said to them: "I have food that you do not know about." The disciples said to one another: "Has someone brought him food?"
Jesus said to them: "My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to complete his work.
Do you not say: 'There are still four months, and the harvest comes'?
Look, I tell you: lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they are already white for harvest.
And the reaper receives wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together with him.
For in this the saying is true: one is the one who sowed, another is the reaper.
I sent you to reap that for which you did not labor; others have labored, and you have entered into their labor."
And many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the word of the woman, for she testified: "He told me everything that I have done."
And when the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them. And he stayed there two days.
And they said to the woman: "We no longer believe because of your word, for we ourselves have heard from him that this is truly the Savior of the world."
I shall not be afraid: turn my soul back to me.
And there in Lystra was a man, powerless in his feet and lame from his mother's womb; he sat there, and he had never walked.
He heard the words that Paul was speaking. When Paul looked at him and saw that he had faith to be saved, he said to him with a loud voice:
"I tell you, man, in the name of Jesus Christ: stand upright on your feet!"
And he stood up and began to walk. And when the crowd saw what Paul had done, they raised their voices in the Lycaonian language and said:
"The gods have become like men and have come down to us." And they called Barnabas the god Zeus, and Paul Hermes, for Paul was the leader in speaking.
And the priest of the god Zeus, for he was the ruler of that city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates of the city with the crowd and wanted to offer sacrifice.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out and saying: "Men, why are you doing this?"
For we too are only men, like you, and we bring you good news, so that you may turn from these vain things to the living God,
who made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything that is in it.
Beloved, do not be astonished at the fiery ordeal among you, which comes upon you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
But insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that at the revealing of his glory you may also rejoice and be glad.
If you are reproached [?] for the name of the Lord, you are blessed, for the Spirit of God is glorified and rests upon you.
Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as a meddler in other people's affairs.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in that name.
For it is the time for judgment to begin first with the house of God; and if it begins first with us,
what will be the end of those who disobey the gospel of God? If the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner be found?
Therefore let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to the faithful Creator by doing good.
for us to dwell in the house.
After two days he went from there to Galilee.
For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honour in his own country.
And when he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, because they had seen everything he had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they too had gone to the feast.
So Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water into wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum.
When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come and heal his son, for he was close to death.
Jesus said to him, "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe."
The royal official said to him, "Lord, come before the child dies."
Jesus said to him, "Go; your son lives." And the man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went away.
And as he was going down, his servants met him and told him, saying, "Your son lives."
He asked them at what hour he had begun to get better. They said to him, "Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him."
And the father of the child remembered that it was at that hour that Jesus had said to him, "Your son lives."
And he believed, and all his household. This again was the second sign that Jesus did when he had come from Judea to Galilee.
The blameless and the upright: my eyes are ever toward the Lord:
who in past generations allowed all the nations to walk in the ways of their own will.
And he did not leave his beneficence without witness, giving you rain from heaven at every season and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.
And when they had said this, they barely restrained the people from sacrificing to them, and [made them] go each to his own home. While they were still staying there and teaching,
the Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, spoke to them openly, and turned the people away from them. They said:
"They say nothing true, only lies." And they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking that he was dead.
The disciples came and gathered around him. He got up and went into the city. And the next day he went out with Barnabas, and they came to Derbe.
And they preached the gospel in that city and made many disciples, and they returned to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch,
strengthening the hearts of the disciples and urging them to stand firm in the faith, and [saying]:

I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder, one who has laboured in the sufferings of Christ, and a sharer in the glory that is to be revealed:
shepherd the flock of God that is among you, and take care of it among you, not under compulsion,
but by the will of God; not for shameful gain, but eagerly; and not lording it over [others] as over the priests,
but be examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
The Lord is the strength of those who fear him.
After this Jesus and the disciples came.
Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem, for the Lord has strengthened...
On the first day of the week we were gathered to bless the bread,
and Paul was speaking the word of teaching, because he was to leave the next day, and he went on speaking until midnight.
There were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered. A young man named Eutychus was sitting at the window,
and as he was overcome by deep sleep during Paul's speech, he fell down while asleep, dropped from the third storey to the ground, and lay dead.
Paul went down, threw himself on him, embraced him, and said: "Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him."
He got up at once, blessed the bread and ate, and talked for a long time until dawn, and then he left.
And they brought the boy in alive and were greatly comforted.
But we went ahead by ship and went up to Assos. From there we meant to take Paul on board, because that is what he had ordered, since he was going to come on foot.
When he came to us at Assos, we took him on board and came to Mitylene.
And from there we sailed on by ship the next day and arrived opposite Keron [Chios?]. In the evening we came to Salmon [Samos?], and the next day we came to Miletus.
Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he would not spend much time in Asia, for he was hurrying to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost, if it were possible for him.
And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called the elders of the church.
When they came to him, he said to them: "You know how I was with you the whole time, from the first day I came into Asia,
serving the Lord the whole time with tears, and through the trials that came upon me from the plots of the Jews;
how I held back nothing that was good for you, but told it to you and taught you before the people and in the house,
testifying to you, both Jews and Gentiles, of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ."
Put away all malice and all deceit, hypocrisy, envy and every [evil] thought,
and like newborn infants, long for that pure milk, so that by it you may grow up to eternal life, if you have tasted that the Lord is good.
Come to him, the living stone, who was rejected by people but chosen and precious to God.
And you also, as living stones, are being built up into a spiritual house, divine and holy, to offer spiritual sacrifices pleasing to God through Jesus.
For it is written in the scripture: "Behold, I lay in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame."
So the honor is for you who believe. But for those who do not believe, the stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner, and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.
They stumble because they disobey the word, as they were appointed to do.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy seed, a people acquired for God, so that you may proclaim the virtues
of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light. Once you were not God's people, but now you are the people of God. Once you had not received favor, but now you have received mercy.
When the feast was already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and began to teach.
The Jews were amazed and said: "How does this man know the scriptures without having been taught?"
Jesus answered them: "My teaching is not mine, but belongs to the one who sent me.
Anyone who does his will shall know whether this teaching is from God or whether I speak on my own.
Whoever speaks on his own seeks his own glory. But whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no falsehood in him."
Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why do you seek to kill me?
The crowd answered him: "You have a demon! Who is trying to kill you?" Jesus answered them: "I did one deed, and you are all amazed.
For this reason Moses gave you circumcision. It is not actually from Moses but from the fathers, and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken, why are you blaming me for making a man completely well on the Sabbath?
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment." Some of the people of Jerusalem said: "Is this not the man they were trying to kill?
Look, he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers really know that this is the Christ?"
But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from." Jesus cried out in the temple,
teaching and saying to them: "You both know me and know where I am from; and I have not come of myself, but the one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.
I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me."
Lord, I have loved the beauty [of your house]: my feet have stood on level ground.

and from there they sailed away and came to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God, strengthened for the work which they had now completed.

Likewise, you young men, submit to your elders;
all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, for God crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.

I am the bread of life that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever.

Jesus said to them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves.
But whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him.
And just as the living Father sent me, and I live with the Father, so whoever eats of me will also live through me.
For this is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like the manna your fathers ate and died.

The Lord is the strength of his people: blessed be the Lord, for he has heard.
Be alert and stay awake: I believe that I shall see the goodness of the Lord.
After this Jesus went about in Galilee and did not want to go into Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.
The feast of the Jews, which is Tabernacles, was near, and his brothers said to him:
Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works you are doing.
For no one does anything in secret if he wants to be known publicly. If you do these things, show yourself to the world.
For not even his brothers believed in him. Jesus said to them: "My time has not yet come;
the world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
You go up to the feast; I am not going up to this feast, because the time has not yet been fulfilled." He said this to them and stayed in Galilee.
And his brothers went up to the feast, and then he himself also went up, not openly but in secret.
The Jews were looking for him at the feast and saying, "Where is he?" And there was much murmuring about him among the people.
Some said, "He is a good man"; but others said, "No, he is leading the people astray."
Yet no one spoke about him openly, for fear of the Jews.
Love the Lord, all [?]. Let [them] be courageous and steadfast [?]:
After some days Paul said to Barnabas:
"Let us go back and visit the brothers in every city where we preached the word of the Lord, and see how they are doing."
Barnabas wanted to take John, who was called Mark, along with them.
But Paul insisted that they should not take along the one who had once left them, the first time, in Pamphylia, and had not gone with them to the work.
So there was a sharp disagreement between them, to the point that they parted from each other. Barnabas took Mark along and sailed off to Cyprus;
but Paul chose Silas, and he too set out from there, by the grace of God, from the brothers.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches. He came to Derbe and Lystra.
There was a certain disciple there named Timothy, the son of a Jewish woman who was a believer and of a Gentile father. He was well spoken of by the brothers at Lystra and Iconium.
Paul wanted him to go out with him. He took him and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they knew that his father was a Gentile.
As they went through the cities, they taught them to keep the law decided by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew in number day by day.
Through Silvanus, your faithful brother, as I consider him, I have written to you briefly,
urging you and bearing witness that I hold this to be the true grace in which you stand.
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be with all of you who are in Christ Jesus.
Rejoice with joy; rejoice in the Lord, you righteous.
The Jews began to murmur about him, because he said:
"I am the bread that came down from heaven." And they said: "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father we know?
How then does he now say, 'I came down from heaven'?" Jesus answered and said to them: "Do not murmur among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless the one who sent me brings him to me. And I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: 'They shall all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned will come to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who was with God; he has seen the Father.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life. I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died. This is the bread that came down from heaven: if anyone eats of it, he will not die.
I am the bread of life that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this, he will live forever."
Praise befits you; hear [?]:
Peter opened his mouth and said: "Truly I know this, that there is no partiality before God.
But among all nations, whoever fears him and does righteousness is acceptable to him.
The word that he sent to the children of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace — he himself is Lord of all. You yourselves know the word
that was throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John preached;
about Jesus of Nazareth, whom the Lord anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power, who came and lived among us,
doing good and healing the sick, freeing those oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
And we are witnesses of all the things that he did in the land of Judea and in the city of Jerusalem; whom they killed and hanged on a tree.
God raised him on the third day and granted that he be made manifest,
not to all the people, but to the chosen witnesses, the saints of God — that is, to us, who ate and drank with him after his resurrection from the dead.
And he commanded us to preach among the people and to testify that he himself is the chosen one of God, judge of the living and the dead.
To him all the prophets bear witness, that all who believe in him receive forgiveness of sins through the name of the Father."
Beloved, [?] for this reason,
for Christ also suffered for you and left you an example, so that you should follow in his steps. He committed no sin,
nor was deceit found in his mouth. When he was reviled, he reviled no one; he was handed over to a judge falsely.
He himself bore our sins in his own flesh on the tree, so that we might be set free from sin and live by righteousness. By his wounds we have been healed.
For we were like sheep gone astray, but now you have turned back to the shepherd and teacher of our souls.
When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
As was his custom, Paul went in to them. He chose three Sabbath readings from the Scriptures for them, and he explained them and set before them
that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and that "this is the Christ whom I proclaim to you."
Some of them believed and joined Paul and Silas, along with a great multitude of the God-fearing Gentiles and a few women.
But the Jews became jealous. They brought in some wicked men from the marketplace, gathered a crowd and stirred up an uproar in the city.
They attacked the house of Jason, looking for them so they could bring them out before the people.
When they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the rulers of the city, shouting:
"These men who have stirred up the whole world have come here too, and Jason has taken them in."
"And all of them act against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."
With these words they stirred up the people and the city authorities, until they took security from Jason. Only then did they let them go.
Know this first of all: no prophecy is a matter of one's own interpretation.
For prophecy never came by human will. Rather, the holy men of God spoke beforehand by the Holy Spirit.
There were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will bring in destructive heresies,
and they will deny the Lord who set them free, bringing swift destruction on themselves.
Many will follow their impurity, and because of them the way of truth will be reviled.
In their greed they will exploit you with deceitful words. Their judgment, pronounced long ago, is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.
For God did not spare the angels who went astray. He bound them in chains of darkness and handed them over to judgment, to be kept for punishment.
He did not spare the ancient world either. He preserved Noah, the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, and brought the flood on the world of the ungodly.
He overthrew the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, condemned them and made them an example for those who would come after. And righteous Lot, who was distressed by the filthy conduct of the lawless,
he rescued. For while that righteous man lived among them, his righteous soul was tormented day after day by the lawless deeds he saw and heard.
"You know me, and you know where I come from. And I have not come on my own [?] where I come from."
"I have not come on my own. The one who sent me is true, and you do not know him."
"But I know him, because I come from him, and he sent me." They tried to seize him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
And many of the people believed in him. And they said, "When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than this man has done?"
And the Pharisees heard the people murmuring about him. And the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.
and Jesus said: I am with you a little while longer, and then I go to the one who sent me.

They said to one another, "Where does he intend to go, that we will not find him?
Does he intend to go to those dispersed among the Gentiles, and to teach the Gentiles there?
What is this word that he says, 'You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you are able [?] to come'?"

When the Jews of Thessalonica learned
that the word of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Beroea as well, they came and began to stir up the people there too.
Immediately the brothers brought Paul out and sent him off toward the sea; Silas and Timothy stayed there.
Those who were escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens;
and they received a command from Paul for Silas and Timothy to come to him quickly, and they departed.
While he was waiting for them in the city of Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city given over to idolatry.
He spoke continually in the synagogue of the Jews and with those who worshipped, and in the marketplace every day.
Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers debated with him; and some said, "What does this babbler want to say?"
Others said, "This man seems to be a proclaimer of foreign demons," because he was preaching to them the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
Now the multitude of those who believed were of one heart and mind; and no one said that any of his possessions was his own, but their possessions were held in common.
And with great power the apostles gave testimony to the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. And great grace was upon them all.
And no one among them was in need; those who were owners of [?] and estates sold them, and brought the price of what they had sold,
and laid it at the apostles' feet. And it was distributed to each person according to what each needed.
Now the one who was called Barnabas by the apostles, which is translated "son of consolation," a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the false under punishment for the day of judgment,
especially those who follow after the flesh in the lust of defilement and despise authority. Bold, they do not tremble, but blaspheme.
But these, like irrational beasts of the flock, born by nature to be slaughtered, blaspheme what they do not know, and they will be destroyed in their own corruption.
And they will receive the wages of their falsehood. They have counted lust as a day of pleasure;
defiled and filthy, they revel in their love-feasts and feast together with you.
They have eyes full of adultery and of unceasing sin; they entice unstable souls; they have hearts trained in greed. They are children of a curse.
They have left the straight way and gone astray. They have followed the way of Balaam of Bosor, who loved the wages of falsehood,
but he was rebuked for his own lawlessness: a dumb donkey speaking with a human voice held back the prophet's madness.
These are waterless springs and mists [?] driven about by the wind, for whom the gloom of darkness is reserved.
For they speak excessive vanity, and through the lusts of the flesh they drive into filthiness those who had barely escaped from the error of [their] way of life.
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved.
For if those who had escaped the defilements of this world through the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ are again entangled in the same things,
it would have been better for them never to have known the way of truth than to know it and turn back.
What has happened to them is just as the true proverb says: The dog has returned to its own vomit, and the sow has washed only to wallow in the mire.
This, beloved, is now the second letter I have written to you, and by it I stir up your better [?] mind with this reminder.
Remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the commandments of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ given through your apostles.
I will confess you, O Lord, in the church.
The officers came back to the chief priests and Pharisees, who said to them:
"Why did you not bring him?" The officers answered them: "Never has anyone spoken like this man."
The Pharisees answered them: "Have you been led astray too? Has any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in him?
But this crowd, which does not know the law, is accursed." Nicodemus, who had come to him earlier and was one of them, said to them:
"Does our law judge a man without first hearing from him and learning what he is doing?"
They answered him: "Are you a Galilean too? Search and see: no prophet has arisen from Galilee."
Then Jesus spoke to them again and said: "I am the light of the world.
Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life."
Lord, your mercy is in heaven; your righteousness is like the mountains.
After this Paul left the Athenians and came to Corinth.
There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had only recently come from Italy,
and Priscilla his wife, for Claudius Caesar had commanded all the Jews to leave Rome; and he came to them.
Because they had the same trade, he stayed with them and they worked together, for they were tentmakers by trade.
And every Sabbath he spoke in the synagogue and tried to persuade Jews and Gentiles.
When Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, the Spirit pressed Paul, and he testified to the Jews that the Christ is Jesus.
Know this first: in the last days many scoffers will come with scoffing, following their own desires.
And they will say: "Where is the promise of his coming? Ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything has remained as it was from the beginning of creation."
For they deliberately forget that the heavens existed long ago, and that the earth was formed out of water by the word of God.
Through these the world of that time was destroyed by a flood of water.
But now the heavens and the earth are stored up by the same word, kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly people.
Jesus said to them again:
"I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins. Where I am going, you cannot come."
The Jews said to one another: "Is he going to kill himself, since he says, 'Where I am going, you cannot come'?"
And he said to them: "You are from the earth, but I am from heaven. You are from this world, but I am not from this world."
"I told you that you will die in your sins. If you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sins."
They said to him: "Who are you?" Jesus said to them: "First, that which I am telling you."
"I have many things to say about you and to judge, that he who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, that is what I say in the world."
They did not understand that he was speaking to them about his Father. Jesus said to them again:
"When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but speak as he taught me." And Jesus said:
"I have come into this world for judgment, so that those who did not see may see, and those who saw may become blind."
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this, and they said to him: "Are we blind too?"
"The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out."
"And when he has brought out all his own, he walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice."
"But they will not follow a stranger. Instead they run away from him, because they do not know the stranger's voice."
Jesus told them this parable, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
So Jesus said to them again: "Amen, amen, I say to you, I am the gate for the sheep."
"All who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them."
I am the door: if anyone enters through me, he will be saved. He will go in and go out, and will find pasture.
But the thief does not come for nothing; he comes only to steal, to slaughter and to destroy.
But I have come so that they may have life, and have it more abundantly.
And it happened there that they found [?]
one woman, a disciple [?]. This became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ,
to you, who have been granted a faith of equal honour through the righteousness of God and of the Saviour Jesus Christ:
Grace to you; may peace be multiplied through the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ!
Through the knowledge of him, he has given us the power of his own divinity for life and for godliness.
He has called us to his own glory and virtue. Through these he has given us very great and precious promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature,
having escaped the corruption of the lust of this world. So make this same effort yourselves, and to your faith add virtue;
to virtue add knowledge; to knowledge, abstinence (fasting); to abstinence, endurance; to endurance, godliness;
to godliness add brotherly love; and to brotherly love, love.
When these things are with you and abound, you will be found neither idle nor fruitless at the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Whoever does not have these things is blind; he sees an insect [?] as a shadow, for he has forgotten that he was cleansed of his former sins.
Therefore, brothers, be all the more eager to make this calling of yours firm through good deeds.
Do this, and you will never stumble. In this way you will be richly granted entry into the eternal kingdom of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Lay hold of all the nations.
Then Peter came to Jesus and said to him:
"Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?"
Jesus said to him: "I do not tell you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven."
"Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
As he began the settlement, they brought before him a man who owed ten thousand talents.
Since he had nothing to pay with, his lord ordered that he be sold, with his wife and children and everything he had, and that the debt be paid.
The servant fell down and bowed before him, saying to him: 'Be patient with me, and I will pay you everything.'
The lord had mercy on that servant and released him, and he forgave him the debt.
And when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He seized him and began choking him, saying to him: "Give me what you owe me."
That fellow servant of his [?] and begged him, saying to him: "Be patient with me, and I will pay you."
But he would not listen to him. Instead he treated him even more harshly and threw him into prison until he should pay him the debt.
When his fellow servants saw this, they were deeply distressed, and they went and told their lord all that had happened.
Then his lord called him and said to him: "You wicked and foolish servant, I forgave you all your debt because you begged me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?"
And his lord was angry with him and handed him over to the torturers until he should pay back all his debt.
So also my heavenly Father will do to you if each of you does not forgive your brothers.
For we shall pass through the place of the wondrous dwellings, with the sound of songs of praise.
After those days we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.
Some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us, and they brought along the man we were to stay with, Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple.
When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us gladly. On the next day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders came.
He greeted them and told them one by one what God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
When they heard this, they glorified God and said to Paul: "You see, brother, how many tens of thousands of believers there are among the Jews, and all of them are faithful to the law.
Some people are saying about you that you teach the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn away from Moses, and that you tell them
not to circumcise their children and not to live by the customs. What, then, is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.
Do what we tell you: there are four men among us who have taken a vow on themselves.

Take them along and purify yourself with them, so that they may shave their heads. Then everyone will know that what they say about you is nothing, and that you yourself also live by the law and keep it.
As for the Gentile believers, we have written and instructed them that they need not keep anything of the kind, except that they should abstain from what is slaughtered to idols,
for the offering was offered for each one of them.
Therefore, beloved,
since you are waiting for this, be eager to be found at peace, undefiled and blameless, and regard the patience of the Lord as salvation,
just as my beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
as he does in all his letters when he speaks of this. In them there are some things that are hard to understand,
which the unlearned and unstable twist, as they do the other books, to their own destruction.
But you, brothers, knowing this beforehand, be on your guard, so that you are not carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your own steadfastness,
but grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The Lord of hosts is with us, our helper:
And the Lord said to those Jews who believed in him:
"If you abide in my words, you are truly my disciples. And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
They said to him, "We are descendants of Abraham and have never been slaves to anyone. How is it that you say, 'You will be set free'?"
Jesus answered and said, "Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
And the slave does not remain in the house forever. But you seek to kill me, because my word finds no room among you.
What I have seen with the Father, that I speak; and what you hear from your father, that you do." They answered and said to him, "Our father is Abraham."
Jesus answered and said to them, "If you were children of Abraham, you would be doing the works of Abraham.
But now you seek to kill me." They said to him, "We were not born of fornication; we know one Father: God."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came forth from God. I have not come of my own accord, but he sent me. Why do you not understand these words?
You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desire of your father; for there is no truth in him.
When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own heart, for his father too was a liar. But I tell you the truth, and you do not believe."
The Jews answered and said to him, "Did we not say rightly that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
Jesus answered them and said, "I do not have a demon; rather, I honor my Father, and you dishonor me. But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges.
Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death."
Those Jews said to him, "Now we know that you are possessed by a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets, and you say:
'If anyone keeps my words, he will never taste death.'
Are you perhaps greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets perished."
Jesus answered and said to them, "If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing;
but it is my Father who will glorify me, of whom you say, 'He is our God.'
And you do not know him, but I know him. If I were to say that I do not know him, I too would be a liar like you. But I know him and I keep his words.
Abraham your father rejoiced that he would see this day of mine; and he saw it and was glad."
The Jews said to him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?" Jesus said to them, "Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham was, I am."
The Jews took up stones to throw at him. But Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple; he passed through their midst and went away.
To you it is fitting. Listen!
Paul stood up and motioned with his hand for them to be silent: "The forgiveness of your sins is proclaimed to you."
It is better,
if it should be God's will that you suffer, to suffer for doing good rather than for doing evil;
for Christ also suffered once for our sins, the righteous for sinners, so that he might bring us to God;
he died in the flesh and was made alive in the spirit, in which he went and preached to the spirits in prison,
who had once been disobedient, when the patience of God waited in the days of Noah,
while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved from the water.
In the likeness of this, baptism now saves you: not the removal of the filth of the flesh, but the pleasing of God by the mind, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, who ascended into heaven, with angels, authorities, and powers made subject to him.
And now, my children, [?] time [?] everyone who does righteousness is born of him.
See what great love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God. For this reason the world does not know us: because it did not know him either.
Beloved, we are now children of God, and it has not yet been revealed what we shall be.
We know this: when he appears, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.
And everyone who has this hope in him purifies himself, just as he is pure.
Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness; sin is lawlessness.
And you know that he appeared in order to take away our sins, and in him there is no sin.
No one who abides in him sins; no one who sins has seen him or knows him.
Brothers, let no one lead you astray. Whoever does righteousness is righteous.
Whoever commits sin is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning.
For this reason the Son of God appeared: to destroy the works of the devil. Everyone who is born of God does not commit sin [?]
After this Jesus went down to Capernaum,
he himself and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples with him; and he stayed there for a few days.
The feast of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple he found people selling oxen, sheep, and doves, and the money-changers sitting there.
And he made a whip of cords and drove them all out of the temple, the sheep and the oxen as well;
and he scattered the copper coins of the money-changers; and he said: Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father's house a house of trade.
His disciples remembered that it is written: Zeal for your house has consumed me. The Jews answered and said to him: What sign do you show us, since you do these things?
Jesus answered and said: Destroy this temple of God, and on the third day I will raise it up.
The Jews said to him: This temple was built over forty-six years, and you will raise it up in three days?
He was not speaking about the temple, but about his own body.
His disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken to them.
And when he was in Jerusalem at the feast of Passover, many believed in him, because they saw the signs that he was doing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to anyone, for he had no need for anyone to testify about man, because he knew what was in man.
Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures, and he said to them:
Thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day, and for repentance and the forgiveness of sins to be preached in his name to all the nations,
beginning from Jerusalem; for you are witnesses of all this. And behold, I will send upon you the promise of my Father.
But you, stay in this city until you are clothed with power from on high.
And he led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
And it came to pass that while Jesus was blessing them, he himself parted from them and was going up into heaven.
And they returned to Jerusalem with great joy. And they were continually in the temple, blessing God.
Let Mount Zion rejoice. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised.
And when the seven days were nearly completed, the Jews who were from Asia
saw him in the temple, stirred up the whole crowd, and laid their hands on him, and they cried out: Men of Israel, help!
This is the man who speaks evil against the people and the law and this place, and teaches the same everywhere;
and besides, he has also brought Gentiles into the temple and defiled the holy place.
For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
The whole city was stirred up, and there was a great uproar among the people. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the doors were shut.
And while they were seeking to kill him, word reached the commander of the thousand that all Jerusalem had gathered together.
At once he took soldiers and a centurion and came down on them; and when they saw the centurion and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
And he called two of the centurions and said to them:
"Get ready two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen and two hundred shield-bearers, from the third hour of the night.
[?] and bring him to Felix the governor." And he wrote a letter in which this was written:
Five days later the high priest Ananias went down with the elders and with a certain Tertullus, and they informed the governor against Paul.
And when he had been called, Tertullus began to accuse him and said: "Through you we live in great peace, and through the provision
that your foresight brings about everywhere for this nation. We welcome it in every place, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
So that I do not keep you any longer, hear us in your kindness.
For we have found this man to be a vile person who stirs up unrest among the Jews throughout the whole world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Galileans.
He even tried to defile the temple, and we seized him. From him you will be able
to examine and learn all the things of which we accuse him." The other Jews also testified that this was so.
When the governor nodded to him, Paul answered and said: "I know that for many years you have been judge of this nation.
I gladly make my defence, for you are able to understand and learn all this, since it is no more than ... [?]
If we say that
we have not committed sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all falsehood. If
we say that we have not sinned at all, we lie to him and his word is not in us. My children!
I write this to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus the righteous.
And he is the one who forgives our sins, and not only our sins but those of the whole world.
And by this let us know that we know him: if we keep his commandments.
But whoever keeps his words, truly the love of God is made perfect in him. By this we know that we are in him.
Whoever says that he abides in him ought himself to walk just as he walked.
This is our God for ever, and he [?]:
But Jesus perceived that they were coming to seize him and make him king, so he withdrew and went away by himself.
And when evening came, his disciples went down to the sea. They got into a boat and were crossing the sea to Capernaum.
It had already grown dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them, and a great wind was stirring up the sea.
When they had rowed about twenty-five stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.
But he said to them: "It is I; do not be afraid!" They wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat was at the land to which they were going.
"And I must do the work of him who sent me while it is still day;
night is coming, when no one can work. And while I am still in the world, I am the light of the world."
And when he had said this, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle, and he smeared the clay on the eyes of the blind man and said to him:
"Get up, go, and wash in the pool of Siloam" (which is translated "Sent"). He went, washed, and came back seeing.
But the neighbours, and those who had seen him before, when he was a beggar, were saying: "Is this not the man who used to sit and beg?"
Others said: "It is he." But some said: "No, he only looks like him." But he kept saying: "I am the one."
They asked him: "So how were your eyes opened?"

Some days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and he summoned Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
And as Paul spoke about righteousness, self-restraint, and the judgment to come, Felix became afraid and said to him: "That is enough for now; when I have an opportunity I will summon you."
At the same time he was also hoping that Paul would give him money; so he summoned him often and talked with him.
When two years had been completed, Festus of Pontus came to Felix as servant [?]. Felix wished to win favor with the Jews, and he left Paul in bonds.
When Festus had come into that province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
The high priests and the leaders of the Jews informed him about Paul, and they pleaded with him.
They asked him for a favor concerning Paul: that he would summon him to Jerusalem. They were lying in wait for him on the road, to kill him.
But Festus told them that Paul was being kept in Caesarea, and that he himself was soon to depart from Jerusalem. And he said:
"Let those among you who are able come down with me, and if there is any wrongdoing in that man, accuse him."
He stayed there no more than eight or ten days, and then went down to Caesarea. He sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought.
When Paul came, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him and laid many grave charges against him, which they could not prove.
But Paul answered in his defense: "We have not offended against the law of the Jews, nor against Caesar."
But Festus wished to win favor with the Jews, and he answered Paul and said to him: "Do you wish to go up to Jerusalem and be judged on this there, before me?"
Paul said to him: "I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you know very well.
If I have done some wrong and have done something worthy of death, I do not try to escape death.
But if I have done none of the things of which these men accuse me, no one has the power to hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar."
Then Festus took counsel with his council and said: "You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go."
