When it was decided that we would sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
We boarded a ship from Adramyttium that was bound for the places of Asia, and we set out.
Aristarchus the Macedonian was with us. On the next day we reached Sidon.
Julius showed kindness to Paul and allowed him to go to his friends to receive provisions.
From there we embarked and sailed past Cyprus, because the wind was against us.
Then we crossed the deep sea of Cilicia and came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
There the centurion found a ship from Alexandria that was sailing to Italy, and he put us on board it.
We sailed slowly for many days and reached Cnidus with difficulty, because the wind did not let us go on. Then we sailed past Crete [?] off Salmone.
After we had passed it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea [?].
Much time had passed, and sailing was now dangerous, because the Fast was already over. So Paul warned them and said to them:
"Men, I see that the voyage will bring fear and loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but our own lives will also be lost on the ships."
But the centurion trusted the helmsman and the owner of the ship more than Paul's words.
Since the harbor was not suitable for spending the winter, many of them resolved to sail on from there,
in case they could somehow reach Phoenix and spend the winter there. Phoenix is a harbor of Crete that faces north and toward the land [?].
When a south wind blew, they thought they had what they wanted. They set out from Assos [?] and sailed along the coast of Crete.
Not much time had passed before a whirlwind called the "Broad-Wave" began to blow against it.
When it seized the ship and the ship could not face into the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
We ran under the shelter of an island called Cauda, and with difficulty we managed to secure the boat [?], which they hoisted aboard.
They used supports and bound them around the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the shoals, they let down the ship's gear, and so they were driven along.
Because we were in a great storm, on the next day they began throwing the cargo overboard. On the third day they threw out the ship's tackle with their own hands.
Neither stars nor sun appeared for many days, because the storm was great.
From then on we gave up our hope and all hope for our lives. And there was a long fast.
Then Paul stood up among them and said: "Men, you should have listened to me and not set sail from Crete, and so brought on yourselves this hardship and loss."
"And now I tell you: take heart, for there will be no loss of life for any one of you,
but only of the ship. For this night an angel of the Lord, whom I serve, stood before me and said to me:
'Do not be afraid, Paul; you are to stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who are with you in this ship.'
Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as he told me."

When the fourteenth night came and we were being driven about in that region, around midnight the sailors thought they were approaching some land.
They let down the sounding line and it was twenty fathoms; after waiting a little they sounded again and it was fifteen fathoms.
Fearing that they might run aground on rocky places, they cast four anchors from the stern of the ship and prayed until daybreak.
But the sailors wanted to escape from the ship, and they let the boat down into the sea under the pretext of letting out anchors.
Then Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers: "Unless these men remain in this ship, you cannot be saved."
Then the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat and let it go, and the waves carried it away.
When day was dawning, Paul urged everyone to take food, and said to them:
"Today is the fourteenth day that you have been waiting and have continued fasting, having taken nothing. Therefore I urge you to take food,
for this is for your survival; for not one hair of the head of any of you will perish."
When he had said this, he took bread, gave thanks to God before them all, broke it, and began to eat.
They all took heart and asked [?]. All of us in the ship were two hundred seventy-six persons.
When they had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the wheat out of the ship into the sea.
When day came, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a bay with a shore, on which they intended, if they somehow could, to bring the ship safely.
They cut loose the anchors and left them in the sea, and at the same time loosened the ropes of the rudders; and they raised the small sail to the wind and held toward the shore.
When they struck a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; the bow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was being broken up by the force of the waves.
And the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners, so that none of them could swim away and escape.
But the centurion, wanting to save Paul, kept them from their plan and ordered those who could swim to go in first.
And the rest went, some on planks and some on other pieces of the ship; and so we came out, and all of us were brought safely to land.
When we had come out, they then learned that the island was called Malta.
And the barbarians showed us great kindness, for they kindled a fire and took us all in because of the rain and the cold, which was severe.
And as Paul was gathering a large bundle of brushwood and putting it on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.
When the barbarians saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to one another:

But he shook off his hand and threw the snake into the fire, and he suffered no harm. They were expecting him to swell up and suddenly fall down dead.
But after they had stood and watched for a long time and no harm came to him, they changed their minds and said, "He is a god."
Now in that area there were estates belonging to the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius. He welcomed us with love and kindly gave us hospitality.

And after three days Paul called together those who were leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them:

which in the same manner as these committed fornication and went after strange flesh, are set forth as an example of eternal fire, having received punishment.
In the same way these men see visions, defile the flesh, despise lordship, and blaspheme glory.
When Michael the archangel was contending with the devil and disputing about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a judgment of blasphemy against him, but said: "May the Lord rebuke you!"
But these men blaspheme what they do not know, and what they know by nature, like irrational beasts, {1} by these things they are corrupted.
Woe to them, for they walk in the way of Cain, and were swept away in the error of Balaam {2} for reward, and perished in the rebellion of Korah.
These are those who, defiled, feast together with you in your love feasts and shepherd themselves without fear.
waterless clouds carried about by the wind, wintry trees without fruit, twice dead, pulled up by the roots, raging waves [of the sea],
foaming out their own shame like foam, wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness is reserved.
Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied about them and said: "Behold, the Lord came with myriads of his holy angels,
to execute judgment on all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their works of ungodliness which they committed, and of all the harsh words
which ungodly sinners spoke against him." These are grumblers, fault-finders, who walk according to their own desire.
And their mouth speaks arrogant things, and they show partiality to persons for the sake of gain. But you, beloved,
remember the words spoken beforehand {3} by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ;
for they told you that in the last times scoffers would come, walking according to their own desires in ungodliness.
These are those who separate themselves, worldly-minded men, who do not have the Spirit.
But you, beloved, build yourselves up in your holy faith and pray in the Holy Spirit;
keep yourselves in the love of God and wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life; and have mercy on some without doubting,
and save some, snatching them as out of the fire; and have mercy on others with fear, hating even the garment defiled by the flesh.
Now to him who is able to keep you without sin and to set you blameless before his glory with joy,
to the only God, our Saviour, {1} through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory and riches, might and authority,
Before all ages, now and unto all times, forever and ever. Amen.
We have an altar, from which:
Judge me, O Lord, in righteousness. My heart:
Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish the Law, but to fulfil it.
Amen, I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota, not one stroke, will pass away from the Law and the Prophets until all this has come to pass.

If anyone breaks one of these commandments and teaches people so, he will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
But I say to you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill; and whoever kills is liable to death.
But I say to you: whoever is angry with his brother without cause is liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother 'Fool!' is liable to the Gehenna of fire;
and whoever says to his brother 'Raca', which means 'contemptible', is liable to be expelled from the assembly.
If you are offering your offering upon the altar, and there you remember that your brother holds some grievance against you,
leave your offering upon the altar, go and be reconciled with your brother first, and only then come and offer your offering.
Your good spirit: O Lord, hear my prayer:
[?] as it pleased you:
Send forth the Spirit of the Lord forever: Bless the Lord, O my soul; O Lord my God:
The command of the Lord is a fountain of life, and it turns one away from the deadly snare.
A multitude of people is the glory of a king, but the diminishing of a people is the ruin of a mighty one.
A long-suffering man has much understanding, but the short-tempered man is very foolish. A [?] man is a healer of the heart; the thought of a man's heart is a moth to the sinews.
Whoever wrongs the poor angers his Creator, but whoever honours the poor will find mercy.
By his own wickedness the ungodly will be cast down, but whoever keeps himself pure, he shall be righteous.
Wisdom dwells in the heart of a generous man, but the heart of the foolish cannot be discerned.
Righteousness exalts the nations, but sin diminishes the nations.
An understanding man is pleasing before the king, and by his own diligence he removes disgrace.
Anger destroys even an understanding man; but a gentle word turns away wrath, and a harsh word stirs up insult.
The tongue of the wise speaks what is good, but the mouth of the foolish speaks evil at all times. At all times the eyes of the Lord watch the good and the evil.
But the healing of tongues is a tree of life; and whoever has it will be filled with spirit.
For he himself is the guide of wisdom and the director of the wise.
In his hand are both we and our words, all understanding and knowledge of works.

For he gave me knowledge of the things that are: the making of the world, the workings of the elements, the beginning to the end, the dividing of times, the changes of forms and the turning of the seasons,
the course of the year and the positions of the stars, the natures of animals and the fury of wild beasts, the force of spirits and the thoughts of men, the various kinds of plants.
Whatever is hidden and unrevealed, I came to know; for wisdom, the craftsman of all things, taught me.
For in her is a holy spirit of understanding, manifold, [?] whence I am refined [?], is given well [?], excellent,
undefiled, spotless, clear, loving the good, swift, unhindered, doing good, loving mankind, steadfast, careful,
free from care, all-powerful, overseeing all things, and it is taken in by all spirits that have holy and subtle understanding.
For wisdom is swifter than any motion and [?] witness; she reaches through and is taken in by all things because of her purity.
For she is a breath of the mighty God and a portion of the true glory of the Almighty; for this reason nothing [?] is joined to her.
For she is the radiance of the eternal light and a spotless mirror of God's working and the image of his goodness.

She is one, and she can do all things, and she remains in herself, and she renews all things; from generation to generation she is given to worthy souls, the friends of God, and she prepares prophets.
God loves nothing so much as those who dwell in wisdom.
For she is more beautiful than the sun, and more beautiful than all the stars.
And he received the Holy Spirit from the Lord, and he led them in this way.
Now bring this people to yourself for the sake of your great name. Turn, O Lord, from heaven, and look down from the holy temple of your glory.
Where is the abundance of your mercies, when you bore with us, O Lord? You are our Father.
But fear me.
And when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all gathered together.
And suddenly there came a sound from heaven like the rush of a violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
And there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire, and one rested on each one of them.
And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in foreign tongues, as the Spirit gave them to speak.
Now there were living in Jerusalem God-fearing men from every nation under heaven.
When this sound came, the crowd gathered and was confused, because each one of them heard them speaking in his own language.
They were all astonished and said to one another: Are not, behold, look, all these Galileans?
And how is it that we hear, each one of us, his own language, we who are Medes and Parthians and Elamites and inhabitants of Mesopotamia,
of Judea and of Cappadocia, of Phrygia and from Pamphylia, from Egypt and the regions of Libya, the parts toward Cyrene, and visiting Romans,
Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabians: we hear their speech in our own tongues, these riches of God?
They were all amazed among themselves and said: What do these men mean to do?
But others mocked them, saying: These men are full of sweet wine, and they say whatever they please.
Peter stood up with the eleven, raised his voice and said to them: Men of Judea, and all who live in Jerusalem!
Let this be known to you, and listen to my words;
for it is not as you suppose, that these men are drunk, since it is the third hour of the day. Rather, this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel:
And it shall be after this, says the Lord, that I will pour out of my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy;
and your young men shall see visions, and I will reveal myself to your old men in dreams;
and on my menservants and on my maidservants in those days I will pour out of my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.
And I will give signs in the heavens and wonders on the earth: blood and fire and vapour of smoke.
The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the coming of that great and appointed day.
And it shall be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
But concerning spiritual things, brothers: You have been pleased [?], O Lord, with your land.
Turn back [?]: their sins: what good [?] or for ever [?]:
If you love me, whenever it may be, and you believe [?]:
Be exalted, O Lord, [?] of your reign:
Give thanks [?] to the Lord, for he is good: we have seen the true light.
Do not cast me away from [your] face: give me the joy of salvation.
I will exalt you, O Lord God, for ever:
But now I am going; send me [?]. And he will tell you:
Praise befits you, O God; let them cry out and sing: a hymn in Zion, prayer in Jerusalem:
O Lord, I have cried out [?]: your good Spirit: O Lord, hear [me] [?].
If you love me, whenever it may be, and you believe:
Rejoice, O songs of praise: say among the nations: Sing to the Lord with song:
But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them.
In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, and their departure was reckoned an evil, and their going from us [?] an entering;
but they are in their abiding inheritance. And though they were punished in the sight of men, their hope is full of immortality.
And though they were disciplined a little, it was because God tested them and found them worthy of himself.
He tested them like gold in the furnace, and he accepted them like the fruit of a whole burnt offering.
And in the time of their visitation they will shine forth like sparks and run through the reeds.
And they will judge the nations and rule over the peoples, and God will reign over them forever.
Then the righteous man will stand with great boldness before the face of his oppressor,
and those who despised his labours will see it and tremble with dreadful fear, and they will be amazed at the glory of his salvation,
and they will say in their heart with repentance, and groan in anguish of spirit: "This is the one whom we once held in derision and made a byword of reproach.
We fools! We counted his life as mockery, and his death [?] as dishonour. How has he been numbered among the sons of God, and his portion among the saints?
We strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us.
We were filled up on the way of lawlessness and destruction; we walked through trackless deserts, and the way of the Lord we did not know.
What has our arrogance profited us, and how has wealth with its boasting helped us?
It has passed away like a shadow, and like a rumour that soon vanishes;
and like a ship that passes through the waves of the sea, and no trace of it is found any more, nor any place of its path on the waves;
or as when a bird flies through the air, no mark of its course is found; the light breeze is struck by the beating of its wings,
it lifts itself, moving its wings powerfully and with effort, and passes through, and afterward no sign of its passing is found;
or like an arrow shot at a target, it cleaves the air, and the air at once closes up again, and its passage cannot be known.
So we too came into being and then ceased, and we have no sign of virtue to show, for we were consumed in our wickedness."
For the hope of the ungodly is like dust carried off by the wind, and like fine frost driven away by a storm,
and like smoke scattered by the wind, and it has passed away like the memory of a guest who stays one day.
But the righteous live forever, and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High.
Therefore they will receive the kingdom of splendour from the hand of the Lord, for he will shelter them with his right hand and help them with his arm.
And the Apostle reading:
For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for the sake of you Gentiles, since you have surely heard of the stewardship of God
that was given to me for you: for the mystery was made known to me by revelation, as I wrote to you briefly before,
so that you may be able to know and understand my insight into the mystery of Christ, which was not revealed to the sons of men in other generations,
as it has now been revealed to the holy apostles and prophets by the Holy Spirit:
that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs, fellow members and of one body, sharing in the promise through Jesus Christ by the gospel.
I became a minister of this gospel according to the gift of the Lord's grace, which was given to me by the working of his power.
To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given: to preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ, and to enlighten everyone
about the plan of the mystery that was hidden from the ages in God, who created all things,
so that now the manifold wisdom of God might be made known through the church to the rulers and authorities in heaven, according to the purpose of the ages
that was carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord, in whom we have boldness and access with confidence through faith in him.
Therefore I ask that you not lose heart over our sufferings, which are for your sake and are your glory.
To all the Gentiles:
After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others as well, and sent them ahead of him two by two into every city and village where he was about to go.
And he said to them: "The harvest is great, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers for the harvest.
Go! Look, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a purse, or bags, or sandals, and do not greet anyone on the road.
Whatever house you enter, first say: 'Peace to this house!'
If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking with them, for the worker deserves his wages; and do not move from house to house.
Whatever city you enter where they welcome you, eat what is set before you, heal the sick in it, and tell them:
'The kingdom of heaven has come near to you.' But whatever city you enter where they do not welcome you, go out into its streets
and say to them: 'Look, we shake off against you even the dust from your city that has clung to our feet;
but know this: the kingdom of heaven has come near.' I tell you, it will be more bearable for the people of Sodom on that day than for that city."
Woe to you, Chorazin, and woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that were done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you. And you, Capernaum, do not be lifted up to heaven; rather, you will go down to hell.
Whoever listens to you listens to me; whoever despises you despises me; and whoever despises me despises the one who sent me.
And the seventy-two returned and said: Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.
Jesus said to them: I see the devil fallen from heaven like lightning.
Behold, I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice in this, that evil spirits submit to you; rather rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
And there was a certain man there:
After some days:
And on that one Sabbath, gathered:
I am the good shepherd:
In those days, at the multiplying:
Beloved, I pray for you:
From tomorrow it must [?].
After days; remember your leaders:
And afterwards:
And it happened, as we were going to worship,
that a certain slave girl met us who had a spirit of python, that is, of divination, and she brought her masters great profit.
She followed Paul and us, crying out and saying: These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the way of life.
She did this continually. Paul became angry, turned to that evil spirit, and said: I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.
And it came out immediately, in that same hour. When the woman's masters saw that the hope of their profit had gone out of her,
they seized Paul and Silas and brought them into their marketplace before the rulers. They led them up, presented them, and said:
These men, who are stirring up our city, are Jews, and they proclaim to us some law which it is not lawful for us to accept, for we are Romans.
And the crowd gathered against them, for the rulers tore off their clothes and ordered them to be beaten with rods;
and when they had laid many blows on them, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them carefully.
Then, having received such an order from them, he put them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, and the prison was shaken to its foundations; at once all the doors of the prison were opened, and everyone's bonds were loosed.
And when the jailer suddenly woke and saw the prison doors open,
he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, for he thought that all the prisoners had escaped.
Paul called out to him with a loud voice and said: "Do yourself no harm, for we are all here."
He asked for a light and went into the prison; trembling seized him, and he fell at the feet of Paul and Silas. He brought them out and said to them:
"Lords, what must I do to be saved?" And they said to him: "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household."
And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, and all believed, together with all the people of his household.
And that same night the jailer took them and relieved them of that beating; he himself was baptized, and with him all his household.
And he brought the apostles up and seated them [?], set a table for them, and rejoiced with all his household, who had believed in the Lord.
For this reason strive, so that you may inherit a blessing.
Whoever loves the love of life and wishes to see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and let his lips not speak deceit.
Let him turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are upon his righteous ones, and his ears are open to their prayer; the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.
Who is there to do you harm, if you become imitators of what is good?
But even if you suffer for the sake of righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear what they fear, and do not be troubled. Hold the Lord Jesus Christ holy in your hearts;
always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for an account of the hope that is in you, but with gentleness and fear;
keep a good conscience, so that those who speak evil may be put to shame, those who abuse you for your good walk in Christ.
For it is better, if the will of God so ordains your suffering, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil;
for Christ also suffered once for our sins, the righteous for the false, that he might bring us to God; he was put to death in the flesh and made alive in the spirit.
Then they returned to Jerusalem:
For to each one: [?]
The next day John was again standing there with two of his disciples.
And he looked at Jesus as he walked by and said: "Behold, the Christ, the Lamb of God." The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them and said to them: "What are you seeking?" They said to him: "Rabbi" (which is translated "Teacher"), "where are you staying?"
He said to them: "Come and see." And they came and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day.
It was about the tenth hour. Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who had heard John and followed him.
He first found Simon and said to him: "We have found the Messiah", which is translated "Christ". He brought him to Jesus.
Jesus looked at him and said to him: "Are you Simon, the son of Jonah? You shall be called Cephas", which is translated "Rock".
And when the apostles [?]:
Put away all wickedness:
I testify before God:
Then Peter answered and said to Jesus:
"Lord, behold, we have left everything and followed you. What, then, will there be for us?" And Jesus said to them: "Amen, I say to you:
you who have followed me, in the life to come, when the Son of Man sits on the thrones of his glory, you too shall sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes.
And everyone who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father and mother, or wife, or children, or land for the sake of my name
shall receive a hundredfold and inherit eternal life. But many who are first shall be last, and the last first.
For the kingdom of heaven is like a man, a householder, who went out at dawn to hire laborers for his vineyard.
And he promised them wages of a denarius each for the day, and sent them into his vineyard.
And he went out at the third hour and saw others standing idle in the streets, and he said to them: 'You go into my vineyard too, and I will give you wages.'
And they went. And then he went out at the sixth and the ninth hour and did the same.
And at the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and he said to them: 'Why do you stand idle all day?'
And they said to him: 'No one has hired us.' The householder said to them: 'You go into my vineyard too.'
And when evening came, the lord of that vineyard said to his steward: 'Call the laborers and give them their wages;
begin with the last and go on to the first.' And those of the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.
And those who came first came and each received a denarius. And when they had received it, they grumbled against the householder, saying:
'These last worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the heat.'
But he answered one of them and said to him: 'Friend, I do you no wrong. Did I not promise you one denarius?
Take what is yours and go! I wish to give to this last one the same as to you.
Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with my own produce? Or is your eye evil because I am good?'
So the first will be last and the last first, for many are called, but few are chosen.
Bring me up out of the pit. And [?]: With patience I waited patiently:
The word of God that came to Jeremiah:
And Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Jucal son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to the people, saying:
"Thus says the Lord: Whoever stays in the city will die by the sword and by famine;
but whoever goes over to the Chaldeans will live; his life will be spared, and he will escape."
"And this is what the Lord says: This city will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it." And the princes said to the king:
"Let this man be put to death, for he is weakening the hands of the fighting men and of the rest who remain in the city, and the hands of all the people.
For he speaks this word to them, because he does not speak for the good of this people, for peace, but for evil."
The king said to them: "Look, there he is; he is in your hands!" For he could not speak to them with authority.
And they seized Jeremiah and threw him into the pit of Malchiah, the king's son, in the court of the prison.
There was no water in the pit, only mud, and he was in the mud.
And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, a eunuch who was over the king's house, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the pit; and the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
And Ebed-melech went out and spoke to the king, saying: "My lord king, these men have done evil in what they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, for they have thrown him into the pit to die;
you are doing evil, for you are killing the man of God with hunger, since there is no bread in this city."
And the king commanded Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying: "Take thirty men with you and bring him up from there, out of the pit, so that he does not die."
And Ebed-melech sent the men, and he went into the king's house, to the lower part, and took old rags and old ropes and let them down to Jeremiah the prophet in the pit.
And he said to him: "Put these ropes under your armpits!" And he did so. And they pulled him up with the rope and brought him up out of the pit.
And Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
The Lord knows those who serve God:
And what then shall we say: I will exalt you, O Lord, for you:
When Jesus came into the region:
Your priests shall be clothed. Remember, O Lord, David.
Keep watch, then, over yourselves and over the whole flock,
in which the Holy Spirit has set you as overseers, as shepherds of the churches of God, which he acquired with his own blood.
I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you, who will not spare the flock;
and from among you men will arise who will speak perverse things, to draw the disciples away to follow them.
Therefore be watchful, and remember that for these three years, night and day, I did not cease teaching each and every one of you.
And now, brothers, I commend you to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all the saints.
For to each person:
I am the good shepherd:
And it came to pass in the year that King Uzziah died that I saw the Lord sitting on high and exalted thrones.
And the temple was full of his glory. And seraphim stood around him; one had six wings and another had six wings;
with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They cried out and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth; the heavens and the earth are full of his glory.
And the curtain was lifted up at the voice with which they cried out, and the temple was filled with wonder. And I said: Alas, wretched me!
For I am a man and have unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean speech, and I have seen the King, the Lord, with my eyes.
And one of the seraphim was sent to me, and in his hands he held a live coal, which he had taken with tongs from the altar, and he touched my mouth with it and said to me:
Behold, I have touched your lips, and I have taken away your lawless deeds and your sins.
And I heard the voice of the Lord saying: Whom shall I send, or who will go to that people?
And I said: Behold, here I am; send me. And the Lord said to me: Go and say to that people:
You will indeed hear but not understand; you will indeed see but not perceive, for the heart of this people has grown dull;
with their ears they heard and did not understand; with their eyes they saw, and they shut them; so that they may indeed see and not perceive,
and indeed hear and not listen, nor understand with their heart so as to turn in repentance, and I would heal them.

To the pious king who has fallen asleep. Tell [?] the heavens righteousness. The Lord reigns; majesty...
Reading: An epistle written
by Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, to the God-loving and pious king, the invincible Constantine:
Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, greets you: rejoice in the Lord. This is the first thing I send to you, God-loving king, from Jerusalem, at the head of my letters.
It is fitting for you to receive it and for me to send it. It is not full of words of flattery, but of a message from heaven and a radiance shining forth from God:
not by collecting words or the writings of learned men, but by things foretold in the holy Gospels and fulfilled in deeds.
with the testimony of truth. Some others receive honour from you, and they often make crowns with their own hands, of beautiful gold and shining carbuncle
of many colours, and they present them to you. But we have not offered you an earthly crown, for an earthly gift comes to an end;
but a heavenly gift brings unfailing help in the times of the reign of your piety.
We have hastened to announce to your love of God what appeared in Jerusalem. It is not that you have now come to the service of God out of ignorance,
for you are able to teach others too the faith you serve. Rather, it is so that you may now know this, and be all the more confirmed,
in that you have received and inherited your father's kingship, granted to you from heaven by God.
Now also give fitting thanks to God, the Ruler of all, and above all, in the face of your enemies,
be strong and fearless. The work of your kingship is the love of God. Understand this wonder which he is doing in your time:
for in the time of your father, the God-loving and blessed Constantine, the life-giving Cross was found in Jerusalem by the grace of God,
and through his diligent, heartfelt search in the service of God, God granted that the hidden holy places be found. But in your time, lord
and all-pious king, whose piety is greater than that of your father, the pious one, [wonders appear] even more now, not from the earth
but from heaven: the wonders of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God,
who trampled down death. I announce to you concerning the holy Cross: it appeared radiantly, like marble [?].
For in these holy days of Pentecost, [?] of the Martyrium [?], on the seventh day of the month of May, at the third hour of the day,
a cross of great beauty, adorned with light, appeared in the sky above holy Golgotha,
stretched out as far as the holy Mount of Olives. It was not shown to just one or two people; it was shown clearly to the whole population of the city.
Nor should anyone think it was a fantasy that passed quickly. It was seen with the eyes and watched for a long time.
For its brightness covered the light of the sun. The sunlight beneath it was overpowered and hidden, because the cross was stronger than the sun.
Those who saw the brightness all around were all struck with trembling by it, and the whole population of the city ran to the church.
Then the divine vision seized everyone at once with fear and joy: all the young men, the old men, and the women alike.
People of every age, with their households, saw it with their own eyes: residents, strangers, and pagans who had come from elsewhere.
All together, with one voice, they praised Christ Jesus our God, the only-begotten Son of God and worker of wonders, now accepted through what they had seen happen.
The faith of Christians is complete piety. Its message does not rest on listening to wisdom,
but on the practice of faith and on power, and not on what people merely tell.
but borne witness to by God from heaven. And now we, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, have seen with our own eyes a marvel beyond comprehension.
And to the only God, and to his only-begotten Son together with the Holy Spirit, we have offered the fitting thanksgiving of worship due to him.
And we shall offer it. We have made earnest [?] prayer at these holy places for your might and sovereignty.
And we shall make it. It is right that this thing made manifest from heaven should not pass by in silence, but should be announced to your God-given kingship.
For this reason I hastened to write to you, so that upon that good foundation (for faith has been with you from the very first)
which God quickly made known to you through understanding, you may build, made firm by the Lord Jesus Christ. Take hope without fear.
As is your custom, you have been filled with every courage, for you have God himself as your courage.
And may you hold the victory through the cross, set ready before your eyes, as your boast, glorying in it.
It is the sign that appeared to you coming from heaven, whose image, or rather the heaven itself, proclaimed it.
For this marvel, O God-loving king, the testimonies of the prophets and the words of Christ
and the writings of the holy Gospels have now been fulfilled in sequence, and will be fulfilled again; for in the very chapter of their Gospel,
when the Saviour wished to reveal the things to come, granting this to his blessed apostles,
he plainly foretold it to them in words, and said: "Then the sign of the Son of Man will shine forth in the heavens."
Now take up the Gospels, the books given by God; as is your custom, take the book into your hand.
Therefore you will find what was ordained and foretold set down in writing as testimony.

Above all, O lord, I beseech you [?] for instruction; I beseech you for the sake of others [to search] there all the writings that came after our Saviour, with the many prophetic utterances of his teaching,
and with entreaty concerning the word [?], so that no harm at all may come upon you from the enemy. This word of ours to you, O God-loving king, I offer to you as my voice,
to you, the orderly and wholly devout, who worship with us Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, our Saviour,
who has filled the whole world with life, in accordance with the divine Scriptures;
who here trampled down death and wiped out the sins of men with his own blood, and granted life, incorruption, and spiritual heavenly grace to all believers,
who are preserved by grace and power. You adorn the most radiant worship of God by your governance,
like lawful children shining forth from a king and flourishing like flowers. May he himself, the Lord God
and giver of every good thing, preserve the world entirely, wholly and altogether, for many seasons of peace and good order, as the glory of Christians.
Gladness to you, virtue adorned in every way, and the custom of the holy churches, the rule of the Romans, the showing of love for humankind,
and above all the ordering of our worship of God: may God grant these to all of us together, O invincible king.
[?] and wholly God-loving one. To whom befit the honour and glory of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and always, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

May the Lord grant mercy to the house of Onesiphorus,
for many times he refreshed me, and he was not ashamed of my chains; but he came to Rome, searched for me eagerly, and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And how much he served in Ephesus, you know better than anyone.
But you, my child, be strong in the grace of Christ. And what you heard from me with great earnestness, entrust this to faithful men who will be able to teach others as well.
Endure hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No soldier gets entangled in the affairs of the world, so that he may please his commander.
If anyone competes, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
The hard-working farmer ought to be the first to receive a share of the fruit.
Understand what I am telling you. For may the Lord give you understanding of what is good in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the seed of David, according to my gospel,
for which I suffer evil, even to the point of chains, like an evildoer; but the word of God is not chained.
Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may find salvation through Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
This saying is trustworthy: if we die with him, we shall also live with him.
If we endure with him, we shall also reign with him. If we deny him, he too will deny us.
If we do not believe him, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself.
Remind them of this, and charge them before God not to quarrel with contentious words, which are of no use and only ruin those who hear.
Strive to present yourself to God as one approved, a workman who has no cause for shame, rightly handling the word of truth.
If I forget you:
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has drawn near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; let those who are inside the city get out; and let those who are out in the countryside not go into it.
For these are the days of its vengeance, so that all the scriptures may be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days, for there will be great distress upon the earth, and wrath upon this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive among all the nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
And there will be signs in the sun, the moon and the stars; and on the earth the nations will be in anguish, bewildered by a roaring as of the sea and of an earthquake;
and people's spirits [?] from fear as they wait for what is coming upon this world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
And when all this begins to happen, lift up your eyes and raise your hands, for your redemption has drawn near.
And he told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees. When their leaves come out, you know for yourselves that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see all these things happening, know that the kingdom of heaven is near.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away until all this has happened. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
Watch yourselves, so that your hearts are not weighed down with envy, drunkenness and the cares of this world, and that day comes upon you suddenly.
For it will come like a snare upon all who live on the face of the whole earth.
So stay awake at all times and pray, so that you may be found worthy to escape all these things that are going to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.

and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will flog in your synagogues and pursue from city to city,

And it came to pass, as they were going to Jerusalem, that he himself entered a certain village; and a certain woman, whose name was Martha, brought Jesus into her house.
And she had a sister, whose name was Mary, and she came and sat at the feet of Jesus and listened to his words.
But Martha was busy with much serving, and she came to the Lord and said to him: "Lord, do you not care at all that my sister has left me alone in this serving?
Tell her to help me." Jesus answered and said to her: "Martha, you are anxious and caught up in many things.
But here little is needed. And Mary has chosen the good portion, which shall never be taken from her."
Thus says the Lord Almighty:
If you walk in my ways and keep my commandments, and you judge my house, and if you guard my court, I will grant you to walk among these who stand here.
Hear now, Joshua the great priest, you and your companions who sit before your face, for these men are watchers of portents.
For behold, I will bring my servant; Dayspring is his name. For the stone that I have set before the face of Joshua:
on that one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will dig a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will lay my hand on it, and I will lay bare the falsehood of that land in one day.
On that day, says the Lord Almighty, each man will call his neighbour under his vine and under his fig tree.
And the angel who was speaking with me turned back and roused me, as a man is roused from his sleep, and said to me: "What do you see?"
And I said to him: "I see a lampstand of gold, with a bowl [?] on top of it, and it is bowl-shaped [?], and a seven-mouthed lamp upon it, and seven lighting-spouts [?] upon it,
and two olive trees, to the right and to the left of the lampstands." I asked the angel who was speaking with me and said to him: "What is this?"
And he answered and said to me: "Do you not know what this is?" I said: "I do not know, lord." And he answered and said to me:
"This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, says the Lord Almighty: not by great power, nor by strength of arm, but by the Spirit of the Almighty.
Who are you, O great mountain, that are exalted before the face of Zerubbabel?
And I brought out the stone of unity, of inheritance and of mercy, together with its grace."
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying: "The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of the house, and his hands shall complete all of it,
so that you may know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you. Who is it that has despised the small days?
They shall rejoice and shall see the stone of lead [?] in the hands of Zerubbabel. These are the seven eyes of the Lord, which look over all the ends of the earth."
I began to speak to the angel and said: "And what are those two olive trees, lord, which stand one to the right of the lampstand and one to the left?
Or what are those two olive branches which pour the oil into the two lampstands and renew the golden lamps?"
And he said to me: "Do you not know what this is?" And I said: "I do not know, lord."
And he said to me: "These are the two sons of fatness, who stand before the Lord of all the earth."
Then I turned and lifted up my eyes, and I saw a flying sickle. And the angel said to me: "What do you see?"
And I said: "I see a flying sickle; its length from its front [?] is twenty cubits and its width is ten cubits." And he said to me:
"This is the curse that goes out over the face of all the earth, for by it vengeance will be taken on every thief;
and by it the vengeance of death will be taken on everyone who swears falsely.
And I will send it out, said the Lord Almighty, and it will enter the house of the thief and of the one who swears falsely,
who swore falsely by the name of the Lord; and it will take up lodging in his house until it [?] and [?] it,
and it will finish off its timber and its stone." And the angel who was speaking with me came out and said to me:
"Lift up your eyes and see what this is that is going out." And I said: "What is this, Lord?"
And he said to me: "This is the measure that is going out to measure." And he said to me: "This is the measure of their iniquity in all the earth."
And behold, I saw a weight of lead being lifted out, and a woman was sitting on that measure.
And he said: "This is lawlessness; throw her into the measure!" And he threw the weight of lead onto its mouth.
And I lifted up my eyes and looked: and behold, two women were coming out, and they became winged, and there was wind in their wings.
And their wings were like those of a hoopoe. And they lifted the measure up between earth and heaven.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me: "Where are they taking this measure, Lord?"
And he said to me: "To build a house for it in the land of the Babylonians and to prepare it; and they will set it there upon its prepared place."
And behold, four chariots were coming out from between two mountains, and those mountains were mountains of bronze.
Black horses were harnessed to the first chariots, and [?] horses were harnessed to the second chariots, and white horses were harnessed to the third chariots,
and dappled [?] horses to the fourth chariots. I began to speak to the angel and said to him: "What are these, Lord?"
And he said to me: "These are the four winds of heaven, which go out to stand before the Lord.
The one to which the black horses were harnessed went out toward the north, and the white ones went out after them, and the [?] ones went out to the land of the south;
and the dappled [?] ones went out and were looking to go about all the earth." And he said to them: "Go, go about all the earth!"
And they went about all the earth. And he cried out and said to me: "Behold, those who go out to the land of the north have quieted my wrath."
And the word of the Lord came to me and said to me: "Take from the captivity, from the hands of the rulers, of its useful men, of those among them who have knowledge:
from Heldai and from Tobijah and from Jedaiah; and on that day you shall go into the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who has come from the land of the Babylonians.
And take some of the silver and gold and make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest."
Say to him: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, the man, and 'Rising of the Sun' [i.e. the Dayspring] they call
his name, and beneath him is radiance, and he shall build the house of the Lord.
And he shall take possession of strength, and shall sit and rule upon his throne. And the priest shall be at his right hand, and there shall be a counsel of peace between the two of them.
And the crown shall stand and wait, and it shall be for those who yield to him, and for those who were useful to him,
and for those who know him, and for the grace of the son of Zephaniah, and for praising the name of the Lord.
Those of them who are far off shall gather and build. And you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
And if one suffers harm:
For this reason also the Wisdom of God said: I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them you killed and persecuted,
so that the blood of all the prophets, shed since the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the altar and the temple.
Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
Woe to you, lawyers, for you have hidden the keys of the kingdom; you yourselves do not enter, and you hinder those who are entering.
And as Jesus was saying this before all the people, the scribes and the Pharisees were plotting evil; and they wanted [?] a word;
and they reviled him over many words, and they watched him to find some word from his mouth, so that they might accuse him.
Meanwhile, when tens of thousands of people had gathered, so that they were even trampling one another,
Jesus began to say to his disciples first: Beware for yourselves of the [?] (text reads 'tribe'; probably an error for 'leaven') of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be made known.
A vine out of Egypt. You who shepherd Israel:

For he himself is God of all,
who enriches all who call upon him. Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.
How then will they believe in him of whom they have not heard? Or how will they preach unless someone sends them?
As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the good news of peace, who bring good news of good things!
But not all have heeded the gospel. Isaiah says: Lord, who has believed what we have heard?
So faith comes from hearing, and hearing by the word of God. But I say: Is it that they have not heard?
For: "Their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world." But I say: Did Israel not know it?
First Moses says: "I will make you jealous of a nation, and with a foolish nation I will make you angry."
Isaiah is bold and says: "I was found by those who did not seek me, and I was revealed to those who did not ask for me."

And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sick and infirm person among the people.
And when he saw the people, he had compassion on them, because they were weary and exhausted, like sheep that have no shepherd.
Then Jesus said to his disciples: "The harvest is great, but the labourers are few.
Pray to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out labourers for the harvest."
And Jesus called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they might cast them out and heal all their infirmities.
Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew the tax collector; the son of James [?] — Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, who was called Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. These twelve Jesus sent out, commanding them and saying to them:
"Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
And as you go, preach and say: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
Heal the infirm, cleanse the lepers. Freely you have received, freely give.
Do not take gold, nor silver, nor copper in your belts, nor a bag for the road, nor two garments, nor sandals, nor a staff, for the labourer is worthy of his wages.
Whatever city or villages you enter, [?] who is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
And when you enter a house, greet it and say: 'Peace to this house!'
And if that house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
If anyone does not receive you or hear your words, when you go out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Amen, I say to you: it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgement than for that land."

And Joash, king of Israel, came to him and wept before him and said to him: "My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horseman!"
And Elisha said to him: "Take a bow and arrows." And he took a bow and arrows before him. And he said to the king of Israel: "Put your hand on that bow!"
And he laid his hand on the bow; and Elisha placed his own hands upon the king's hands and said to him: "Open the windows toward the east!"
And he opened it. And Elisha said: Shoot! And he shot. And Elisha said: The arrow of the Lord's salvation, and the arrow of might against Syria!
And Syria will be struck down at Aphek until it is destroyed. And Elisha said to the king of Israel: Take your bow!
And he took it; and Elisha said to him: Shoot at the ground! And the king shot at the ground three times, and the king struck [?].
And the man of God was grieved and said to him: If you had shot five times, or six times, then you would have struck Syria down completely.
And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the bands [?] of Moab came into the land in the eighth year.
And it happened that, as they were burying a man, they saw the raiders, and they threw the dead man onto Elisha's grave;
and he rolled down and touched Elisha's bones and came to life; and he stood up on his feet.
And what shall we say? For [?]: I have loved, because he has heard.
Truly I tell you:
There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut so that no rain fell for three years and six months, when there was a famine over the land.
And Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to Zarephath in Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was healed, but only Naaman the Syrian.
And when they heard this, all those in the synagogue were filled with anger.
And they rose up and drove him outside the city and brought him to the brow of the mountain on which their city was built, so that they might throw him down from the cliff.

We who are strong ought
to bear the weaknesses of the feeble, and not only to please ourselves; rather, let each one please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
For Christ too did not please himself, but, as it is written: The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.
For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through patience and the comfort of the Scriptures we might have hope.
Now may the God of patience and comfort grant you to be of the same mind toward one another through Christ Jesus,
so that together, with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore receive one another, just as Christ received you, to the glory of God.
For I say that Christ became a servant of the circumcision for the sake of God's truth, so that the promise made to the fathers might be confirmed,
and that [?] for the sake of mercy, might glorify God, as it is written: Therefore I will confess you and sing to your name.

And Jesus returned in the power of the Holy [?] to Galilee;
and the report about him went out through all that region. And he taught in their synagogues and was glorified by all.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and as was his custom he went into their synagogue on the Sabbath day.
And they gave him the book of the prophet Isaiah. And he stood up to read, and he opened the book and found the place where it was written:

to proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, and to set free, to heal the sick, and to proclaim the year of the Lord."

that came out of his mouth.
The words of Amos the prophet, which came to him in Kariathim,
which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judea and in the days of Jeroboam son of Amos, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

And the Lord showed me, and behold, he called for judgment by fire, and it devoured many deeps.
And he said: Go and devour that portion. And I said: Lord, Lord, have mercy. Who will raise up Jacob, for he has become small?
Repent of this, O Lord. "And this shall not be," says the Lord. And again the Lord showed me something.
And behold, I saw a man standing on a wall of adamant, and in his hands he held adamant.
And the Lord said to me: "What do you see, Amos?" And I said: "I see adamant."
And he said to me: "Behold, I will set adamant in the midst of Israel, and I will no longer pass by it again."
"And those houses of the singers shall be destroyed, and the high places of Israel shall fall, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam and judge it with the sword."
And Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam, king of Israel, [saying: ?] "The land cannot bear all the words that he speaks."
"For this is what Amos says: 'Jeroboam shall fall by the sword, and Israel shall be led away captive from its land.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos: "Seer, go, get away, and go to Judea, and stay there and prophesy there, for this is the king's sanctuary, and it is a royal house."
And Amos said to Amaziah: "I was not a prophet, nor the son of a prophet, but I was a herdsman and a gatherer of mulberries,
and the Lord took me from my flock and said to me: 'Go and prophesy to my people Israel.'

and your land shall be measured with a line, and you shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall be led away captive from its land.'"

"On that day I will raise up the tent of David,
which has fallen, and I will rebuild its ruins; I will raise it up and rebuild it as in the days of old, so that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord,
and all the nations upon whom my name is called," says the Lord, who made all these things known from of old.

"Behold, the days are coming," says the Lord, "when the threshing shall overtake the vintage, and the grapes shall ripen at sowing time, and the mountains shall drip sweetness, and all the hills shall be planted.
And I will bring back the captivity of my people Israel, and I will rebuild the ruined city.
And they shall dwell in it; they shall plant vineyards and drink wine, and they shall make gardens and eat their fruit.
And I will plant them in their land, and they shall no longer be uprooted from their land, which I have given them," says the Lord Almighty.
And what then shall we say: to all the nations: [?]
On that day the Sadducees came to him, saying that there is no resurrection.
They questioned him and said: "Teacher, Moses said this: 'If someone dies and leaves no child, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up an heir for his brother.'
There were among us seven brothers. The first married a wife and died, and having no child, he left his wife to his brother.
The same happened with the second and the third, up to the seventh. Last of all, the woman also died.
Now then, in the resurrection of the dead, whose wife will she be of them?" Jesus answered and said to them:
You are wrong, because you know neither the scripture nor the power of God. For on the day of the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in heaven.
And about the resurrection, have you not read what God said, when he says: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
Who serves as a soldier at his own expense?
Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink the milk of the flock?
Am I saying this only from a human point of view? Does the law not say the same? For it is written in the law of Moses: You shall not muzzle the ox while it is threshing.
Is it oxen that God is concerned about? Surely he says it for our sake, for it was written for us.
For the ploughman ought to plough in hope, and whoever threshes gathers in hope.
If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?

For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness."
