But for the one who does not work but only believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness.
Just as David speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom he counted righteousness apart from works:
"Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered; blessed is the man to whom the Lord did not count sin."
Now then, was this blessedness upon the circumcision or upon the uncircumcision? For it says: "Abraham's faith was counted to him as righteousness."
Was it then counted in circumcision or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
And he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the righteousness of faith in circumcision,
so that he might be the father of all believers who are circumcised, so that it might be counted as righteousness.
and the father of the circumcision, not only of those who are of the circumcision, but of those who walk in the footsteps of the circumcision of the faith of our father Abraham.
The descendants of Abraham:
On that day they were loosed [?]:
The descendants of Abraham: the covenant that he made with Abraham:
And the Lord God appeared to Abraham:
Tell me, you who want to be under the law: have you not read the law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman.
But the one by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, and the one by the free woman through the promise. This is an allegory, for these are the two laws:
the one is the law received from Mount Sinai, which is Hagar. For Mount Sinai in Arabia corresponds to this Jerusalem, which is in slavery with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. For it is written: "Rejoice, O barren one, you who do not bear;
lift up your voice and cry out, you who were not in labor, for the children of the desolate woman are more than those of the woman who had a husband."

But we, brothers, are children of the promise through Isaac. But just as once the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now as well. But what does the Scripture say?
"Cast out this slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman."
Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman, with the freedom with which Christ has set us free.
The princes ... of Abraham:
A certain man came up to him:
Into all the earth: The heavens declare;
Then they returned to Jerusalem: All the nations.
And Jesus went about the cities:
Thus says the Lord Almighty:
And it came to pass in the year;
In the third year of Jehoiakim, king of Judea, Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, came
to Jerusalem and besieged it. And the Lord gave Jehoiakim, king of Judea, into his hands, together with treasure and the people, from the house of the temple of God.
He came and brought him to the land of Shinar, and he brought the treasure and put it into his own house.
And the king commanded Ashpenaz, his chief eunuch, to select from the captives of the sons of Israel, from the royal line,
from the offspring of the nobles, chosen youths in whom there was no blemish at all, handsome in appearance, intelligent, trained in wisdom,
thoughtful in heart, chosen, strong, so that they might stand always before the king. And he commanded that they be taught the letters and the knowledge of the counsel of the Chaldeans.
And the king assigned them a perpetual daily ration from the royal tables and wine from the king's drink,
so that they would bring them up and teach them for three years, and afterwards bring them before the king and appoint them to his service.
And among the sons of Judah were found chosen youths: Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael.
And the chief eunuch gave them names: Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.
And Daniel resolved in his heart that he would by no means taste anything from the king's table or from his drink.
And he came and pleaded with the chief eunuch that he not force them to taste of it.
And the Lord gave Daniel grace and mercy and favor before the chief eunuch.
The chief eunuch answered Daniel and said to him: "I am afraid of my lord the king, because he has assigned you this ration of your food and your drink.
What if your faces look more sorrowful than those of the other youths of your own age? Then you would make me answer with my own head before the king."
Then Daniel said to Amelsar, whom the chief eunuch had put in charge: "Test us for just ten days. Give us only seeds [?] to eat, and let us eat that and drink water.
Then look at our faces, the faces of those who eat seeds, and at the faces of those youths who eat from the royal table.
Then, as you see when you have tested us, so deal with your servants." He listened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.
After those ten days their faces looked full and had a good colour.
They themselves [?] were stronger and sturdier than the youths who ate from the royal table.
So from then on Amelsar held back from them that ration and the wine that was the king's drink, and gave them seeds for food.
To those four youths God gave understanding, wisdom and knowledge, and all the wisdom of learning and skill.
Daniel had knowledge of every vision of thoughts and the understanding of dreams.
Then, when the days were over after which the king had ordered that they be brought, the chief eunuch presented them before King Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked with them, and no one was found equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael.
In every matter of wisdom that the king asked them about, he found them ten times better than all the wise men and magi who were in his kingdom.
Daniel remained there until the ninth year of King Cyrus.
What then shall we say?
For the kingdom is like [?]
Now the [days] of Elizabeth were fulfilled. [?] was upon the child:
O Forerunner, preacher of Christ, you [?] to the King. "Do not touch the anointed." He did not permit [?].
A man is great, and a merciful man is precious, but a faithful man is hard to find.
Whoever walks in justice without blemish leaves blessed children after him.
For when a righteous king sits on the throne of judgment, no wicked person can stand before his eyes.
Who can boast in his heart, saying, "I am pure from sin"? A large and a small weight and two different measures are an abomination before the Lord, and so is whoever uses them.
By these same things a young man is fettered and entangled, but whoever walks in purity, his ways are upright.
The ear hears and the eye sees, and the Lord made them both. Do not love evil speaking, so that you are not destroyed.
Open your eyes and be filled with bread. Whoever goes in it speaks badly of what is bad [?], and afterwards [?] he boasts.
There is gold and the depth of the abysses, but knowing lips are a precious vessel.
Behold, lo,
I will send you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of that great and appointed day, who will turn the heart of the father to the son, and the heart of a man to his neighbour.
lest I come and strike the earth utterly. Behold, lo, I will send you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of that day of the Lord, great and appointed,
who will turn the heart of the father toward the son, and the heart of a man to his neighbour, lest I come and strike the earth utterly.
And Elisha fell sick:
The God of this people Israel: ... of his cords [?]:
And what then shall we say? The mouth of the righteous one [?] ... killed him.
At that time Herod, the tetrarch, heard the report about Jesus, and he said to his servants:
"This is John the Baptist. He has risen from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him."
For Herod had then seized John and put him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother.
For John had been telling them, "It is not lawful for you to have her as your wife."
And although he wanted to kill him, he feared the people, because they held him to be a prophet.
And when Herod's days of festivity came, the daughter of Herodias danced among them, and her dancing pleased Herod. Because of this he promised her with an oath to give her whatever she might ask.
And she, prompted beforehand by her mother, said, "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
And although the king was grieved, yet because of his oath and those reclining at table with him, he commanded that it be given to her.
And he sent and had John beheaded in the prison. And they brought the head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And his disciples came and took away his body and buried it. And they came and told Jesus.
O Forerunner, preacher of Christ, although ... By the Holy Spirit: We offer the bloodless sacrifice: The hosts praise you.
Your testimonies are sure. Of the days: The Lord reigns; beauty ...
For this reason I bow:
When Jesus came to the place:
You will bless [?] the crown of the year: you will enrich beauty:
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because of this:
For Christ did not enter holy places made with hands, in the likeness of the true ones, but he entered the heaven above, to intercede for us before God.
Nor was it that he should offer himself many times as a gift, as the high priest enters the holy place once a year with the blood of another;
for then he would have had to suffer many times since the creation of the world. But now he has appeared once, at the end of the ages, to put away sins by his own sacrifice.
And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after that comes the judgment,
so Christ was offered once for many, to blot out sins; and he will appear a second time, without sin, to those who wait for him as Savior in faith.
For the law had a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities. With the sacrifices they offer year by year continually, it could never make perfect those who offer them.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased from offering? For the offerers would no longer have had any doubt about sins, having been cleansed once for all.
But in them there is a remembrance of sins year by year, for the blood of goats and calves cannot blot out sins.
Therefore, when he comes into the world, he says: "Offering and sacrifice you did not desire, but a body you have established for me. Burnt offering for sins I did not ask for [?]."
"Then I said: Behold, I come; at the head of the book it is written of me." Blow the new trumpet.
And Joshua turned back with power:
The sea saw: What is it with you?
And after it was completed;
And Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all his people with him, for battle.
And God said to Joshua: "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hands, and none of them will stand before you."
And Joshua rushed upon them suddenly; all night he marched from Gilgal.
And the Lord threw them into confusion before the sons of Israel, and the Lord crushed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and they pursued them along the ascent of Beth-horon.

And they kept striking them down as far as Azekah. And when they were fleeing before the sons of Israel down the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast hailstones down on them from heaven as far as Azekah.
And more died from the hailstones than those whom the sons of Israel killed with the sword in battle.
Then Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day when the Lord God delivered the Amorites to the sons of Israel,
when the Lord God crushed them at Gibeon, and they were crushed before Israel.
And Joshua said: "Let the sun stand still over Gibeon, and the moon over the valley of Aijalon, until I fight this people." And the sun and the moon stood still until he had overcome those enemies.
And behold, all this is written in the Book of Righteousness: "And the sun stood still in the midst of heaven and did not go toward its setting for one day."
And there had been no such day before, when God listened to a man, for the Lord fought together with Israel.
And after this Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten years.
And they buried him within the borders of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Galaad; and there they placed with him in the tomb,
in which they buried them, those stone knives with which he circumcised in Gilgal when he brought them out of Egypt, as the Lord had commanded him.
They are there to this very day. And the sons of Israel brought the bones of Joseph up out of Egypt and buried them in Shechem, in the portion of the field
which Jacob had acquired from the Amorites, for they were in Shechem. He acquired it for a hundred lambs and gave it to Joseph as a portion.

And after this it came to pass that Eleazar, son of Aaron, the priest, died, and his priesthood [?], and he was buried in Gilead [?] of Phinehas his son, for he had given him the hill country of Ephraim.
On that day they took the ark of the law and carried it about among them to Phinehas [?], for Eleazar, his father's grandson [?], served as priest
until his death, and he was buried in his own Gabaoth. And the sons of Israel went away, each man to his own place.
And the sons of Israel served Astarte and Ashtaroth, the gods of the nations that were round about them.
And he gave them into the hands of Eglon king of Moab, and he ruled over them for eighteen years.
There is faith: The Lord reigns;
Therefore, behold, I:
The sea saw, and: The mountains rejoiced like rams:
And the Lord said to Moses: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up onto Mount Hor before the whole congregation.
And strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son; and let him be gathered to his people and die there.
And Moses did as the Lord had commanded him, and brought them up onto Mount Hor before the whole congregation.
And he stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died on the top of that mountain. And Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
And the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, and the whole house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.
And Moses said to the tribes of Israel:
Let each man kill those of his household who defiled themselves with Baal-Peor. And there came a man of the sons of Israel,
and he went in to a Midianite woman before Moses and before the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
And they were sitting and weeping before the tent of witness.
And Phinehas, son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron the priest, saw it, and he rose up from the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
And he went in after that Israelite man into the inner chamber.
And he struck with the spear and pierced both of them through the belly: the Israelite man and the Midianite woman.
And the plague ceased from the sons of Israel. And those who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said: Phinehas, son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron the priest,
He has calmed my wrath against the sons of Israel, because he took vengeance for my sake among them, and so I did not destroy the sons of Israel.
So say to him: Behold, I make with you the covenant of peace.
And there shall be for him and for his descendants after him an everlasting covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and delivered the sons of Israel.
God is wonderful in his saints. [Verse:] Let God arise, and…
And it came to pass,
two years after those days, that Pharaoh had a dream. He thought he was standing on the bank of the river.
And behold, seven cows came up out of the river, beautiful to look at and fat in flesh, and they grazed on the riverbank.
And seven other cows came up out of the river after them, ugly to look at and thin in flesh, and they grazed beside them on the riverbank.
And they ate up the seven beautiful, fat cows. And Pharaoh woke up from the dream, and then he had a second dream.
And behold, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and good.
And then seven other ears sprouted after them, withered and scorched.
And they ate up the seven good, choice ears. And Pharaoh woke up, and behold, it was a dream, and he was troubled in his heart.
And when morning came, he called for all the wise men and learned men of Egypt and told them the dream.
And there was no one who could explain it, speak of it, or tell him the meaning of the dream.
Then the cupbearer said to Pharaoh: Today I remember my sin.
You were angry with your servants, Pharaoh, and you put us in prison in the house of the chief cook, me and the chief baker.
And we each had a dream on the same night, he and I, each of us his own dream.
And there was a young man there, a servant of the chief cook, and we told him our dreams, and he explained them to us.
And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my own office, and him you hanged on a tree, and he died.
And Pharaoh sent and brought Joseph out of the prison. And they cut his hair and changed his clothes, and he stood before Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: I have had a dream, and there is no one who can explain it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream, you interpret it.
Joseph answered and said: Without God I cannot give an answer to your majesty. And Pharaoh said to Joseph: In my sleep I saw this:
Behold, I was standing on the bank of the river, and it seemed that seven cows came up out of it, beautiful to look at and fat in flesh, and they grazed on the riverbank.
And then seven other cows came up after them, wretched and ugly to look at and thin in flesh, such as I have never seen anywhere in Egypt.
And they ate up the seven good, beautiful cows. And there was no sign in their bellies that they had eaten anything, and they were just as thin and ugly as before.
And then I saw again in a dream: and behold, seven ears of grain came up before me, full and good.
And then again seven other ears, withered and blighted, came up beside them, and they devoured those seven full and [?] ears.
And I told this to the wise men and counselors of Egypt, and they could not explain it to me.
Joseph said to Pharaoh: "Your dream, O king, is one and the same in both, for God has shown you what he is about to do. The seven good cows are seven years.
And the seven lean cows that came up after them are also seven years, in which there will be famine.
This is what I tell you, Pharaoh: God has shown you what he is about to do.
Behold, seven years of great plenty are coming throughout all Egypt.
And after them seven other years of famine will come, in which the plenty of the land will be forgotten because of the famine that comes after it, for it will be very severe.
As for the dream being repeated a second time, it is so that you may know that this word from God is true, and the Lord will hasten to bring it about.
So now look for a wise and knowledgeable man and set him over all Egypt, and do this, Pharaoh:
appoint overseers [?] over all the land, and take a fifth of all the produce of Egypt during the seven years of plenty.
And gather all the food for the seven coming years, and gather the wheat under the hand of Pharaoh, and store the food in the cities
for the land, for the seven years of famine that are to come on the land of Egypt, so that the land will not perish from the famine."
And these words pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to his servants: "Where can we find such a man as this, in whom is the spirit of God?"
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: "God has made this known to you; there is no other man wiser than you, who has understood it this way.
So now you shall be over my house, and my people shall obey your word, and nothing shall be beyond your authority except my throne."
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: "Behold, from this day I have set you over all the land of Egypt."
And Pharaoh took off his own ring and gave it to Joseph, and he clothed him in fine linen and put a gold collar around his neck.
And he had him ride in his second chariot. And he ordered it proclaimed before him that Pharaoh had made Joseph ruler over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph: "I, Pharaoh, tell you that without you no one shall lift his hand in all the land of Egypt."
And Pharaoh named Joseph Suntuphanerek (Zaphenath-paneah), and gave him as wife Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of the City of the Sun (Heliopolis).
Joseph was thirty years old when he went in before the king of the Egyptians.
And Joseph went out from Pharaoh and went throughout all Egypt. And the land brought forth abundant produce during the seven years of plenty.
And during those seven years Joseph gathered a great deal of food throughout all the land of Egypt, and he stored the food in each city, from the fields around that city.
And Joseph gathered grain like the sand of the sea, until they could no longer count it, for it was beyond number.
Before the years of the famine came, two sons were born to Joseph. Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis (the City of the Sun), bore them to him.
Joseph named his firstborn son Manasseh, for he said: "The Lord has made me forget all my suffering and everything of my father's house."
And the name of the second was Ephraim, for he said: "The Lord has made me increase in my humiliation."
When the brothers saw:
And Moses was there on the mountain before the Lord forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water.
And there he wrote on the tablets the commands of the covenant, the ten commandments of the law.
And when the time came for Moses to come down from the mountain, the two tablets were in his hands.
And when he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that glory had come down and rested on his face.
And Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses' face, for the appearance of his face was made glorious with the glory of God.
Terror seized them, for they were afraid, and they fled and could not come near him.
Moses called to them aloud, and Aaron and all the leaders of the people turned back to him. And Moses began to speak.
Only then did all the children of Israel come near to him. And he commanded them all the commands that the Lord had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
And when Moses had finished delivering the command to them, he covered his face with a veil.
And whenever Moses went in before the Lord, he took off the veil until he came out; and when he came out to speak to the people, he put the veil over his face.
For the children of Israel could not look at Moses' face, because the glory of the Lord had come down and rested on his face.
By faith, concerning those who would come after: the testimony with Joseph:
Then Peter came to him:
There was a certain sick man, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and of Martha her sister.
This was the Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair.
It was her brother Lazarus who was sick. His sisters sent to him and said: "Lord, behold, the one you loved is sick."
When Jesus heard this, he said: "This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified."
Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus too. When Jesus heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.
After this he said to his disciples: "Come, let us go back to Judea."
The disciples said to him: "Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?"
Jesus said to them: Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not slip, for he sees the light of this world.
And if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, for the light is not in him.
When he had said this, after that he said to them: Lazarus, my friend, has fallen asleep, but I will go and wake him.
His disciples said to him: Lord, if he is asleep, he will recover. Then Jesus told them plainly: Lazarus has died.
And I am glad for your sake, so that you may believe in me, that I was not there. But come, let us go to him.
Thomas, who was called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples: Come, let us go too, so that we may die with him.
And when Jesus came to Bethany, he found that he had already been four days in the tomb. Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
And many of the Jews had come to Mary and Martha to comfort them about their brother.
Mary was sitting in the house, but when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him.
They [?] said to Jesus: Lord, if you had been here, our brother would not have died. And now I know that whatever you ask of God, he will give you.
Jesus said to her: Your brother will rise. Martha said to him: I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.
Jesus said to her: I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even if they die, will live.
And everyone who is alive and believes in me will never die. Do you believe me?
Martha said to him: Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Son of God who is coming into the world.
And when she had said this, she went away and secretly called her sister Mary, and said: The Teacher has come and is calling you.
When she heard this, she got up quickly and went to him. For Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.
The Jews who were with her in the house comforting her, when they saw Mary,
that she had got up quickly and gone out, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep.
When Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
When Jesus saw that she was weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also, he was deeply troubled in spirit, as if with anger, and said to them: Where have you laid him?
They said to him: Lord, come and see. And Jesus wept. So the Jews said: See how much he loved him!
Some of them said: Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have done something so that this man also would not have died?
Then Jesus, again as if with anger within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay over it.
Jesus said to them: Take away that stone. Martha, the dead man's sister, said to him: Lord, he already smells, for it is the fourth day.
Jesus said to her: Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God? And take away [?] that stone.
Then Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: Father, I thank you that you have heard me.
And I knew that you always hear me, but I do this for the sake of this people standing around me, so that they may believe
that you sent me. And when he had said this, he cried out with a loud voice and said: Lazarus, come out!
And the dead man came out, bound hand and foot, and his face was wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said to them: Unbind him and let him go, and let him walk.
Many of the Jews who had come to Mary and Martha saw what had happened, and they believed in him.
But some of them went away and told the Pharisees what Jesus had done.
Your Nativity, O Mother of God. He has made his dwelling holy: the Lord of hosts [is with] us:
I loved her and sought her from my youth, to bring her home as my bride, and I became enamoured of her beauty. Her nobility glorifies the one who lives with her.
She prays to God, and the Master of all loved her, for she is the mystery of the knowledge of God and the discoverer of his works.
And a rod shall come forth. Its sides [?]:
And in that day there shall be the root of Jesse, and the one who rises up to be ruler of the nations.
In him the nations shall hope. And his rest shall be in honour. And his throne shall be set up in mercy.
And he shall sit upon it in truth. On the throne of David he shall judge and seek out justice and be swift to do righteousness:
And in that day there shall be the root of Jesse, and the one who rises up to be ruler of the nations; in him the nations shall hope, and his rest shall be in honour.
And his throne shall be set up in mercy, and he shall sit upon it in truth on the throne of David; he shall judge and seek out justice and be swift to do righteousness.
For if that first one had been blameless, no place would have been sought for a second. For he finds fault with them and says to them:
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel, not like the covenant
that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they did not abide in my law,
and I disregarded them, said the Lord Almighty. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after [?], says the Lord:
I will put my laws into their minds and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
And no longer shall each one teach his neighbour and say, "Know the Lord," for all shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest;
for I will be merciful toward their falsehoods, and I will remember their lawlessness and their sins no more. In saying "new," he has made the first one old.
What is growing old is near to destruction. Now the first law had its ordinances, the holy service of this world.
For a tabernacle was set up, the first one, in which were the lampstand and the table and the setting out of the bread; this was called "the Holy Place."
Then behind the curtain of the temple, in the part called "the Holy of Holies," were a golden censer and the ark of the law,
covered inside and outside with gold, in which was a golden jar full of manna, and Aaron's rod that had budded, and the tablets of the law;
and above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Of these things we cannot now speak one by one.
And these things having been set up in this way, the priests continually enter the outer tabernacle and carry out the service.
But into the inner one the high priest alone enters once a year, and not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people.
By this the Holy Spirit was making clear that the way into the holy places had not yet been revealed while the first tabernacle still had its standing.
This was a figure for the time to come, in which gifts and sacrifices were offered that could not make the worshipper perfect in heart,
but dealt only with foods and drinks and various washings [?] and ordinances of the flesh, until the time of the coming dispensation.
At your birth, O all-holy Mother of God. God reigns over the nations:
For to each and every person: Sing to the Lord with a song:
The apostles said to the Lord: Increase our faith!
The Lord said to them: If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you could say to this fig tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, would say to him at once when he comes in from the field, 'Come here and sit down'?
Will he not rather say to him, 'Get something ready for me to dine, and gird yourself and serve me while I eat and drink, and after that you too may eat and drink'?
Does he thank that servant because he did what he commanded? I do not think so.
So you also, when you have done what you were commanded, say: 'We have done what we were obliged to do.'
Therefore they will praise you.
We will remember your name: they shall be brought to the king;
And it came to pass in those days:
How immeasurable is your reign. Let all the earth worship you. Shout to God, all the earth:
Brighter than the orb of the sun. All the seeds, as many as you have made: You, Lord, help me:
O God of our fathers and Lord:
Thus says the Lord Almighty:

They love the place of honour in their synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called 'Teacher!' by people.
But you, do not call anyone teacher, for you have one teacher, the Christ, and you are all brothers.
And call no one on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

Then he sent another servant. They beat him too and sent him away empty-handed.
Then he sent yet a third servant. They seized him, wounded him, and threw him out.
Then the lord of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.'
But when the tenants saw him, they discussed it among themselves and said,
'This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance will be ours.' So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
What, then, will the lord of the vineyard do to them? He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others." When they heard this, they said, "God forbid!"

and he set the table of provisions [?] in the tent of witness, on the north side, outside the veil of the tent of witness, in the place on the south side.
And he set its lamps on it before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And he set the golden altar in the tent of witness, in front of the veil.
And he burned compounded incense on it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And he set the altar [?] of fruits at the doors of the tent of witness.
And he set up the court around the tent and the altar, and Moses finished all the work.
And the cloud covered the tent of witness, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
And Moses could not enter the tent of witness, because the cloud overshadowed it, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Therefore, brothers, of the appointment [?]:
And on the last day;
Your testimonies are faithful [?] of days: The Lord reigns, majesty:
And Elisha fell sick:
If the first:
When Jesus came to the regions
Bless God in the church: O God, have mercy on us and bless us:
And Haggai, the messenger of the Lord, spoke among the messengers of the Lord to the people: I am with you, says the Lord.
God stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, of the tribe of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest, and of all the remnant of the people;
and they came in and did the work on the house of the Lord God Almighty, their God.
And Haggai spoke among the messengers of the Lord to the people: I am with you, says the Lord,
and the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, of the tribe of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest,
and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came in and did the work on the house of the Lord on the twenty-fourth of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
In the seventh month, on the twenty-first of the month, the Lord spoke through the prophet Haggai and said:
Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and to Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest, and to all the remnant of the people, and say:
Who is there among you who saw this house in its former glory, and how do you see it now? It is as though it were nothing before you.
"And let all the people of the land be strong," says the Lord, "and work, for I am with you," says the Lord Almighty.
"This is the word that I promised you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid!"
For this is what the Lord Almighty says: "Once more I will shake [?] the earth, the heaven, the sea and the dry land, and I will shake all the nations,
and I will bring the chosen ones of all the nations, and I will fill this house with glory," says the Lord Almighty.
"The silver is mine and the gold is mine," says the Lord Almighty.
"For the later glory of this house will be greater than the former," says the Lord Almighty, "and in this place I will give peace,"
says the Lord Almighty, "and the peace of the world as a help to everyone who builds, to raise up this temple."
For you have not come:
And it was only in those days:
I will enter your house: Shout to God, all the earth; let it sing:
And King Solomon completed all the work that he did on the temple of the Lord.
And Solomon brought in the holy things of his father David and all of Solomon's own holy things, the silver and the gold, and he gave all the vessels as treasure to the temple of the Lord.
Then Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel, together with all the leaders, according to the divisions of the fathers' houses, from the city of David.
And all the sons of Israel gathered to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month, and all the elders of Israel came.
And the priests took up the ark of the Lord and the tent of witness.
And all the holy service vessels that were in the tent of witness, the priests and Levites also brought in.
And King Solomon and all the people of the sons of Israel were gathered before the ark, and they sacrificed oxen and sheep in numbers too great to count.
And the priests brought the ark of the covenant inside, to the place of the Debir, into the house of the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
And the wings were spread over the place where the ark stood, and the cherubim covered the ark and its holy things from above.
They stood out [?] above the holy things, and the ends of the consecrated holy things [?] could be seen facing the Debir, but they could not be seen from outside.
And nothing lay in the ark except the two tablets of the covenant, which he had placed in it at Horeb,
the covenant that the Lord made with the sons of Israel after they came out of the land of the Egyptians.
And when the priests came out of the holy place, the temple of the Lord was filled with a cloud.
And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the temple was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Then Solomon began to speak and said: "The Lord said that he would dwell sheltered in thick cloud. I have built him a temple as a dwelling-place for his throne forever."
And King Solomon turned around and blessed all Israel. And all the people of Israel were standing.
And Solomon said: Blessed is the Lord God of Israel today, who spoke with his own mouth about David my father, and has fulfilled it with his own hand, and said:
'From the day that I brought my people Israel out of the land of Egypt,
I have not chosen a city in any one of the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name; but I chose David to be leader of my people Israel.'
And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord.
And the Lord said to David my father: 'Because it came into your heart to build a house for my name, it is good that it came into your heart.
But you shall not build that house; your son, who will come forth from your loins, shall build it.
He shall build me a house for my name.' And the Lord has fulfilled the word that he spoke;
and he has raised me up in place of David my father and set me on the throne of Israel, as the Lord said; and I have built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
And I have prepared a place to set the ark of the covenant of the Lord, which the Lord made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord, facing it, and before all the people of Israel, and he lifted up his hands to heaven and said:
O Lord God of Israel, there is no one like you in the heavens or on the earth, you who have kept covenant and mercy
with your servant David my father, to whom you spoke and said; and you have fulfilled it with your hand, as it is this day.
And now, O Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him, when you said:
'You shall not lack a man before my face to judge on the throne of Israel, provided only that your sons take heed to their ways to walk before me.'
And now, O Lord God of Israel, let your word be confirmed which you spoke to your servant David my father.
But will God truly dwell among men? If the heavens of the heavens cannot contain you, how then shall this house that I have built for your name be a dwelling place for you?
And now, O Lord, look upon the prayer of your servant, O Lord God of Israel, to hear the prayer of your servant, who stands before you, with you, today.
May your eyes be open to look day and night upon this place, of which you said:
'My name shall be there,' so as to hear the prayer with which your servant now entreats you in this place day and night.
And hear the voice of your servant and of your people Israel, who will worship you in this place;
and may you hear in the place of your dwelling in the heavens, and grant forgiveness for whatever each person has sinned against his neighbour.
And if anyone takes up a curse to curse someone, and confesses before the altar of this temple, then may you hear from heaven,

and act, and judge among the people of Israel: requite the lawlessness of the lawless, bringing the recompense of his ways upon his own head, and justify the righteous, rewarding him according to his righteousness.

And when your people Israel are defeated [?] before their enemies, because they have sinned against you, and they turn to you and confess your name, and pray and make supplication to you in this temple,
then hear them from heaven, forgive the sins of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that you gave to their fathers. When the rain is withheld, so that there is no rain,
when they sin against you, and pray in this place, and confess your name, and turn from their sins when you have humbled them,
then hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your servants and of your people Israel. Show them the good ways to walk in, and give rain to your land,
which you gave to your people as an inheritance. And if there is famine in the land, or pestilence, or blight from burning, or caterpillar, or locust,
or venom [?], or if an enemy oppresses them in one of their cities, whatever calamity and whatever sickness there is, whatever request and prayer
is made by any person or by all your people Israel, when each person knows the pain of his own heart and stretches out his hands toward this temple,
then hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and forgive. Deal with each according to his ways, since you know his heart, for you alone know the hearts of all people,
so that they may fear you all the days they live on the face of the land that you gave to our fathers.
And the foreigner who is not of your people Israel, but has come from a distant land,
where your glorious name has been heard of, and your great and mighty hand, and your outstretched arm,
when they come and worship at this place, then hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and do according to all
that the foreigner asks of you, so that all the nations of the earth may know your name,
and so that your people Israel may fear you and may know that your name is called upon this temple that I have built.
And if your people go out to battle against their enemies, by the way on which you send them,
and they pray to the name of the Lord toward the city that you have chosen and toward this temple that I have built for your name,
then hear from heaven their prayer and their supplication, and grant them justice and forgiveness for the sins they have committed against you, for there is no one who does not sin.
And if you bring disaster upon them and hand them over to their enemies, and their captors carry them away captive to the land of the enemies, whether far or near,
and they take it to heart in the land to which they were carried captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wickedness,'
and they turn back with all their heart and with all their strength in the land of the enemies to which they were carried captive,
and they pray to you toward [?] their own land, which you gave to their fathers, and toward this city that you have chosen, and toward this temple
that I have built for your name, then hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, their prayer and their supplication. Grant them justice and forgive their wrongdoings,
the sins they committed against you and all the insults with which they insulted you. Make their captors take pity on them, and show them mercy,
for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace.
And let your eyes and your ears be attentive to the prayer of your servant Israel, to hear them according to their supplication.
For you chose me as your inheritance out of all the peoples of the earth, as you told Moses your servant when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord, Lord.
At that time Solomon began to speak, and he spoke about the temple when he had finished it:
"The Lord set the sun in the heavens, and he said he would dwell in the cloud: 'Build me a beautiful house, to dwell in it in newness.'"
Look, all this is written in the book of the singers. And when Solomon had finished all this prayer and petition to the Lord,
he rose up before the altar of the Lord, where he had been kneeling on his knees with his hands lifted up toward heaven.
And he stood up, turned, and blessed all the people of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
"Blessed is the Lord God today, who has given rest to his people Israel in keeping with everything he said,
which he spoke, and not a word [?] of the people has failed of all his words that he spoke to Moses his servant.
May the Lord be with us. May he not abandon us to our hearts turning away from him, but let us walk in all his ways and keep all his commandments that he gave our fathers.
And may these words of mine, which I pray before the Lord my God, be there day and night, so that he does justice for me, this servant of yours, and does justice for your people Israel day and night,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that you are the Lord God, and there is no other besides you.
May our minds be fully devoted to the Lord our God, to walk blamelessly according to his commands and to keep his statutes, as on this very day."
And the king and all Israel with him were offering sacrifices before the Lord.
And King Solomon made the offering of peace offerings. He offered to the Lord twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred twenty thousand sheep.
And the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.
On that day the king consecrated the court in front of the temple of the Lord, because there he offered the whole burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings,
because the bronze table that stood before the Lord was too small and could not hold the whole burnt offerings and the peace offerings.
And on that day Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Hamath
as far as the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God at the temple that he had built.
They ate and drank and rejoiced before the Lord our God seven days and seven nights.
On the eighth day he sent the people away. They blessed the king and went each to his own home with joy of heart, glad for all the good things
that the Lord had done for David his servant and for his people Israel.
This I write to you:
And then there was the dedication:
More than the disk of the sun: your altar, O God: for they are beloved:
O God of our fathers and Lord of mercies, who made all things by your word,
and by your wisdom formed man, so that he should have dominion over the creatures made by you, and govern the world in holiness and righteousness, and pronounce judgment with uprightness of heart:
give me the wisdom that stands beside your thrones, and do not cast me out from among your servants, for I am your servant and the son of your handmaid,
a weak man, of short life, lacking in understanding of judgment and of the law.
For even if someone is perfect among the sons of men, without your wisdom he is counted as nothing.
You chose me to be king of your people and judge of your sons and daughters.
And you told me to build a temple on your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of your dwelling, in the likeness of the holy tabernacle which you prepared from the beginning.
And with you is your wisdom, which knows your works and was present when you made the world, and she knows what is pleasing in your eyes and what is right in your commandments.
Send her forth from your holy heavens and from the thrones of your glory; send her, so that she may be with me and labour with me, and I may know what is pleasing before you.
For she knows and understands all things, and she will guide me in my deeds in holiness and guard me with her glory.
And my works will be acceptable, and I will judge your people with righteousness, and I will be worthy of the thrones of my father.
For what man can know the counsel of God, or into whose heart will it come what the Lord wills?
For the thoughts of mortals are timid, and our plans are liable to fall.
For the corruptible body weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling burdens [?] the mind that is full of thoughts.
For we hardly understand the things of the earth, and what lies under our feet we find out with labour; but who can search out the things in the heavens?
And who could understand your counsel, unless you had given wisdom to all [?] and sent your holy spirit from on high?
And so the paths of those on earth were set straight, and people were taught by your goodness.
And they were saved by your wisdom.
And it came to pass in that year:
We have an altar: Praise befits you;
Then Jesus said to the people:
Lord, I have loved the beauty: My feet have stood:
Thus says the Lord of all:
Give thanks to him for all things:
After this Jesus crossed over:
Let us enter the gates. Shout to God, all [the earth].
I will go in before the altar. I will confess you [with?] blessing [?]. But I am like an olive [tree?] [?]. I will confess you, for you have done [it].
[Help?] us [?], O God our Savior.
A hymn befits you. For your name's sake, O Lord, be merciful. To you, O Lord, I have lifted up [my soul].
Let my sighing come in before you. Help me quickly. Come, let us worship. We are his people.
O Lord, your mercy is forever, O Lord. If [you mark] iniquities…
From the depths we cry out. Where are [your] mercies? Mercy and truth shall go [before you].
Thus says the Lord God, the Mighty One of Israel, the Lord of Hosts:
Woe to the mighty ones of Israel, for my wrath will not cease against my adversaries, and I will execute judgment on my enemies;
and I will lay my hand upon you and refine you pure. But I will destroy the disobedient, and I will remove all the lawless from you, and I will humble all the proud.
And I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After this you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful city, Zion.
For her captives will be saved with justice and with mercy. And the sinners and the lawless will be crushed together, and those who have forsaken the Lord will be destroyed.

For they will be ashamed of their idols, which they desired, and they will be ashamed of their carved images, which they made, and they will be ashamed of their gardens, which their hearts longed for.
For they will be like terebinths whose leaves have fallen, and like a garden that has no water.
And their strength will be like a strand of tow, and their works like sparks of fire. The lawless and the sinners will burn together, and there will be no one to quench [the fire].
For in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be made manifest, and the house of God on the top of the mountains, and it will be raised above all the hills, and all the nations will come there.
And many peoples will come and say: "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will tell us his way, and we will walk in it."
For the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
And he will judge between the peoples and rebuke many people. And they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles;
and nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will no longer learn war.
And now you, O house of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.
For he has forsaken his people, the house of Jacob, because their land was filled with divination as at the beginning, like that of the foreigners, and they bore many children of foreigners.
For their land was filled with gold and silver, and there is no number to their chariots.
And their land was filled with the abominations of their hands, and they worshipped what their fingers had made.
And the common man bowed down and the great man was humbled, and I will not forgive them.
And now enter into the rock and hide in the earth from the face of the fear of the Lord and from the glory of his might.
For the eyes of the Lord are lofty, but man is lowly. The righteousness of men shall be humbled, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
God is with us.
Know this, you nations, and be defeated. Listen, to the end of the earth: you who have grown strong, be defeated. If you grow strong again, you will be defeated again.
Whatever plan you devise, God will bring it to nothing. The word you speak will not stand with you, for God is with us.
Thus says the Lord: with a strong hand, concerning those who are disobedient and the walking in the way of this people. And they say:
"Do not call it 'harsh,' for everything this people says is harsh. Do not fear what they fear, and do not be terrified.
Sanctify the Lord himself, and he shall be your fear. If you trust in him, he will be a sanctuary for you,
and you will not strike your foot against a stone or against a stumbling-block in your path, and no stumbling will befall you.
But the house of Jacob is like a snare in the ravines, for those lurking in dens in Jerusalem.
Therefore many among them shall grow powerless. They shall fall and be crushed, and men shall be struck down for destruction.
Then those who were binding and sealing the law, so that no one should learn it, will be exposed."
Then he said: "I will remain and wait for God, who has turned his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will put my hope in him.
Behold, I and these children of mine whom God has given me. It shall be a sign and a portent against the house of Israel from the Lord God of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion."
Therefore thus says the Lord of Hosts (Sabaoth):
"Do not be afraid of the Assyrians, my people who dwell in Zion. He will strike you with a rod, and I will bring a blow upon you, so that you see the way of Egypt.
For in a little while my wrath against you will cease, but my anger will be against their wrath.
God will raise up against them a torment like the blow against Midian in the place of distress, and his anger will be on the way by the sea toward Egypt.
And in that day his yoke will be taken from your neck and the fear of him from you, and his yoke will be broken off your shoulders.
For he will come to the city of Aggai, pass through Mageddo, and lay down his equipment at Michmash.
That hand [?] will pass on and reach Gibeon and will turn about. Fear will seize the city of Saul.
The daughter of Gallim will flee. Laish will hear, Anathoth will hear. Madmenah and its inhabitants will be dismayed. Let them pray by day;
they will plead to stop on the way. With a gesture of the hand, the daughter of Zion appeals to the mountains and the hills that were in Jerusalem.
Behold, the Lord of Hosts (Sabaoth) will make the created ones tremble with might, and the lofty will be crushed with disgrace.
Those who live in luxury will be brought low, and the lofty will fall by the sword, and Lebanon will fall with its loftiness."
O Lord our God, we glorify you, we sing praise to your name, you who have done wonderful deeds;
May the counsel of old be true, O Lord, for you have thrown cities down to the ground, strong cities, so that the foundations of the ungodly might fall; the city will not be rebuilt for ever.
Therefore a poor people will bless you, and the cities of oppressed men will bless you,
for you have become a helper to every lowly city, and a shelter to the faint-hearted [?] in their need. You have rescued them from wicked men,
a shelter to the thirsty and to the faint-hearted, men who are despised. For faint-hearted men suffer thirst in Zion because of the ungodly men to whom you have handed us over.
And the Lord of hosts will do this for all the nations: on this mountain, Zion, they will drink wine and anoint themselves with ointment.
And they will be given on this mountain. Let all this be given to the nations, for this counsel is directed at all the nations. It has swallowed up.
Death prevailed, and God again took away every falsehood [?] from every face, the reproach of his people, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
And they will say on that day: "Behold our God, in whom we hoped; and we rejoiced in his salvation."
You will see the king in glory, and your eyes will see the land from far away, and your soul will meditate on fear.
Where are the scribes? Or where are the counsellors? Where is the one who counted them?
The small and the great, with whom he did not take counsel, not by a loud voice; so that it would not hear. The people have been brought to nothing, and the one who hears has no understanding.
Behold, Zion, the city of our salvation! Your eyes will see, Jerusalem, rich city, tents
that will not be shaken, and the pegs of its tent will not be moved for all time, and its cords will not be broken.
For the name of the Lord is great upon you; it will be a place for you where there are rivers and broad and wide channels.
You will not travel that way, and do not let your ships go. For our God is great; the Lord will not pass us by. The Lord is our judge, the Lord is our ruler,
the Lord is our king, the Lord is our saviour, and he himself will save us.
But you, Israel, are my servant; you, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham, whom I have loved,
you whom I took by the hand from the ends of the earth and called from its watchtowers, and I said to you: "You are my servant; I have chosen you and I will not forsake you."
Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not go astray. For I am the one who has strengthened you, helped you, and upheld you with my righteous right hand.
Behold, all your enemies will be ashamed and put to disgrace, for they will become as if they had never existed, and all who bring judgement against you will perish.
You will seek the men who treated you with contempt and will not find them, for they will become as nothing, and your wars will be no more.
For I am the Lord, who took hold of your right hand and said to you: "Do not be afraid."
My child Jacob, and you, my few men of Israel, I will help you, says the Lord, your Redeemer, the God of Israel.
Behold, I have made you like a cart wheel for threshing, like a new saw, and you will thresh the mountains, grind the hills fine, and make them like dust.
And you will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away. But you will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel and be glad.
And the poor and the needy will rejoice. For they will seek water, and there will be none, and their tongue has dried up with thirst.
I am the Lord God; I will hear them, I, the God of Israel, and I will not forsake them,
but I will make rivers flow upon them, and I will make springs in the midst of the plains, the desert into pools of water, and streams of water will flow in the thirsty land.
And in the waterless land I will make the fir and the box tree and the myrtle and the cypress and the poplar grow,
For they shall see and know and understand and believe together that the hand of the Lord made all this, and the Holy One of Israel revealed it.
It is not that I have now called you, Jacob, nor have I wearied you, Israel;
you did not bring me anything of your sacrifices, nor did you glorify me with your offerings; I did not make you serve me with offerings, nor did I weary you over incense;
nor did you buy me fragrant incense with silver, nor did I desire the fat of your sacrifices; instead, your sins and your falsehoods stood before you.
I am the one who wipes out your iniquities for my own sake, and I will no longer remember your sins.
But you, remember, and let us go to judgment together. State your iniquity first, so that you may be justified.
Your fathers sinned first, and your rulers acted lawlessly against me.
And your rulers defiled my sanctuary; I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to reproach.
But you, hear, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
Thus says the Lord God, who made you and who formed you from your mother's womb:
I have helped you.
Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad, for God has had mercy on Israel;
blow the trumpet, foundations of the earth; and cry out with joy, mountains and hills and all their trees, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel shall glorify him.
Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: I am the Lord, who made all things, and I alone stretched out the heavens and made the earth firm.
Who else, then, will bring it to nothing? I am the one who brings to nothing the signs of the ventriloquists and the divinations of the heart;
I have turned the wise backward and made their counsels foolish; and I will confirm the word of my servant, and the counsel of his messengers shall prove true;
for it is he who says to Jerusalem, 'Be inhabited,' and 'Let the cities of Judah be built, and let its desolate places be raised up';
who says to the abyss, 'Be laid waste!' and 'I will dry up your rivers'; who says to Cyrus, 'Be wise!'
'and all your will shall be done'; who says to Jerusalem, 'Be rebuilt!' and 'I will lay the foundation of my holy temple.'
Thus says the Lord our God to my anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held,
to make the nations submit to him; and I will shatter the strength of kings; I will open gates before him, and his cities shall not be shut.
I went before him and leveled the mountains, and I broke in pieces the gates of bronze and shattered the bolts of iron.
And I will give you the treasures of darkness, hidden ones, and I will open to you unseen ones, so that you may know that I am the Lord God,
who called you by your name, the name of Israel [?], for the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, and I received you.
For you did not know me; for I am the Lord your God, and there is no one besides me, and you did not know me,
so that those of the rising of the sun and those of the setting of the sun may know that there is no one besides me.
Hear this, O house of Israel, you who are called by the name of Israel and who have come forth from Judah,
who swear by the name of the Lord God of Israel and who make mention of God, but not in truth and not in righteousness,
and who trust in the holy city [?] of God, with the support of Israel [?]. The Lord Almighty is his name.
I told you the former things long ago, and you were made to hear them from my mouth; I did them suddenly, and they came to pass.
I know that you are stubborn, and your neck is a sinew of iron, and your forehead is bronze.
And I told you at that very time, and I made you hear it before it came upon you, so that you would not say, 'My idols did this for me';
so that you would not say, 'The carved images and the molten images commanded me.' You heard this, and you did not understand.
But now I make you hear the new things as well, which are to come from now on.
And you did not know them. They have been made now, and not at that time, and not in former days, and you did not hear of them. Do not say, 'Yes, I know them.'
You neither heard them nor knew them, and I did not open your ears from the beginning, for I knew that you would deal utterly treacherously, and you were called lawless from your mother's womb.
For my name's sake I will show you my anger, and I will bring my glory upon you, so that I may destroy you.
Behold, I have sold you, but not for silver, and I have rescued you from the furnace of poverty.
I do this for you for my own sake, because my name is being profaned, and I will not give my glory to another.
Hear me, O Jacob and Israel, whom I have called: I am the first, and I am forever.
My hand laid the foundations of the earth, and my right hand established the heavens. I called them, and they stood forth together; and they will gather and hear.
Who will tell them this? Out of love for you, may your will be done, to take away from Babylon the race of the Chaldeans.
I spoke, and I called, and I brought him, and I made his ways prosper. [?] to me, and hear me.
From the beginning I did not speak this in secret; when it was coming to pass, I was there. And now the Lord has sent me, and his Spirit.
Thus says your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord your God; I have shown you the way to find, the way in which you should walk.
If only you had listened to my commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea; and your offspring would have been like the sand of the sea.
and your offspring like the dust of the earth. Even now you will not be wiped out, and your name will not perish before me.
Proclaim a voice of joy, and make this heard. Speak it to the ends of the earth; say:
"The Lord has redeemed Jacob, his servant." They did not thirst in the wilderness when he led them through the waterless land. He split the rock for them and water flowed out, and my people drank.
"There is no joy for the ungodly," said the Lord. Listen to me, you islands, and pay attention, you nations: this is what will come about after a long time.
I tell you, said the Lord: he called me from the womb, and from my mother's belly he gave me my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp [?] sword, and he hid [?] me in the shelter of his hand. He made me like a chosen arrow and covered me in his quiver. And he said to me:
"You are my servant, Israel, and I went [?] toward you." And I said: "Have I then laboured in vain, for nothing? Have I worn myself out and given my strength for nothing [?]?"
Therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my labours are before God.
And now thus says the Lord, who formed me as his servant to gather Jacob and Israel to him: "Let them be gathered." And I shall go [?] before the Lord, and my God will be my strength.
And he said to me: "It is a great thing for you to be called my servant, to establish the tribes of Jacob and to gather the scattered ones of Israel.
Behold, I have given you as a covenant for the peoples and a light for the nations, and you will be for salvation to the end of the world."
Thus says the Lord: "In a time of favour I will hear you, and on the day of salvation I will help you.
I formed you and made you a covenant for the nations, so that you may establish the land and inherit [?] the heritage of the wilderness,
and so that you may command the prisoners to come out of prison, and bring out those who sit in darkness and in the shadows of death.
They will graze along every road, and every place will be their pasture. They will not hunger or thirst or grow weary; no scorching wind will strike them, and the sun will not harm them.
For the one who had mercy on them will comfort them and lead them to springs of water.
And I will make every mountain a road, and every place a pasture for them.
Now then, some will come from far away, some from the north, some from the direction of the sea [?], and some from the land of Persia."
Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad. Let the mountains break out in joy and the hills in righteousness, for he has had mercy on his people and comforted the lowly among his people.
But Zion said: "The Lord has forsaken me, and my God has forgotten me."
Will a woman forget her child, or have no mercy on the offspring of her womb?
Even if a woman should forget these, I will not forget you, said the Lord.
Behold, I have inscribed your walls on my hands, and you are always before my eyes.
You will soon be rebuilt by the very ones who tore you down, and those who laid you waste will quickly go away from you. Lift up your eyes and see all your offspring.
For behold, all your children have gathered together, come, and surrounded you. As I live, says the Lord.
For you will put on all these like garments and adorn yourself with them, as a bride adorns herself with her ornaments.
For the desolate places of your land will now come and press upon you for their rebuilding.
They will spread out, grow wide and multiply, and those who were harming you and swallowing you up will go far away from you.
And your children, whom you had lost, will say to you: "Make the place wide for us to live in, for we are cramped."
Then you will begin to speak in your heart and say: "Who, then, bore these to me?
For I am a widow, barren and without an heir, a stranger and left behind. Who, then, brought these up for me? I was abandoned and despised, so where were these?"
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will stretch out my hand over the nations and raise up my sign over the islands. I will bring my sons in their bosom, and they will bring your daughters,
and princes will be your nurses, and their wives will carry your children.
With their faces to the ground they will bow down to you and lick the dust beneath your feet.
And you will know that I am the Lord, and that none who wait for me will be put to shame.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness and seek justice.
Look to the solid rock from which you were cut, and to the deep pit from which you were dug out.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who gave birth to you, for he was only one, and I called him, blessed him and multiplied him.
And now I will comfort you, Zion, and I will comfort all your desolate places, and I will make all your deserts
like a garden of delight, and its western parts like the garden of God. Joy and gladness will be in it, thanksgiving and the voice of praise.
Listen to me, listen to me, my people, and you kings, give ear to me, for the law will go out from me, and my judgment will be a light to the nations.
My righteousness is coming near soon, and my righteousness will go out like light, and the nations will hope in my arm. The islands wait for me and hope in my arm.
Lift up your eyes to heaven and look at the earth, for the heaven is set firm like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment,
and its inhabitants will pass away like them. But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will not fail.
Listen to me, you who know justice, my people, who have my law in your hearts.
Do not fear people's reproach, and do not be dismayed by their contempt, for they will wear out like garments worn for a long time,
and they will be eaten like wool by moths. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation from generation to generation.
Awake, awake, Jerusalem, and put on the strength of your arm. Awake as in the beginning of days.
Are you not the one who laid waste the sea and the many waters of the abyss?
Who made the expanse of the sea a road for the rescued and the redeemed to cross over?
For by the Lord they shall return and come to Zion with joy and gladness forever.
And upon their head shall be praise, and gladness shall overtake them; pain and sorrow shall depart.
I am he who comforts you, I myself. Know what you were: you were afraid of mortal man and of the son of man, who wither like grass.
You forgot God your Creator, who made the heaven and founded the earth.
You were afraid continually, all the days, of the face of the wrath of your oppressor, as he planned to take you away.
Now where is that God of your oppressor? For he shall not stand against your salvation, nor shall he linger.
For I am the Lord your God, who stirred up the sea, and its waves roar. God and Almighty is my name.
And I will put my words in your mouth, and under the shadow of my hand I will cover you, the hand by which I set up the heavens and founded the earth, and I said to Zion:
"You are my people."
Awake, awake, arise, Jerusalem,
you who drank from the hand of the Lord the cup of his wrath; and the bowl of my anger you drank and drained empty.
And there was no one to comfort you among all your children whom you bore;
and there is no one who took you by the hand among all your sons whom you raised up.
These two things are to call [?] to you; who will grieve with you? Downfall and destruction, famine and sword.
Who will comfort you? Your sons, who are given up to ruin, who have been stretched out [?] at the head of every road,
like a half-boiled beet [?], who are full of the wrath of the Lord, undone by the Lord your God.
For instead of the thorn the cypress shall spring up for you, and instead of the nettle the myrtle. And the Lord shall be for a name and for a sign forever, and it shall not fail.
Thus says the Lord: Keep justice and do righteousness, for my salvation has arrived and drawn near; and now is the time for my mercy to come.
Blessed is the man who does this, and the person who holds fast to it.
Thus says the Lord: Now cry out:
Is the hand of the Lord not able to save? Or has his ear grown dull so as not to hear?
But it is your sins that separate you from God, and because of your sins he has turned his face away from you so as not to accept you.
For your hands are stained with blood and your fingers with sin, your lips with lawlessness, and your tongue devises falsehood.
No one speaks for justice, and there is no true judgment. They trust in vanity and speak sin, for they conceive pain and give birth to vanity.
They have broken asps' eggs and weave a spider's web; and whoever was about to eat those eggs broke one and found a scorpion and a viper inside it.
Their web will be their clothing, and they will not clothe themselves with their works, for their works are works of lawlessness.
Their feet run to evil, and they are quick to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are the thoughts of fools;
ruin and misery are in their ways. They have not known the way of peace, and there is no [?] in their ways.
For the paths they walk in are crooked, and they do not know peace.

Therefore justice has gone far from them, and righteousness will not reach them. They waited for light, and it became darkness for them; they waited for the dawn, and they walked in the untimely hour.
They groped for the wall like the blind, and like those who have no eyes, so they [?]. They fell at midday as if at midnight.
Like dying bears they panted out their breath, and like doves they [?] together. We waited for justice, and there is no salvation; it has [?] far from us,
for our lawless deeds before you are many, our sins have stood against us, our lawless deeds are among us, and we have recognized our falsehood.
We became ungodly and lied to God, and we turned away from following our God.
We spoke falsehood and became lawless. We conceived them in the womb; we practised false words from our heart,
and we turned away from following justice. We turned our back on judgment, and righteousness was taken far from us, for truth [?] from their thoughts, and they could not walk in the straight way.
Truth was taken from them, and their mind turned away from understanding. [?] saw this, and it did not please him, for there was no justice.
He looked, and there was no one; he considered, and there was no helper. So he prevailed over them with his own arm and established his mercy.
He put on righteousness like a coat of mail, set his salvation on his head like a helmet, and put on the garment of vengeance,
with which he will repay his enemies with reproach as their due. Those in the west will fear the name of the Lord, and those in the east his glorious name.
For the name of the Lord will come forth like a fierce river.
A deliverer will come for Zion's sake and will turn ungodliness away from Jacob, said the Lord Almighty.
And this is my covenant with them, says the Lord: my Spirit, which is upon you, and my words, which I have put in your mouth,
will not fail from your mouth or from the mouth of your descendants, said the Lord, from now on and forever.
Lord, have mercy on me, for we [?] you;
let my soul rejoice in the Lord.
For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation and the ornament of joy. He set a crown on me as on a bridegroom, and he adorned me with jewels like a bride. And as the earth
makes its fruit grow, and as a garden makes its seed sprout, so the Lord will make his salvation shine forth before all the nations.
Now for Zion's sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until my righteousness goes forth like light and my salvation blazes like a light;
and the nations will see my righteousness, and kings will marvel at my glory. You will be called by a new name, the name the Lord himself will give you.
And you shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
And you shall no longer be called Forsaken, and your land shall no longer be called Desolate. For you shall be called by my name, and your land shall be called Inhabited World.
And as a young man settles down with a virgin, so shall your sons settle down with you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride, so shall the Lord rejoice over you.
And on your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen over you all day and all night, who shall never be silent in making mention of the Lord.
For there is no one like you. If you prosper, the Lord will also make Jerusalem renowned on the earth.
The Lord, judge over the house of Israel, will send upon us according to his mercy and according to the righteousness of his righteousness.
And he said: "Are my children not mine?" And they will not despise me. And he became their savior from all their affliction.
For it was not an apostle, nor an angel from heaven, but the Lord himself who saved them, protected them, and lifted them up all the days of old.
But they became disobedient and angered his Holy Spirit. And he turned against them as an enemy; the Lord himself fought against them. And he remembered those days of old:
Where is he who brought up the shepherd of the sheep? And where is he who put the Holy Spirit among them?
He who led Moses by his right hand, with the arm of his glory?
He [?] the waters before him (perhaps "divided"), to make for himself an everlasting name.
He led them out of the deep like horses through the wilderness, and they did not grow weary, and like [?] through the plain.
And a spirit came from the Lord and guided them. Thus: "Lead your people and make for yourself a glorious name."
Turn, O Lord, and look down from your holy temple of your glory.
Where is the abundance of your mercies and your compassion, when you bore with us, O Lord?
For you are our father, O Lord, for Abraham did not know us. But you are our father. Save us, for from the beginning your name has been upon us.
Why, O Lord, do you lead us astray from your way and harden our hearts, so that we do not fear you?
Turn back for the sake of your servants and the tribes of your inheritance, so that we too may inherit some small part of your holy mountain.
We have become as we were at the beginning, when you did not rule over us and your name was not called upon us.
If you open the heavens, trembling will seize the mountains because of you, and they will melt as wax melts before fire,
and fire will burn up your enemies, and your name will be made manifest among those who hate you. Before your face the nations will tremble, [and the?] mountains.
From of old we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen, any God besides you.
Your works are true, for there was mercy for those who wait for you; for mercy would come to meet those who do justice, and they remembered your ways.
Behold, you were angry, and we sinned; and for this reason we went astray. And we all became unclean.
