All our righteousness is like the rag of a menstruating woman, and we have all fallen like leaves because of our iniquities.
And so the wind has carried us away, and there is no one who calls on your name or remembers to follow after you.
For you have turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins.
And now, Lord, you are our father, and we are all clay, the work of your hands.
Do not be utterly angry with us, Lord, and do not remember our sins at this time. Now look upon us, for we are all your people.
And the cities of your holiness [?]
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold [?]
Now hear the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his words.
Call those who hate you and those who have despised you your brothers, so that your name may be glorified and made manifest in your face, and they may be put to shame.
A voice of crying from the city, a voice from the temple, and again a voice of retribution and repayment to his enemies.
Before the pains of childbirth, and before the labour pains came, she was delivered and bore a male child.
Who has heard such a thing, or who has come near to such a thing? Has the earth ever conceived in a single day, or a nation been born all at once? For Zion conceived and bore her children.
But I gave such a hope, and you did not remember me, said the Lord. Did I not make both the one who bears and the barren woman? says the Lord your God.
Rejoice together, Jerusalem, and gather in her with joy, all you who love her, all you who mourned for her,
so that you may nurse and be satisfied at the breasts of her consolation, so that you may nurse and delight in the entrance of her glory. For thus says the Lord:
Behold, I will turn toward them like a river of your peace, and like a torrent they will bring the glory of the nations to you.
Their children will be carried on the shoulder and comforted on their knees.
As a mother comforts her children, so I will comfort you, and Jerusalem will be comforted.
And when you see this, your hearts will rejoice, and your bones will sprout like flowers.
And the hand of the Lord will be revealed to those who fear him, and he will be angry with the lawless.
Return to me, you dwelling of Israel, says the Lord, and I will not set my face against you to do you harm,
for I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not hold a grudge against you forever. But know and understand your disobedience to the Lord,
for you have sinned against your God and scattered your ways toward strangers under every leafy tree, and you did not listen to my voice, says the Lord.
Return, you apostate sons, says the Lord, for I will be lord over you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion,
and I will give you shepherds, the desire of your heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge.
"And it shall be, if you multiply and increase on the earth," said the Lord, "in those days," says the Lord, "they shall no longer speak
of the ark of the covenant of the Holy One of Israel. It shall not come to mind, nor shall it be named among them [?], nor shall they seek it any more.
In those days and at that time they [?] shall call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord,
and all the nations shall gather there to Jerusalem in the name of the Lord, and they shall no longer walk wickedly after the will of their heart.

In those days the house of Judah shall gather with the house of Israel, and they shall come together from the north, out of all the lands, to the land [?] which I gave as an inheritance to their fathers.
And I said: 'So be it, Lord.' I will establish you as a son and give you a chosen land, a renowned inheritance of God the Almighty, among the nations; and I said:
You shall call me Father, and you shall not turn away from me.
Return, children, return, and I will heal you of your brokenness."
"Behold, we entreat you, for you are the Lord our God.
For truly the hills and their powers were a lie, but from you, the Lord, comes the salvation of the house of Israel.
And falsehood has consumed the labors of our fathers from their youth: their sheep and their calves, their sons and their daughters.
We have lain down in our shame, and our own mind has covered us, for we have sinned before our Lord, we and our fathers, from our youth until this very day,
and we have not listened to the voice of our God."
"It was mine [?]; and let them turn to you, but you shall not turn to them.
And I will make you to this people like a strong wall of bronze; they will fight against you but shall not prevail over you, for I am with you to save you,
said the Lord, "and I will deliver you from the hands of the wicked."
O Lord, my strength, my helper and my refuge in the day of evil, to you the nations shall come from the ends of the earth and say:
"Our fathers acquired idols in vain, and there is no profit in them. If a man makes gods for himself, they are not gods."
"Therefore, behold, I will make known to them my power, and they shall know that my name is the Lord."
Cursed be the man who puts his hope in man and does not strengthen the hand of his arm upon him [?], and whose heart has turned away from the Lord.
He shall be like a wild shrub [?] in the desert, which does not see when good comes; he shall dwell in famine and in a salty desert land that is not inhabited.

And blessed be the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord is his hope. He is like a fruitful tree by the water's edge that spreads its roots into the depths, and it does not fear when the heat comes.
And there shall be [?] upon it; in a year of drought it shall not fear, and it shall not fail to bear fruit. The heart is deep beyond all things, and it is man; who can know it?
I am the Lord, who examines the heart and the kidneys, to repay each person according to his way and according to the fruit of his deeds.
Thus says the Lord God of Israel, and he said:
Write down for yourself, in a book, everything I have commanded you. For behold, the days are coming, says the Lord,
when I will bring back the captives of my people Israel and Judah, said the Lord. I will bring them back to the very place that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.
These are the words that the Lord God of Israel and of Judah spoke.
Thus says the Lord: You have heard a sound of fear. There is fear, and there is no peace among them.
Ask, then [?], and see: has a male [?] given birth? And why the fear that has seized your loins and your life?
For I saw a man with his hands on his loins like a woman giving birth. Every face has turned and has been changed into ruin.
For that day is great, and there is no other time like it for Jacob, and he will be saved out of it. And on that day, said the Lord of hosts, it will happen that
I will break the yoke on their neck and burst their bonds. They will no longer serve foreigners. Instead they will serve the Lord and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
But you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, and do not tremble, Israel. For behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring from their captivity.
Jacob will return and be at rest and rejoice, and no one will make him afraid. For I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.
For I will make an end of all the nations among which I have scattered you, but I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you with justice.
Thus says the Lord: Let Jacob rejoice! Be glad and exult over the head of the nations. Proclaim it and give praise, and say: The Lord has saved his people, the remnant of Israel.
Behold, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the ends of the earth at the feast of Passover, and a great people will have children among them:
the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the woman giving birth, gathered together, and they will return here. They went out with weeping, and they will comfort them and bring them back.
They will pass along streams of water and on a straight road, and they will not go astray on it. For I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the Lord, you nations, and tell it to the distant islands [?]: He who scattered Israel will gather him himself, and will guard him as a shepherd guards his flock.
For the Lord has redeemed Jacob and rescued him from the hands of one stronger [?] than he.
They will come and rejoice and be glad on Mount Zion. They will come to the good things of the Lord, to a land of wheat and wine, of the produce of sheep and cattle.
Their soul will be like a fruitful tree [?], and they will hunger no more.
Young women will rejoice in the assembly, and old men will rejoice. I will turn their mourning into gladness, and they will be made joyful after their sorrow.
I will exalt the soul of the priests, the sons of Levi, and make it drunk with abundance, and I will fill my people with good things, said the Lord.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: They will again speak these words in the land of Judah and in its city, when I bring back its captives:
'Blessed is the Lord on his holy mountain.' Judah and all its cities will live there together, along with its farmers, and they will rejoice [?] with the flock.
For I have made every thirsty soul drink its fill, and I have satisfied every hungry soul with good things.

Because of this I woke up and looked, and my sleep had been sweet to me. Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Judah and the house of Israel with the seed of men and the seed of cattle.
And it shall be that, just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, to destroy, to bring harm and to ruin, so I will take thought over them to build up and to plant, says the Lord.
You who are [?], O Lord.
And now, behold, the Lord God of Israel has said about this city, of which you say, 'It will be given into the hand of Babylon by sword, by famine and by exile':
Behold, I will gather them from all the land where I scattered them in my anger, my wrath and my great fury. I will bring them back to this place and settle them in hope.
And they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
And I will give them understanding and a single way, so that they may fear me all their days, for their own good and for the good of their children after them.
And I will make them an everlasting covenant, from which I will not turn away after them, for they will do good. And I will put my fear in their heart,
so that they do not turn away from me. I will look on them to do them good, and I will plant them in that land in faithfulness, with all my heart.
For thus says the Lord: Just as I brought all this great evil on this people, so I will bring on them all the good that I am speaking about them.
And fields shall be bought in the land of which you say, 'It is impassable to men and to cattle, and it has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans.'
And they shall buy fields with silver. Write it in a deed and seal it, and they shall call witnesses in the land of Benjamin, for I will bring back their captives, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord, who made it, who created it and who establishes it; the Lord is his name.
Call out to me, and I will answer you and tell you great and mighty things that you do not know.
For thus says the Lord God of Israel about the houses of this city and the house of the king of Judah, which lies under an army and a siege mound [?] because of those who are coming
to fight the Chaldeans, to fill it with the corpses of the men whom I struck down in my anger. And I will turn my face away from them because of all their wickedness.
Behold, I will bring it [?] together, and I will heal them with healing. I will reveal to them [?] to hear, and I will make peace in faithfulness.

And I will bring back the captives of Judah and the captives of Israel, and I will build them up as before. I will cleanse them of all their falsehood, by which they sinned against me and turned away from me.
And it shall bring me joy, praise and holiness before all the earth, before everyone who hears of all the good
that I have done for them. They shall be afraid and shall be distressed because of all the good things and all the peace.
Thus says the Lord: There shall again be heard in this place, of which you say
that it is a waste without men and without cattle — the cities of Judah and the fields of Jerusalem, laid waste because there is no man, no inhabitant and no cattle —
the sound of rejoicing, the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, the voice of the bride, and the voice of those who say:
"Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever."
And pray for us to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his anger and his wrath have not turned away from us until this very day.
And read aloud this book, which I have sent to you, to make it known in the house before the Lord on feast days and on days of the appointed seasons, and say:
To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us shame of our faces, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
and to our kings and our priests and our prophets and our fathers, who sinned before you.
And we became disobedient to him and did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his commandments,
which he commanded us before our face, from the day the Lord brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt until this very day.
To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers shame of face, as it is this day,
according to what the Lord our God spoke concerning us: all the evil that has come upon us. And we did not entreat the face of the Lord, for each one to turn from the madness of his own evil heart.
And the Lord kept watch over the evils, which he brought upon us, for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he commanded us.
And we did not listen to his voice, to walk in his commandments, which he commanded us before our face.
And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand,
with signs and wonders and great power, and made for yourself a house [?] (probably for 'name'), as it is this day:
we have sinned, we have acted lawlessly, and we have been false toward you, O Lord God, in all your ordinances.
Let your anger turn away from us, for we are left few among the nations, there where you have scattered us.
Hear, O Lord, our prayer, and deliver us for your own sake.
Grant us favor before those who carried us captive, so that all the earth may know that you are our God, for your name is called upon Israel and upon his race.
O Lord, look down from your holy temple and take heed of us; incline your ear and hear us.
Open your eyes, for it is not the dead in hell, whose spirit has been taken from their bodies, who will give you glory and righteousness, our God;
but the soul that is grieved over greatness, that goes about bowed down and feeble, and whose eyes fail,
and the hungry soul will give you glory and righteousness, O Lord. For it is not on account of the righteous deeds of our fathers and our kings that we spread out [our plea for] your mercy,
O Lord our God; for you have sent your anger and your wrath upon us, as you spoke by the hand of your servants the prophets.
O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a heart in distress and a weary spirit cry out to you.
Hear, O Lord, and have mercy on us, for we have sinned before you. For you abide forever, and we perish forever.
O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear the prayer of the inhabitants of Israel,
who sinned before you, the sons of sin, who did not listen to the voice of the Lord God, and this evil has come upon us.
Do not remember the iniquity of our fathers, but at this time remember your hand, O Lord our God, and we will praise you, O Lord.
For this reason you have put the fear of you in our heart, so that we may call upon your name, and we will praise you in our captivity,
for in our heart we have turned away from all the iniquity of our fathers, who sinned before you. Behold, here we are in our captivity;
and behold, you have scattered us, to be a reproach and a curse, and liable for all the iniquity of our fathers, who turned away from you, our God.
Hear, O Israel,

the commandments of God, and listen so as to know understanding. Why is it, Israel, that you are in the land of your enemies, that you have grown old in a foreign land, that you are defiled along with the dead, that you are counted among those in Hades?
You have forsaken the mercy [?] of wisdom. If you had walked in the ways of God, you would have dwelt in peace in your land for everlasting times.
Learn where wisdom is, where understanding is, so that you may know along with it where long life is, where the light of the eyes and peace are.
Who has found her place and entered into her treasuries? Where are the rulers of the nations, and those who have dominion over the beasts of the earth,
who made sport with the birds of the heaven and stored up silver and gold, which men guard [?], and there is no end to their getting?
Those who worked silver and were full of care, and there is no searching out of their works? They were taken away and brought down to Hades, and others rose up in their place.
Young men saw the light and dwelt upon the earth, but they did not understand the way of knowledge;
nor did they know her paths, nor did they keep them; their sons went far astray from their way.
She was not heard of in Canaan, nor was she seen in Teman; nor did the sons of Hagar have understanding, who were upon the earth, the merchants of Merran and of Teman,
and the storytellers and the seekers of understanding. But they did not know the way of wisdom, and they did not remember her paths.
O Israel, how great is the name of the Lord, and how long is the place of his possession!
It is great, and there is no promise [?]; it is high and immeasurable.
Who has gone up into heaven and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?
Who has crossed over the sea and found her, and acquired her with choice gold? There is no one who knows her way, nor anyone who has come near her paths.
But the one who knows all things knows her by his understanding, he who prepared the earth for everlasting time and filled it with cattle,
with four-footed beasts; he who sends forth the kindreds [?], and it goes; he called it, and it obeyed him with trembling.
And the stars shone forth in their season and rejoiced. He called them, and they said: “Here we are.”
And they shone with joy for their Creator. This is our God; no other god shall be counted beside him.
He searched out the way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved.
After this she appeared upon the earth and lived among men. This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures,
…is life. But those who abandon it will be put to shame. Turn back, Jacob, and hold fast to it, and walk in the presence of the brightness of its light.
Do not give your glory to another, or what is better for you to a foreign nation.
Blessed are we, Israel, for what pleases God is made known among us.
Do not be afraid, my people, you memorial of Israel!
You were sold among the nations, but not for destruction. Because of God's anger you were handed over to my enemies, for you angered your Creator by sacrificing to demons and not to God.
You forgot the eternal God who raised you, and you also grieved Jerusalem, who nursed you. For she saw the wrath of God that came upon you from God, and she said:
"Listen, you who live in Zion: God has brought great mourning upon me, for I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting sent upon them.
For I raised them with joy, and I sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Let no one [?] over me, a widow left behind by many. I have been made desolate because of the sins of my children.
For they turned away from the law of their God and did not keep his ordinances. They did not walk in the way of his commandments, nor did they walk in righteousness on the paths of instruction.
Come, you sojourners of Zion, and let us remember the captivity of our sons, which the Everlasting sent upon them.
For he brought against them a nation from far away, foreign and shameless. They had no respect for the old and no pity for the young.
They led away the widow's beloved ones and left her alone, bereft of her daughters. What can I do to help you?
The one who brought the evil upon you will deliver you from the hands of your enemies.
Go, children, go, for I am left desolate.
I have taken off the garment of peace and put on the sackcloth of my supplication, and I will cry out to the Everlasting all my days.
Do not be afraid, children. Cry out to God, and he will deliver you from the power and the hand of the enemies.
For I have put my hope in the Everlasting for your salvation, and joy has come to me from the Holy One because of the mercy that will soon come to you from the Everlasting.
I sent you away with mourning and weeping, but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever.
Just as the sojourners of Zion have now seen your captivity, so they will soon see your salvation from God, which will come to you with the glory and brightness of the Everlasting.
Children, bear patiently the wrath that has come upon you from the Lord. Your enemy has persecuted you, but you will see their destruction and tread on their necks.
My delicate ones have travelled rough roads. They were led away like a flock carried off by the enemy.
Do not be afraid, my children. Cry out to God, for deliverance will come to you from the one who brought this upon you.
Just as your [?] (literally "scourging") was to stray from God, so now turn back tenfold to return and seek him.
For the one who brought the evil upon you will himself bring you everlasting joy with your salvation."
Do not be afraid, Jerusalem: the one who gave you your name will comfort you.
Wretched are those who did you evil and who rejoiced at your fall. Wretched are the cities that your children served.
Just as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad at your humiliation, so she will be grieved at her own desolation.
I will take away her joy in her great population, and I will turn her loud rejoicing into mourning.
For fire came down upon her from the Everlasting for many days, and demons shall dwell in her for a long time.
Look toward the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy that is coming to you from those who are on their way to you.
Look, those who were sent away from you are coming to you. They are coming, gathered from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
How lonely the city sits that was full of people! She has become like a widow among the nations; the ruler of cities has been made to pay tribute.
She wept bitterly in the night, with tears on her cheeks, and among all her lovers there was no one to comfort her. All her friends treated her with contempt and became her enemies.
Jerusalem was carried away captive because of her humiliation, from the rulers [?], from her servitude. She has settled among the nations and has found no rest.
All her pursuers overtook her. The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to her feast.
All her gates are destroyed, her priests groan, her virgins have been led away captive, and they are bitter within her.
Her oppressors have become her masters, and her enemies prosper, because the Lord has humbled them with the humiliation of their lawlessness.
Her little children went into captivity before the face of their oppressor. And all her beauty has departed from the daughter of Zion.
Their rulers became like rams that find no pasture, and they went out without strength before the face of the pursuer.
And Jerusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and all her precious things,
all that she had had since the days of old, when her people fell into the hand of her oppressors and there was no one to help her.
Her enemies saw her and laughed in their hostility. Israel committed grievous sin; therefore she has become [?] (literally "a profit").
All who had honoured her humiliated her, because they saw her shame. She herself groaned and turned away backward.
Her uncleanness is under her feet. She did not remember her end, and he brought her down utterly. There was no one to comfort her.
The Lord saw that the enemy had grown great. The oppressor stretched out his hands over all her precious things,
for she saw the nations entering her sanctuary, the very people you commanded not to enter your assembly.
All her people groan and search for bread. They gave their precious things for food, to keep themselves alive.
Look, O Lord, and see, for she has been treated with contempt.
Zion has stretched out her hands, and there is no one to comfort her.
The Lord gave orders concerning Jacob that his oppressors should be all around him. Jerusalem became like a woman sitting apart among them.
The Lord is righteous, for they rebelled against his mouth. Hear, all you people, and see my pain. My young women have gone into captivity.
I called to my lovers, but they despised me. My priests and my elders failed in the city, for they looked for food to revive their souls and did not find any.
See, O Lord, that I am in distress. My belly trembles, and my heart is turned over within me, for I have been made utterly bitter.
Outside, the sword has left me childless, as [?] death has done within the house.
Hear, for I groan, and there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my misfortune and rejoiced,
for you have done it. You have brought the day upon me and called it, and it has become "woe, woe" to me.
Let all their wickedness come before your face, and strip them as you have stripped me for all my sins, for my groans are many.
Therefore I will wait:
Why should a living man complain, a man about his sins?
Let us search out our ways, and he examined [?], and return to the Lord. Let us lift up our heart to the height of heaven.
We have sinned and become lawless, and you have not shown us favour. You have covered us with wrath and did not help us. You have killed us and did not seek us.
He covered himself with clouds because of sin, so that my eyes are shut and turned away [?]. You have placed us among the people.
All my enemies opened their mouths against me. Fear and [?] have come upon us, [?] and shattering.
My eyes have poured down streams of water over the shattering of the daughter of my people that has come upon me.
My eyes are afflicted, and I will not be silent, so that I may not be roused at all [?]. Let the Lord look down from heaven and see.
My eye will search within my soul more than all the daughters of my city.
They have hunted me down like prey:
The Lord has carried out his anger. He has poured out his furious wrath, lit a fire in Zion, and it has devoured her foundations.
The kings of the earth and all who live in the world did not believe that enemies and oppressors would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
Because of the sins of her prophets, who shed righteous blood, her watchmen were defiled in their going out.
They were polluted with blood, for they could not save themselves, and they grabbed hold of their garments.
"Depart from the unclean! Do not touch!" For they cried out and were defiled. Say among the nations: "They will no longer continue their sojourning."
The face of the Lord is their portion; he will not look upon them again.
They showed no respect for the priests and had no pity on the elders. While we still lived, our eyes failed, looking for help; we looked to what was vain.
We kept watching for a living nation; they hunted our little children, so that we could not walk in our streets.
Our time has drawn near, our days are fulfilled; the time has come. More than the eagles of the sky [?] — upon them [?] they lay in wait for us.
The breath of our face, Christ the Lord, was taken in their corruption, he of whom we said: "Under [his] shadow we shall live among the nations."
Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land, for the cup of the Lord will pass to you too; you will become drunk and vomit.
Your iniquities have come to an end, O daughter of Zion; he will not again send you into captivity.
The Lord has looked upon your wickedness, O daughter of Edom; he has revealed your iniquity.
For thus says the Lord to the house:
On that day I will set up:
The word of the Lord that came to Joel the son of Bethuel.
Hear this, you elders, and give ear, all who dwell in the land: has anything like this happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Tell your children about it, and let their children tell another generation.
What the plague left, the locust ate; what the locust left, the fly ate; and what the fly left, the venom [?] ate.
Wake up, you who are drunk with your wine, and weep; lament, all you who drink wine to drunkenness, for delight and gladness have been taken from your mouth.
For a nation has come up against my land, strong and without number; their teeth are lion's teeth, and their back teeth are those of lion cubs.
I [?] made my vineyard a thing to be ruined, and my fig trees a thing to be shattered; searching, I [?] searched them out, and he cast them away.
And he stripped its branches white. Lament to me like a bride clothed in sackcloth for the husband of her maidenhood.
Offering and sacrifice are to be satisfied [?] from the house of the Lord. Mourn, you priests, ministers of the church, for the fields have been made wretched.
Let the land mourn, for it has been made wretched for lack of wheat and barley, for the [?] has perished from the valleys.
The vine has withered and the fig trees have dwindled; the pomegranate, the [?] palm, the apple, and every tree of the field have withered, for they have put joy to shame.
Gird yourselves and mourn, you priests; lament, you ministers of God, for offering and sacrifice have ceased from the house of your God.
And now thus says the Lord God:
Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, proclaim a service.
Gather the people, sanctify the assembly, choose out the infants, those who nurse at the breast; let the bridegroom come out of his resting place and the bride out of her bridal chamber.
And between the steps of the altar let the priests who minister to the Lord weep and say:
"Spare your people, O Lord, and do not give your inheritance over to reproach, and let them not say: 'Where is their God?'"
And the Lord was jealous for his land and for his people. And the Lord answered his people and said to them:
Behold, I will send you wheat and wine and oil, and you will be satisfied, and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.
Do not fear, O land; rejoice:
And it shall come to pass after this:
On that day, says the Lord, I will gather those who were crushed and receive those who were driven out, whom I had sent away,
and I will make those who were crushed into a remnant, and those who were sent away into a great and mighty nation, and the Lord will reign over them in Zion from now on and for ever.
And you, O tower of the flock, lofty daughter of Zion, upon you it will come, and the first dominion will enter, that of the king of Babylon, to the daughter of Jerusalem.
And now why have you known evil? Did you have no king? Your counsel has perished, for pains have seized you like those of childbirth.
Be in pain and be strong, and draw near, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth.
For now you will go out of the city and dwell in the field, and you will go as far as Babylon.
From there he will deliver you, and from there the Lord your God will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
And now many nations have gathered against you, who say: Give us life, and let our eyes look upon Zion.
But they did not know the thought of the Lord and did not understand his will, for he has gathered them like sheaves on the threshing floor.
Arise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will put horns of iron on you and fix hooves of bronze on you, and you will crush to pieces
many peoples, and with it you will overthrow the nations, and you will devote their multitude to the Lord as accursed, and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
Hear this, what the Lord says:
But I will hope in the Lord:
And it shall come to pass in the last days;
And the word of the Lord came to Jonah;
The Lord is good to those who wait patiently;
The word that Habakkuk saw. How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and you will not hear?
I call to you in distress, and you do not save me? Why have you shown me toils and pains, to look upon wretchedness and ungodliness?
Judgment has been done before me, and the judge takes [bribes]. Therefore the law is made void, and justice does not go forth.
For the ungodly man overpowers the righteous; therefore judgment goes forth perverted.
Behold, you scorners, look on and marvel at wonders, and perish.
I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe if someone told you.
For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, bitter and swift, who go across the breadth of the earth to take possession of dwellings not their own.
He is terrible and renowned; his judgment shall come from himself, and his word shall go out from himself.
His horses shall leap more than leopards and be swifter than the wolves of Arabia. His horsemen shall ride out and set out from afar, and they shall fly like eagles, eager to devour.
The end shall come upon the ungodly, the adversaries, like sand swept along by a torrent.
He shall make sport among kings, and the mighty shall be his plaything. He shall mock every stronghold; he shall heap up earth against it and seize it.
Then his spirit shall change, and he shall pass on, and the power of our God shall be gracious [?] to him. Are you not God from the beginning, my Holy One?
We shall not die. You have appointed him for judgment, and you formed me for the comfort [?] of his instruction.
Your eye is pure, so that it does not look on evil, and you cannot look on suffering.
Why do you look on those who act with contempt, and keep silent at the [?] (literally "promise") of the righteous by the ungodly one who is greater in number than he?
Do you make people like the fish and like creeping things that have no leader?
But fear me:
And Haggai said to the angels:
In the eighth month,
in the second year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo the prophet, saying:
The Lord was angry with our fathers with great anger. And he said to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn to me, and I will turn to you.
Do not be like your fathers, whom the former prophets rebuked, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty:
Turn from your evil ways and from your wicked deeds. But you did not listen to me and did not take heed to hear me, says the Lord.
Where are your fathers, the prophets? Are they still alive?
But receive my words and my law, all that I commanded my servants the prophets, which overtook your fathers.
They answered and said: The Lord Almighty is resolved to deal with you according to your ways and your doings; so he has done to us.
The angel of the Lord answered and said:
O Lord Almighty, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem, the city of Judah, which you have disregarded? Behold, this is the thirtieth [?] year.
And the Lord Almighty answered the angel who was speaking with me with good words and words of comfort.
And the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Cry out and say: Thus says the Lord concerning Jerusalem and Zion, with jealousy and great anger,
Against those who rose up against them, I was angry a little, but they gathered against them for evil.
Therefore thus says the Lord Almighty:
After glory he sent me to the nations that took you captive, for whoever touches you is like one who touches the pupil of his eye.
For behold, I will bring my hand upon them, those whom you served.
They shall become a spoil, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.
Rejoice and be glad:
And the word of the Lord came to me and said: Say to all the people of the city and to the priests:
If you fast, if you mourn in the fifth or the seventh month, behold, it is seventy years; was it indeed for me that you fasted?
And if you drink, surely you eat what is your own and drink what is your own.
Are these not the words that the Lord spoke to you by the hand of his prophets who were before,
when Jerusalem was still inhabited and prosperous, and its cities around it, in the hill country and in the plain, were still inhabited?
And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah and said: Judge righteous judgment, and show mercy and compassion each to his brother.
Let none of you oppress the widow, the stranger, the orphan, or the poor, and let none of you remember in his heart evil against his brother.
But they became disobedient [and refused] to give heed [?], and turned their back in contempt, and made their ears heavy so as not to hear my law and my words.
Thus says the Lord Almighty:
Return, Zion, and dwell in Jerusalem, and call Jerusalem a holy and true city, and the mountain of God Almighty a holy mountain.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Again old men and old women shall sit in the streets of Jerusalem, and each one shall have a staff in his hand because of the great number of his days.
And the streets of that city shall be filled with children singing. Thus says the Lord Almighty:
If there is any lawlessness before the remnant of this people in that day, do not commit lawlessness before me also, said the Lord Almighty.
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have remembered my people from the land of the sunrise and from the land of the sunset.
I will bring them into the midst of Jerusalem, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God in truth and in righteousness.
Thus says the Lord Almighty:
And the Lord their God saved them on that day, his people like sheep; holy ones shall roll upon the land.
For what is good of his is food: wine for the young men, and fragrant [wine] for the virgins.
Ask of the Lord rain in its season, early and late; the Lord gave them wondrous winter rain upon every green plant.
For the oracle-speakers spoke of trouble, and the diviners of a vision of falsehood and of [?] dreams; they spoke vanity and gave comfort.
Therefore they withered away, for there was no healing for the shepherds. My wrath was kindled, and shall I look upon the lambs?
And the Lord God Almighty looked upon his flock, the house of Judah, and set them in order like seven [?] horses in battle.
His peoples he looked upon from him, and from him he set them in order, and from him gentle [?] wrath went forth; the Lord is the one who exposes [?] over him.
And they shall be like warriors who trample mud on the road in battle, and they shall be drawn up with them and shall put to shame those mounted on horses.
And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and the house of Joseph I will save, and I will settle them, for I have loved them, and they shall be thus, as in [?] manner;
I will not turn away from them, for I am the Lord their God, and I will hear them; and they shall be like the warriors of Ephraim, and their hearts shall rejoice in the Lord as with wine.
And their children shall see it and shall rejoice in heart in the Lord.
And now entreat the face of your Lord, and he will show mercy to you;
This was done by your hand; [shall he] show favour to you [?], says the Lord Almighty.
For among you also the doors shall be shut, and you shall not kindle my altar in vain.
I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.
For from the rising of the sun to the setting of the sun my name is glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my house, and a pure sacrifice,
for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord Almighty.
Behold, lo, he comes, said the Lord Almighty.
And who shall endure the day of his coming? Or who shall stand at his appearing?
For he himself shall come like the fire of a furnace, and he shall bring them out [?] and purify them like silver and gold.
He shall cleanse the sons of Levi, he shall melt them down and purify them like silver, and they shall be to the Lord as offerers of sacrifices in righteousness.
And the sacrifice of Judah and the sacrifice of Israel shall be pleasing to the Lord, as in the former days and as in the years of old.
And I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a faithful and swift [witness] against fornications and sorceries, and against those who swear by my name falsely,
and those who withhold the wage of the hired labourer, and those who rob widows and strike [?] orphans,
who turn aside justice from strangers, and who did not fear me, said the Lord Almighty.
I am the Lord God, and I have not changed.
Return to me, and I [?]:
And return and see the difference between the righteous one and the lawless one, and between the one who has fallen away from [?] the service of God, and between the obedient and the disobedient,
For behold, the day has come, burning like a furnace of fire, and it shall consume all those who do lawlessness;
like stubble that day which is coming shall burn up all around them, said the Lord Almighty, and there shall remain of them neither branch nor root.
And upon you who fear my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, which has healing under its wings;
you shall go out and weep [?] like calves that have been loosed from their bonds, and you shall trample down the lawless,
and they shall be like ashes under your feet on that day which I shall make, said the Lord Almighty.
O Lord Almighty, give us a heart that bears fruit and cultivation of the mind,
from which fruit may be found, so that every corruptible one may be able to live, and they may find mercy.
For we are all formed together and as one by your hands, as you know.
For you give life when you form the body in the womb and give it its limbs, and you protect that creature of yours from heat and from water,
O Lord, and for nine months your own creature and formation, which you created along with it, carries it.
And all the while your word protects it, and afterwards the womb gives up what was stored within it.

And you commanded one of its members, the breast, to nourish it with milk; then that creature of yours, nourished with milk, lives for a long time, that member brought to completion by your providence [?], and you showed it mercy.
For you raised him by your effort, and you instructed him by your law, and you gave him understanding by your knowledge,
and you put him to death as your creature, and you give him life as your own work.
Now then, will you destroy a human being, your creature, made and commanded with so much labor, and set in order by you with hard labor? If so, why did you make that human being at all?
But now I will speak about everything, and above all about what you commanded me, and about your people, for whom I grieve.
And for your inheritance I mourn, and for the race of Jacob I am deeply troubled.
Therefore I will begin to pray before you for myself and for them, for I see the stumbling of all the inhabitants of the earth.
But I have also heard from the law and about the creation that is to come [?]. Therefore hear my prayer, and give ear to the words of my mouth.
O Lord, you who dwell from eternity to eternity, who move above the heights of the high places, whose dwelling is in the upper air,
whose throne is invincible and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before whom the hosts of angels stand in fear and trembling, whose words are turned into wind and fire,
whose word is established and what is spoken stands forever, whose providence is firm and whose command is terrible, whose glance dries up the abysses,
and whose wrath melts the mountains, and whose truth is attested.
Hear, O Lord, the voice of your servant, and give ear to the prayer of your creatures, and attend to my supplication.
For while I am still alive I will speak, and while I still have this understanding I will pray to you.
Do not look, Lord, on the sins of your people, but look on the service of your servants.
Do not regard the deeds of the lawless, but regard those who eagerly keep your covenants.
Nor remember those who conduct themselves wickedly before you, but remember those who eagerly trust in the fear of you.
Nor, Lord, be pleased to destroy those whose ways have become like those of beasts, but regard those who have been taught by the splendour of your law.
Nor be angry with those who are worse than wild beasts in their wickedness, but remember the love of those who always hope in your glory.
We and our forefathers have stood in the way of corruption. But you, Lord, are called merciful on account of us sinners.
Now if you wish to receive us completely, we who have no works, then let your name be merciful.
For the righteous, whose works are before you, will receive their reward from their own works.
Or what is man, that you should not be angry with him? Or what is the race of men, that you should not be embittered against it for this?
Lord, truly there is no one born of men who has not sinned against you. But you are called beneficent toward us;
by this your long-suffering will be made manifest, Lord: when you have mercy on those who have no store of good works.
Therefore let sin not reign in your mortal bodies, so that you obey its desires; nor present your members to sin as instruments of falsehood,
but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members to God as instruments of righteousness.
Sin has no dominion over you, for you are not under the law but under grace.
What then, shall we sin because you are not under the law but under grace? By no means!
Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are the slaves of the one you obey, whether of sin unto death or of obedience unto righteousness?
Thanks be to God that you were slaves of sin, and you became obedient from the heart to that to which you were handed over as a pattern of obedience.
And now you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of righteousness. I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh:
just as you presented your members as slaves to uncleanness and to lawlessness for lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness for holiness.
When you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.
What fruit, then, did you have at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.
But now you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God; you have the fruit of righteousness, and the end is eternal.
For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Christ Jesus our God.
This you know, that for those who love God:
Or do you not know that:
I myself am also persuaded about you, brothers, that you too are full and complete in all knowledge, and able to teach one another.
I have written to you rather boldly, brothers, in part as if reminding you, by the grace of God that was given to me by God,
so that I may be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving the gospel of God as a priest,
so that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable and holy through the Holy Spirit. I have a boast through Christ Jesus before God.
For I will not dare to speak of anything that Christ has not done through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed,
and by the power of faith and by signs, by the Spirit of God. For from Jerusalem and all around as far as Illyricum I have been sent to fulfil the gospel of God.
So I have been honoured to preach the gospel, not where Christ has already been named, so that I would not build on someone else's foundation, but as it is written:
"Those who have not been told about him will see, and those who have not seen will understand." This is also why I was greatly [?] (literally "I went beyond") from coming to you.
But now I no longer have any place in these regions, and I have wanted to come to you for a long time.
When I go to Spain, I hope, as I pass through, to see you as well, and to be sent on there by you, once I have first been satisfied in part by seeing you.
Now, look, I am going to Jerusalem to serve the saints.
For Macedonia and Achaia have decided to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
They decided it, and they are indebted to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they ought also to serve them in material things.
When I have completed this and sealed this fruit of theirs for them, I will go to Spain by way of you. And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
I appeal to you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in prayer to God for me,
that I may be rescued from the lawless Jews, and that this ministry of mine in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
so that by the service of the gospel I may come to you by the will of God and be refreshed together with you.
And may the God of peace be with you all.
And I, brothers, came to you:
Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
the merciful Father and God of comfort, who comforts us in all our afflictions,
so that we too may be able to comfort all who are afflicted with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also our comforts overflow through Christ.
If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation, which is brought about by enduring the same sufferings that we also suffer.
And our hope for you is firm. You know that just as you share in the sufferings, so also you share in the comforts.
For we are the temple of the living God, as the Lord said:
"I will dwell among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people."
"Therefore come out from among them and be separate," says the Lord, "and do not touch what is unclean, and I will receive you."
"And I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters," says the Lord Almighty.
Since we have this promise, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of spirit and flesh, and let us bring holiness to completion in the fear of God.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: for your sake he who was rich became poor, so that through his poverty you might become rich.
In this I give you advice, for this is better for you, who were the first to begin not only to act but also to be willing.
But now, see, complete the doing as well, so that just as there was eagerness to be willing, so also there may be completion out of what you have.
For if the eagerness is there, it is acceptable according to what one has. It is not that others should have relief and you hardship, but that there should be equality.
At this time your abundance [supplies] their need, so that their abundance may also [supply] your need, and so there may be equality.
As it is written: "Whoever gathered much had nothing left over, and whoever gathered little had no lack."
Know this, that no [?]:
Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience.
Do not be like them, for once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord.
Let us walk as children of light, for the fruit of the light is in all goodness, righteousness and truth.
Find out what is pleasing to the Lord, and do not take part in the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them.
For the things they do in secret are shameful even to speak of.
I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has served rather to advance the gospel,
so that these bonds of mine have become known in Christ throughout the whole palace and to all the others,
and through most of the brothers in the Lord, who have gained confidence from my bonds, I dare all the more to speak the word of God.
Some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, and some out of goodwill; for I stand for the defence of the gospel.
Those who proclaim Christ out of rivalry, insincerely, think they are bringing afflictions on these bonds of mine.
So then, in every way, whether as a pretext or in truth, Christ is preached; and for this I rejoice, and I will go on rejoicing.
I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your prayer and your help, by the Spirit of Jesus Christ, in keeping with my eager expectation and my hope,
that I will be ashamed in nothing, but that with all boldness, as always, so now too Christ will be glorified in this body of mine, whether by life or by death.
For to me, life is Christ, and death is gain.
But if this life in the flesh is the fruit of my work, then I do not know which I shall choose.
I am held fast between these two: I desire to depart from the flesh and to be with Christ, which is far better.
Yet to remain in the flesh is [?unwillingly] for your sake. And this I know with hope: that I shall remain and continue with you all for your progress.
But now, my beloved,
just as you have always been obedient, not only when I was present but much more now that I am far away, work with fear and trembling for your salvation.
For it is God who works in you both the will and the help toward virtue. Do this without murmuring and without disputing thoughts,
so that you may be spotless and innocent, children of God, undefiled in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, so that you may shine like stars in the world.
Hold fast the word of eternal life as a cause for boasting on the day of Christ, that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
Even if I am offered up on this sacrifice and this service of your faith, I rejoice, and I rejoice with you all.
In the same way, you too rejoice, and rejoice with me.
Brothers, I no longer count myself [?]:
Put on, therefore, as God's chosen ones,
holy and beloved: mercy, kindness, gentleness, humility, and patience. Bear with one another and forgive one another if anyone has a complaint against anyone.
Just as the Lord forgave you, so you also must forgive them. And above all these, put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of Christ be established in your hearts, to which you were called in one body; and be thankful.
And let the word of Christ dwell among you richly in all wisdom.
Teach and admonish one another with psalms, hymns, and songs; with spiritual grace sing to God in your hearts.
And whatever you do, in word or in deed, do everything in the name of God.
Give thanks to God the Father:
I beseech you,
brothers, to acknowledge those who labor among you, who are your leaders in the Lord and your teachers,
and to esteem them very highly in love because of their work. And be at peace with them.
I beseech you, brothers: instruct the disorderly, comfort the faint-hearted, support the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Take care that no one repays evil for evil; instead, always do good to one another and to everyone. Rejoice always.
Pray without ceasing. Give thanks in everything, for this is the will of God through Christ Jesus toward all of you. Do not trouble the Spirit.
Do not despise prophecy. Test everything and accept what is better. Keep away from every evil deed.
And may the God of peace himself make you holy with all perfection and all life, and may he keep your souls and body for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
He who called you is faithful, and he will also do it. Brothers, pray for us too.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss. I put you under oath by the Lord: read this letter to all the brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
But we ought always to give thanks for you,
brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you as the fruit of salvation through the sanctification of the spirits and through faith in the truth,
to which he also called you through our gospel, for the help [?] of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, stand firm and hold on to this teaching that you were taught, whether by word or by this letter of mine.
And may our Lord Jesus Christ himself and our God,
who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through his grace, comfort your hearts and strengthen them in good deed and word.
Finally, brothers, pray that the word of God may spread and be glorified among you,
and that you may be delivered from lawless and wicked people, for not everyone has faith.
But God is faithful, who has made you firm and will guard you from evil.
I trust in God concerning you that you will do, and are doing, what I commanded you.
And may the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and the patience of Christ.
O God, you turn and [?]: Do not turn away your face:
You were pleased, O Lord, with your land; you brought back: Hear, O Lord, the voice of prayer: In you, O Lord, I have hoped; let me not be put to shame: I have loved, because he heard:
May the Lord hear you in the day: The Lord is the strength of his people: Let us sing: O Lord, to my help: Where are the mercies:
Then Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seashore.
And a great crowd gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat down. And the whole crowd stood on the shore.
And he spoke many things to them in parables, and said: "Look, a sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some seed fell on the path.
And the birds of the sky came and ate it. Other seed fell on rock, where there was not much soil;
it sprang up at once, but because the soil had no depth, the sun rose and scorched it, and because it had not yet put down roots, it withered.
And other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choked it.
And some fell on good ground and gave fruit: some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, and some thirtyfold.
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
His disciples came to him and said to him: "Why do you speak to them in parables?"
And Jesus said to them: "Because it has been given to you to know the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, but it has not been given to them.
For whoever has, to him it will be given, and more will be added; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
This is why I speak to them in parables: because they see and are not afraid [?], they hear and do not listen, nor do they understand.
And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of the prophet Isaiah, which said: 'Hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.'

For the heart of this people has grown coarse, and with their ears they have heard with difficulty, and they have shut their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I should heal them.
But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
Amen, I say to you that many prophets longed to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you have heard, and did not hear it."
Jesus put another parable before them and said:
"The kingdom of God is like a man who sowed seed in his field.
And while people were asleep, an enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went away.
And when the blade sprang up and bore fruit, then the tares also appeared.
The servants came and said to the master of the house: 'Lord, we sowed good seed in your field; where did the tares come from?'
And he said to them: 'An enemy has done this.' And the servants said to him: 'Do you want us to go and bring them out [?]?'
But he said: 'No, lest in gathering the tares you uproot the wheat along with them.
Let them grow together until the time of harvest, and at harvest time I will command the reapers:
"Gather the tares first and bind them into bundles so that they may be burned, but gather the wheat into his storehouse."'"
Jesus put another parable before them and said:
"The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his garden; it is the smallest of all seeds,
but when it has grown, it is greater than all the herbs and becomes a great tree, so that the birds come and settle in its branches."
Then he spoke another parable to them and said: "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened."
Jesus spoke these things to the crowd in parables, and without a parable he said nothing to them, so that the word of the prophet might be fulfilled:
"I will open my mouth in parables, and I will speak parables from the beginning of the world."
Then Jesus left the crowd and came into the house.
His disciples came to him and said to him: "Explain to us this parable of the tares and the field."
And he answered and said to them: "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man, and the field is this world;
and the good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, and the tares are the sons of wickedness.
And the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of this world, and the reapers are the angels.
Just as they gather the tares and burn them with fire, so [?] will it be at the end of this world.
For the Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all who do lawlessness,
and they will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping of eyes and gnashing of teeth.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of heaven. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure:
And when he was alone, his disciples asked him: "What is this parable?"
And he said to them: "To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to those outside everything is spoken in parables,
so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they be forgiven."
And he said to them: "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
The one who sows sows this good word. And these are the ones along the path, where the word is sown;
when they hear his word, the devil comes and takes away his word that was sown in them.
And these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy,
but they have no root in themselves and last only for a time; and when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
And those sown among thorns are the ones who hear the word, but the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches come in and choke the words,
and it becomes unfruitful. And these are the ones sown on good ground, who hear the word and bear fruit, thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold."
And he said to them: "Do people bring a lamp and put it under a bushel? Do they not put it on a lampstand?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor any secret that will not come to light."
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And he said to them: "Pay attention to what you hear: the measure you measure with will be measured back to you, you who hear.
Whoever has will be given more; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him."
And he said to them: "The kingdom of God is like this: as when a man sows seed in the ground,
and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how, for the earth bears fruit by itself:
First the blade, then the ear, and then the full grain in the ear. And when it yields its fruit, at once he sends the sickle, because the harvest has come.
And he said to them: To what shall we compare the kingdom of God? Or what parable shall we use?
It is like a grain of mustard seed which, when it is sown in the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds that are on the earth.
And when it is sown and comes up, it becomes greater than all the garden plants and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can settle under its shade.
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
And he said nothing to them without a parable; but privately he explained everything to his disciples.
On that day, when evening came;
And at once he called [?]:
A sower went out to sow his seed;
and as he sowed, some fell beside the road and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it.
And other seed fell on rock. It sprang up and withered, because there was no depth of soil.
And other seed fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up and choked it. And other seed fell on good ground, and it sprang up and produced fruit a hundredfold.
He said this in a loud voice: Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear! His disciples asked him: What is this parable?
And he said to them: To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to others it is given in parables,
so that they may look and not see, and hear and not understand. Now this is the parable: the seed is the word of God.
Those along the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
And those on the rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, but these have no root; they believe for a time, and in the time of testing they fall away.
And the seed that fell among the thorns stands for those who hear the word, and as they go on they are choked by the cares, riches and pleasures of this world, and they do not bear fruit.
And the seed on the good ground stands for those who hear the word with a good and kind heart, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed; instead they set it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor any secret that will not be known and come out into the open.
So take heed how you hear: whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken from him.
His mother and his brothers came to him, and they could not reach him because of the crowd.
And they told him, saying: Your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to see you.
And he said to them: These are my mother and my brothers: those who hear the word of God
and do it.
And it happened that he was praying in a certain place.
And when he had finished praying, one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his own disciples.
And he said to them: "When you pray, say: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done,
give us this our daily bread day by day, and forgive us our sins, as we also forgive all who are indebted to us, and do not lead us into temptation."
And he said to them: "Which of you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him:
'Friend, lend me three loaves, for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.'
And he answers him from inside and says: 'Do not trouble me, for the door is shut,
and my children are with me on the [?]; I cannot get up and give to you.'
I tell you, even if he cannot get up and give because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks
receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened. Which of you, then, if his son asks his father for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake instead of a fish? Or if he asks for a rod [?], will he give him a scorpion?
If you, then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!"
Therefore,
just as sin came into the world through the one man, and death through sin, and so death came upon all men,
in whom all sinned; for until the law came, sin was in the world, but sin was not counted, because there was not yet law.
Yet death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of Adam's transgression, for he is a type of the times to come.
But the grace is not like the trespass. If many died through the trespass of the one,
how much more has the grace of God, and the gift by the grace of the one man Jesus Christ, abounded for many!
And the gift is not like what came through the one who sinned; for the judgment came from the one unto condemnation, but the grace from many who had sinned unto justification.
If by the trespass of the one death reigned through the one, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life!
As through the trespass of the one it came upon all men unto condemnation, so also through the righteousness of the one it came upon all men unto justification of life.
As through the disobedience of the one man many came in as sinners, so also through the obedience of one man many came in as righteous.
For the law came in between, so that sin might increase; and where sin increased, there grace abounded all the more,
so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness unto eternal life through Christ Jesus our Lord.
But if God wished to show his wrath,
he who has endured with much long-suffering the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction, and in order to show the riches of his glory upon the vessels of mercy,
whom he prepared beforehand for glory, whom he also called, namely us, not only from among the Jews but also from among the Gentiles?
As he says in Hosea: "I will call those who were not my people 'my people,' and her who was not my beloved 'my beloved.'
And in the very place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called sons of the living God."
And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the sons of Israel be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will be saved;
for it is a word that accomplishes and is cut short in righteousness, because the Lord will carry out a shortened word upon the earth."
And as Isaiah said beforehand: "If the Lord Almighty had not left us offspring, we would have become like the people of Sodom and been made like the people of Gomorrah."
What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not seek righteousness, have attained righteousness, the righteousness that comes from faith.
Israel pursued the law of righteousness and did not attain the law of abundance [?]. Why?
Because they did not pursue it by faith but by the works of the law, for they stumbled over the stone of stumbling.
As it is written: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence, and everyone who believes in him will never be put to shame."
Such is the hope we have through Christ toward God;
not that we are capable by ourselves of reckoning anything as coming from us, but our capability is from God, who made us capable of being ministers of a new covenant.
Such is the hope we have through Christ toward God; not that we are capable by ourselves of reckoning anything as coming from us, but our capability is from God,
who made us capable of being ministers of a new law, not of the letter but of the Spirit, for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
If the ministry of death, engraved in letters on tablets, came with glory,
so that the sons of Israel could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, a glory that was fading away, how much more will the ministry of the Spirit be in glory?
If the ministry of condemnation is glory, how much more will the ministry of the Spirit exceed it in glory.
For indeed what was glorified is no longer glorified in this respect, because of the glory that surpasses it.
If what was fading away came with glory, how much more will what abides be in glory. Since, then, we have such a hope, let us act with great openness.
And as Moses put a veil over his face, so that the sons of Israel would not see the end of what was fading away.
But their minds were blinded, for to this very day the same veil of the old law remains unremoved, because it is taken away only through Christ.
To this very day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
But when anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away. Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of God is, there is freedom.
And we, with unveiled face, behold the glory of the Lord and are transformed into that same image, from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.
And it happened on another Sabbath also that he entered their synagogue and taught them.
And there was a man there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees were watching him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find a way to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts, and he said to the man whose hand was withered: "Get up and stand in the middle!" And he got up and stood in the middle.
Then Jesus said to them: "I will ask you something: what is lawful on the Sabbath, to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?"
And he looked around at all of them and said to the man: "Stretch out your hand!" And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, like the other one.
But they were filled with fury and talked with one another about what they might do to Jesus.
Let no one judge you in matters of food and drink, or with regard to a festival, or a new moon, or sabbaths. These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body belongs to Christ.

Let no one get the better of you, wishing to do so through humility and the worship of angels. Such a person, pleased with himself over things he has not seen, is puffed up for nothing by his fleshly mind.
and he does not hold fast to the head. From the head the whole body is formed and held together by its joints and parts, and it grows with the growth that comes from God.
If you died with Christ to the rules of this world, why do you submit to rules as if you were still living in the world:
"Do not go near, do not touch"? All these things are meant to perish as they are used, and they follow human commandments and teaching.

These things do seem to have some appearance of wisdom, with their self-chosen discipline and order, their humility, and their harsh treatment of the body, but they have no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
If you have been raised with Christ, seek the things of heaven, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on the things of heaven, not on the things of earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is our life, appears, then you too will appear with him in glory.
Take care, brothers, that none of you has an evil heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is still called "today," so that none of you is hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold the confidence we had at the beginning firm to the end.
As it is said: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."
For some heard and rebelled, but not all of those who came out of Egypt under Moses.
With whom was he angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
To whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest? Was it not to the disobedient? And we see that they could not enter because of their unbelief.
Therefore let us fear that, while the promise of entering his rest still stands, any of you should think himself to have fallen short of it.
For the good news has been proclaimed to us, just as it was to them. But the message they heard did not benefit them, because it was not joined with faith in those who heard it.
But we who have believed enter that rest, just as he said: "As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter my rest."
And indeed the works had been made from the foundation of the world.
For he has said somewhere of the seventh day thus: And the Lord rested on the seventh day from all his works.
After this he says again: They shall not enter into my rest.
For since it remains for some to enter into it, and those to whom the good news was proclaimed beforehand did not enter because of unbelief,
he again designates the same day, "Today," through David, and says, after so long a time, as was said before:
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.
For if Joshua, the son of Nun, had brought them into that rest, he would not speak afterward of another day.
So does a sabbath rest remain for the people of God?
For whoever has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his own.
At that time Jesus was going through their grain fields on the sabbath day, and his disciples were hungry and began to pluck the heads of grain and to eat.
But when the Pharisees saw it, they said to him: Behold, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the sabbath.
But he said to them: Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God and ate the bread of the offering, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests?
Have you not read in the law that on the sabbath the priests profane the sabbath? But I tell you: something greater than the temple is here.
If you had known what this means, 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the innocent; for the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.
And then he entered the synagogue:
And he went out from there and came to his own hometown, and his disciples followed him.
And it was the sabbath, and he began to teach them in the synagogue, and many who heard him were astonished and said: Where did this man get these things?
Or what is this wisdom that has been given to him, and such great power, that is done by his hands?
Is this not the carpenter's son and the son of Mary, the brother of James and John, Judas and Simon, and are not all his sisters with us?
And they took offense at him. But Jesus said: A prophet is not without honor except in his own country and among his kinsfolk and in his own house.
And he did not do a single miracle there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And Jesus was teaching in a synagogue on the sabbath.
And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not look up at all.
Jesus saw her, called her, and said to her: Woman, you are set free from your infirmity.
And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight, and she walked and glorified God.
The ruler of the synagogue answered and spoke in anger, because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, and he said to the people:
"There are six days on which work ought to be done. Come and be healed on those days, and not on the Sabbath day."
Jesus answered and said to them: "Hypocrites! Does not each one of you untie his ox or his donkey from its manger on the Sabbath, lead it away and give it water?
And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom the devil has kept bound for eighteen years now: was it not right to loose her from her bonds on the Sabbath day?"
And as he said these things, all his opponents were put to shame;
and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things that were being done by him.
And it came to pass,
when he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the Sabbath day to eat bread, that they were watching him closely.
And behold, there was a man with dropsy in front of him. Jesus answered and said to the lawyers and the Pharisees:
