"Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" But they kept silent. And he brought the man, healed him and sent him away.
And he said to them: "Which of you, if his son or his ox falls into a pit, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?"
And no one dared to answer him any further.
"You worked salvation"; "Yours is the day"; "Come and see"; "Cry out to God";
"He magnified the salvation of the king"; "My God, blameless"; "Let your hand be strengthened"; "Your mercies";
"You are the God who did"; "With my voice"; "I will praise the Lord in my life"; "My soul blesses the Lord";
"Incline your ear, O Lord, and"; "Save your servant"; "But I will praise your power"; "My helper, I will sing to you";
"Stir up your power"; "You who shepherd Israel"; "My heart is ready"; "For he magnified salvation";
"It is good to give thanks"; "Praise with the ten-stringed instrument";
"Come, sing"; "Let us come early before"; "Who is a great God"; "With my voice"; "Sing to God our helper";
"The Lord reigns, let it see"; "Great is the Lord and praised"; "God reigns"; "Great is our Lord, great"; "Praise the Lord, for he is good";
"My God, teach me"; "In you, O Lord, I have hoped, let not";
"Help me by your word"; "Deal with your servant"; "Let me hear in the morning"; "Teach me, that";
"You loved righteousness"; "Grace was poured out"; "Hear, O Lord, of righteousness"; "Establish the feet";
"The Lord is good, for he heard"; "The Lord is the strength of the people"; "We will rejoice in salvation";
"Your mercies"; "For great are the works"; "My soul blesses";
He loves mercy: for he spoke and they came to be; show your face:
In you, O Lord, I have hoped, let [me] not: you yourself are the Lord God;
In God we will boast; where are the mercies: good is the Lord God to Israel;
I will love you, O Lord, [my] strength: you will arise and have mercy: let the nations fear: the earth is the Lord's and its fullness:
He himself the sea: the heavens declare the glory. I waited patiently for the Lord: he brought me up from the pit:
With mercy and judgments: the heavens will confess your wonders: give ear to my words:
For to you I will pray, O Lord, at dawn; sing to the Lord with song; great is the Lord and greatly praised: rejoice, you righteous:
The Lord reigns, majesty: he established the world: its foundations: glorious things have been spoken of you:
Sing to the Lord with song: his holy [?]: the Lord has shown salvation: to all the nations:
For his name is exalted: I will exalt you, O Lord, for you: your mercies are many; your throne, O God, is forever:
The Lord reigns, let [them] rejoice: cloud and darkness: O God, your judgment to the king: let the mountains receive peace;
The Lord reigns, majesty: he established the world: all the nations: God has gone up with shouting:
Have mercy on me, O God, [according to your] great; wash me more: you who shepherd Israel, look: you who sit upon the cherubim:
And he shall be like a tree planted: blessed is the man who does not. The right hand of the Lord has done:
The Lord is my light and savior: the desire of the heart: I rejoiced in those who. said to me; Jerusalem is built as a city;
The Lord [shall recount?] in writing; I loved, for he heard; the Lord reigns, rejoice: those who trust in the Lord are like a mountain:
Do good, O Lord, of goodness [?]; you who dwell in the heavens: you were pleased, O Lord, with your land; you turned back:
It is good to confess: I will exalt you, my God, and: every day I will bless you;
Those who trust in the Lord are like a mountain: mountains are round about it and: judge, O Lord, those who do harm: praise the Lord, O Jerusalem, sing:
Let God arise and let [them] be scattered: kings of the earth: bless: come, let us sing to the Lord:
Let us come early before [his] face: you who shepherd Israel, look; stir up your power: what is good or what [?]: arise, O God, judge the judgment:
And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; she got up and served him.
And when evening came, they brought to him many who were possessed by demons, and he drove out the spirits with a word, and all who were grievously sick he healed with a word,
so that the word spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, which said: "He took up our infirmities and healed our diseases."
And when he saw a great crowd around him, he gave orders to go over to the other side.
Then one of the scribes came to him and said to him: "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
Jesus said to him: "Foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
And one of the disciples said to him: "Teacher, first command me to go and bury my father."
But Jesus said to him: "You, follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead."
And he went up into the boat, and his disciples followed him. And behold, there was a great storm on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves.
But he himself was asleep. The disciples came to him, woke the Lord, and said to him: "Lord, save us, for we are perishing."
And Jesus said to them: "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?" Then Jesus got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and at once there was a great calm.
And they were all amazed and said: "What sort of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!"
Or do you not know: [?]
And he came to the other side, to the country of the Gergesenes,
and two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that no one was able to pass along that road.
And they cried out, saying: "What have you to do with us, Jesus, Son of God?
Have you come here before the time to torment us?" And at a distance from them there was a herd of swine feeding.
And the demons begged him, saying: "If you cast us out, command us to go into that herd of swine."
And he said to them: "Go!" And they came out of the men and went into the herd of swine.
And the herd of swine rushed down the steep bank into the sea and perished.
And the herdsmen fled into the city and told everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men. Then the whole city went out to meet him.
They saw him and begged him to depart from their region.
By the law of the spirit [?] ... whose spirit dwells among you.
And as Jesus was passing on from there, he saw a man
sitting at the tax booth; Matthew was his name. And he said to him: "Follow me." And immediately he got up and followed him.
And as [?] he was sitting in the house, many tax collectors and sinners were also sitting with Jesus.
The Pharisees saw this and said to his disciples: "Why does your teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
When Jesus heard this, he said to them: "It is not the living who need a physician, but the sick.
But go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice.' For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Then John's disciples came to him and said, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?"
Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridegroom [mourn] [?] ...?"
And Jesus answered and said to them, "Go and tell John what you have heard and seen:
the blind see again, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is proclaimed to the poor.
Blessed is the one who does not stumble because of me." And as they went away, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John, and said, "What did you go out into the wilderness to see?
A reed shaken by the wind? But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing?
For look, those who wear soft clothing are in the king's house.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? I tell you, more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: 'See, I send my angel ahead of you, who will prepare your ways before you.'
Amen, I tell you: among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist; but the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
For from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.
For the Law and all the prophets prophesied until John.
If you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who is to come. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
Therefore, since we have this ministry, as we have received mercy,
we do not lose heart. Rather, we have renounced the hidden things of shame, for we do not walk in craftiness, nor do we falsify the word of God,
but by the open declaration of the truth we commend ourselves to every human conscience before God.
If this gospel of ours is hidden, it is hidden to those who are perishing, the unbelievers whose minds God has blinded,
so that the light of the glory of Christ, who is the image of the invisible God, might not shine on them.
We do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as servants of Christ Jesus.
God, who commanded light to shine out, who also has shone light into our hearts to give the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of the great God in the face of Jesus Christ.
And Jesus went on from there and came into their synagogue.
And there was a man there whose hand was withered. They asked him, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" so that they might accuse him.
But Jesus said to them, "Which man among you, who has one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
Is not a man worth more than a sheep? Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day."
Then he said to the man, "Stretch out your hand!" And he stretched out his hand, and it was restored, alive again like the other one.
But the Pharisees came and plotted how they might destroy him. And Jesus perceived it, withdrew from them, and went away.
And many people followed him, and he healed them all. And he commanded them not to make him known.
This was so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which says: "Behold, my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved, with whom my soul is well pleased.
I will put my spirit upon him, and he will proclaim judgement to the Gentiles. He will not quarrel or cry out, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
He will not break a bruised reed, and he will not quench a smouldering wick, until he brings judgement to victory.
And the Gentiles will hope in his name." Then they brought to him a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute. He healed him completely, and the man spoke properly.
And the people were amazed and said: "Can this be the Son of David?"
Now therefore we know the fear of the Lord. Is it men we persuade, or God?
But we are made manifest before God, and I hope that through the Holy Spirit we are made manifest in your minds as well.
For I am not commending ourselves to you again. Rather, I am giving you a reason to boast on my behalf, so that you may have something to say to those
who boast only in outward appearance and not in heart. For if we have gone out of ourselves, it is for God; or if we make you wise, it is for you.
For the love of Christ compels us, since we have reached this judgement: One died for all. Shall we not all, then, die?
For he died for all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again.
From now on we know no one according to the flesh. Even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know him that way now.
From now on, whatever is through Christ: the old has passed away, and now, behold, it has become new.
All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself together through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
For God was with Christ and reconciled the world to himself. He did not count their sins against them, and he established the word of reconciliation.
We are messengers for Christ's sake, as God entreats us. We beg you for Christ's sake: be reconciled to God.
For he made him who knew no sin to be [?] for our sake, so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.
We are your fellow workers. I beg you: do not receive the grace of God in vain.
"At the time of favour I will hear you, and on the day of salvation I will help you."
And Jesus went out and saw a great crowd. He had compassion on them and healed their sicknesses.
When evening came, his disciples came to him and said: "This is a deserted place, and the hour is already past.
Send these people away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and buy food for themselves."
And the Gospel readings: next [?]
Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, an appointed apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
which he promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy scriptures, concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
who was declared Son of God in power and by the Spirit of holiness, through the resurrection from the dead of our Lord Jesus Christ,
from whom we have received grace and apostleship, to bring about the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles for the sake of his name, among whom you also are called of Christ Jesus,
to all of you who are in Rome, beloved of God, chosen saints: grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Christ!
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed throughout the whole world.
For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, is my witness how unceasingly I make mention of you.
In my prayers I pray for you, that the way may be made open for me to come to you, for I long to see you, so that I too may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you.
And this is the mutual encouragement among you, through that faith of ours, yours and mine.

I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I have wanted to come to you and have been hindered until now, so that I might reap some fruit among you as well, as among the other nations.
I am a debtor to Gentiles and to barbarians, to the wise and to the foolish.
So it is my eager desire to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome, for I am not ashamed of the gospel,
for it is the power of God for salvation to all who believe, to the Jews first and then to the Gentiles.
For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, as it is written: "The righteous will live by faith."
When Jesus heard that John had been handed over to prison, he withdrew and went to Galilee.
And he left Nazareth and came and settled in Capernaum, by the seashore, in the territory of Babylon [?] and Naphtali, so that what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, who said:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles:
the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and on those who sat in darkness and in the shadows of death, light has shone."
From then on Jesus began to preach: "Repent, for the kingdom has drawn near." And as Jesus was walking along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers,
Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And he said to them, "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men." And they immediately left their nets and followed him.
And going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James and John, the sons of Zebedee, in the boat with Zebedee their father, and he called them.
And they left the boat and their father and followed him.
And he went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the kingdom of God, and healing all the sick and all the infirm among the people.
And the report about him spread throughout all Syria.
And they brought to him all who were grievously sick with various kinds of diseases, those seized by torments, the demon-possessed and the lunatics, and he healed them.
And a great crowd followed him from Galilee, from the Decapolis, from Jerusalem and from beyond the Jordan, and he healed them.
Glory in the highest, and on earth peace. O God, you who never left the heavens came down to earth and filled us with joy. O Lord, glory to you.
The earth has yielded its fruit.
Long ago Isaiah said: "Behold, a virgin has conceived and borne a son, whose name is Emmanuel." O Lord, lover of humankind, glory to you.
The Lord shepherds me in a green place. You who shepherd Israel.

At the Lord's birth in Bethlehem from the holy Virgin, the world was filled with light. The shepherds piped [?], the Magi worshipped, and Herod trembled, for God appeared in the flesh as the Savior of our souls.
My heart has poured forth [a good word]. And unto ages of ages.
Rejoice, you righteous; be glad, you heavens; sing, you mountains, at the appearing of Christ.
The Virgin, like the cherubim, carries in her bosom the Word of God made flesh.
The shepherds fall down before the newborn and offer gifts to the Lord.
The angels cry aloud and say: O Lord beyond words, glory to you.
He is greatly exalted above all the nations.
For the grace of God has appeared as the Savior of the whole world, for Christ the King was born in the city of David, in Bethlehem of Judea.
He appeared on earth and lived among people. He is God from God, Light from Light.
You are the true God, who were born of the Virgin. Have mercy on us.
Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised. He will shepherd us forever.
What the prophets said has been fulfilled, the message they proclaimed about you, our Savior.
For long ago they saw you, the Creator of all, as a child in the bosom of the Virgin.
This is the one born of the Virgin Mary, whose name is Emmanuel.
This is God, the Savior of the world and the redeemer of our souls.
O God, have mercy on us, and [let] the ends of the earth [fear him].
We saw in the cave a child lying in the manger, adorned with a star and wrapped in swaddling clothes: the King, the Judge, and the champion of souls.
O God, [give] your judgment to the king. So be it, so be it.
Today the heavens rejoice and the earth is glad. The sea and everything in it rejoices with the hosts of heaven, because Christ our Savior is born.
The Magi came from the east and offered gifts at the birth of the King.
They cried out with joy and said: "This is our God, in whom we hoped, and he has become our salvation."
Peoples of light, come, let us worship the one who has appeared as Saviour of our souls.
The earth was pleasing to you, O Lord; its course [?]
"Where have you come from, O Magi, and whom are you seeking?" the Jews cried out. "If you are seeking a king, here is Herod."
But the Magi said to them: "We have seen the star of the King's birth, which the prophets proclaimed long ago, and the patriarchs announced to us the Creator of the world.
Let us offer gifts to him and say: You are the Lord our God; have mercy on us."
His foundations, [?] theirs, are from you.
The Magi worshipped the one born of the Virgin. The shepherds cried out with the angels and said: "Come, you peoples, and let us worship God from God."
Your mercies forever. So be it, so be it.
At the manifestation of Christ a star shone out. The shepherds saw it, the Magi worshipped, Herod trembled, and God appeared in the flesh as Saviour of our souls.
The Lord said to my Lord: ... He will lift up his head.
Christ, King of the Jews and our Deliverer, who was born of a Virgin, about whom the shepherds also cried out and said:
"Here is the star, here are the Magi. Where is the mother? Who will show us the newborn child who was born in Bethlehem?"
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
You called the city you loved, Bethlehem, your own womb, and you made the humble cave like the heavens.
For the Magi saw you lying in the manger, and so it was called a resting place.
Remember, O Lord, David. My holiness.
Arise, O Lord, to your resting place. Remember, O Lord, David.
Christ is born on earth. The angels glorify the King; the Magi together [?]
You created Tabor and Hermon; they will rejoice in your name.
And at your baptism, O Christ, they saw you at the Jordan and leaped like lambs of the flock.
For you sprang up from the earth as peace and appeared from heaven as righteousness. O Lord, lover of humankind, glory to you.
Today you came to the Jordan, O Saviour, and you, the sinless one, were baptized by John.
You who bent the heavens like vaults bowed your incorruptible head under the hand of the Forerunner.
Then the voice of the Father was heard from above, bearing witness: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I have been well pleased from eternity." O Lord, glory to you.
At the baptism of Christ, the waters … The voice of the Lord is upon the waters.
The voice of the Lord is in power. Come, let us sing to the Lord, let us cry out …
Our Enlightener, Christ, who [?] … You, O Christ, were baptized; the waters saw you.
Like the voice that cried in the wilderness: "Prepare the ways of the Lord."
You came, our Savior, and took the form of a servant. You, who knew no sin, asked to be baptized.
The waters saw you, O God, and were afraid. The Forerunner also trembled in spirit, and he cried out and said: "How is the Light of Light baptized? How shall the servant lay his hand on the Lord?"
Sanctify me, O Christ, and these waters too, you who take away the sins of the world, O lover of mankind.
It befits John …
Sprinkle me with hyssop … Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great …
The sea saw …
The hosts of angels …
You were baptized in the Jordan, O Savior. You sanctified the waters, took on yourself the will of a servant, and blotted out sins.
Great is the mystery of your manifestation, O Lord, lover of mankind. Glory to you.
When John was sent to preach at the Jordan, the service of the Law was dissolved, and grace was revealed for our salvation.
Bring to the Lord, you sons of God …
In peace …
John stood at the Jordan. All the waters fell silent. A great wonder took place, for the servant was baptizing the Lord.
Let us bless the Lord at all times … Those who hope in him …
Today there was joy for the whole world, when you came, O Savior, and were baptized by John for our deliverance.
The lawless one said to sin … [?] that they may be able to stand [?] …
Fear seized John the Forerunner when he saw you, the Creator of all, in the Jordan, borne witness to by the Father at that sanctification of the water.
As the hart longs … and to my God …
John saw the Holy Spirit coming down from heaven like a dove, and he cried out and said: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world."
Our God is a refuge … the God of Jacob …
The Holy Spirit, coming down from the Father upon Christ :
John saw [him], through whom the Holy Trinity is openly worshipped :
Praise befits you, O God, in Zion, and let them sing :
God made man was receiving baptism from a servant, not to receive holiness, but to wipe away the sins of the world.
Come, you peoples, let us joyfully worship God who has appeared :
With my voice I cried to the Lord, with my voice to God, and of Aaron [?] :
We praise you, O God, who came for the salvation of your creatures, for you appeared at the Jordan and received baptism from John, you who wiped away the sins of the world.
The Lord reigns; majesty : ... for length of days :
You came down to the Jordan and received baptism from John. Blessed are you forever, O Lord, God of our fathers.
Sing to the Lord a new song, for wonderful [things] : ... the peoples with equity.
John was sent from on high to the Jordan. When Christ was being baptized, the heavens were opened.
And the voice of the Father bore witness from above: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased :
When Israel went out : ... from this time forth and forever :
God is the Lord, and he has appeared to us.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good :
Let us draw near, you faithful, to the Passion of the Saviour, Christ our God :
Let us glorify his countless long-suffering, so that in his own love for mankind he may raise up with himself us who have perished through sin, since he is good and loves mankind :
Hear us, O God our Saviour : ... far off :
Praise befits you : be gracious to me [?] :
You peoples, let us consider the terrifying judgment of the Lord. Let us not hide the talent of faith, nor let the lamps of our souls be put out by worldly cares.
Instead, let us make them shine with the oil of love for mankind, so that we may receive peace and great mercy from Christ our God :
To you, O Lord, I have lifted up [my soul]; let me not be put to shame
nor let [my enemies] laugh at me : ... teach me :
When the sinful woman was offering the ointment, the disciple was then plotting with the lawless men :
She rejoiced and poured out that very costly [ointment], but he hurried to hand over the One beyond price :
He recognized God, but that one was departing from God.
This one was being set free, and Judas was becoming a slave of the evil enemy by his own intention.
How great is the repentance that you have given us, O Savior!
You who suffered for us and saved us. His heart gathered [?] together; he would go outside to evil.
Blessed is he who has regard for his enemies.
Today Jesus gave his disciples the teaching, the law, and that great counsel: the holy body and blood for the forgiveness of sins.
Of your mystical supper today, O Son of God, make me a partaker and make me worthy. I will not tell your mystery to your enemies, nor will I give you a kiss as Judas did,
but like the thief I cry out: Remember me, O Lord, in your kingdom.
In what manner did you, Judas... O the wretchedness of Judas!
Let us bless the Father, let us bless the Son, let us bless the Holy Spirit, now and forever.
May the Father bless us, may the Son bless us, may the Holy Spirit bless us, now and forever.
Blessed is the Father, blessed is the Son, blessed is the Holy Spirit, now and forever.
At all times you are worthily praised, O God, but now above all it is fitting to glorify you with undivided attention, O King of peace.
For when you were about to give yourself up for our sins, you rose from that life-giving supper.
You girded yourself with a towel, poured water into a basin, and began to wash the feet of your disciples.
The archangels standing by trembled, along with the countless hosts of angels.
But Peter cried out in fear: "You shall never wash my feet, O Lord!" To which you said to him: "If I do not wash your feet, know that you have no part with me."
Then he eagerly said to you: "Not my feet only, O Redeemer, but my hands and my head as well."
You who willingly suffered the passion, grant us forgiveness of sins, O God, and great mercy.
You, O Redeemer, washed... side [?]
The rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his anointed.
Why did the nations rage, those who hoped in him?
Along with the other disciples, O Lord, you also washed well the feet of your betrayer. But he was running toward evil.
For after receiving the immortal food, he spoke the word of betrayal and sold you for a worthless price, you, the treasure that enriches the whole world, to whom we sing: Have mercy on us.
In what manner, Judas, did you turn out to be the Savior's betrayer? Did he separate you from the company of the disciples?
Did he leave you lacking in the grace of healings? Or did he wash the feet of the others and neglect yours?
Or did he keep you away from the table at the supper with them?
O, how many good things you showed yourself forgetful of! The mind is narrowed by wretchedness.
But his invincible long-suffering and great mercy are proclaimed.
They have laid a lawless word against me, O Lord.
Lord, do not forsake me. Blessed is the one who has understood. So be it, so be it.
David prophesied about Christ and about the disciple by whom he was to be betrayed.

O man of my peace and companion of my [?] ("dagebay", perhaps "spread table"), why do you torment me? Together, I and my Father received you, and with the Holy Spirit we strengthened you against the demons.
But you sold me for silver. The band of the apostles remained, and you yourself have separated from the kingdom.
Now you hold death as your torment and the noose [?] as your accuser [?].
But I will endure crucifixion and turn back those who have gone astray, and I will give them eternal life.
Wretched Judas saw the harlot kissing your feet and craftily plotted a betrayal by a kiss.
She loosened her hair, and he was bound by envy. Instead of ointment, he brought an evil betrayal. For envy does not know how to honor what is better.
O the wretchedness of Judas! O God, deliver our souls from it.
The master's disciple agrees to a bribe. He sold him for thirty pieces of silver, and with a false kiss he handed him over to the lawless to be put to death.
Give ear to my prayer, O God. Lord, I trust in you.
The master's disciple:
The master cried out and said to his disciple: "My disciple, you loved silver, you loved silver, and you handed me over to death.
You have been blotted out from among the disciples, and you could not join with the Jews. I will be lifted up to heaven and will enlighten all creation."
At your mystical supper
Today his disciples heard the voice of the Lord: "One of you will hand me over to death."
But Judas sold the Lord and received the price of the one he sold.
O God, do not keep silent about my praise. [?] my soul from the persecutors.
Today the voice was heard:
What do you think, Judas, you who took the price? Are you expecting some honor from Caiaphas the high priest, now that today you have handed the Savior over to the lawless?
He endured being struck on the cheek, took the crucifixion upon himself, and tasted death, so that he might save the world.
While he was bowing down in prayer, Peter was dozing.
At that time he was struck with terror from fear of the maidservant. For this was the one who was going to die with you, yet he could not endure the vigil and was defeated in advance by that vigil.
But he quickly rose up from that sin and washed away his sins with tears. Christ the Savior, glory to you.
Today the Creator of heaven and earth said to his disciples: "The hour has drawn near; Judas, my betrayer, is coming.
Let none of you deny me when you see me on the cross between two thieves.
I will suffer as a man, and as the lover of mankind I will save my faithful."
Save me, O God, for the waters have come in. They were founded upon it.
Today the Creator said:
Peter understood his denial and said with lamentation: "I have been swallowed up by a maidservant, worse than by the abyss of the earth.
For there I cried out, 'Save me, Lord,' and I found help; but now I have abandoned the Savior and I am perishing through sin.
But I cry out to you with tears, long-suffering Lord. Glory to you."
Caiaphas held you for judgment, and Peter fell. The lawless priest was judging you, and your first disciple denied you.
But he had heard from the law that you do not disregard fountains of tears.
You who are the comforter [?] of hidden things and willingly took judgment upon yourself, Lord, glory to you.
Tell us, then, O Jews: what did you see from the Savior? Did he overturn the law or the teaching of the prophets?
How did you not fear to hand over to Pilate God, the Word of God and the Redeemer of our souls?
Judge, O Lord, those who wrong me.
Your salvation. Tell us, then, O Jews:
You, the Word of the Father, were handed over by my [?] disciple to be slaughtered like a sheep.
Once the cherubim hid beneath the thrones of the chariot's wheels, unable to look.
When the Lord was judged by a servant, you were long-suffering, Savior. Glory to you.
